33021fef93dd.title: Software Engineer, Shop/Feed Ads
33021fef93dd.description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The Monetization team is a new cross-functional group spanning engineering, product, research, and design. We are building the foundational systems that will help OpenAI scale access to intelligence responsibly.

Our mission is to create user-first, privacy-preserving monetization products—including next-generation ads experiences—that strengthen trust, expand economic opportunity, and support OpenAI’s long-term innovation. We believe monetization should deliver clear user value, uphold rigorous privacy and safety standards, and sustain a healthy ecosystem for developers and businesses.

The team operates in a greenfield environment, moving quickly through prototyping, experimentation, and iterative deployment. We partner closely across Product, Design, and Research to bring new capabilities into real-world systems at global scale.



ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for an experienced Software Engineer to lead the design and development of the systems that turn advertiser feeds (eg. retail feeds, travel feeds etc.) into relevant, reliably delivered ads. In this foundational role, you will build across the full ads lifecycle—from ingesting and organizing retailer or travel catalogs into efficient retrieval systems, supporting ranking models, and serving ads at scale.

This role is well suited to an engineer with direct experience in product ads retrieval, ranking, and delivery, along with a strong understanding of merchant feeds and shopping systems such as Google Shopping, YouTube product ads, or Amazon. We also welcome engineers with Senior Staff-level or greater scope who have deep ownership of large-scale catalogs, search and indexing, ads serving, or closely related distributed systems.

You will independently own complex systems, make sound technical tradeoffs, and help define the architecture and roadmap for Shopping/Travel/Feed Ads. You will collaborate closely with Ads ML, Ads Delivery, Product, Design, and Research to connect accurate, fresh advertiser feed information with useful ads experiences in ChatGPT.

This role is based in San Francisco and Mountain View. We offer relocation assistance to new employees.



IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL

 - Design and build pipelines that ingest, validate, normalize, and refresh merchant product feeds, keeping catalog information accurate and available for serving.

 - Develop scalable catalog storage and indexing systems that make large inventories searchable and reflect changes in product availability, pricing, and attributes.

 - Build search and retrieval systems that efficiently identify relevant, eligible products across merchant catalogs.

 - Partner with Ads ML to connect product retrieval with ranking models through dependable interfaces, features, and serving infrastructure.

 - Engineer low-latency, high-throughput ads delivery systems with strong reliability and correctness guarantees.

 - Design real-time event pipelines and distributed storage that support catalog freshness, serving decisions, and downstream feedback.

 - Build observability and quality controls to detect feed errors, stale inventory, indexing delays, and serving issues.

 - Define technical direction and drive complex projects from early prototypes through production deployment and operation.

 - Operate systems with high engineering rigor through testing, monitoring, privacy and security reviews, and strong operational practices.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU

 - Have extensive experience building and operating large-scale distributed systems, with direct ownership of product ads retrieval, ranking infrastructure, or delivery.

 - Understand merchant feeds and shopping systems, including how catalog quality, product availability, and freshness affect relevance and ads performance.

 - Have built systems for shopping or product ads at platforms such as Google Shopping, YouTube, Amazon, or a comparable environment.

 - Alternatively, have operated at Senior Staff-level scope or above, leading the architecture and delivery of large-scale catalogs, search and indexing platforms, ads serving, or related backend systems.

 - Have built low-latency, high-throughput services and data pipelines with demanding reliability and correctness requirements.

 - Can reason across ingestion, storage, indexing, retrieval, ranking, and serving, and make thoughtful tradeoffs between freshness, relevance, latency, and cost.

 - Are comfortable partnering with machine-learning teams to bring ranking models and signals into dependable production systems.

 - Can define technical direction in an ambiguous 0→1 environment and independently drive complex work across teams.

 - Communicate clearly and make technical decisions grounded in user value, merchant experience, and long-term system health.

Life sciences is one of the clearest areas where advances in intelligence can meaningfully benefit the world at large. You’ll work across the stack, partnering with researchers, scientists, and infrastructure engineers to turn complex needs into reliable, intuitive products.

 - Work autonomously, make sound technical decisions, and drive projects forward with limited direction.

 - Are excited about advances in AI and how they could change scientific work.

4af0fdf258b3.description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The Growth team drives user and revenue growth across ChatGPT’s consumer and business segments and other OpenAI products worldwide. We work across the full funnel—from awareness and acquisition through activation, retention, and expansion—using experimentation, data science, machine learning, and product engineering to help more people discover and realize durable value from OpenAI’s products.

Our team partners closely with Product, Engineering, Data Science, Design, Finance, Lifecycle, and Growth Marketing. We move quickly, test rigorously, and hold a high bar for measurement, privacy, reliability, and user trust.




ABOUT THIS ROLE: 

We are looking for a Machine Learning Engineer to build the models and decision systems that optimize paid marketing investment for ChatGPT and other OpenAI products. You will develop budget allocation and control algorithms that determine where to invest, how quickly to spend, and how to adjust as performance changes.

The challenge is to make reliable decisions from noisy, delayed, and incomplete signals. You will combine machine learning, optimization, and experimentation to improve incremental growth and long-term user value within budget and efficiency constraints. You will own this work from problem formulation and prototyping through deployment, evaluation, and ongoing operation.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to eligible employees.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Build budget allocation algorithms. Decide how to distribute investment across channels, campaigns, and markets using estimates of marginal returns, while accounting for diminishing returns, uncertainty, and business constraints.

 - Develop spend pacing and adaptive control systems. Adjust budgets and spending rates as performance changes, balancing responsiveness with stability when feedback is delayed or noisy. Build in spend limits, monitoring, and safe fallback behavior.

 - Model marketing response and user value. Develop forecasts and models of conversion, long-term value, and saturation that help determine where the next dollar can have the greatest impact.

 - Evaluate decisions rigorously. Use simulations, backtesting, and online experiments to test allocation and control policies. Partner with Data Science to measure incrementality and validate whether offline improvements translate into better investment outcomes.

 - Own reliable production systems. Build data pipelines, training and inference workflows, and integrations that turn model outputs into budget decisions. Establish data-quality checks, monitoring, and retraining with thoughtful treatment of privacy and consent.

 - Turn business goals into optimization problems. Partner with Growth Marketing, Data Science, Engineering, and Finance to define objectives and constraints, communicate tradeoffs, and use evidence to improve investment decisions.

 - Help build a diverse and inclusive culture where people feel welcome, challenge assumptions, and collaborate with candor and respect.




You might thrive in this role if you:

 - 5+ years of experience as a Machine Learning Engineer, Applied Scientist, Data Scientist, or in a comparable quantitative engineering role, or an equivalent record of impact.

 - Experience building and operating production ML or quantitative decision systems, from problem formulation and data pipelines through deployment, experimentation, and monitoring.

 - Strong software engineering skills, proficiency in Python and SQL, and hands-on experience with ML frameworks and large-scale data systems.

 - Strong foundations in machine learning and statistics, with experience applying optimization or control methods to decisions under uncertainty.

 - Experience evaluating models or algorithms with noisy, delayed, or incomplete data, and the judgment to balance model quality, causal impact, and operational reliability.

 - The ability to turn ambiguous goals into focused experiments, interpret mixed results, and communicate clear decisions with technical and non-technical partners.

 - A collaborative working style and a commitment to deploying AI responsibly, in service of OpenAI’s mission to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity.

OpenAI’s Research Data team exists to accelerate the evaluation, safety and capabilities of our models and products. Made up of technical operators and software engineers, we design the methods through which we acquire and create data.

The work could range from acquiring existing datasets to shaping research collaborations. You’ll carry opportunities from initial investigation through commercial discussions, agreements, delivery and research use, exercising sound judgement around sensitive data and relationships.

Our current work focuses particularly on biology and chemistry. We welcome different combinations of scientific, technical and partnership experience.

This role is based in our San Francisco HQ.

In this role, you will:

c79771135941.title: Software Engineer, HSM Infrastructure Security, Consumer Devices
c79771135941.description:
We are hiring a Security Software Engineer to design and implement the hardware-backed security foundations used across OpenAI’s device ecosystem.



A central focus of this role is hardening the boundary between our policy systems and the HSMs that protect sensitive cryptographic keys. This boundary determines which operations may be performed, what may be signed, which policies must be satisfied, and how changes to trusted software and policy are authorized.



You will develop security-critical software and firmware within, or immediately adjacent to, an HSM trust boundary. Depending on your background, this may include HSM trusted applications, firmware services, cryptographic mechanisms, device drivers, PKCS#11 components, secure-provisioning protocols, or signing-policy enforcement systems.



This is a hands-on software-engineering role. You will be expected to design systems, write and review production code, debug across hardware and software boundaries, and carry projects from initial requirements through deployment. It is not an HSM administration, PKI operations, compliance, or architecture-only position.



In This Role, You Will

 - Design and implement security-critical software and firmware for HSMs, secure elements, trusted execution environments, and hardware roots of trust.

 - Build and harden the policy-to-HSM boundary responsible for authorizing certificate issuance and cryptographic signing operations.

 - Develop HSM trusted applications, firmware components, host interfaces, device drivers, SDKs, or cryptographic service integrations.

 - Implement or extend cryptographic interfaces such as PKCS#11, OpenSSL providers or engines, platform key-storage APIs, or comparable hardware-security interfaces.

 - Build firmware and software that cryptographically enforces key generation, provisioning, usage, rotation, recovery, and destruction policies.

 - Design and implement HSM-backed certificate authority, code-signing, key-management, and device-identity systems.

 - Develop end-to-end cryptographic protocols spanning devices, secure hardware, policy services, and backend infrastructure.

 - Build security capabilities supporting device attestation, secure boot, factory provisioning and restoration, user registration, and authentication.

 - Design controls that make trusted software and policy changes verifiable, auditable, and subject to appropriate multi-party authorization.

 - Write, review, test, and audit secure embedded software for resource-constrained environments.

 - Develop test harnesses, emulators, fuzzers, and fault-injection tooling to validate security properties and failure behavior.

 - Threat-model hardware and software trust boundaries and translate findings into concrete engineering improvements.

 - Partner with hardware, firmware, infrastructure, application, and security teams to integrate secure-by-default capabilities into production systems.

 - Help establish engineering standards for HSM development, applied cryptography, secure key management, and certificate infrastructure.



Minimum Qualifications

 - 5+ years experience building secure embedded firmware for constrained environments

 - Deep programming experience in C, C++, or Rust.



You Might Thrive in This Role If You Have

 - A strong track record of designing, implementing, debugging, and shipping production systems software.

 - Hands-on experience developing security-critical software or firmware within, or directly adjacent to, an HSM, secure element, TEE, or hardware root of trust.

 - Experience developing one or more of the following:
   
   - HSM firmware or trusted applications
   
   - Cryptographic mechanisms or hardware-accelerated cryptographic services
   
   - HSM device drivers, host libraries, SDKs, or middleware
   
   - PKCS#11 providers, mechanisms, or integrations
   
   - Secure key-provisioning or key-injection protocols
   
   - HSM-backed certificate authority or code-signing systems
   
   - Signing-policy enforcement within a hardware-backed trust boundary

 - Strong knowledge of applied cryptography, digital signatures, key hierarchies, secure key management, and cryptographic protocol design.

 - Experience with PKI, X.509 certificates, certificate authorities, certificate issuance, and certificate lifecycle protocols.

 - Familiarity with secure boot, measured boot, device identity, remote attestation, or hardware-backed storage.

 - Experience reasoning about concurrency, memory safety, privilege separation, hardware interfaces, failure modes, and side-channel or physical attack considerations.

 - The ability to evaluate security designs and personally implement the software required to realize them.

 - Clear communication skills and the ability to collaborate across hardware, firmware, backend, and product teams.



Additional Experience That May Be Helpful

 - Firmware development for ARM TrustZone or another trusted execution environment.

 - Experience with commercial or cloud HSM platforms such as Thales Luna, Entrust/nShield, Utimaco, Marvell LiquidSecurity, AWS CloudHSM, or comparable systems.

 - Experience with PKCS#11, KMIP, OpenSSL providers or engines, secure-element APIs, or platform-native key-storage frameworks.

 - Device manufacturing, secure provisioning, factory restore, or silicon bring-up experience.

 - Secure boot ROM, bootloader, firmware-signing, anti-rollback, or authenticated-update development.

 - Developing trusted applications or cryptographic services inside an HSM or secure coprocessor.

 - Hardware/software co-design involving cryptographic accelerators, secure processors, or custom silicon.

 - Multi-party authorization, quorum-controlled deployments, tamper-resistant audit mechanisms, or attestable policy systems.

 - Secure or private storage systems based on hardware-protected keys.

 - Experience sustaining high-assurance security software in production.

About the Team

OpenAI’s Applied AI Engineering team helps organizations turn frontier AI capabilities into safe, reliable, and high-impact production systems. We work with customer executives, product and engineering teams, security leaders, and transformation teams to identify valuable opportunities, accelerate technical implementation, and scale what works.

Production-ready deployments are defined by complexity rather than any one industry: existing architectures, diverse data environments, security and governance requirements, multiple stakeholder groups, and organization-wide change. We turn lessons from these deployments into better products and reusable patterns for customers everywhere.

About the Role

As an Applied AI Engineer you will partner directly with leading organizations to design, build, and deploy AI systems that deliver measurable business outcomes. You will combine deep technical judgment, hands-on engineering, and customer leadership to take ambitious ideas from use-case selection and architecture through prototyping, evaluation, production launch, and scale.

You will write and debug code, build evaluation systems, resolve complex integrations, and guide decisions involving model behavior, reliability, latency, cost, safety, security, governance, and operational readiness. Success is measured by production systems, sustained adoption, and meaningful customer impact—not simply activity or successful demonstrations.

This is a rare opportunity to work on consequential real-world deployments at the frontier of AI while directly influencing how OpenAI’s products evolve.

This role is based in Munich. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees

In this role, you will:

 - Partner directly with enterprise and digital native customers to identify high-value opportunities and translate them into technical architectures, implementation plans, evaluation strategies, and measurable success criteria.

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops custom silicon and systems for advanced AI workloads. Our first-party accelerator team works across chip architecture, design, software, and systems to build the computing platforms that power frontier models. We are a small, dynamic team that values technical breadth, hands-on engineering, and creative approaches to building complex hardware.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a SoC Engineer to help architect, design, and integrate OpenAI’s first-party AI accelerators. You will build the processor, interconnect, I/O, and platform infrastructure that connects our accelerator designs into complete, functional systems.

This role combines architectural judgment with hands-on implementation. You’ll work closely with design, architecture, verification, and software teams throughout development, from defining subsystem requirements and integrating IP to pre-silicon validation, silicon bring-up, and post-silicon debug. You should enjoy stretching across domains, rolling up your sleeves, and doing the work needed to make a complex system function end to end.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Define and implement SoC architectures spanning embedded processors, AMBA interconnects, peripheral subsystems, PCI Express, Ethernet and die-to-die interfaces.

 - Develop the microarchitecture and RTL design of subsystems supporting I/O and SoC functionality.

 - Integrate Arm Cortex-M and Cortex-A processors, AXI/APB fabrics, and third-party controller IP, including the RTL and glue logic needed to connect these components.

 - Develop reset and boot architectures, working with firmware and software teams to define sequencing, initialization, and survivability behavior.

 - Incorporate debug, test, and security requirements into the SoC architecture and implementation, partnering with other silicon designers to make the silicon observable, testable, and secure.

 - Drive PCIe and other I/O integration, including controller and PHY interfaces, high-speed SerDes, and die-to-die connectivity.

 - Contribute to power management and security architecture and design.

 - Work directly with third-party IP vendors to define technical requirements, evaluate IP capabilities, coordinate deliverables, and resolve issues from integration through silicon bring-up.

 - Work across architecture, design, verification, physical design, and software teams to define interfaces, resolve integration issues, and carry designs through pre-silicon validation and post-silicon bring-up.

 - Work closely with Firmware and Software teams to define boot, configuration and runtime behavior and functionality.

 - Build and apply automation and AI-assisted tools to accelerate design, IP integration, consistency checking, and debugging while maintaining engineering quality.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have experience in SoC architecture, RTL design, and subsystem or full-chip integration, with hands-on ownership through implementation and silicon bring-up.

 - Are familiar with Arm processor subsystems, including Cortex-M and Cortex-A, and AMBA protocols and interconnects such as AXI and APB.

 - Understand PCIe protocols and have experience configuring, integrating, and debugging controller IP.

 - Have experience integrating high-speed I/O, including SerDes/PHY interfaces and die-to-die links.

 - Have experience working directly with third-party IP vendors to evaluate technical fit, communicate requirements, and drive integration and debug issues to resolution.

 - Understand reset and boot architecture and the interactions between hardware, firmware, and software during initialization and recovery.

 - Have experience designing for debug, test, and security, and can reason about how these requirements affect the broader system.

 - Are comfortable writing and debugging Verilog/SystemVerilog and building scripts or tools to make integration work more efficient and reliable.

 - Enjoy stretching into multiple domains, learning unfamiliar parts of a system, and rolling up your sleeves to build and debug.

 - Enjoy working on a small, dynamic team where priorities evolve and engineers take broad ownership.

 - Are excited about creatively applying automation and AI tools to hardware design and integration work.

About the Team

Dots is building personal AI agents that help people make progress on their goals, including when they are away from ChatGPT. These agents can learn preferences, maintain context, work across applications, and use cloud computers to carry out tasks.

Our team brings together product engineering, design, and research to turn frontier model capabilities into useful everyday experiences. We are defining how people delegate work, understand what an agent is doing, and stay in control. Engineers help shape both the product and the systems behind it, from early prototypes through launch and iteration.

We are looking for Senior and Staff Software Engineers to build the mobile web experience for Dots. You will create responsive, accessible interfaces that let people start work, follow progress, and guide their agents from a phone or browser. You will help establish interaction patterns for ongoing, asynchronous work and make sophisticated agent capabilities feel clear and approachable.

 - Design and ship mobile web experiences for creating tasks, reviewing agent activity, and providing feedback or direction.

 - Build interfaces that handle streaming updates, long-running tasks, interrupted sessions, and changing connectivity.

 - Improve responsiveness, loading performance, accessibility, and usability across screen sizes and browsers.

About the Team

Identity is the foundation of trust in an AI-powered world. As people build a rich personal and organizational context in ChatGPT, they need systems that protect it, remember it, and let them share it securely across apps and agents. Without strong identity, context stays locked away or exposed. With it, AI becomes safe, personal, and truly useful, empowering users while keeping control firmly in their hands. Our team builds the trusted OpenAI account layer that connects people, enterprises, developers, and agents to OpenAI apps and the broader AI ecosystem. Our systems are the front door to OpenAI—held to an exceptionally high bar for availability, security, and latency—and are depended on by many internal teams.

About the Role

As an Engineering Manager, Identity Platform you will lead a team owning foundational identity services that must be highly reliable, secure, and fast under extreme load. You’ll set direction, grow and support the team, and partner closely across engineering and security to strengthen the platform that enables trusted access to OpenAI products.

In this role, you will:

 - Build, lead, and develop a high-performing engineering team. Coach and mentor engineers and senior technical leads to increase their impact and support their growth.

 - Define and own the technical strategy, roadmap, and execution for OpenAI’s core identity systems.

 - Guide the architecture of distributed systems operating at massive scale, with high requirements for reliability, privacy, and performance.

 - Partner closely with Product and Infrastructure teams to support new product needs and uphold high system standards.

 - Ensure the team operates effectively, maintains strong engineering rigor, and consistently delivers against ambitious goals.

 - Establish processes and a culture that enable fast learning, high trust, and responsible innovation.

 - Lead the team responsible for the authentication stack and token exchange infrastructure, ensuring high availability, strong security posture, and low-latency performance.

 - Own and improve request validation at the edge for logged-in users, delivering extremely high reliability and fast validation under high throughput.

 - Oversee systems that enable secure access to user data, improving scalability, reliability, and access patterns for internal consumers across the company.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have 10+ years of experience building, scaling, and operating distributed systems at large scale.

 - Have 3+ years of experience managing high-performance engineering teams in fast-paced, rapidly shifting environments.

 - Care deeply about people leadership, coaching, and helping engineers achieve peak performance.

 - Communicate clearly, think holistically, and make decisions grounded in both user needs and long-term sustainability.

 - Have experience managing an infrastructure team and are effective at hiring, coaching, and developing engineers while maintaining strong operational excellence.

 - Have deep experience building and operating high-scale backend systems, with a track record of improving reliability, latency, and security in production.

The Applied AI Engineering team is responsible for ensuring the safe and effective deployment of Generative AI applications for developers and startups. We act as a trusted advisor and thought partner for our customers, working to build an effective backlog of GenAI use cases for their industry and drive them to production through strong technical guidance. 2a45e3a50b16.description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI’s Client Platform Engineering team builds and operates the platforms that make employee devices secure, reliable, and easy to use. Our work spans device posture and trust, onboarding, application delivery, operating-system updates, fleet telemetry, and employee-facing remediation. We partner with Security, IT, Research, Applied, and specialized engineering teams to reduce friction while protecting OpenAI’s systems and data.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Client Platform Engineer, You will build and own agentic solutions that automate OAI fleet operations and reduce employee friction, with measurable outcomes and reliability. You will develop first-party software, integrate commercial and open-source tools, and own changes from design and testing through deployment and production operations. Your work will improve security, reliability, and the employee experience.

We’re looking for people who are passionate about automation, endpoint security, and building scalable solutions that improve employee experience. You should have deep experience securing and managing heterogeneous fleets at scale, with strong software engineering skills to automate security controls and fleet operations across environments with different compliance requirements. Your problem-solving mindset and attention to detail will be key to success in this role.

In this role, you will:

Build the platforms that help employees do their best work on devices they can trust.

 - Own the design, development, deployment, and operation of secure endpoint management systems across environments with different compliance requirements.

 - Create magical employee experiences by building agentic workflows with OpenAI products and models that use fleet telemetry to anticipate issues, guide remediation, and design friction out of everyday work.

 - Make new hires productive from day one, using OpenAI products to simplify device setup, software delivery, and onboarding support.

 - Build secure, reliable workflows with scoped access, human review for sensitive changes, traceable actions, and tested recovery.

 - Partner with IT, Security, Research, and Engineering to deliver consistent provisioning, updates, and support across our heterogeneous fleet.

 - Develop first-party software and integrate commercial and open-source tools for software packaging, deployment, and application management.

 - Manage fleet configuration as code through GitOps, version control, peer review, and automated validation.

 - Build and operate CI/CD pipelines for fleet infrastructure across Azure, AWS, and GCP, with staged deployments and tested rollback.

 - Use fleet telemetry to proactively improve performance and reliability, detect configuration drift, and verify deployment outcomes.

 - Participate in engineering on-call, own incident resolution, and turn operational lessons into lasting improvements that reduce recurring failures and manual work.


YOU MAY BE A FIT FOR THIS ROLE IF YOU HAVE: 

 - Built, shipped, and operated production software or automation for an endpoint fleet using Python, Go, or another modern programming language.

 - Managed and secured an endpoint fleet at scale, with deep experience in at least one operating system and hands-on work in areas such as enrollment, policy enforcement, software delivery, OS updates, or device trust.

 - Demonstrated success with open-source endpoint tools for configuration, device and application management, and telemetry.

 - Rolled out fleet changes safely using version-controlled configuration, automated testing, staged deployments, and tested rollback. Used telemetry to verify changes and diagnose failures.

 - Deep experience managing infrastructure at scale with IaC and GitOps, using tools such as Terraform, Ansible, and Chef.

 - Experience integrating and operating fleet infrastructure with CI/CD and DevOps workflows.

 - Operated infrastructure that supports endpoint management in at least one public cloud, such as Azure, AWS, or Google Cloud.

 - Familiarity with compliance frameworks such as SOC 2, ISO 27001, FedRAMP, and NIST.

 - Initiative, analytical judgment, and the ability to turn problems into practical improvements.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU HAVE:

 - Integrated or contributed to open-source tooling for endpoint management, software delivery, or fleet telemetry.

 - Deep experience with open-source fleet management tools and frameworks.

 - Operated containerized services using Docker or Kubernetes

 - Strong soft skills, including stakeholder communication and cross-functional collaboration.

 - Relevant professional certifications such as CISSP, CISA, CISM, CCSP.

 - A security thought leader with contributions to CPE open-source projects or technical communities.

31795b58abfe.description:
About the Team

Enterprise Security protects the systems, identities, devices, and services that enable OpenAI's employees to work securely and effectively. We partner across IT and Security to understand risk, build practical defenses, and support a rapidly evolving technical environment.

About the Role

We are looking for an Enterprise Security Engineer with a focus on vulnerability management, novel vulnerabilities, and zero-day response. You will investigate vulnerabilities and security weaknesses across networks, endpoints, and SaaS, prioritize them in the context of real exposure, and drive remediation through verified outcomes.

You will also build security capabilities and automation, use AI agents to solve practical problems, and help shape how enterprise security operates as agents become a larger part of everyday work.

This role is open to candidates in San Francisco, CA, and to remote candidates in the United States.

In this role, you will:

 - Discover, investigate, and prioritize vulnerabilities and misconfigurations across enterprise systems, including novel vulnerabilities and zero-days with incomplete information and no established playbook.

 - Translate technical findings into clear attack paths, business impact, and actionable remediation.

 - Develop and validate emergency mitigations when patches are unavailable, coordinate with system owners, vendors, and incident responders, and drive durable fixes through verified closure.

 - Improve asset visibility, ownership, vulnerability data quality, and reporting.

 - Build and operate security tools and integrations using code, APIs, automation, and AI agents.

 - Design controls for agent access, execution, and accountability.

 - Contribute across endpoint, network, identity, and SaaS security, and support incident investigations when needed.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have independently investigated novel or emerging vulnerabilities and driven enterprise remediation from uncertain initial reports through mitigation and verified closure.

 - Bring technical depth in a relevant security domain and working knowledge across networks, endpoints, and SaaS.

 - Can understand and improve code and safely integrate APIs and security systems.

 - Have solved substantive problems using AI agents and can explain how you evaluated and corrected their work.

 - Think clearly about security tradeoffs, ambiguous evidence, and the changing risks of agentic systems.

8aceea39fb06.description:
WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!


WHY THIS ROLE?

We're building the foundational infrastructure that will define how the world thinks about and deploys AI, and we want the sharpest, most driven, and most curious people to help us do it. As the founding lead of Agentic Analytics, a new team in our Analytics and Data Insights organization, you'll own how Cohere gets answers from its own data: an agentic analytics system that answers business questions over governed data, shows the source, query, and freshness behind every answer, and asks for clarification or declines when the evidence is insufficient.

Agentic analytics is far from a solved problem, and correctness is the hard part. A query that runs can still answer the wrong question. Agents go wrong when a business term maps to more than one table, when data goes stale, and when the right context never reaches the model. The worst failures are silent and plausible: a join that double-counts, a wrong denominator, missing data read as zero. Getting this right takes governed definitions, context an agent can use, and an evaluation bar that decides what ships.

You'll build on work already in motion: an internal analytics agent in pilot on our BigQuery warehouse, which is fed by tested ingestion pipelines and modeled in dbt. In your first year, you'll take it to production for teams across Cohere, one domain at a time, and make it replicable: each new domain stands up with configuration, a fresh evaluation set, and very little new code.

This is a hands-on  staff engineering role reporting to our Senior Director of Data Analytics. You'll write production code and evaluation sets yourself while managing a small founding team that grows as the system proves itself. You may have held the title software engineer, AI engineer, or data scientist; what matters is that you've built a system like this and run it in production.



RESPONSIBILITIES

As the lead of Agentic Analytics, you will:

 - Own the system end to end. Set the architecture for how a business question becomes a governed query and a verifiable answer: interpreting the question, retrieving the right context, applying approved definitions and joins, enforcing the asking user's permissions, and attaching the evidence (source, query, freshness) to every answer.

 - Build and run it in production. Design the core services and write much of the first version yourself: agent-facing data tools (MCP or equivalent), context retrieval, agent skills for analytics, and the APIs that serve answers. Hold them to production standards for reliability, latency, cost, security, and observability. Put it where people already work: Slack, North, IDEs, and other agents.

 - Hold every release to the evaluation bar. Build and run the evaluation harness, and define what correct means in each domain: ground-truth question sets, including held-out cases and questions the agent should clarify or decline; result-level scoring, correct-or-decline rates, coverage, and error severity; and regression tests on every change to context, skills, or models. Nothing ships below the bar, and the call on when a domain is ready for production is yours.

 - Engineer the context layer. Turn metric definitions, approved joins, documentation generated from the code that builds each table, a business glossary, and worked examples into context the agent can use. Every correction becomes a reviewed definition and a regression test.

 - Roll it out across Cohere. Bring domains such as marketing, revenue, finance, and product onto the system one at a time, each with named owners, certified definitions, and its own evaluation set. Measure adoption, accuracy, turnaround, and correction effort against how those teams work today.

 - Make it replicable. Package the tools, skills, context templates, and evaluations, and document them well enough that other teams at Cohere can run the system without you.

 - Hire and lead the team. Bring on the team's first engineers, set the technical bar, review the work, and develop the people doing it.

 - Partner across Cohere. Work with our data platform team on the warehouse and semantic models, our model evaluation team on evaluation methodology, our security team on access, and each domain's owners on definitions and rollout.


QUALIFICATIONS

You may be a good fit, if you have:

 - 10+ years building and operating production analytics or software systems, including technical leadership of a team or of systems that span teams

 - Experience shipping LLM agents to production: tool use, MCP or similar, retrieval and context engineering, guardrails, and observability, with firm opinions on where they fail

 - Hands-on experience building natural-language or agentic analytics (text-to-SQL, analytics agents, question answering over a semantic layer) that real users relied on, and evidence that it was right

 - Depth in evaluating LLM systems: golden sets, result-level comparison, abstention metrics, error taxonomies, and regression testing in CI, plus the judgment to tell a good demo from a system you'd put in front of a CFO

 - Strong Python and SQL, and experience designing and running

a8cbe4771bd9.description:
WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!

Why this role?

The Data Infrastructure team at Cohere is responsible for the storage and data movement layer underlying every model training run. We're building the unified storage layer that feeds our training workloads. It needs to serve petabytes of training data and model checkpoints fast enough to keep thousands of GPUs busy across several training clusters. In this role, you’d have an opportunity to build this system from the ground up. You’d be a key contributor, working on a problem few teams have had to solve at this scale.


In this role, you will:

 - Design, build, and operate the distributed storage system that feeds model training and evaluation.

 - Run this system multiple on Kubernetes clusters at petabyte scale.

 - Work with researchers and training-infra teams on how jobs actually read and write data, and turn that into throughput, latency, and durability requirements

 - Work through the networking, I/O, and consistency problems of moving large datasets and checkpoints across regions and backends, with GPU idle time and time-to-insight as the measures of success
   

You may be a good fit if you have:

 - Strong storage fundamentals, including replication, consistency, caching, and data lifecycle management.

 - Strong coding ability. We work in Python and Go; experience in either is enough, but you should be willing to pick up the other

 - Experience running stateful systems on Kubernetes, including Persistent Volumes, CSI drivers, and StatefulSets.

 - Hands-on experience with cloud object storage such as S3 as well as POSIX-style filesystems.
   

It’s a bonus if you have:

 - Experience with parallel or HPC filesystems such as Weka, VAST, or Lustre.

 - Familiarity with the data-loading and checkpointing patterns used in large-scale model training.

 - An interest in how large models are trained and evaluated, including the trajectory and eval data those runs generate, and a desire to understand the workloads the platform is serving.

Role Overview:
As a Senior Member of Technical Staff specializing in web data for pre-training, you will play a pivotal role in developing the large scale web data pipeline that underpins Cohere’s advanced language models. In this role, you will work extensively with large-scale web corpora, transforming raw, noisy internet data into high-quality training data for pretraining. You will own key components of the data pipeline, including extraction, parsing, deduplication, and filtering. You will also analyze the composition and quality of web data, study its impact on downstream model performance, and collaborate closely with the broader data and evaluation teams to iterate on the training corpus.

Your work will be essential to Cohere’s mission of delivering efficient and reliable language understanding and generation capabilities, driving innovation in natural language processing. If you are passionate about transforming data into the foundation of AI systems, this role offers a unique opportunity to make a meaningful impact.

Please Note: We have offices in London, Paris, Toronto, San Francisco and New York but also embrace being remote-friendly! There are no restrictions on where you can be located for this role. (EST/EU)

 - Analyze web data composition across domains, languages and time periods.

 - Develop and maintain highly-performant deduplication pipelines.

 - Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including researchers and engineers, to ensure data pipelines meet the demands of cutting-edge language models.



Qualifications:

 - Strong software engineering skills, with proficiency in Python and experience building data pipelines.

 - A passion for bridging research and engineering to solve complex data-related challenges in AI model training.

WHO ARE WE?

Why this role?

This role will focus on evaluating data science and coding tasks, requiring you to review and debug code, analyze model trajectories, and assess data visualization script development and logical flow implementation. Your work will contribute to our model development efforts and the logic our models apply when completing task requests.

Please note: This is a part-time independent contractor position available within Canada. We seek candidates who are able to commit to 16 hours per week minimum at a 40 CAD/hour contract rate. This role is BYOD 💻 - Bring Your Own Device (laptop). Remote work within Canada. 12 month contract. 

As a Data Annotation Specialist, you will:

 - Evaluate the model's ability to respond to coding requests, workflows, and code base-related questions using available tools.

 - Assess agent trajectories and model capabilities for code generation, tabular and graphic manipulation, and debugging requests.

 - Prompt models to complete complex data science tasks and review the accuracy of generated responses.

 - Label, proofread, and improve machine-written and human-written software engineering-related outputs.

 - Report quality and performance trends related to model/agent behaviour and project assignments.

You may be a good fit if you have:

 - Exceptional data analysis and visualization skills.

 - 3+ years of relevant industry experience working on real-world data science problems and pipelines.

 - Proficient knowledge and understanding of Python and industry-standard data science packages (numpy, pandas, matplotlib, sqlite, or others).

 - Strong understanding of SQL syntax writing and workflows; and a deep familiarity with file/data formats, such as markdown, JSON, XML, YAML, and HTML.

 - Prior experience re-writing, proofreading, and delivering feedback on code.

 - Familiarity with code agents (OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex) or evaluating agent trajectories is a plus.

The Candidate Journey:

 - Initial Screening: Our Talent Team will review your application.

 - First Assessment: If selected to move forward, you’ll receive a multiple-choice assessment by email.

 - Second Assessment: Candidates who achieve a passing score will be contacted by a member of our team to complete a more comprehensive assessment focused on their area of expertise.

 - Video Screen: If selected to move forward, you’ll have a short video call with a member of our Operations Team.

 - Final: Selected candidates will receive an Independent Contractor Agreement.

As an independent contractor, you maintain control over how you complete your work and may work with multiple clients simultaneously. We request that you declare any external work relationships with Cohere’s direct competitors and always maintain the IP confidentiality of the Cohere project. Independent contractors are not eligible for health benefits or other benefits provided to employees. Compensation for services is provided to contractors by self-invoicing for services provided pursuant to the terms of our agreement with the contractor.

It is important to understand that, as an independent contractor, continuous work is not guaranteed. The client-contractor relationship is fundamentally project-based, meaning engagements may be temporary, periodic, or intermittent based on our organizational needs and project availability. As an independent contractor, you should anticipate fluctuations in workflow and, therefore, compensation for services when Cohere does not require as many hours of services in a week.

Prospective candidates, please be advised: this role involves working with human-generated and model-generated tasks that may involve exposure to not safe for work (NSFW) text content as part of data annotation tasks, including explicit, offensive, or other inappropriate material.

Cohere’s TPMs would often be described as organized, execution-oriented, pragmatic leaders who are adaptable to the needs of the company and the programs they lead.

As a reward for the depth and breadth of expertize that you bring to the table, you will get to work alongside some of the most talented AI researchers and industry experts in the world on building cutting edge AI technology. No day will be the same as the one before, and the dynamic high growth environment will be absolutely perfect for anyone excited about solving novel problems, bringing structure to oftentimes chaotic and fast-paced environments, and ambitious about scaling their own impact and growth alongside the company!



Please note: While we are remote-first and accept candidates from all over the world, we are highly prioritizing hiring for people who are within 1-2 hours of British Standard Time (BST).




AS A MACHINE LEARNING TECHNICAL PROGRAM MANAGER, YOU WILL:

 - Establish, improve, and scale foundational processes that allow the Generative Modeling teams to execute better, faster, and more predictably

 - Scale the operational capacity and effectiveness of the Modeling TPM team in collaboration with the Modeling TPM lead to ensure the function can remain lean and effective during a period of the program portfolio complexity and size continuing to rapidly increase

 - Flexibly adapt to the needs of the company, programs, and the team from tackling long-horizon programs that can span quarters or even years to jumping onto often highly ambiguous short-term challenges that can have company-wide impact

 - Partner directly with leaders within and outside of the Modeling organization on efforts to design, train and improve our core generative models

 - Lead cross-functional, oftentimes company-wide programs and strategic initiatives, collaborating and coordinating with cross-functional teams such as Product, Engineering, Legal, Platform, Infra, Policy, and Finance

 - Operate as an organizational expert in improving engineering execution rigor and operations on the ground, while contributing to the strategic layer in areas such as long-term strategic planning with senior modeling leadership

 - Map out dependencies and risks, and ensure that cross-functional execution across the program runs smoothly, communicating status with non-technical and technical stakeholders and senior management

 - Both own and enable a useful communication flow of priorities, ideas, and knowledge throughout and beyond the Modeling organization in line with your programs

 - Respond quickly to program-level changes, clarifying new scope, and managing resource needs in response to evolving priorities
   
   


YOU MAY BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU HAVE:

 - 5-10 years as a Technical Program Manager AND 5+ years of experience working directly on AI/ML. Strong preference for candidates that have worked directly in building foundation models.

 - In-depth knowledge of machine learning, particularly when it comes to Natural Language Processing & Large Language Models (LLMs). Bonus points for experience with Multimodal AI.

 - Experience with working in a chaotic, fast paced, low structure environment. We need someone who is pragmatic, can roll up their sleeves when needed, and can function at the tactical and strategic level to do whatever it takes to make Cohere’s models succeed

 - Personal hands-on understanding of the unique challenges of managing projects and programs in the AI/ML development space as opposed to traditional software program management

 - Managed projects & programs requiring a strong general business acumen, such as coordinating with Finance on reporting needs or Policy on regulatory compliance matters — the broader your experience beyond ML technical program management, the better!

This is a judgment-driven role, not passive data entry. You will review, assess, and provide structured feedback across a broad and evolving range of tasks, evaluating, stress-testing, and improving our models on English-language data spanning multiple modalities (text, image, and structured formats such as JSON, CSV/TSV, and Markdown).  - Calibrate and maintain consistency: Participate in calibration exercises and inter-annotator agreement checks to align on standards, and flag ambiguous or uncovered edge cases rather than guessing, since a single misjudgment replicated at scale degrades a model.

 - Adapt to experimental work: Take on new and evolving task types as project needs shift, applying sound judgment in areas where guidelines are still being developed.

80d48e71cd4f.description:
WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!




WHY THIS ROLE

Enterprises hand Cohere their most sensitive data and put our models inside workflows they can't afford to get wrong. Securing that means working on problems the industry hasn't settled yet, what authorization means when an agent acts on a user's behalf, how to contain tools that consume untrusted input, and whether tenant boundaries hold when a model can be steered by the data it reads. The established playbooks only take you so far.

We're hiring a Senior Product Security Engineer to work these problems alongside the engineers building the products, reviewing architecture and code, threat modeling before implementation, testing what ships, and turning what you learn into defaults other teams inherit. This is a hands-on engineering role, not an advisory one.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Lead security reviews. Review architecture, code, and security-sensitive changes. Identify both individual vulnerabilities and the recurring design patterns behind them.

 - Secure AI-powered products. Evaluate risks such as prompt injection, unsafe tool use, identity and delegation failures, excessive agency, data exposure, tenant isolation, and sandbox escapes.

 - Threat model new capabilities. Identify trust boundaries, abuse cases, and high-impact failure modes before implementation. Translate findings into practical, prioritized mitigations.

 - Perform hands-on testing. Investigate suspected vulnerabilities, develop proofs of concept, assess exploitability and impact, and partner with engineers through remediation.

 - Build scalable guardrails. Develop secure defaults, approved patterns, reusable controls, review requirements, and automated checks that reduce recurring risks.

 - Strengthen engineering capability. Pair with engineers, document practical guidance, and help product teams develop durable security expertise.

 - Influence risk decisions. Explain technical findings, business impact, and remediation options clearly to engineers, product leaders, and executives.




YOU MAY BE A GOOD FIT IF

 - You have strong software engineering fundamentals and can independently understand, test, and contribute fixes to production codebases.

 - You are proficient in at least one of Python, Go, or TypeScript.

 - You have led security reviews or threat models for complex production systems and can point to meaningful design or risk improvements that resulted.

 - You understand common vulnerability classes and their underlying design failures, including injection, authorization flaws, IDOR, SSRF, unsafe deserialization, race conditions, cryptographic misuse, and software supply-chain risks.

 - You understand modern application architecture, including web applications, APIs, OAuth/OIDC, cloud platforms, containers, Kubernetes, and CI/CD systems.

 - You can reason rigorously about untrusted input, authorization, isolation, identity, delegation, and data boundaries. Direct experience with agentic AI systems is valuable but not required.

 - You have driven security improvements involving multiple engineering teams, including situations where influence mattered more than authority.

 - You communicate clearly with both technical and non-technical audiences.




NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience building or operating security tooling such as SAST, DAST, SCA, custom linters, or policy-as-code.

 - Experience securing multi-tenant SaaS, enterprise software, or systems that process sensitive customer data.

 - Offensive security experience through penetration testing, red teaming or security research.

 - Experience operating or participating in a vulnerability disclosure or bug bounty program.

 - Contributions to open-source security projects, published research, conference talks, or credited vulnerability discoveries.

We're looking for a design engineer to help build and maintain Waypoint, our design system, across both the Figma library and the production codebase. This is not a "designer who codes a little" or an "engineer who dabbles in Figma" role. You should be genuinely fluent on both sides, comfortable defining a component's behavior and states in Figma one hour and shipping the same component to npm the next.

You'll take direct ownership of the Figma side of our library (structure, variants, tokens, documentation) while also contributing to the core Waypoint system: our component packages, our token pipeline, and the tooling that keeps design and code in sync. If the idea of being the single point of continuity between a Figma frame and a production component sounds exciting rather than exhausting, this is your role.

We're also thinking beyond the system we have today. Waypoint isn't just meant to serve designers and engineers, it's meant to become something a model can read, reason about, and build with directly. We want someone who can help us get there: grounded enough to do the unglamorous work of making today's system solid, and forward looking enough to help define what an intelligent design system looks like next.



WHY THIS ROLE

Waypoint is still early enough that the decisions you make now will shape how the system scales. You'll have real ownership, not just a queue of component tickets, and you'll be working alongside a team that treats design and engineering as one discipline rather than two departments that hand work back and forth. And you'll be helping define what a design system becomes when it has to serve a third audience: the models that will increasingly build with it.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own and evolve the Figma library for Waypoint: component structure, variants, properties, and documentation, so it stays a reliable source of truth for design teams.

 - Build and maintain core Waypoint components, contributing directly to our component packages alongside the design engineering team.

 - Work across our token pipeline, keeping design tokens in Figma and their code representations (CSS custom properties, Tailwind config) tightly synced.

 - Partner with product designers to translate new patterns into system components, and with product engineers to make sure those components are easy to adopt correctly.

 - Help define and refine the workflows and tooling that connect Figma and code (sync scripts, plugins, documentation sites) rather than relying on manual handoff.

 - Write clear documentation and usage guidance so the system scales without you being the bottleneck.

 - Weigh in on system architecture decisions: when to add a new component versus extend an existing one, how to version and package changes, how to keep the system consistent as it grows.

 - Help shape how Waypoint evolves to serve a third consumer beyond designers and engineers: the model itself. That means thinking about how components, tokens, and patterns get structured so they're legible to AI systems, not just to humans.




QUALIFICATIONS

 - 6+ years of combined design and/or engineering experience, with real depth in both. We care less about your job titles and more about whether you can move fluidly between Figma and code without losing fidelity in either direction.

 - Strong command of Figma at a systems level: component architecture, variants, auto layout, variables and tokens, and library management, not just using components someone else built.

 - Solid front end engineering skills, ideally TypeScript and React, with the ability to build accessible, well tested, production quality components.

 - Experience working with or building design tokens and understanding how they flow from design tool to codebase.

 - A systems mindset. You think in terms of reusable, composable patterns rather than one off solutions, and you can explain the tradeoffs of a system level decision to both designers and engineers.

 - Strong communication skills. You'll be the connective tissue between design and engineering, so you need to be able to advocate for system decisions to both audiences.

 - Comfort with ambiguity. Design systems work means constantly balancing consistency against the need to move fast and support new product surfaces.

 - A genuine interest in where design systems are headed, not just where they are. You should be able to hold the practical reality of today's system alongside a point of view on what it means to build for a future where AI is a first class consumer of your system, not just an afterthought.

 


NICE-TO-HAVES

 - Experience building or contributing to design-to-code sync tooling (Figma plugins, token pipelines, MCP-based workflows, or similar).

 - Familiarity with accessibility standards (WCAG) and how to bake them into components rather than bolt them on.

 - Experience packaging and versioning component libraries for multiple consuming teams (npm scoped packages, semver, changelogs).

 - Exposure to multi-platform design systems work (iOS/SwiftUI, Android/Jetpack Compose, or token build tools like Style

In 2026, we launched Computer, the defining product for the new era of agentic AI. Millions of people now use Perplexity to transform knowledge into action, and every action an agent takes is metered, budgeted, and settled through the billing platform this role owns.

As a monetization engineer at Perplexity, you'll own the abstractions that let product teams ship new SKUs, run pricing experiments, and convert users into paying customers, without needing to understand billing internals. The usage-based billing system this team owns is foundational to Perplexity Computer and our agentic products: metering every agent action in real time, enforcing credit budgets, and settling costs across entirely new interaction models. You'll work across subscriptions, usage-based billing, and enterprise contracts to ensure every revenue path is reliable, observable, and easy to extend.

Tech Stack: Python | Go | Stripe | PostgreSQL | AWS | Docker




WHY PERPLEXITY IS DIFFERENT

 - Craftsmanship. We build high quality, tasteful products targeting both the AI native and AI curious.

 - Ownership. You identify the problem, design the solution and ship it.

 - Entrepreneurship. We think like founders, act with urgency, and hustle to deliver for each other and our users.

 - Scholarship. Work among highly talented peers, pursuing knowledge and truth, upleveling ourselves, our teams, and our products.

 - Partnership. We amplify each others' strengths, break down silos, and give selflessly to help our colleagues deliver excellence.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Design, build, and own the billing platform and monetization systems that power Computer and every paid experience across Perplexity.

 - Lead features end-to-end, from problem definition through technical design, implementation, and launch, including the billing API abstractions that let product teams ship new SKUs, pricing models, and monetization experiments with minimal friction.

 - Build and operate the subscription, invoicing, and usage-based billing systems that serve millions of users across consumer and enterprise plans.

 - Hill-climb on reliability: tiered SLOs organized by customer impact, proactive monitoring, and alerting to catch revenue-affecting issues before customers do.

 - Partner closely with Finance, Data Science, Growth, Security, Support, and go-to-market teams to keep billing data accurate, auditable, and compliant, and to expand payment method coverage and optimize authorization rates globally.

 - Build internal tooling that empowers Support and Finance to diagnose and resolve billing issues quickly.


QUALIFICATIONS

 - 4+ years of professional software engineering experience.

 - Direct experience building or scaling billing, payments, subscription, or monetization systems.

 - Deep familiarity with payment processors (Stripe, Square, etc.), including subscriptions, invoicing, disputes, refunds, and webhooks.

 - Demonstrated experience and appetite for building in-house billing solutions that rival leading best-in-class buy options.

 - Strong backend engineering skills in Python with the ability to reason about complex distributed systems.

 - Experience with relational databases (PostgreSQL) and making data-informed decisions to prioritize work.

 - Strong product judgment, you translate user and stakeholder problems into simple, effective technical solutions.

 - Self-motivated with strong ownership instincts, you ship major features ahead of schedule and drive improvements without asking for permission.

 - Track record of cross-functional collaboration with Finance, Support, or Growth stakeholders.

 - Genuine interest and adoption of AI products and willingness to learn quickly.


NICE TO HAVE

 - 2+ years of hands-on experience with the Stripe APIs and SDKs.

 - Experience with usage-based or metered billing models, especially metering agent actions, tokens, or other non-traditional units.

 - Experience with Apple and Google Play in-app purchase billing.

 - Familiarity with growth experimentation and PLG/self-serve SaaS monetization.

 - Experience building platform constructs that support pricing experiments and A/B testing.

 - Full-stack experience (our frontend is Next.js/React/TypeScript).

 - Experience in a regulatory or compliance-heavy billing environment.

 - Time spent at a fast-growing startup or on a high-ownership engineering team.

ddca70d2b1bb.title: Member of Technical Staff (AI Inference Engineer)
ddca70d2b1bb.description:
We build and run the inference engine behind every Perplexity query and deploy dozens of model architectures at scale with tight latency and cost budgets. Our stack is Rust, Python, CUDA, and CuTe DSL - and we need another engineer to join us.




WHAT YOU WILL WORK ON

Examples of real work the team does:

 - New models support. Support transformer-based retrieval, text-generation, and multimodal models in our inference infrastructure, from weight loading, request scheduling and KV-cache management to support in API Gateway.

 - GPU kernels migration to CuTe DSL. Port our in-house CUDA kernels to NVIDIA's CuTe DSL so they run on GB200 today and are portable to Vera Rubin racks tomorrow.

 - Rust-native serving runtime. Develop our internal Rust-based inference server to solve all Python pains and keep up with rapidly growing traffic.

 - Performance optimisation. Profile and fix bottlenecks from network ingress through continuous batching and GPU kernel interleaving.

 - Reliability and observability. Build dashboards, alerts, and automated remediation so we catch regressions before users do. Respond to and learn from production incidents.




WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Deep experience with GPU programming and performance work (CUDA, Triton, CUTLASS, or similar). Any other deep systems programming experience is a plus.

 - You understand modern LLM architectures and are able to bring them up reliably in a production environment.

 - You've built and operated production distributed systems under real load - ideally performance-critical ones.

 - Comfortable working across languages and layers: Rust for the serving runtime, Python for model code, CUDA/CuteDSL for kernels.

 - You own problems end-to-end. You can read a research paper on Monday, write a kernel on Wednesday, and debug a production incident on Friday.

 - Self-directed. You do well in fast-moving environments where the path forward isn't laid out for you.




GOOD IF YOU TOUCHED ANY OF

 - ML compilers and framework internals: PyTorch internals, torch.compile, custom operators.

 - Distributed GPU communication: NCCL, NVLink, InfiniBand, RDMA libraries, model/tensor parallelism.

 - Low-precision inference: INT8/FP8/FP4 quantization, mixed-precision serving.

 - Profiling and debugging tools: Nsight Compute/Systems, CUDA-GDB, PTX/SASS analysis.

 - Container orchestration: Kubernetes, GPU scheduling, autoscaling inference workloads.




QUALIFICATIONS

 - 3+ years of professional software engineering experience with meaningful work on ML inference or high-performance systems.

 - Familiarity with at least one deep learning framework (PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow).

 - Understanding of GPU architectures (memory hierarchy, warp scheduling, tensor cores).

 - Understanding of common LLM architectures and inference optimization techniques (e.g. quantization, speculative decoding, prefill-decode disaggregation).

c2268501fab2.title: Member of Technical Staff (AI Researcher)
c2268501fab2.description:
Perplexity is seeking top-tier AI Research Scientists and Engineers to advance our AI products and capabilities. We're building the future of AI-powered search and agent experiences through our Sonar models, Deep Research Agent, Comet Agent, and Search products. Join us in creating SOTA experiences that handle hundreds of millions of queries and continue to scale rapidly.

Team Structure

Depending on your interests and expertise, you'll work on one of three specialized teams:

1. Core Research Team (Horizontal)

Focus on generating and improving base models that power all our products. This team works on foundational model capabilities, post-training techniques, building RL infra and infrastructure that benefits the entire organization.

2. Agent Products Team (Vertical)

Concentrate on fine-tuning and optimizing models for our Deep Research Agent and Labs/Canvas products. This team bridges research and product, ensuring our agent capabilities deliver exceptional user experiences.

3. Comet Agent Team (Vertical)

Dedicated to developing and enhancing our Comet Agent product. This specialized team focuses on the unique requirements and optimizations needed for Comet's specific use cases.

Responsibilities

Research & Development

 - Post-train SOTA LLMs using the latest supervised and reinforcement learning techniques (SFT/DPO/GRPO)

 - Leverage our rich query/answer dataset to scale model performance across Sonar, Deep Research, Comet, and Search products

 - Stay current with the latest LLM research, especially in model training, optimization, and personalization techniques

 - Implement preference optimization and personalization capabilities to enhance user experience

 - Invent in-house improvements and optimizations to enhance SOTA models

 - Turn research ideas into algorithms and run experiments to launch new models

Infrastructure & Implementation

 - Own full-stack data, training, and evaluation pipelines required for model development

 - Build robust and effective training frameworks (on top of Megatron/PyTorch) for post-training LLMs

 - Implement necessary infrastructure and components to support cutting-edge model training at scale

 - Integrate models seamlessly into our product ecosystem

Collaboration

 - Work closely with engineering teams to integrate models into Perplexity's product suite

 - Collaborate across teams to ensure cohesive AI experiences throughout our platform

 - Partner with product teams to understand user needs and translate them into model improvements

Qualifications

Required

 - Proven experience with large-scale LLMs and Deep Learning systems

 - Strong programming skills in Python/PyTorch; versatility is a plus

 - Experience with post-training techniques and reinforcement learning

 - Self-starter with a willingness to take ownership of tasks

 - Passion for tackling challenging problems

 - Minimum 2-6 years of experience on relevant projects (depending on seniority level)

Nice-to-have

 - PhD in Machine Learning, AI, Systems, or related areas

 - Experience in post-training LLMs with SFT/DPO/GRPO

 - Experience building LLM training frameworks

 - Academic publications and research impact

96bf3d2eecd6.title: Member of Technical Staff (AI Inference Engineer)
96bf3d2eecd6.description:
We are looking for an AI Inference Engineer to join our growing team. We build and run the inference engine behind every Perplexity query and deploy dozens of model architectures at scale with tight latency and cost budgets. Our stack is Rust, Python, CUDA, and CuTe DSL.





RESPONSIBILITIES: 

 - New models support. Support transformer-based retrieval, text-generation, and multimodal models in our inference infrastructure, from weight loading, request scheduling and KV-cache management to support in API Gateway.

 - GPU kernels migration to CuTe DSL. Port our in-house CUDA kernels to NVIDIA's CuTe DSL so they run on GB200 today and are portable to Vera Rubin racks tomorrow.

 - Rust-native serving runtime. Develop our internal Rust-based inference server to solve all Python pains and keep up with rapidly growing traffic.

 - Performance optimisation. Profile and fix bottlenecks from network ingress through continuous batching and GPU kernels interleaving.

 - Reliability and observability. Build dashboards, alerts, and automated remediation so we catch regressions before users do. Respond to and learn from production incidents.


WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR:

 - Deep experience with GPU programming and performance work (CUDA, Triton, CUTLASS, or similar). Any other deep systems programming experience is a plus.

 - You understand modern LLM architectures and are able to bring them up reliably in a production environment.

 - You've built and operated production distributed systems under real load - ideally performance-critical ones.

 - Comfortable working across languages and layers: Rust for the serving runtime, Python for model code, CUDA/CuteDSL for kernels.

 - You own problems end-to-end. You can read a research paper on Monday, write a kernel on Wednesday, and debug a production incident on Friday.

 - Self-directed. You do well in fast-moving environments where the path forward isn't laid out for you.


NICE-TO-HAVE: 

 - ML compilers and framework internals: PyTorch internals, torch.compile, custom operators.

 - Distributed GPU communication: NCCL, NVLink, InfiniBand, RDMA libraries, model/tensor parallelism.

 - Low-precision inference: INT8/FP8/FP4 quantization, mixed-precision serving.

 - Profiling and debugging tools: Nsight Compute/Systems, CUDA-GDB, PTX/SASS analysis.

 - Container orchestration: Kubernetes, GPU scheduling, autoscaling inference workloads.


QUALIFICATIONS:

 - 3+ years of professional software engineering experience with meaningful work on ML inference or high-performance systems.

 - Familiarity with at least one deep learning framework (PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow).

 - Understanding of GPU architectures (memory hierarchy, warp scheduling, tensor cores).

 - Understanding of common LLM architectures and inference optimization techniques (e.g. quantization, speculative decoding, prefill-decode disaggregation).

Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors including experience and expertise.

Equity: In addition to the base salary, equity may be part of the total compensation package.
