362e875964f9.title: Data Center Electrical R&D Engineer
362e875964f9.description:
About the Team

OpenAI, in close collaboration with our capital partners, is building the world’s most advanced AI infrastructure ecosystem. The team defines the technical direction for next-generation data centers and develops the architectures needed to support rapidly evolving AI hardware and workload requirements.

Operating at the intersection of research, engineering, infrastructure, and deployment, the team translates emerging compute requirements into validated electrical designs, reference architectures, prototypes, and scalable infrastructure solutions.

About the Role

We are seeking an experienced Data Center Electrical R&D Engineer to develop and validate next-generation power architectures for high-density AI infrastructure.

This role is focused on research, advanced design, modeling, prototyping, and technical validation rather than ongoing facility operations. You will investigate emerging electrical technologies, develop system-level architectures, and evaluate new approaches to utility integration, power distribution, backup generation, energy storage, controls, and rack-level power delivery.

You will work closely with compute hardware, mechanical, controls, construction, commissioning, operations, and external technology partners. Your work will shape reusable reference designs that can move from concept and simulation through pilot testing and large-scale deployment.

Key Responsibilities

 - Develop advanced electrical architectures for high-density AI data centers, from utility interconnection through rack-level power delivery.

 - Translate evolving compute-platform requirements into electrical capacity, topology, redundancy, power-quality, protection, and control requirements.

 - Create conceptual designs, basis-of-design documents, specifications, one-line diagrams, design standards, and reusable reference architectures.

 - Model electrical-system performance, capacity, efficiency, reliability, fault conditions, transient behavior, and failure scenarios.

 - Evaluate emerging technologies such as medium-voltage distribution, solid-state power conversion, advanced UPS systems, energy storage, alternative generation, and direct-current architectures.

 - Build technical and economic comparisons across competing design approaches, including reliability, efficiency, scalability, cost, constructability, maintainability, and deployment speed.

 - Develop prototypes, test plans, acceptance criteria, and validation frameworks for new electrical technologies and system architectures.

 - Lead laboratory, factory, pilot-site, and field testing to validate design assumptions and identify performance or integration gaps.

 - Partner with mechanical and thermal engineers to optimize power and cooling architectures as an integrated system.

 - Collaborate with AI hardware and compute teams to understand workload behavior, rack density, utilization, power variability, and future platform requirements.

 - Work with controls and software teams to define instrumentation, telemetry, protection, monitoring, and automated-control requirements.

 - Partner with construction, commissioning, and operations teams to ensure new designs can be safely built, tested, operated, and maintained.

 - Engage equipment manufacturers, utilities, engineering consultants, and research partners to evaluate capabilities and accelerate technology development.

 - Investigate system failures and unexpected test results, identify root causes, and translate findings into design improvements.

 - Document validated designs, technical decisions, operating envelopes, lessons learned, and deployment guidance.

 - Provide technical direction and design-review leadership across internal teams and external engineering partners.

Qualifications

 - 10+ years of experience in electrical engineering, power-system design, data-center infrastructure, industrial power, or another critical-infrastructure environment.

 - Deep expertise in electrical power distribution, including medium- and low-voltage systems, substations, transformers, switchgear, protection, UPS systems, generators, and rack-level power delivery.

 - Demonstrated experience developing electrical designs for large, complex, or high-availability facilities.

 - Strong understanding of power-system modeling, short-circuit analysis, load flow, coordination studies, arc-flash analysis, power quality, grounding, and reliability.

 - Experience translating uncertain or evolving technical requirements into testable engineering concepts and system architectures.

 - Experience designing experiments, prototypes, pilots, or validation programs for new equipment or infrastructure technologies.

 - Ability to reason across electrical, mechanical, controls, compute hardware, construction, commissioning, and operational boundaries.

 - Experience evaluating engineering tradeoffs using quantitative analysis, simulation, testing, and field data.

 - Strong technical writing and communication skills, including the ability to explain complex engineering decisions to technical and executive audiences.

 - Experience directing engineering consultants, equipment manufacturers, and external technology partners.

 - Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering or a related engineering discipline.

Preferred Skills

 - Master’s degree or PhD in electrical engineering, power systems, power electronics, energy systems, or a related field.

 - Professional Engineer license or equivalent professional certification.

 - Experience supporting high-density data centers, AI infrastructure, semiconductor manufacturing, advanced industrial facilities, or hyperscale computing environments.

 - Experience with ETAP, SKM, EasyPower, PSCAD, MATLAB/Simulink, or comparable power-system analysis tools.

 - Experience with power electronics, energy storage, microgrids, alternative generation, or advanced grid-interconnection technologies.

 - Familiarity with digital twins, hardware-in-th

93e10a5e5642.title: Applied Data Scientist, Personalization & Machine Learning
93e10a5e5642.description:
About the Team

We work across product, growth, and monetization to help people get more value from OpenAI’s products. We identify opportunities for machine learning, build and test early solutions, and partner with engineering and product to bring successful approaches into production.

About the Role

We’re looking for a data scientist who can enter an unfamiliar product area, find a useful ML application, and turn it into a working product intervention. You will own the work from problem definition and data preparation through modeling, experimentation, and launch evaluation.

Projects will include personalization, next-best-action recommendations, lifecycle management, promotion targeting, and models of retention and customer lifetime value. You will help identify opportunities, build proofs of concept, evaluate, and iterate.

In this role, you will:

 - Identify opportunities with product and business partners, define the decision a model will inform, and prioritize work by user value, feasibility, and expected impact.

 - Build datasets, features, reproducible training workflows, and models. You’ll use a combination of tools appropriate to the task at hand. 

 - Translate predictions into product actions. Design experiments and use causal reasoning to establish whether those actions improve user and business outcomes.

 - Partner with engineers on integration, serving or batch scoring, monitoring, and rollout. Stay involved through launch and iteration.

 - Explain results and limitations clearly, document decisions, and build reusable methods that other teams can adopt.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have built and evaluated applied ML systems that influenced a product or business decision, with clear ownership of the modeling work.

 - Write effective Python and SQL and can investigate imperfect data, debug models, and make pragmatic implementation choices. 

 - Build and schedule production scoring pipelines using dbt, airflow, and flyte.

 - Understand supervised learning, evaluation, experimentation, and the difference between predicting an outcome and changing it.

 - Can scope ambiguous problems, work across disciplines, and explain technical tradeoffs to colleagues with different backgrounds.

 - Are motivated by helping people use AI effectively and by learning unfamiliar product domains.

 - Are excited to take on challenging, impactful ML problems across multiple areas.

 - Have experience with recommendation systems, personalization, growth, retention, lifetime value, or treatment-effect modeling would be useful. We welcome candidates whose relevant experience comes from other domains.

e728c970fd6a.title: Revenue Operations Intern (Winter, 2027)
e728c970fd6a.description:
WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!

Business Need

We are overhauling our Salesforce system, which will require significant updates to the data models and pipelines that support revenue reporting. We also lack scalable visibility into self-serve revenue due to fragmented data sources and manual reporting processes. This role will help build and maintain the data infrastructure and automated reporting needed to support these changes and improve visibility across go-to-market and finance teams.

Role Description

This intern will support Revenue Operations data infrastructure and automation, including data enrichment and management, building and updating data pipelines, and developing automated reporting for go-to-market and finance stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities

 - Support go-to-market reporting, systems, and processes that help teams make data-driven decisions and drive revenue growth.

 - Help maintain and improve data quality across Salesforce and other go-to-market systems.

 - Work with cross-functional teams to bring together customer data across product usage, sales activity, marketing engagement, support, and contract data.

 - Support the development and maintenance of dashboards and reporting for go-to-market and finance leadership.

 - Assist with data pipelines and processes that connect data across Salesforce, BigQuery, and other systems.

 - Help identify opportunities to automate manual reporting and operational processes.

 - Support ad hoc data analysis and operational requests from the Revenue team.

What You Bring

 - Interest in learning about Revenue Operations, data analytics, and how technology companies go to market.

 - Some experience working with data through coursework, internships, projects, or extracurricular activities.

 - Comfort with spreadsheets and a willingness to develop skills in tools such as SQL, Salesforce, BigQuery, Looker, or Tableau.

 - Strong problem-solving ability and an enjoyment of figuring out how data, systems, and processes fit together.

 - Detail orientation and a commitment to data accuracy and quality.

 - Comfort with learning new tools and working across multiple projects.

 - Ability to communicate findings clearly and explain what the data means and why it matters.

Position Details

Duration: 4 months

Start date: January 4

Location: Toronto or New York

4f267972c37c.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Claude is trained and served on hardware in data centers Anthropic operates and in sites partners build and run for us. DCSE secures that footprint: the sites, the hardware moving through them, and the people and vendors who touch it. Security at that scale runs on data, and you'll be the engineer who owns it and the systems that produce it: component-level hardware inventory and chain of custody, fed by software that runs at our sites and on hosts, and continuous control monitoring, with the posture calculations that decide what each site is cleared to run. You set the architecture, agree schemas and interfaces with the teams, operators and vendors that own the sources, build the pipelines, stores and tools, and run what you ship. The goal is security that runs itself: custody, access and evidence verified continuously from records, with tools and AI agents doing the reviews. We favor simple, standard controls and tools that can be verified over elaborate ones. We use Claude throughout our engineering workflow and expect you to as well. You'll work with the rest of DCSE, including the engineers on its security monitoring platform, with Anthropic's compute and data center operations teams, and directly with data center operators, hardware vendors and logistics providers. The role is based in San Francisco, with remote applicants in the US considered, and involves regular travel to data center sites, which are critical infrastructure. 19d491c8ae81.title: Android Engineer, Identity
19d491c8ae81.location: Seattle, WA; San Francisco, CA; New York City, NY
19d491c8ae81.description: Who we are About Stripe Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career. About the team Before Stripe, every growing internet platform needed a payments team. Today, every growing internet platform needs a way to establish trust in its users. Identity verification is a core piece of economic infrastructure for online businesses. Stripe Identity enables businesses to digitally verify their users through identity documents and other signals for fraud prevention, regulatory, and trust and safety use cases. We are building the future of identity verification and trust in the digital economy. The Identity Product Experience team owns Stripe Identity’s mobile SDKs for iOS, Android, and React Native. These SDKs enable businesses to embed secure, high-quality identity-verification experiences directly in their mobile applications. Our work spans mobile user experience, reusable SDK architecture, camera and document-capture experiences, developer experience, security, accessibility, reliability, and integration with Stripe’s backend systems. Why Stripe Identity? Build mobile experiences that help establish trust between businesses and their users. Solve challenging product and technical problems involving mobile platforms, sensitive data, fraud prevention, and global scale. Create SDKs used by developers across industries, including fintech, marketplaces, and online platforms. Help shape the future of digital identity and make verification easier, safer, and more accessible. Our vision is to build the world’s most trusted store of verified identities, enabling frictionless identity verification across Stripe and beyond. We’re looking for engineers who care deeply about mobile craft and the entire user journey. You should enjoy translating complex technical and regulatory requirements into simple, polished experiences; working through ambiguity; and learning new technologies and systems. Join us to build mobile identity-verification experiences that businesses can integrate easily and that their users can trust. What you’ll do Responsibilities As an Android engineer on the Identity team, you will: Design, build, and maintain Stripe Identity’s mobile SDKs and verification experiences across iOS, Android, and React Native. Create intuitive, polished experiences for complex flows such as identity-document and selfie capture, while accounting for accessibility, device capabilities, and varied real-world conditions. Build reliable and extensible SDK APIs and reusable components that make it easy for developers to integrate Stripe Identity into their applications. Work across mobile clients, supporting APIs, and services to deliver features end to end rather than treating the mobile application as an isolated layer. Improve SDK performance, reliability, observability, testing, release processes, and backward compatibility. Make thoughtful architectural decisions that balance user experience, developer experience, security, privacy, and long-term maintainability. Partner closely with product managers, designers, machine-learning engineers, backend engineers, user researchers, and other mobile teams. Work with Stripe users and field teams to understand integration challenges and turn their feedback into product and platform improvements. Help establish and evolve mobile-engineering practices across Identity and Stripe. Operate and maintain the systems and SDKs the team owns, including diagnosing production issues and improving them based on what we learn. Who you are We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement. Minimum requirements 3+ years of professional software-development experience, including meaningful experience building and shipping mobile applications or SDKs. Experience developing for at least one major mobile platform using technologies such as Kotlin or Java for Android. Strong software-design fundamentals and experience creating maintainable APIs, components, or frameworks. Experience delivering mobile functionality beyond an isolated UI layer for example, integrating with APIs and services, handling local state, or working with device capabilities. Experience testing, debugging, monitoring, and improving mobile software in production. Ability to collaborate effectively with engineering, product, design, and other technical and non-technical partners. A demonstrated commitment to building high-quality user and developer experiences. Preferred qualifications Experience building mobile SDKs, shared libraries, or developer-facing APIs used outside your immediate team. Experience with both iOS and Android, or with cross-platform technologies such as React Native or Kotlin Multiplatform. Experience with camera, image-processing, document-capture, biometrics, or other device-integrated mobile experiences. Experience designing mobile software that handles sensitive data and applies security and privacy principles by default. Familiarity with accessibility, internationalization, mobile performance, and unreliable network conditions. Experience with mobile CI, automated testing, release automation, observability, or developer-productivity tooling. Experience contributing to backend APIs or services that support mobile products. Ability to simplify complex requirements and favor durable, scalable solutions. Comfort reasoning clearly and moving with urgency in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment. F

About the Team

The Value Engineer Team helps customers turn frontier AI into real business value. We accelerate adoption of OpenAI technology at scale and guide organizations from initial activation to measurable, organization-wide impact. We partner closely with Sales, Product, Solutions Architecture, and Security to deliver safe and responsible AI transformation. Our work shapes how customers generate and measure tangible outcomes from OpenAI products and creates a repeatable blueprint for successful enterprise launches and expansions.



About the Role

We are hiring a Value Engineer to help articulate and quantify the business value of OpenAI’s technology across Enterprise, Education, and Government customers. In this role, you will help customers and internal teams translate AI adoption into measurable financial and operational impact.



As an early member of the Value Engineering team, you will help define how OpenAI measures and communicates the real-world impact of AI across its customers. You will partner closely with Sales, AI Success Engineers, AI Deployment Engineering, and Product teams to identify high-impact AI use cases and build financial and operational business cases. Your work will directly influence executive alignment, investment decisions, renewals, and long-term expansion.



You will play a key role in helping build and shape the value engineering function from the ground up — developing repeatable frameworks, ROI models, value narratives, dashboards, and collateral that help internal teams and customers understand and measure the impact of AI adoption.



Success in this role is measured by how clearly customers and internal teams can quantify the value of AI, how effectively business cases support adoption and expansion, and how scalable value frameworks become across the GTM organization.



This role is based in San Francisco or New York City and we offer relocation benefits to new employees.



In This Role, You Will

 - Lead business value assessments for our largest deals, working closely with customers to identify key business drivers and quantify the value of OpenAI’s products to support investment decisions

 - Build and maintain standardized ROI, TCO, and value modeling tools for internal and customer use.

 - Lead structured value discovery to identify high-impact use cases and define measurable outcomes.

 - Publish executive-ready business cases that quantify results and strengthen relationships with C-level stakeholders.

 - Codify value frameworks, methodologies, and reusable assets that scale value-based selling across the global GTM organization.

 - Establish baselines, KPIs, and dashboards to track and communicate value delivery.

 - Partner closely with Account Directors and post-sale teams to influence deal strategy, renewals, and expansion opportunities.

 - Contribute to thought leadership on AI-driven business transformation by identifying emerging patterns in how organizations realize value from AI.
   

You Will Thrive in This Role If You

 - Bring 6–10 years of experience in value engineering, management consulting, or adjacent roles.

 - Have strong financial and analytical skills, with experience quantifying and presenting value to executive stakeholders.

 - Demonstrate exceptional executive presence with strong written, verbal, and presentation skills.

 - Have experience working on large-scale AI, cloud, or digital transformation initiatives.

 - Communicate with clarity and confidence across technical and business audiences.

 - Can translate AI capabilities into compelling financial, productivity, and workforce transformation narratives.

 - Enjoy managing multiple complex customers and driving toward concrete, measurable outcomes.

 - Demonstrate humility, curiosity, and a customer-first mindset.

 - Operate with high ownership, urgency, and comfort navigating ambiguity.

 - Are a creative builder who thrives in 0→1 environments and enjoys rolling up your sleeves to balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Physical Engineering team sits within OpenAI’s Enterprise Verticals organization. We’re exploring how frontier AI can help people design, simulate, and build better physical products—shortening development cycles, improving product performance, and expanding what engineering teams can accomplish.

Our initial focus is on mechanical and electrical engineering. We’re building experiences within ChatGPT and integrations with engineering software to help engineers move from early concepts through design, simulation, and preparation for production.

We operate as a small founding team within OpenAI, working directly with customers and closely with research, design, and forward deployed engineers. We learn by building, putting products in users’ hands, and using their feedback to guide our next steps.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Founding Full Stack Software Engineer, you’ll help define and build the product and technical foundations of this new vertical. You’ll work across frontend experiences, backend services, and integrations to bring AI into complex engineering workflows.

You’ll combine strong software engineering fundamentals with product judgment and an eye for intuitive user experiences. Working directly with engineers and design partners, you’ll identify valuable problems, prototype solutions, and develop them into reliable products.

We’re particularly interested in engineers who have built CAD, CAE, simulation, or other engineering design software. You should be comfortable owning work independently, making decisions with incomplete information, and moving between product details and system architecture.

This is an opportunity to shape a new product area from its earliest stages, with significant influence over what we build, how it works, and the team we become.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Build and ship full-stack AI products that help mechanical and electrical engineers work through design and simulation tasks.

 - Own projects from customer discovery and prototyping through production deployment and iteration.

 - Create intuitive interfaces that help users understand, inspect, and refine complex engineering outputs.

 - Develop backend services, APIs, plugins, and integrations that connect OpenAI models with engineering software.

 - Work directly with customers to understand engineering constraints, identify valuable applications, and translate specific needs into broadly useful products.

 - Partner with research, design, platform, and forward deployed engineering teams to bring emerging AI capabilities into practical workflows.

 - Bring strong product instincts and UI judgment, especially for tools that make complex work easier to understand and perform.

 - Enjoy working directly with users and translating their needs into thoughtful product and technical decisions.

 - Can turn an ambiguous opportunity into a clear starting point and a working product.

 - Move quickly, make pragmatic tradeoffs, and stay accountable for quality after launch.

 - Learn unfamiliar tools and domains quickly and communicate clearly across disciplines.

PARTICULARLY RELEVANT EXPERIENCE

e32482383364.title: Product Cost Management Lead - AI Infrastructure
e32482383364.description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization is building the infrastructure foundation for frontier AI systems. The Supply Chain organization enables scalable, resilient, and efficient supply chains across custom silicon, systems, networking, memory, storage, and rack-scale infrastructure.

Our team connects engineering, supplier strategy, manufacturing, planning, deployment, and finance to make hardware cost, supply, and execution tradeoffs clear from early architecture through production and sustaining operations.

About the Role

OpenAI is seeking a Product Cost Management Lead to own the official costed bill of materials (BOM), system and cluster cost and price baseline, and platform-to-platform total cost of ownership (TCO) for our 1P AI infrastructure. You will turn component, system, POD, manufacturing, deployment, DC, service, and lifecycle inputs into a trusted view of product economics that informs technical and business decisions, including transition timing.

You will partner with Engineering, Strategic Sourcing, Manufacturing-partner management, Finance, Planning, Supply Chain Program Management, Operations Program Management, and infrastructure teams to evaluate engineering / design changes, compare alternatives, identify cost-reduction opportunities, and track realized benefits.

This is an individual contributor role with broad cross-functional ownership. The ideal candidate combines hardware cost expertise, rigorous modeling, sound judgment, and the ability to explain complex tradeoffs clearly to engineering, operations, and senior leaders.

In this role, you will:

 - Own the official costed BOM and system/pod roll-up by platform, generation, configuration, build phase, volume, and mix. Maintain version control and traceability to quotes, source owners, assumptions, and engineering revisions.

 - Publish and maintain the system/pod cost and price baseline, reconciling component pricing and manufacturing-partner inputs with approved configurations and planning assumptions.

 - Build platform-to-platform TCO comparisons covering component content, non-recurring engineering, tooling, manufacturing labor and overhead, yield, scrap, test, logistics, deployment, housing and site costs, power and cooling, networking, spares, service, warranty, and lifecycle costs.

 - Partner with housing and site teams to integrate their cost inputs into product economics, documenting scope, timing, allocation assumptions, and gaps so platform comparisons are consistent and avoid double counting.

 - Quantify the cost impact of engineering change orders and notices (ECOs/ECNs), architecture, specification, configuration, and qualification changes before approval. Assess recurring and one-time costs, implementation timing, inventory exposure, and expected benefits.

 - Develop a prioritized cost-reduction, value-engineering, and second-source opportunity funnel with Engineering, Strategic Sourcing, and manufacturing-partner management. Evaluate qualification costs, investment, payback, supply improvements, and execution risk.

 - Analyze actual, forecast, quoted, committed, and purchase-price costs against the baseline. Explain material variances, identify root causes, and track recovery actions with accountable owners and dates.

 - Build sensitivity and scenario analyses for supplier and manufacturing-partner options, capacity, volume and mix, yield, configuration, site, deployment timing, and lifecycle tradeoffs. Present clear recommendations with assumptions, confidence ranges, and decision deadlines.

 - Validate savings and cost avoidance with Finance and accountable source owners. Distinguish identified opportunities, approved actions, and realized benefits, including offsets and implementation costs.

 - Establish cost-data definitions, BOM hierarchy, allocation methods, currency and volume assumptions, refresh expectations, and change-control processes. Flag stale, incomplete, or unsupported inputs before they affect decisions.

 - Lead recurring product-cost and TCO reviews. Publish concise cost bridges, opportunity updates, risks, and decision packages while retaining the supporting detail needed for technical and financial review.

 - Build scalable models, reporting, and data workflows that improve baseline completeness, refresh speed, analysis turnaround, and decision quality as the hardware portfolio grows.

 - You will own integrated product economics and the cost-analysis methodology and the cost analysis itself. Our redesigned fuel cell is more compact, has higher power density and costs less to produce. We build high-performance, cost-effective fuel cell solutions to help address climate change and the move toward decentralised energy. As Senior Stack Scientist, you will own the scientific understanding of how our stacks perform and age. You will connect cell-level electrochemistry with stack-level design, operating conditions and manufacturing, and turn that understanding into stacks with higher power density, longer life and repeatable performance. Key Responsibilities Lead stack-level performance and durability investigations, from short stacks to full-size stacks. 0a3637669e07.description: P-1625 Important Notes: This is a hybrid role and requires ~3 days in the office in São Paulo-SP. Our office is in Av Faria Lima. Please, submit your application and resume in English. Mission As a Staff Data & AI Technical Solutions Engineer, you will personally drive and mentor others in producing Data & AI technical solutions for any issues reported by customers - including deep diving into production data pipelines, AI workflows, streaming data ingestion, and more. You have deep expertise in Data & AI architectures, having seen a broad set of use cases and successfully maintained complex production environments while adhering to SLA’s. You collaborate effectively with other teams, such as product engineering and customer account teams, to deliver results for customers, especially during critical production downtime situations. You provide customers with the guidance, knowledge, and expertise to build performant architectures and reliable services to achieve their strategic objectives using Databricks’ platform. Reporting to a TSE manager, you are a technical expert within a world-class global support engineering organization, recognized for your leadership, technical depth, and ability to troubleshoot even the most complex customer situations. The impact you will have: Be directly responsible for leading and driving technical solutions for a breadth of complex problems reported by Databricks customers, including escalated and critical scenarios. Deep Dive into code-level analysis and systems architecture of customer workloads to address issues related to Databricks products - including Spark core internals, Spark SQL, Delta, DLT, and Model Serving. Serve as a customer support advisor - be able to diffuse escalations during incidents directly with customer stakeholders, quickly find mitigations and solutions for advanced use cases, and be strategic at helping prevent future customer issues. Help make the Databricks products simpler to use and customer production environments more stable, such as by influencing Engineering and Backline Support teams to identify areas for product improvements. Be known as a deep technical expert and leader in the Databricks platform and productionizing systems, and mentor others in those areas to spread your knowledge. What we look for: Minimum of 8 years of experience in designing, building, testing, and maintaining data pipelines. Relevant past Apache Spark ™ experience is mandatory. Expertise in SQL databases or data warehouses (such as Oracle, Teradata, SQL Server, MySQL) and ETL technologies (such as Informatica, DataStage, Talend, Fivetran). 5 years of hands-on experience in developing two or more Big Data technologies, such as Spark & Hadoop, Lakehouse architecture - such as Delta, Data Ingestion, Data Streaming applications, or ML/AI applications for industry use cases. Prior Support or customer-facing experience is not required for this role, but proven ability to influence cross-functionally is, such as with internal stakeholders or engineering teams. Preferably: Hands-on experience with public cloud (AWS, Azure, or GCP). Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science or related field/experience. Mandatory Bilingual Proficiency (English & Portuguese): Full professional fluency in English is required for daily collaboration with US-based internal teams, alongside full professional fluency in Portuguese to directly support our Brazilian customer base. f3614ddef075.title: Backend Engineer, UI Platform
f3614ddef075.description: Who we are About Stripe Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career. About the team The UI Platform team, known as Sail, builds the foundations behind Stripe’s Dashboard and many other user interfaces. Sail Services owns the systems that evaluate feature flags and experiments, ingest frontend analytics, and improve Dashboard load times for Stripe’s largest merchants. We build backend-for-frontend capabilities that connect Stripe’s backend systems to its UI platform. This gives product teams a consistent way to build and operate user experiences without recreating the same infrastructure. What you’ll do As a Backend Engineer on the Sail Services team, you’ll help build and evolve the systems that power Stripe’s user interfaces. You’ll independently drive software projects from problem definition through production, working closely with other UI Platform engineers, product teams, and infrastructure partners. Your work will range from APIs and GraphQL integrations to edge systems, architectural migrations, and the tooling needed to operate them safely at scale. Responsibilities Take end-to-end ownership of software projects, aligning on priorities and then independently scoping problems and carrying solutions through design, implementation, testing, rollout, and operation Design, build, and operate reliable, scalable APIs and backend systems that support Stripe’s Dashboard, mobile applications, and other user interfaces Help modernize Stripe’s UI architecture through incremental migrations, automated validation, shadow traffic, and carefully controlled production rollouts Improve the reliability, observability, performance, and operability of services on critical user paths Partner with frontend, backend, and infrastructure engineers to understand their needs and turn recurring problems into reusable platform capabilities Use AI-assisted and agentic development workflows to improve implementation, testing, validation, and delivery Contribute thoughtful code reviews, technical discussions, documentation, and runbooks that improve the quality of the team’s work Who you are We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement. Minimum requirements Fluency in using AI-assisted and agentic development tools as part of day-to-day software engineering, including critically reviewing, validating, and improving generated code 2+ years of professional software engineering experience, or equivalent practical experience, building, shipping, and operating production systems Strong knowledge of backend technologies and infrastructure, including the fundamentals of APIs, data storage, distributed systems, and production operations Ability to independently scope and deliver open-ended software projects, making practical technical and product tradeoffs with limited oversight Strong problem-solving and debugging skills, with attention to testing, maintainability, reliability, and user impact Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively with frontend engineers, product engineers, and infrastructure partners Preferred qualifications Experience building backend-for-frontend systems, UI platform services, developer platforms, or shared infrastructure Experience designing or integrating APIs, including GraphQL APIs Experience with high-throughput event ingestion, feature flag or experimentation systems, or other latency-sensitive platform services Familiarity with caching, asynchronous systems, configuration systems, or data-consistency tradeoffs Experience executing large migrations using automated validation, shadow traffic, feature flags, or staged rollouts Experience using data, developer feedback, or operational signals to improve a platform or developer-facing product

af526b1559c9.description: Who we are About Stripe Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career. About the team Brand Studio team works on a variety of brand-centric projects for Stripe, from our brand standards to campaigns, events, IRL experiences, packaging, digital products, and even printed publications. The brand designers on this team are multidisciplinary in nature, able to design robust visual systems, art direction, and craft surfaces that focus on brand and product storytelling. Collaborating with other teams at Stripe, as well as external partners, we raise the quality and consistency of experiences with the Stripe brand IRL, virtually, and everywhere in between. We craft the creative vision and strategy for different types of projects and audiences, and amplify them across various mediums, channels, objects to environments, and digital and physical experiences. About Stripe Creative Lab Stripe Creative Lab aims to create breakthrough, culturally resonant, and exquisitely crafted projects that reveal Stripe’s magic in surprising ways. We dedicate ourselves to meticulously crafting the work to ensure the highest possible creative quality. The work is experimental, often starts with ambiguous briefs and requires finding a way where others might deem it impossible. We are making it up as we go, and that’s the way we love to work. What you’ll do You’ll be joining a highly creative team working across digital experiences, interactive projects, physical installations, experimental technology, and whatever else an idea might require. The work often begins without an obvious technical solution and sometimes without knowing exactly what form the final project should take. As a Design Engineer, you’ll work closely with designers, art directors, and producers to figure out what’s possible, prototype ideas quickly, and turn ambitious creative concepts into working experiences. You’ll bring deep technical expertise in at least one area of creative engineering, alongside the curiosity and technical range to work confidently beyond it. A significant amount of our work lives on the internet, so you should be comfortable independently building and shipping highly crafted digital experiences. Other projects may involve hardware, physical computing, unusual displays, installations, or technical systems we haven’t encountered before. You won’t be expected to be an expert in everything, but you should be excited to learn, experiment, and know when to bring in specialists. Responsibilities Prototype and build highly crafted, experimental digital experiences, interactive projects, and creative tools Work closely with designers and art directors to translate ambitious creative direction into technically excellent experiences, while contributing your own judgment to make the work better Explore emerging technologies and unfamiliar technical approaches, quickly determining what is possible and how best to build it Independently navigate ambiguous technical problems, moving pragmatically from early experiments to finished work Build and publish standalone web experiences when appropriate, while identifying and communicating the additional engineering support required for more complex projects Experiment with hardware, physical computing, displays, sensors, embedded systems, and other technologies when projects call for them Collaborate with external engineers, fabricators, technical studios, and other specialists, contributing enough technical fluency to be an effective creative and engineering partner Maintain a high bar for performance, reliability, usability, and craft without allowing conventional technical approaches to unnecessarily constrain an idea Who you are We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement. You can analyze a vulnerability advisory or proof of concept, reproduce the exploit in a controlled environment, and identify the request characteristics that distinguish exploitation from legitimate traffic. You use SQL to investigate large datasets and a language such as Python, Go, or Rust to build research tools, automate analysis, and validate detections. You make evidence-based tradeoffs between detection coverage, false positives, and performance. You are comfortable investigating ambiguous reports and following issues through to resolution. You work effectively with engineers, product partners, and customer-facing teams, and communicate technical findings clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences. You use AI fluently in research and coding workflows and have the judgment to know where it accelerates the work and where its outputs need independent validation. You will collaborate with engineering and research partners to close coverage gaps and continuously improve the quality of our WAF protections. Design, test, and deploy WAF managed rules and exploit signatures, keeping protections effective as applications, exploits, and attacker techniques evolve. Investigate false positives and missed attacks. Analyze customer reports and request telemetry, reproduce issues, and refine detections to improve protection without unnecessarily blocking legitimate traffic. Validate coverage and resistance to bypasses. Use targeted penetration testing, exploit variants, and adversarial testing to identify detection gaps and evaluate proposed mitigations. Automate research and validation. Build tools and reproducible test cases that accelerate exploit analysis, rule validation, regression testing, and traffic analysis. Measure detection quality. Use SQL, dashboards, and production data to assess rule efficacy, track attack trends, and guide improvements to coverage, false-positive rates, and performance. Collaborate across teams. 51b81b7e141e.description:
About the Team

OpenAI's infrastructure teams design, build, activate, and operate the critical systems that support large-scale AI compute. Field Service Engineering partners across design, construction, commissioning, site operations, hardware operations, and equipment providers to turn complex infrastructure into safe, reliable, and serviceable systems.

About the Role

We are seeking a senior, field service engineer to build the technical operating model responsible for critical electrical and mechanical infrastructure across our data center portfolio. This is a field-oriented electrical & mechanical engineering role, not a traditional facilities operations position. You will combine deep systems understanding in data center power and cooling systems to aid in SOO, design, maintenance & operability, troubleshooting and other engineering related responsibility around key equipment.  The role will include leveraging training and experience to establish standards, develop people, coordinate vendors, and drive issues from design, first principles, first signals through verified resolution. The strongest candidates will have deep expertise in either electrical and mechanical systems and strong working fluency across the other discipline (e.g. controls, business acumen).

Remote - travel 50%

Key Responsibilities

 - Lead field support for startup, commissioning, troubleshooting, repair, and reliability improvement across critical data center infrastructure.

 - Serve as the senior technical owner for transformers, switchgear, UPS systems, generators, PDUs, protection and controls, chillers, cooling towers, pumps, CDUs, CRAH units, and associated control systems.

 - Diagnose complex failures across power, cooling, controls, and hardware interfaces; distinguish symptoms from root causes and drive corrective actions through validation.

 - Build the field service operating model, including staffing recommendations, coverage, escalation paths, response expectations, spare-parts strategy, documentation, and performance metrics.

 - Aid in hiring, development, and coaching other field service engineers and technicians while creating a culture of safety, technical rigor, accountability, and continuous learning.

 - Partner with design, construction, commissioning, site operations, and hardware teams to improve maintainability, readiness, and lifecycle reliability.

 - Manage OEM and service-provider relationships, technical escalations, repair plans, warranties, and sustained corrective action.

 - Establish and improve safe work practices, including lockout/tagout, switching and maintenance procedures, MOPs, SOPs, EOPs, and incident response.

 - Translate field learning into design feedback, preventive maintenance improvements, training, and reusable standards.

Qualifications

 - 8+ years of hands-on experience supporting critical electrical, mechanical, or electromechanical infrastructure in data centers, industrial facilities, utilities, manufacturing, or similarly complex environments.

 - Deep technical expertise in at least one discipline, electrical or mechanical, with demonstrated ability to troubleshoot across electromechanical and controls boundaries.

 - Experience building, leading, or materially developing a field engineering, service, maintenance, or technician team.

 - Demonstrated success leading high-severity troubleshooting, root-cause analysis, corrective action, and reliability improvement.

 - Ability to read and use one-line diagrams, schematics, P&IDs, sequence-of-operations documents, control diagrams, equipment manuals, and commissioning records.

 - Strong safety judgment and experience working under formal energization, isolation, maintenance, and change-control procedures.

 - Clear written and verbal communication with engineers, technicians, vendors, construction teams, and senior stakeholders.

 - Ability to travel up to 50% and support planned or urgent field activity when required.

 - Bachelor's degree in engineering or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred Skills

 - Experience with hyperscale data centers, high-density compute infrastructure, or other mission-critical environments.

 - Experience bringing new sites from construction and commissioning into steady-state operations.

 - Working knowledge of BMS, EPMS, SCADA, PLC, or other infrastructure monitoring and controls platforms.

 - Experience establishing service programs, readiness criteria, technical training, or fleet-wide reliability standards.

 - Relevant electrical, mechanical, HVAC, controls, safety, or trade certifications.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for developers and enterprises who are building AI systems to power magical experiences like content generation, semantic search, RAG, and agents. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. We like to work hard and move fast to do what’s best for our customers.

Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are passionate about their craft. Each person is one of the best in the world at what they do. We believe that a diverse range of perspectives is a requirement for building great products.

Join us on our mission and shape the future!



Why this role?

We are on a mission to build machines that understand the world and make them safely accessible to all. Data quality is foundational to this process. Machines (or Large Language Models to be exact) learn in similar ways to humans - by way of feedback. By labelling, ranking, auditing, and correcting text output, you will improve Large Language Model’s performance for iterations to come, thus having a lasting impact on Cohere’s tech.


Cohere seeks dynamic and dedicated Data Annotators with exceptional Modern Standard German Writing, Translation, and Data Manipulation skill.



Please Note: This is a part-time independent contractor position available within Canada. We seek candidates who are able to commit to 16 hours per week minimum at a 30 CAD/hour contract rate. This role is BYOD 💻 - Bring Your Own Device (laptop). Remote work within Canada. 12 months contract. Performance incentives included!



As a Data Annotation Specialist, you will:

 - Label and Rank: Accurately label and rank machine learning data with advanced proficiency in German, ensuring data integrity and quality.

 - Audit and Correct: Scrutinize and rectify any inaccuracies in language data (may include text, image, JSON, TSV/CSV, Markdown), maintaining the highest standard of data accuracy.

 - Reading and Text-Based Tasks: Efficiently complete reading and text-based assignments, with high attention to detail.

 - Preference-Based Tasks: Evaluate and complete tasks, assessing which responses in German best conform to project guidelines.

 - Recommend Optimizations: Identify and suggest opportunities for improving data quality and model performance in German language tasks.

 - Provide Feedback: Collaborate and communicate effectively, providing feedback to cross-functional team members, particularly on German language-related matters.

 - Detail-Oriented Execution: Maintain meticulous attention to detail while performing repetitive and precise tasks, particularly when working with language data.



You may be a good fit if you have:

 - Language Proficiency: Native or near-native proficiency in German; excellent command over English.

 - Expert reading and writing skills - which you are ready to prove on our written test.

 - Basic familiarity with JSON/TSV/CSV/Markdown data manipulation.

 - Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy - you’re the type to proofread all of your emails!

 - High tolerance for repetitive and monotonous work.

 - Ability to follow complex instructions, navigate ambiguity and work independently.

 - Superb sense of urgency and time management.

 - Curiosity about technology and a knack for tackling problems in creative ways.

 - A reliable laptop.



The Candidate Journey:
Initial Screening - Once you have submitted your application our Talent Team will review your resume and writing samples.
Virtual Annotation Test -  This assignment will test your written skill through various language-based tasks, such as a a writing sample, interacting with a chat bot, and more.
Video Screen - If selected to move forward, you will have a short video call with a member of our Operations Team!
Offer - Independent Contractor Agreement


As an independent contractor, you maintain control over how you complete your work and may work with multiple clients simultaneously, although we ask you to declare if any of these are with a direct competitor of Cohere and maintain IP confidentiality of the Cohere project. Independent contractors are not eligible for health benefits or other benefits provided to employees. Compensation for services is provided to contractors by contractors invoicing for services provided pursuant to the terms of our agreement with the contractor.

It is important to understand that as an independent contractor, continuous work is not guaranteed. The client-contractor relationship is fundamentally project-based, meaning engagements may be temporary, periodic, or intermittent based on our organizational needs and project availability. As an independent contractor, you should anticipate fluctuations in workflow and therefore compensation for services when Cohere does not require as many hours of services in a week.

Prospective candidates, please be advised: this role involves working with human generated and model generated tasks that may involve exposure to not safe for work (NSFW) text content as part of data annotation tasks, including explicit, offensive, or other inappropriate material.



If some of the above doesn’t line up perfectly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply!

We value and celebrate diversity and strive to create an inclusive work environment for all. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12a6IrLdF3kI2nonKSr4tiFuz18rLQbaeYV-JM9L4o9Q/edit, and we will work together to meet your needs.

The Web team builds cohere.com http://cohere.com, the public face of Cohere. We work with marketing, design, and leadership to ship polished pages quickly: landing experiences, content-driven UI, and the CMS systems behind them.

 - Build and iterate on growth-focused UI: styling, layout, and content-driven pages

 - Improve performance and reliability where it actually moves the needle, not chase tech for its own sake

 - Use AI coding tools every day, while owning what you merge: you should be able to debug, explain, and stand behind the code

 - You’re comfortable with Next.js and a headless CMS like Sanity or ready to ramp up quickly

 - You like partnering with design and marketing, and you leave code a bit clearer than you found it

 - You’re excited to try new tools when they help, and skip them when they don’t

 - You care about the end result for users, not just the framework of the week
   
   

Bonus: Eye for design or motion; a portfolio, GitHub, or shipped marketing work. Familiarity with monorepos (pnpm/Turborepo) or Vercel is a plus.

 - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

 - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.

 - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

 - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.

 - Annual enrichment benefits:
   
   Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.
   
   Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

 - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)

 - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.




HOW AND WHERE WE WORK:

 - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.

 - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.

 - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.

 - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.

47ad19666e38.description: Who we are About Stripe Stripe is a technology company focused on improving the conditions for economic growth and prosperity. We build programmable financial infrastructure, rethinking from first principles how financial services should work, to make it easier and cheaper for any business to start and scale. More than 10 million businesses build on Stripe, spanning the economic frontier—from solo founders to established enterprises—united by a practical focus on growth. The most ambitious companies in the world use Stripe as core infrastructure to grow faster. They process trillions of dollars a year on Stripe, equivalent to around 1.6% of global GDP. While economic growth makes everyone better off, open markets also enable greater variety. When any business can easily serve a global customer base, the quality and diversity of products in the world increase, and craft and creativity are unleashed into the smallest niches. Our own growth is wholly contingent on the success of the businesses building on Stripe. We therefore invest back into our technology at an unusual rate. We make upgrades to our products every single day to deliver compounding gains to our customers. We maintain some of the most reliable APIs on the internet. We build entirely new pieces of financial infrastructure to enable new ideas. And our significant advances in risk and fraud infrastructure over many years are making the internet economy safer and more accessible. Though people at Stripe don’t tend to take themselves seriously, Stripe is a fairly serious place: our customers are depending on us for their livelihoods. We admire ambition, intensity, curiosity, humility, and rigor. The most effective people become knowledgeable about many domains besides their own. Any company is an applied exercise in understanding some aspect of society or the market. In working with so many (especially the new and innovative ones), we think that Stripe is one of the very best places to learn about how the world works. Your role Stripe is large enough that individual products and projects can be rapidly deployed to a meaningful fraction of the world’s businesses, but small enough that individual agency still has outsized impact. Small teams can impact how millions of businesses grow. Right now the global economy is replatforming around AI, creating new opportunities for growth. We’re at the center of this, and we think the best work is still in front of us. To meet this moment, we’re looking for people who move with urgency, like hard problems, and want their work to matter at a time of great change. If that’s you, there’s no better place to build your career. Who you are Ambitious builder: You’re energized by building solutions without clear precedent and solving problems with far-reaching consequences. Successful Stripes are deeply curious, and prefer the joy of discovery to the comfort of certainty. Rigorous thinker: You appreciate that things worth doing are rarely simple. You enjoy working on problems that have never been tackled before. Adaptable problem solver: You adapt quickly and treat obstacles as opportunities. At Stripe we embrace kindness while encouraging Stripes to take measured risks and act boldly, even in the absence of consensus. We believe new programming languages can be learned if the fundamentals and general knowledge are present. Experience from either previous internships or working collaboratively on multi-person coding projects (in a university or professional setting). Ability to operate with high agency in navigating complex technical obstacles independently, knowing precisely when to unblock oneself and when to ask for help.

About the Team

OpenAI’s Compute organization builds the infrastructure that powers frontier AI training and inference. This work brings together commercial, technical, strategy, and operations teams to secure and develop the sites and capacity needed for large-scale compute deployment.

We partner across real estate, power, engineering, legal, finance, and delivery to connect infrastructure needs with viable development opportunities and executable commercial agreements.

About the Role

We’re looking for a commercial real estate (CRE) development professional to help secure land and data-center capacity for OpenAI’s compute infrastructure. This is a combined role spanning land acquisition and development, data-center leasing, and real estate acquisitions. The ideal candidate is particularly strong in land and can also contribute across data-center transactions.

You’ll source and evaluate opportunities, structure and negotiate agreements, and coordinate commercial and technical diligence. Working with legal, finance, engineering, and development partners, you’ll connect transaction decisions with infrastructure requirements and carry opportunities through agreement execution and handoff.

Responsibilities

 - Lead sourcing, evaluation, and commercial execution of land acquisition opportunities for data-center development.

 - Support data-center leasing and real estate acquisitions, working across land and data-center transactions as priorities require.

 - Build relationships with landowners, brokers, developers, and data-center counterparties to source opportunities.

 - Manage the transaction pipeline, keep stakeholders aligned, and resolve issues that affect decisions and execution.

 - Drive transactions through agreement execution and coordinate clear handoffs to the teams responsible for development and delivery.

Qualifications

 - Strong commercial real estate development experience, with depth in land acquisition, site control, and development feasibility.

 - A record of sourcing, structuring, and negotiating complex real estate agreements.

 - Ability to work across land transactions and data-center leasing, with sound judgment about their different commercial and development requirements.

cce20f79fd1c.description:
About the Team

OpenAI's Industrial Compute organization delivers the infrastructure that powers frontier AI models. Within Infrastructure Delivery, we turn engineering concepts into safe, reliable, and operational AI campuses by working across design, construction, utilities, commissioning, operations, and external partners.

The fire protection function establishes the life-safety and property-protection strategy for these campuses. The team connects code requirements and engineering standards to practical design, construction, testing, incident readiness, and long-term operations.

About the Role

We are seeking a Fire Protection Engineer to lead owner-side fire and life-safety engineering across large-scale data center programs. You will establish design criteria, review complex fire protection systems, coordinate with authorities and delivery partners, and ensure that fire and life-safety requirements remain clear from early design through construction, commissioning, and operational handover.

This role requires strong technical judgment across detection, alarm, suppression, smoke control, water supply, emergency response, and code compliance. You will work closely with engineering, construction, safety, security, commissioning, and operations teams to resolve risks quickly without compromising life safety, reliability, or schedule.

Key Responsibilities

 - Develop and maintain fire protection and life-safety design criteria, technical standards, and review requirements for self-build data center campuses.

 - Review fire protection drawings, specifications, code analyses, fire and life-safety narratives, hydraulic calculations, equipment submittals, and sequences of operation across all project phases.

 - Provide owner-side engineering direction for fire detection and alarm, automatic suppression, fire pumps and water storage, smoke control, emergency communication, and related life-safety systems.

 - Integrate fire protection requirements with architectural, structural, electrical, mechanical, controls, security, hardware, and operational systems.

 - Partner with code officials, authorities having jurisdiction, insurers, consultants, contractors, and equipment vendors to resolve code interpretations and approval risks.

 - Support constructability reviews, RFIs, submittals, field inspections, deficiency resolution, and change management during active construction.

 - Define commissioning, integrated-system testing, acceptance, turnover, and operational-readiness criteria for fire and life-safety systems.

 - Assess fire and life-safety risks associated with high-density compute, battery and energy-storage systems, generators and fuel systems, utility infrastructure, cooling systems, hazardous materials, and construction activities.

 - Support incident response, root-cause reviews, corrective actions, and lessons learned, translating operational findings into improved designs and standards.

 - Maintain clear records of design decisions, code positions, approvals, testing results, open risks, and turnover requirements.

 - Travel regularly to project sites to support design reviews, field execution, testing, commissioning, and operational readiness.

Qualifications

 - Bachelor's degree in Fire Protection Engineering or a related engineering discipline, or equivalent practical experience delivering fire and life-safety systems.

 - 8+ years of fire protection engineering experience supporting data centers, industrial facilities, advanced manufacturing, energy infrastructure, or other mission-critical environments.

 - Strong knowledge of applicable building and fire codes and standards, including IBC, IFC, NFPA requirements, and local authority approval processes.

 - Technical depth in fire alarm and detection, water-based suppression, special-hazard suppression, fire pumps and water supply, smoke control, egress, and integrated life-safety systems.

 - Experience reviewing fire protection designs, specifications, hydraulic calculations, equipment submittals, testing procedures, and commissioning results.

 - Demonstrated ability to work with authorities having jurisdiction, engineering consultants, contractors, insurers, vendors, and internal stakeholders.

 - Experience resolving field issues and design changes while maintaining clear code compliance, safety, quality, schedule, and documentation.

 - Strong written and verbal communication, sound engineering judgment, and the ability to create clarity when requirements or ownership are ambiguous.

 - Professional Engineer licensure in Fire Protection Engineering, or the ability to obtain licensure in relevant jurisdictions.

Preferred Skills

 - Experience with hyperscale data centers, high-density compute environments, or global multi-site infrastructure programs.

 - Experience with battery rooms, energy-storage systems, generator plants, fuel systems, high-voltage substations, or other campus utility infrastructure.

 - Familiarity with performance-based design, fire and smoke modeling, quantitative risk assessment, or fire-hazard analysis.

9756e373bb4d.title: Member of Technical Staff (Software Engineer, GPU Cluster Infrastructure)
9756e373bb4d.description:
Perplexity serves hundreds of millions of queries a month, and every one of them fans out into multiple AI inference requests running in real time. Behind that sits a large GPU fleet spread across several cloud providers. Today, our inference engineers and researchers build models while also managing networking, securing capacity, and operating the underlying GPU clusters, responsibilities we want a dedicated platform team to own. Your job is to take ownership of that infrastructure and hide its complexity behind a unified, self-serve platform for running training and inference workloads.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Build a self-serve compute platform. Design and own the systems that let inference engineers and researchers launch training jobs and operate inference services without managing GPU provisioning, cluster configuration, or provider-specific infrastructure.

 - Operate the GPU fleet. Own provisioning, lifecycle management, reliability, and capacity integration across providers, giving teams a consistent way to use compute regardless of where it runs.

 - Solve for GPU scarcity. Build the scheduling and placement logic that finds available capacity across providers, packs it efficiently, and gets the right workload onto the right hardware under real constraints.

 - Support two very different workloads. Keep long-running distributed training jobs healthy while simultaneously guaranteeing the availability and latency of production inference services on the same fleet.

 - Own the Kubernetes for GPU orchestration. Write the operators and CRDs, and manage many clusters across providers so the platform behaves the same everywhere we run.

 - Make failure boring. Build the fault tolerance, autoscaling, and observability that keep the fleet utilized and let workloads survive node loss, provider hiccups, and capacity shifts without human intervention.

 - Set technical direction across teams. Partner with inference and cloud infrastructure engineers to turn operational constraints into a coherent platform architecture and roadmap.




QUALIFICATIONS

We expect you to have real depth in most of these:

 - Deep Kubernetes experience — custom operators, CRDs, and multi-cluster federation, not just running kubectl apply.

 - You've managed GPU clusters at scale: NVIDIA hardware, CUDA, and the networking that makes them fast (InfiniBand or RoCE).

 - You've orchestrated compute across multiple clouds (CoreWeave, AWS, GCP, or similar) and understand how different each one really is.

 - Strong distributed systems fundamentals: scheduling, resource allocation, and fault tolerance under load.

 - You write infrastructure and systems-level code in Go, Rust or C++.

 - You've supported both long-running training jobs and high-availability inference services, and you know why they pull infrastructure in opposite directions.

 - You own problems end-to-end and do well when the path forward isn't laid out for you.




ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE WE VALUE

 - Inference serving stacks: vLLM, SGLang, or TensorRT-LLM.

 - Slurm or other HPC schedulers.

 - GPU kernel work in CUDA or Triton — not required, but notable.

 - High-speed interconnects: InfiniBand, RoCE, or RDMA in production.

 - Observability for ML workloads: Prometheus, Grafana, or Weights & Biases.

13abdfefaa96.title: Member of Technical Staff (Site Reliability Engineer, Cloud Infrastructure)
13abdfefaa96.description:
Perplexity serves hundreds of millions of queries a month. Every answer, every Perplexity Computer task, and every enterprise deployment runs on production infrastructure owned by the Cloud Infrastructure team: a fleet of Kubernetes clusters across a multi-account AWS estate, private networks that reach hyperscalers and the neoclouds serving our models, and the storage underneath our user data and agentic workloads. We're looking for SREs who treat reliability as a software problem. You'll own compute, networking, and storage at scale and keep production stable while everything built on top of it is changing fast.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own production at scale. Run the compute, networking, and storage foundation behind Perplexity's consumer, Computer, API, and enterprise products, and own its availability, latency, and cost.

 - Run our Kubernetes fleet. Operate and upgrade the EKS clusters that host web services, search, datastores, and secure sandboxes. Tune scheduling, autoscaling, node lifecycle, DNS, and service networking so clusters stay healthy under bursty, fast-growing load.

 - Engineer the network. Design and operate VPC architectures, Transit Gateway and PrivateLink connectivity, load balancing, DNS, and egress across accounts, regions, and cloud providers.

 - Keep data durable and fast. Own the storage layer (EBS, S3, DynamoDB, and the managed databases and caches our services depend on), including performance, durability, backups, and restores that have actually been tested.

 - Manage everything as code. Run infrastructure through Terraform and CI/CD. Build reusable modules and guardrails, and make every change reviewable, repeatable, and safe to roll back.

 - Prepare for failures. Define SLOs, build alerts that someone can act on, design for zone and regional failure, and run game days and disaster-recovery exercises that prove recovery works.

 - Lead incident response. Be on the critical path when things break. Drive incidents to resolution, write blameless postmortems, and land the fixes so the same failure never pages anyone twice.

 - Scale ahead of demand. Own capacity planning, quotas, reservations, and cost efficiency so product launches and traffic spikes never wait on infrastructure.

 - Automate away the toil. Build tooling, increasingly agent-driven, that turns provisioning, upgrades, and remediation into self-serve, hands-off workflows for every engineering team.




QUALIFICATIONS

We expect you to have real depth in most of these:

 - Deep AWS expertise. You know VPC, IAM, EC2, EKS, ELB, Route 53, S3, EBS, etc. well past the console, including their limits, failure modes, and the bill that comes with them.

 - Production Kubernetes at scale: cluster upgrades, CNI, CoreDNS, autoscalers like Karpenter, and debugging a misbehaving node at 3 a.m. Writing Helm charts alone doesn't count.

 - Terraform mastery. You've designed module structures, managed state across many accounts, and run large refactors and imports without taking production down.

 - Strong networking fundamentals (TCP/IP, DNS, TLS, load balancing, routing).

 - You write real code in Python, Go, or Rust for automation, tooling, and controllers, and you'd rather automate a runbook than follow it.

 - Fluency with observability tools like Datadog, Prometheus, or Grafana, and the judgment to turn metrics, logs, and traces into SLOs and alerts that matter.

 - A track record of leading production incidents and turning root-cause analysis into durable fixes.

 - You own problems end-to-end and do well when the path forward isn't laid out for you.




ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE WE VALUE

 - Multi-region active-active or failover architectures, and disaster-recovery programs with real recovery targets.

 - Proxies, service meshes, and kernel-level networking: Envoy, Istio, Cilium, or eBPF.

 - GitOps and progressive delivery: Argo CD, Flux, or similar.

 - Enterprise and compliance environments: single-tenant or BYOC deployments, KMS/BYOK, SOC 2 or similar controls.

 - Running stateful systems in production: Postgres, Redis, or search engines like Vespa or Elasticsearch.

 - Multi-cloud or neocloud operations (GCP, CoreWeave, or similar).

 - FinOps: cost attribution, Savings Plans and reservations, and making infrastructure cheaper without making it fragile.
