b8586827aa97.description:
About the Team

OpenAI, in close collaboration with our capital and delivery partners, is building the infrastructure required to support frontier AI systems. The Data Center Engineering team defines repeatable technical standards and carries them through design, construction, commissioning, and operational readiness. The team works across data center facilities, power generation, compute infrastructure, construction, procurement, and operations to deliver reliable capacity at unprecedented scale and speed.

About the Role

We are seeking a Power Generation Design Engineer to help design and integrate generation plants and balance-of-plant systems for large AI data center campuses. This role spans electrical and mechanical systems, including generation equipment, campus and grid interfaces, fuel and auxiliary systems, cooling, controls, and data center loads.

The ideal candidate brings deep expertise in either electrical or mechanical engineering, along with the cross-disciplinary judgment to evaluate how the full plant operates as an integrated system. You will establish technical requirements, assess vendor and EPC solutions, resolve design interfaces, and carry systems from concept through commissioning and validated operation.

Travel: 50%

Responsibilities

 - Develop and review generation-plant basis-of-design documents, design criteria, specifications, diagrams, calculations, and reference architectures.

 - Define and coordinate interfaces among generation equipment, substations, campus distribution, grid connections, fuel systems, cooling, controls, and data center loads.

 - Evaluate generation technologies and operating modes, including grid-connected and islanded operation, synchronization, load sharing, black start, and restoration.

 - Lead or review discipline-specific engineering analyses. Electrical studies may include load flow, short circuit, arc flash, protection coordination, transient, grounding, and motor starting. Mechanical analyses may include thermal performance, hydraulics, pressure drop, ventilation, vibration, acoustics, and heat recovery.

 - Review OEM and EPC proposals, equipment ratings and performance data, operating envelopes, failure modes, test plans, maintenance strategies, and lifecycle tradeoffs.

 - Translate data center load profiles and operating requirements into generation-system capacity, redundancy, performance, and control requirements.

 - Coordinate with electrical, mechanical, controls, CSA, fuel, utility, environmental, fire-protection, and data center engineering teams to resolve design and delivery interfaces.

 - Support procurement, factory acceptance testing, construction, startup, energization, commissioning, performance testing, and root-cause investigations.

 - Develop repeatable technical standards and reference designs that improve reliability, maintainability, and deployment speed across future projects.

Qualifications

 - 8+ years of engineering experience in power generation, utilities, industrial systems, microgrids, oil and gas, or mission-critical infrastructure.

 - Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related field.

 - Deep technical expertise in either electrical power systems or mechanical/process systems, with experience collaborating across the other discipline.

 - Electrical expertise may include generators, transformers, HV/MV switchgear, protection and controls, grounding, auxiliary power, grid interconnection, and power-system studies.

 - Mechanical expertise may include rotating equipment, fuel and fluid systems, piping, heat transfer, cooling, ventilation, lubrication, water treatment, exhaust, and mechanical auxiliaries.

 - Experience evaluating OEM data, equipment performance, operating scenarios, failure modes, and maintenance requirements.

 - Experience carrying engineering designs through construction, startup, commissioning, and operational validation.

 - Ability to communicate technical risks and tradeoffs clearly across engineering, vendors, construction, and operations.

Preferred Skills

 - Professional Engineer license.

 - Experience with gas turbines, reciprocating engines, battery systems, combined heat and power, heat recovery, or hybrid generation plants.

 - Familiarity with relevant codes and standards, including NEC, NFPA, IEEE, NERC, ASME, API, ASHRAE, and utility requirements.

 - Proficiency with applicable analysis or modeling tools, such as ETAP, PSCAD, PSS/E, SKM, EasyPower, process simulation, hydraulic modeling, or CFD.

 - Experience supporting high-density data center loads and rapidly changing AI compute demand.

About the Team

The Human Flourishing team’s mission is to ensure AI systems understand and advance human flourishing. As AI becomes more capable and plays a larger role in people’s lives, we want its human benefits to grow with its capabilities. The Human Flourishing team is part of the broader Post Training organization.

Our approach has two parts. Firstly, we measure and improve models’ understanding, capability, and propensity to act according to people’s values and to help them achieve their long-term goals. Secondly, we directly scale tangible impact for users in human domains like education and mental health, working across research, product, and partnerships to increase the benefits over a billion people experience weekly when they use ChatGPT.

Our recent work includes Beneficial RL https://alignment.openai.com/beneficial-rl/, which investigates how training for beneficial behavior generalizes across settings, and MentalHealthBench https://openai.com/index/introducing-mentalhealthbench/, a benchmark developed with mental health experts to evaluate realistic conversations.

About the Role

We’re looking for an exceptional, hands-on researcher to turn difficult-to-define signals of long-term flourishing into measurable improvements in model behavior. You’ll help set research direction, build what is needed to test your ideas, and drive successful work into the models and products we ship.

We’re especially interested in researchers with deep experience improving frontier models through pretraining or reinforcement learning (RL) / post-training, especially on less verifiable problems, or researchers who combine strong LLM skills with deep expertise in domains like education or mental health. Prior experience in these domains is not required.

In this role, you will

 - Develop scalable training methods across the training stack that improve how models understand people’s values, support their agency, and help them achieve long-term goals.

 - Lead high-leverage research from an open question to a shipped improvement: choose a hard-to-define problem, iteratively define success, run experiments, and integrate into frontier models.

 - Build RL environments for difficult-to-verify outcomes, and study whether beneficial behavior generalizes across settings.

 - Create evaluations grounded in human expertise and feedback that reveal capability gaps, unintended incentives in RL, and failures that aggregate scores can miss.

 - Test whether measures of model behavior predict better learning, wellbeing, and other long-term outcomes, and use those findings to guide training.

 - Build new 0→1 capabilities in human domains that may have an increasing impact with upcoming increases in model intelligence and test-time compute.

 - Partner with product teams, engineers, partnerships teams, and domain experts to deploy promising methods, measure their effects in real use, and turn what you learn into further improvements.

 - Assess AI’s impacts on human flourishing at the scale of over a billion users.

You might thrive in this role if you

 - Care deeply about helping AI improve people’s lives, and feel this is a responsibility that comes with increasingly capable models.

 - Have an unusually strong research record in pretraining or RL / post-training research, especially in a hard-to-verify area; or combine strong LLM research skills with deep expertise in education, mental health, or a related field of human benefit.

 - Are a hands-on builder who can turn ideas into rigorous experiments, write and debug code, and work directly with data and training infrastructure.

 - Have the taste to choose consequential problems and actionable steps on the path to solving those problems.

 - Take ownership of ambiguous problems and choose methods based on the impact they can deliver, including when the most useful work is unglamorous.

 - Care about whether a capability will scale, generalize, and make it into the real world—not just whether it can be shown in a paper or prototype.

 - Work well across disciplines and can grok the most important bottlenecks to scaling our impact in a multidisciplinary problem.

If you’re excited about ensuring AI systems advance human flourishing, we’d love to hear from you.

6625f4a0213b.description:
About the Team

Cloud service providers give developers a way to use OpenAI models in the environments where they already build and run software. Our team works with Go-to-Market (GTM), Product, Engineering, and Finance to understand which customers we can reach through these providers and what helps them grow from a first API call to a production workload.

About the Role

In your first few months, you’ll identify a customer segment or workload where OpenAI can grow, recommend an investment to GTM, Product, and Engineering, and define how we’ll know whether it brought new usage to OpenAI. Your first priority will be to explain what drives usage and revenue across providers. You’ll use that understanding to help GTM decide which customers and workloads to invest in and to build forecasts the team can plan against.

A customer might sign a substantial cloud commitment and send very little traffic. You can sit down with the account team, trace the customer’s first requests, and work out whether they need help launching, access to a different model, or more capacity. When you see the same opportunity across customers, your work can change where OpenAI invests.

In This Role, You Will:

 - Build a reliable view of the business from provider usage reports, billing records, and API logs. Show how new workloads, expansion, changes in price, and shifts in model mix contribute to growth.

 - Estimate how much demand cloud distribution adds to OpenAI. Trace customer activity across channels to distinguish new use cases from traffic that moved from the direct API.

 - Identify where customers are ready to scale. Combine what account teams hear with evidence on request failures, latency, and model availability. Work with Product and Engineering on a change and measure what happens to usage.

 - Shape growth plans with GTM and Finance. Estimate what existing workloads and upcoming launches can contribute by year end, test the assumptions that matter most, and recommend where to focus with each provider.

 - Own the consumption forecast. Compare forecasts with actual usage over the same period, explain the biggest misses, and use what you learn to improve the next forecast.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You:

 - Like questions that take you from a conversation with an account team to a query about a single API request. You’re curious about why a customer’s behavior differs from what the numbers first suggest.

 - Are comfortable making a recommendation while some questions are still open. You can tell a sales leader where you’d invest and explain to an engineer what evidence would change your mind.

Qualifications

 - Experience independently leading data science work on a product, growth, or commercial question that changed a business decision.

 - Strong SQL and Python skills. You can join incomplete datasets, choose the right unit of analysis, and validate an aggregate result against individual customers or workloads.

 - Experience using cohorts, experiments, or observational comparisons to assess what drove a change. You can explain how customer selection affects the conclusion and evaluate a forecast against a simple baseline.

Preferred Qualifications

 - Experience with API platforms, cloud marketplaces, enterprise GTM, or a usage-based business.

 - Experience connecting service reliability or capacity to customer adoption, or using demand forecasts to guide a commercial or infrastructure investment.

ae979a817866.description:
WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!

Why this role?

Are you energized by bridging the gap between frontier AI capability and complex customer reality? Do you want to architect high-performance, resilient machine learning systems directly inside strategic enterprise environments? We are looking for a Staff Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) to join our team. The team is responsible for taking our large language models and making them work reliably, securely, and at peak performance within our customers' custom infrastructure and data perimeters.

In this role, you will act as the principal technical translation layer between our core engineering teams and our strategic partners. You will own the architecture for highly ambiguous, customer-specific inference challenges—ranging from multi-tenant model serving to multi-datacenter disaster recovery and custom hardware validation. You will lead technical adoption end-to-end, ensuring our models achieve exceptionally low latency, high throughput, and seamless resilience in the field.



As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you will:

• Embed directly with customer engineering teams to architect the "connective tissue" between our AI models and their live, complex production environments.

• Design advanced model serving topologies, implementing multi-tenant architectures, intelligent model routing, and cross-datacenter failover strategies for multi-cluster environments.

• Optimize "AI-in-a-box" and private deployments, balancing localized SRE constraints like Kubernetes multi-cluster scale with raw model performance.

• Conduct rigorous benchmarking and profiling of customer LLM workloads, root-causing performance degradation (e.g., slow generation) via metrics, dashboards, and distributed logs.

• Accelerate hardware validation, collaborating with clients to run and support Cohere models on next-generation accelerators (GPUs, TPUs, AMD, and custom ASICs).

• Translate complex field friction into platform upgrades, delivering prescriptive feedback and contributing directly back to core product features.

• Ensure Day-1 production reliability, assisting customers in establishing sound deployment patterns, SLOs, and observability frameworks.



You may be a good fit if you have:

• 8+ years of engineering experience running production infrastructure, designing large-scale distributed systems, or deploying enterprise software in complex environments.

• Deep technical depth in production Kubernetes, including orchestration across multi-cluster and hybrid/multi-cloud ecosystems (GCP, Azure, AWS, OCI).

• Strong understanding of LLM architecture and inference dynamics, specifically how attention mechanisms, compute-bound prefill, and memory-bound decode phases dictate live performance.

• Hands-on experience with modern inference engines and optimization stacks (e.g., vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, lmd, or Dynamo).

• Familiarity with distributed serving techniques, such as prefill/decode disaggregated serving, distributed KV caching, and multi-GPU workloads.

• Exceptional customer-facing technical leadership, with a proven track record of scoping highly ambiguous problems and steering executive technical stakeholders.

• The high agency, grit, and adaptability to write same-day production code while managing client-side deployment politics or blockers.

• Strong programming foundations in Python, Go, or C++, comfortable moving fluidly between backend data pipelines and infrastructure layer tuning.






FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS:

 - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

 - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.

 - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

 - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.

 - Annual enrichment benefits:
   
   Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.
   
   Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

 - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)

 - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.




HOW AND WHERE WE WORK:

 - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.

 - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.

 - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.

 - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.
   
   

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply.

104ce9687032.description:
WHO WE ARE

Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents think together https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vkpYpWfEK5s. We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion.



Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work.




ABOUT THE ROLE:

Notion's mission is to make toolmaking ubiquitous—from wikis and documents to notes, tasks, and databases. Strong product intuition and user focus have driven adoption across organizations of all sizes. Millions of users now rely on Notion's building blocks to get work done.



As Notion scales, there's a unique opportunity to build the data foundations that help our product and company reach their full potential. You'll design and build reliable, trusted datasets that accelerate decision-making across product and business functions, directly impacting our roadmap and growth.

NOTE: Although this position is in support of our US Government work, this role is located in Wiesbaden, Germany.
 
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


The Role
 
Forward Deployed Software Engineers (FDSEs) work directly with customers to quickly understand their greatest problems and design and implement solutions to use data against them. Our customers rely on Palantir’s platforms for some of their most critical operations, and projects often start with an open ended question like “Why are we delaying so many flights?” or “How can we better identify instances of money laundering?” As an FDSE, you’ll apply your problem solving ability, creativity, and technical skills to help organizations use their data to drive a real impact in the world. You’ll have the opportunity to gain rare insight into and contribute to some of the world’s most important industries and institutions.
 
As an FDSE your responsibilities look similar to those of a startup CTO: you’ll work in small teams with minimal supervision and own end-to-end execution of high stakes projects. Your day might span discussing architecture with fellow engineers, wrangling massive-scale data, coding a custom web app, speaking with customer executives, or establishing strategy for your team. 
 
Whether you aspire to be an entrepreneur or an engineering leader, we believe Palantir is the best place — with the best colleagues — to learn how. You’ll learn how to unpack a problem and understand the costs and consequences of its solution. You’ll learn new technologies and languages, and even develop them yourself. You’ll work autonomously and make decisions independently, within a community that will support and challenge you as you grow and develop.

Our Principles
Impact: We take on meaningful and challenging projects that change the world for the better. Ownership: We see projects through from beginning to end, working through any obstacles we may encounter. Collaboration: We work internally with people from a variety of backgrounds — such as other FDSEs, product teams, and Deployment Strategists. We also work externally with our customers, often on site, to understand and solve their problems. Trust: We trust each other to effectively manage time and priorities and give people the space to think for themselves. Growth: We encourage ourselves and our peers to seek new challenges and opportunities for growth, as well as find new ways to innovate and share knowledge. Learning: We often face entirely novel problems where we need to pick up a lot of new knowledge and learn how to use it to make progress. We believe experiential learning is one of the best teachers.
What We Value
Strong engineering background, preferred in fields such as Computer Science, Mathematics, Software Engineering, Physics. Experience with logistics, materiel, sustainment, aviation, or readiness analysis is a plus. Familiarity with data structures, storage systems, cloud infrastructure, front-end frameworks, and other technical tools. Understanding of how technical decisions impact the user of what you’re building. Strong coder with demonstrated proficiency in programming languages such as Python, Java, C++, TypeScript/JavaScript, or similar. Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively in teams of technical and non-technical individuals, and comfortable working in a rapidly changing environment with dynamic objectives and iteration with users. Demonstrated ability to continuously learn, work independently, and make decisions with minimal supervision. Willingness and interest to travel as needed.
Requirements
Active US Security Clearance at or above the Secret level.
Salary
 
The estimated salary range for this position is estimated to be $135,000 - $200,000/year. Total compensation for this position may also include Restricted Stock units, sign-on bonus and other potential future incentives. Further note that total compensation for this position will be determined by each individual’s relevant qualifications, work experience, skills, and other factors. This estimate excludes the value of any potential sign-on bonus; the value of any benefits offered; and the potential future value of any long-term incentives.

5a5b43392952.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role As a Senior Engineer on the Life Sciences team, you'll build biology software that our own scientists and the wider research community can depend on, and you'll be one of the main people representing that work to computational biologists outside Anthropic. The Life Sciences team works to accelerate progress in biology with AI, combining frontier models with hands-on computational and experimental research. We want the tools, pipelines, datasets, and benchmarks we build in genomics and structural biology to be useful beyond our own projects, so we plan to release them to the community. Computational biology has a long tradition of open, shared software, and we want to contribute to it well. Every release should be something a researcher can install, run on their own data, and trust: correct on real inputs, validated against reference data and established methods, documented, versioned, and maintained after launch. You'll own that standard. You'll write a large share of the code yourself, decide when something is ready to ship, and stay with it once people start using it. You'll also be an active member of the biology software community: maintaining public repositories, answering issues, speaking at conferences and workshops, and bringing what you hear from researchers back into what we build next. We use Claude and AI coding agents heavily to build software, and we expect you to do the same across design, implementation, testing, and review. Code written by an agent is held to the same standard as code written by hand: you should understand it, test it, and measure its performance before it ships. We're looking for someone with deep software engineering experience who already works this way. The shape of the role is flexible. You might spend most of your time as an individual contributor, or you might lead a small group of engineers and scientists while continuing to contribute directly. Your focus can be genomics, structural biology, or both. Experience in other areas of computational biology is welcome, and we expect the work to range more widely over time. What matters most is a record of biology software that other people have adopted and relied on. This is a chance to shape how AI is put to work in biological research, on problems that matter for human health and scientific understanding. If building software that scientists trust is the work you want to do, we want to hear from you. As a Senior Field Engineer on the Data Center Design and Engineering team, you will work side by side with developers, general contractors and engineers of record to resolve technical issues on site and speed up construction. You will spend most of your time on active sites, acting as our team's eyes, voice and technical judgment in the field. You will spot problems first, get the right people moving, and stay with each issue until it is closed. You don't need a data center background. We care more about whether you have delivered complex industrial projects from the field and can get contractors and partners to act when you have no formal authority over them. What you'll do Be our engineering presence on site. You will walk installed work against the approved design and build working relationships with developers, general contractors, engineers of record, vendors and commissioning teams. You will hold design acceptance on our team's behalf, deciding whether installed work meets the design. When field conditions and drawings disagree, you will be the first call. You will follow up in person, challenge dates that don't hold up, and escalate early with a clear recommendation when something is stuck. Find out why things fail. When equipment, an installation or a test fails, you will gather the evidence, test the first explanation, and trace the failure to its underlying cause. You will confirm that the fix works and check whether other sites carry the same risk. Clear the path to commissioning and handover. You will drive RFIs, deviations and field changes to decisions, so that open engineering questions don't hold up the crews. Bring the field back into the design. You will turn recurring site problems into changes to our designs, standards and audit checklists. Each project should make the next one easier to deliver. 592a921b26da.title: Product Manager Intern (2027) - Austin, TX
592a921b26da.description: About Us At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company. At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in. Available Locations: Austin, TX Available Terms Summer (May - September 2027) About the Role Every product decision we make directly impacts the millions of Internet properties (powering websites, remote teams, APIs, and mobile apps) running on our global network. Cloudflare's network is one of the largest in the world, spanning over 330 cities in more than 125 countries, and operating within 50 milliseconds of 95% of the Internet-connected population globally (for context, the blink of an eye is 300 to 400 milliseconds!). We are passionate about making the Internet more secure, reliable, and faster for everyone. Cloudflare’s Product Management team defines the vision, strategy, and roadmap for the features that power this massive global footprint. Product Managers bridge the gap between user needs, technical feasibility, and business impact by working directly with engineering, design, sales, and marketing to solve complex problems at scale. Whether defining APIs, shaping control plane workflows, or launching new security and performance features, our PMs turn ambitious ideas into intuitive products. The ideal Product Manager Intern is curious, user-focused, and passionate about making the Internet a better place. You won't just shadow team members; you will own product initiatives, gather customer insights, define requirements, and collaborate closely with experienced engineers and designers to ship real features that reach millions of people worldwide. We like to get things done, so we are looking for interns who are proactive, analytical, and eager to drive projects from concept to launch. This is a unique opportunity for aspiring PMs to learn how to manage and scale products at Internet scale. You can check out our internship blogs to learn more about our program and hear directly from our past interns. Responsibilities As a Product Manager Intern, you will be the voice of the user. You will own a project focused on improving our products, enhancing the user experience, and driving the development of key features. Your responsibilities will include: Define the Future: Conduct user research and competitive analysis to understand user needs and market trends. You will identify pain points and uncover opportunities to make our tools best-in-class. Collaborate to Build: Work hand-in-hand with engineering, design, and product leaders to bring your vision to life, ensuring features are built to spec, meet user expectations, and solve hard technical problems at scale. Drive for Impact: Help define success metrics and ensure the features you launch are not only technically sound, but also drive measurable business value and solve real-world problems for our users. Solve Complex Problems: Proactively analyze challenges, balance technical feasibility with user needs, and turn market constraints into opportunities for innovation and growth. Desirable Skills, Knowledge, and Experience: Currently pursuing a degree (Bachelor's or Master's) in Computer Science, Human-Computer Interaction, Business, Engineering, or a related field. A strong passion for technology and a deep empathy for user needs. Technical literacy, with the ability to understand architectural concepts and empathize with developer workflows. Strong analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to articulate complex concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences. A self-starter mindset that thrives in ambiguity and takes initiative. Ability to commit to a full-time (40 hours/week) 12-week internship. In-office expectation of 3–5 days per week in Austin, TX. Bonus Points: Familiarity with networking, security, or Zero Trust concepts (e.g., TCP/IP, HTTP, DNS). Hands-on experience with developer tools, APIs, or personal projects using Cloudflare products (such as Cloudflare for Students ). Previous experience writing product specifications, building wireframes, or conducting user research. Basic coding ability or familiarity with command-line tools and developer workflows. Please Note: We hire interns on a rolling basis until all roles are filled. We are not considering remote or part-time applicants. This is a full-time (40 hours/week) internship with in-person expectations during standard business hours (typically 9:00 AM – 6:00 PM). You should not be enrolled in conflicting classes during the internship term. What Makes Cloudflare Spe

782e6bab0353.description: About Us At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company. At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in. Available Locations: Lisbon, Portugal or London, UK About the Role Cloudflare built its reputation helping build a better Internet, defending millions of sites, giving away SSL and DDoS mitigation when the industry charged premium prices. In an acceleratingly dangerous world, the scope of that mission has changed. We are becoming something more: critical infrastructure. Banks run their payment rails on us. Governments run public services on us. Media companies depend on us during live events. Health systems depend on us to provide care. Reliability for these customers is no longer a feature of our product. It is a mission. Serving that customer base demands a different operating model. Traditional support organizations route tickets. Traditional engineering organizations ship features. Neither alone is enough when the stakes are this high. We are pivoting to something different: a customer-facing engineering organization, directly engaged with our customers at scale. This is work a central dev team cannot do from the inside of the network. The Customer Reliability Engineering function is the spine of that pivot. CRE is SRE applied outward, the same engineering discipline, applied to the reliability of the systems our customers run on Cloudflare. You are the engineer who owns the problems that matter most to the customers who matter most, and you contribute directly to our products and tooling, in partnership with Product Engineering, to hold that standard across the entire customer base. The Role CRE is a rapid response team and a proactive engineering team. You fix things at the edge as they come up, and you help build the product capabilities that identify customer issues before they become a crisis. Both modes are equally core. Rapid response. When a customer issue surfaces that is high-severity, cross-layer and complex, you are the engineer who answers. You reproduce the defect, isolate the root cause across Cloudflare's infrastructure and the customer's stack, drive the fix with Product Engineering, and confirm resolution. You hold on-call for high-severity incidents as part of a global shift rotation. Proactive engineering. When no fire is burning, you work with Product Engineering and our platform teams to build the capabilities that make the next fire cheaper or unnecessary: telemetry pipelines that correlate signals across the customer base, detectors that fire before a human notices, diagnostic tooling that scales across hundreds of customers, automation that reduces toil for Customer Support. Every incident you carry generates engineering output that reduces the cost of recurrence. The work compounds. Cloudflare is building CRE as an AI-native function. You will work with and help build agents and tooling that pre-diagnose incidents, surface relevant logs and configuration, and propose fixes with cited evidence. Engineers who ship AI-assisted diagnostics are the ones defining this discipline. What You Might Work On Rapid response: Own a Sev-1 incident where a large financial services customer sees asymmetric latency from a single POP. Trace it through BGP routing and identify transit provider policy change that is required to resolve. Diagnose a recurring WebSocket disconnect a media customer has been experiencing across multiple release cycles. Isolate it to a specific interaction between a Cloudflare service release and the customer's connection lifecycle. Drive the fix with the owning engineering team. Partner with a government customer's SRE team during an active DDoS event. Help them shape their Magic Transit and WAF configuration in real time. Proactive engineering: Build, with Product Engineering, a distributed tracing capability that correlates Cloudflare edge signals with customer origin metrics so a single query tells the story of a failing request end-to-end. Ship a detector for a class of WAF false positives silently degrading several customers. Get it into production before the next renewal cycle. Prototype an AI agent that takes a new customer case, pulls relevant logs and config, and proposes a root cause with linked evidence. Deploy it internally. Measure whether it makes engineers faster. Iterate. Responsibilities Rapid incident response and root cause analysis. Own the most complex, high-severity customer issues end-to-end, from first signal through confirmed resolution. Lead deep-dive debugging across the full stack: edge, network, DNS, transpor

About the Department Cloudflare’s Customer Support team helps customers resolve complex technical problems and build a better Internet. Within Developer Platform, we work with individual developers, startups, and enterprise engineering teams building production applications on Cloudflare. We bring together technical investigation, thoughtful customer communication, and close collaboration with Product and Engineering to resolve issues and improve the developer experience. About the role As a Technical Support Engineer on our Developer Platform team, you’ll help developers build and run applications on Cloudflare Workers, Workers AI, Durable Objects, R2, D1, Workflows, Pages, Queues, and Workers KV. You’ll investigate platform behavior, replicate reported issues in a test account, guide customers on enabling logs and tracing, and turn findings into clear, practical guidance. You’ll also improve the scripts, documentation, and AI-assisted workflows that help the team solve problems consistently. This role combines hands-on troubleshooting, customer communication, and ownership across a rapidly evolving platform. Responsibilities Own technical support cases from initial investigation through resolution via email, chat, and phone, providing clear next steps, timely follow-up, and empathetic communication. Troubleshoot builds and deployments, runtime errors, resource limits, routing, and bindings to storage, databases, and external APIs. Replicate reported behavior in a sandbox environment, analyze platform logs and request telemetry, and guide customers on enabling observability and tracing to isolate root causes. Partner with Engineering on escalations with clear customer impact, reproduction steps, and diagnostic evidence, keeping customers informed through resolution. Define and update runbooks, AI skills, conversational journeys, and documentation to ensure automated workflows and customer guidance remain accurate and up to date. Use and improve diagnostic scripts, tools, and test examples that help customers and teammates troubleshoot faster. Prioritize concurrent cases by customer impact, provide clear handoffs across time zones, and help identify and communicate recurring issues or incidents. Collaborate with teammates, Product, and Engineering to report reproducible bugs, validate fixes, and improve product reliability and support workflows. Ability to write or modify small scripts in JavaScript, Python, Bash, or a similar language to reproduce issues and inspect API behavior. Excellent written and verbal communication: explain complex findings clearly, ask focused questions, set realistic expectations, and guide customers with different levels of technical expertise. A structured troubleshooting approach: isolate variables, compare environments, and interpret logs, stack traces, and error messages to pinpoint root causes. Strong understanding of HTTP(S), DNS, SSL/TLS, caching, and how web requests flow between clients, edge networks, and origin servers. Familiarity with REST APIs, JSON, authentication headers, and basic SQL queries when investigating application or data issues. Experience supporting or deploying cloud-hosted web applications, including environment configuration, build logs, and runtime errors. b766797162fe.location: San Francisco, CA • New York, NY • United States
b766797162fe.description: Figma is growing our team of passionate creatives and builders on a mission to make design accessible to all. Figma’s platform helps teams bring ideas to life—whether you're brainstorming, creating a prototype, translating designs into code, or iterating with AI. From idea to product, Figma empowers teams to streamline workflows, move faster, and work together in real time from anywhere in the world. If you're excited to shape the future of design and collaboration, join us! As the Engineering Manager for Design Systems, you'll lead the team building the workflows, tools, and quality feedback loops that help customers create design and code that correctly adheres to their design system when working with Figma’s Agents. This work spans context engineering i.e making guidelines, examples, and documentation useful to AI, agent architecture improvements as well as creating datasets, evaluators, and benchmarks that show how well outputs follow a customer's design system. You'll set strategy across these areas, raise the bar on adherence measurement, and turn evaluation results and customer feedback into feedback loops that make design quality better. This is a high-impact opportunity to shape Figma's Agent and improve overall design quality. An organization’s Design System is one of the key differentiators of design quality as we can use it to make agent output adhere to their specific brand, products and design language. We are also aiming to solve Design <> Code parity and minimize drift away from the defined design system in both code and designs. The IP Infrastructure team builds and operates the systems that enable OpenAI to share research and engineering technology securely and reliably with strategic partners. Our work spans continuously running pipelines for model weights, configurations, code, and container images.

We work closely with research, security, developer infrastructure, and partner engineering teams to turn complex requirements into dependable software. We’re a small, collaborative team with direct ownership of systems that support important partnerships.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a software engineer to build and improve the backend services behind these workflows. You’ll work primarily in Python, take projects from design through production, and make our systems more reliable and easier to operate as partner integrations evolve.

The work combines hands-on engineering with careful judgment. You’ll translate requirements about what can be shared into clear, testable business logic, debug problems across system boundaries, and collaborate with the teams that build and use the underlying infrastructure.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week.

83447e93d814.title: Network Infrastructure Engineer, Global Network Infra (WAN)
83447e93d814.description:
About the Team

OpenAI's Global Network Infrastructure team is responsible for building and operating the global network backbone that connects our rapidly expanding compute infrastructure. Our work enables reliable, high-performance connectivity across data centers, cloud service providers, and network points of presence (PoPs), supporting the infrastructure behind OpenAI's research and products.

As OpenAI continues to scale its compute footprint globally, we are expanding our network infrastructure to meet increasing demands for capacity, reliability, and operational efficiency. Our team works across physical network design, carrier connectivity, network deployment, and operational troubleshooting to deliver resilient infrastructure at exceptional scale.

About the Role

We are looking for a hands-on Network Infrastructure Engineer to help design, deploy, activate, and operate OpenAI's global wide area network (WAN) infrastructure.

In this role, you will take direct ownership of bringing new network connectivity online, working closely with fiber providers, cloud service providers, and internal infrastructure teams to establish reliable connectivity across our global backbone.

You will be involved in everything from physical network design and circuit provisioning to troubleshooting complex connectivity issues across Layer 1, Layer 2, and Layer 3. You will play a critical role in expanding our network footprint, bringing new PoPs online, and ensuring that our infrastructure operates reliably as OpenAI continues to grow.

We're looking for engineers who enjoy working close to the infrastructure, thrive on solving difficult networking problems, and bring an automation-first mindset to scaling network operations.

In This Role, You Will:

 - Design, deploy, and support WAN infrastructure across data centers, network PoPs, and cloud connectivity environments.

 - Own the end-to-end activation and turn-up of network circuits, working directly with fiber carriers and cloud service providers to establish and validate connectivity.

 - Troubleshoot complex network issues across physical, Layer 2, and Layer 3 infrastructure, including optical signal problems, FEC errors, routing issues, and connectivity failures.

 - Diagnose and isolate network failures across carrier, cloud provider, and internal infrastructure boundaries, driving issues through resolution.

 - Contribute to physical network infrastructure design, including port mappings, fiber and cable layouts, optical distribution frames (ODFs), and connectivity planning.

 - Monitor network health, circuit utilization, and performance to proactively identify capacity constraints and reliability risks.

 - Build automation and tooling to streamline network provisioning, deployment validation, troubleshooting, and operational workflows.

 - Collaborate with network engineering, data center infrastructure, and external service providers to support the expansion of OpenAI's global backbone.

 - Participate in an on-call rotation to maintain the reliability and availability of critical network infrastructure.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You:

 - Have hands-on experience deploying, activating, and troubleshooting WAN circuits with telecommunications carriers, fiber providers, or cloud service providers.

 - Have a strong understanding of networking fundamentals, including optical networking, Ethernet, TCP/IP, BGP, and Layer 2/3 connectivity.

 - Are comfortable debugging network issues across multiple layers, from physical fiber connectivity and optical errors to routing and traffic forwarding.

 - Have experience working with data center networking, carrier infrastructure, cloud interconnects, or large-scale WAN environments.

 - Understand physical network infrastructure concepts such as fiber cabling, port mappings, optical distribution frames, and network equipment connectivity.

 - Can independently investigate ambiguous connectivity problems, isolate root causes, and work across internal and external teams to restore service.

 - Have experience with scripting or automation tools and are motivated to reduce manual work through repeatable, scalable processes.

 - Enjoy working directly with infrastructure and take pride in owning technical problems from initial deployment through operational resolution.

 - Thrive in a fast-moving environment where infrastructure requirements evolve rapidly and engineering decisions have a direct impact on global scale.

Nice to Have

 - Experience building or operating large-scale backbone networks, hyperscale data center networks, or cloud provider interconnect infrastructure.

 - Familiarity with optical transport technologies, network telemetry, and advanced troubleshooting of physical network links.

 - Experience automating network operations using Python, Go, or infrastructure automation frameworks.

 - Experience deploying new network PoPs or supporting large-scale network expansion projects.

 - Experience collaborating with carriers, colocation providers, and cloud networking teams on complex connectivity deployments.

Why This Role Matters

OpenAI's ability to advance AI research and deliver products at global scale depends on reliable, high-performance infrastructure.

As a member of the Global Network Infrastructure team, you will help build the connectivity foundation supporting some of the world's most demanding compute environments. Your work will directly contribute to expanding OpenAI's global network footprint, bringing critical infrastructure online, and ensuring the reliability of the systems powering frontier AI.

This is an opportunity to work on challenging infrastructure problems, take meaningful ownership of global network deployments, and help shape the next generation of OpenAI's network backbone.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Infranomics team builds the software and data foundations that help OpenAI understand, plan, and improve the economics of its infrastructure. The team works across engineering and finance to make infrastructure spend visible, allocate capacity effectively, and improve efficiency as our products grow.

Our systems support the CPU, network, storage and GPU infrastructure behind products such as ChatGPT, the API, and Codex. We are expanding these foundations to connect resource usage, cost, forecasting, and planning so teams can make better decisions at scale.

 


ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for a Software Engineer to lead the design, implementation, and operation of systems for infrastructure cost and efficiency. You will build the platforms that explain where infrastructure spend goes, identify opportunities to improve utilization, and help teams plan the capacity they need.

We ideally want direct experience building and operating software for infrastructure economics, such as usage metering, cost attribution, resource efficiency, budgeting, forecasting, or capacity planning. You should have owned systems that connect compute, storage, or network consumption to cost and help teams make measurable efficiency and investment decisions.

You will set technical direction for a growing area while staying close to the code. Working with infrastructure engineers, product teams, finance, and leadership, you will turn ambiguous business and engineering problems into reliable software, shared data, and measurable improvements. This role offers substantial autonomy and the opportunity to shape how OpenAI manages its infrastructure investment.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA; Seattle, WA; or New York City, NY. This is an on-site role.

 


IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Define the technical direction and roadmap for infrastructure cost and efficiency systems, and lead projects from problem definition through implementation, adoption, and ongoing operation.

 - Build billing, usage metering, and cost attribution systems that connect infrastructure spend to resources, workloads, services, and the teams that own them.

 - Develop data pipelines and shared data models that combine cloud billing, resource inventory, and utilization signals into a dependable view of cost and capacity.

 - Build tools for budgeting, forecasting, and capacity planning that help teams anticipate demand, allocate resources, and inform procurement decisions.

 - Identify underutilized resources and other sources of waste, then partner with engineering teams to deliver and measure improvements while preserving performance and reliability.

 - Create APIs, reporting tools, and automated controls that help teams understand their consumption, manage budgets, and make informed infrastructure tradeoffs.

 - Provide technical leadership across teams, mentor engineers, and own the correctness, scalability, and production behavior of the systems you build.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have over 7 years of experience designing, building, and operating production software and distributed systems, with technical ownership across multiple teams or a significant infrastructure domain.

 - Have built systems for infrastructure efficiency, cloud cost attribution, usage metering, budgeting, forecasting, or capacity management, and can connect that work to measurable outcomes.

 - Remain a hands-on engineer who can move between architecture, implementation, debugging, and operational improvements.

 - Understand how compute, storage, and networking consumption translate into cost, and can reason about the tradeoffs among utilization, performance, reliability, and growth.

 - Care deeply about data correctness and can build trustworthy systems from complex billing and operational data.

 - Work effectively across engineering, finance, product, and leadership, translating broad goals into a clear plan and driving adoption without relying on formal authority.

 - Thrive with substantial autonomy, take ownership of loosely defined problems, and make pragmatic decisions as requirements evolve.

 - Have experience building internal platforms that give engineering teams visibility into cloud spend, resource utilization, and ownership.

 - Have experience developing batch or streaming data pipelines, financial data platforms, or large-scale analytics systems.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Cloud Infrastructure team builds and operates the infrastructure behind OpenAI’s products, including ChatGPT and the API. Within Cloud Infrastructure, the Traffic team owns how traffic enters our cloud environments, moves between services, clusters, and regions, and reaches external dependencies.

Our work spans cloud networking, Kubernetes networking, ingress and egress gateways, proxies, load balancing, and traffic steering. We build the systems, controls, and observability that make these paths reliable, secure, efficient, and straightforward for other engineering teams to use.

 


ABOUT THE ROLE

You’ll build and operate the networking and traffic infrastructure that connects OpenAI’s products and services across clouds and regions. The team’s work spans L3, L4, and L7—from IP connectivity, NAT, and transport behavior to service proxies and application request routing.

You’ll bring depth in part of this stack and curiosity about how the whole path works. Projects may include building gateways and control planes, improving cross-region connectivity, diagnosing packet loss or connection exhaustion, and making routing changes safer and easier to operate.

This role combines software engineering with production ownership. You’ll turn ambiguous networking problems into durable improvements, working closely with service owners, infrastructure teams, Security, and cloud providers.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA or Seattle, WA.

 


IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Design, build, and operate ingress, egress, and service-to-service connectivity across clusters, regions, and clouds.

 - Develop proxies, gateways, controllers, and automation for routing, load balancing, failover, and traffic management.

 - Build and evolve cloud networking infrastructure, including private connectivity, NAT, and network isolation.

 - Diagnose failures and performance bottlenecks across application, proxy, transport, and cloud networking layers; work with cloud providers when issues extend into their infrastructure.

 - Build telemetry and diagnostic tools that explain traffic paths, identify failing components, and help engineers take effective action.

 - Partner with Security to implement and validate traffic-path protections, including secure service communication, access controls, egress restrictions, and DDoS defenses.

 - Improve latency, throughput, availability, and network efficiency through measurement, testing, and careful production rollouts.

 - Create clear interfaces and safe defaults for service teams, participate in on-call, and turn operational lessons into changes that prevent recurring failures and reduce manual work.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have 5+ years of experience building production infrastructure or distributed systems, including substantial work on networking or traffic infrastructure.

 - Have depth in one or more areas such as cloud networking, Kubernetes networking, proxies and gateways, service meshes, load balancing, or global traffic routing.

 - Understand networking fundamentals and can reason about how IP routing, TCP/UDP, DNS, NAT, TLS, and HTTP/gRPC affect connectivity and performance.

 - Have hands-on experience building or operating systems such as Envoy, NGINX, Istio, Cilium, or comparable networking infrastructure.

 - Write production software in Go, Rust, C++, Python, or a similar language, and use software and automation to solve operational problems.

 - Can investigate unfamiliar failures using evidence, test hypotheses, and follow problems through to a verified resolution.

 - Take ownership of design, implementation, rollout, and ongoing reliability, and communicate clearly across teams when a problem crosses ownership boundaries.

 - Care about making infrastructure secure and understandable for the engineers who depend on it.

We value deep expertise and the willingness to learn across boundaries. You do not need prior experience with every technology or networking layer listed above.

Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents think together https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vkpYpWfEK5s. We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion.



Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a Business Systems Engineer to own the systems that turn a signed deal into a correct invoice and accurate revenue numbers. You’ll work across our go-to-market and finance stack: CRM, quoting and CPQ, billing, the data warehouse, and the integrations between them. Salesforce is one important part of that stack, not the whole job. This is an engineering role with business ownership: you’ll design how data and money move between Sales, Finance, Billing Ops, and Data teams, build the automation that keeps them in sync, and use AI to remove manual work and surface timely signals to reps and operators. You’ll partner closely with Sales, Deal Desk, Billing Ops, Revenue Accounting, and Data Engineering.

 - By day 90, develop AI-powered and agent-based workflows that reduce manual work for reps, Deal Desk, and Billing Ops while improving the quality of signals available to reps and operators.

 - By the end of your first year, automate billing-critical workflows such as upgrades and prorated refunds, early renewals, true-ups, and credit deferment, with audit trails Finance can trust.

 - By the end of your first year, improve data integrity and reporting through clear data models, deduplication, validation rules, reconciliation, and monitoring—including accurate ARR, pipeline, dashboard, and forecasting infrastructure.

 - Raise the bar for how the team ships and operates: sound access, change management, and release practices; thoughtful documentation and tool decisions; reusable tests, runbooks, code review, and AI-assisted development practices.

 - Strong SQL skills and experience working with a data warehouse such as Snowflake or BigQuery; you design for clean, traceable data and understand how to protect its integrity across systems.

ABOUT US

At LangChain, our mission is to enable every company to own its intelligence. We believe agents will transform how companies operate, and we're building the foundation to make that future possible. Our open-source harnesses and LangSmith platform give developers and enterprises the infrastructure to run, improve, and govern agents at scale.

We've raised $460M to date, with our most recent funding round valuing the company at $3B, backed by leading investors including Sequoia, Benchmark, IVP, and CapitalG. As we continue to expand our platform and tackle some of the hardest challenges in agent engineering, every team member has the opportunity to make a meaningful impact and help shape both our technology and the future of the industry.

More than 7,000 organizations rely on LangSmith, from fast-growing startups to Fortune 500 enterprises, including NVIDIA, Bridgewater, LinkedIn, Workday, and Rippling. We're just getting started on making high-performing agents easier to build and manage at scale.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re hiring a Technical Support Engineer to lead our customer support experience for highly technical users, from AI engineers to infrastructure architects. You’ll be on the front lines helping teams debug production LLM applications and agents, improve AI observability and evaluations, and unblock critical issues. You’ll also help define what world-class technical support looks like for modern AI platforms




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Be the go-to escalation point for technical support inquiries—diagnosing issues across customer setup, LangChain products, and deployment issues.

 - Work directly with engineering, operations, documentation, and product teams to resolve bugs, suggest patches, and advocate for customer needs.

 - Partner with Deployed Engineering to support critical enterprise customers.

 - Build and refine internal tooling, diagnostics, and runbooks for complex issue triage.

 - Lead post-mortems for critical incidents and feed learnings back into product and documentation.

 - Help refine KPIs for support health (MTTR, CSAT, bug recurrence) and drive continuous improvement.

 - Improve documentation and knowledge articles to improve 1-to-many resources and provide proactive support.

 - Mentor and coach other support engineers.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - 4+ years in technical support, solutions engineering, or SRE roles in deeply technical B2B environments (e.g., observability, infrastructure, data platforms).

 - Expert troubleshooting skills across APIs, SDKs, distributed systems, and cloud-native stacks.

 - Programming experience with Python. Bonus if you have TypeScript experience.

 - Hands-on knowledge of Kubernetes and Docker

 - Comfort working with logs, traces, metrics in Datadog, and 3rd-party integrations (e.g., OpenTelemetry, LLM providers).

 - Experience supporting enterprise customers and collaborating with engineering on complex escalations.

 - A bias for clarity and continuous improvement: you write succinct, helpful, and accurate responses and build a foundation for case deflection.

 - High ownership — want to do what’s best for the customer and the company and are relentlessly results oriented




COMPENSATION PHILOSOPHY

We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks. 

We are hiring for this role across a range of scope, and the compensation band reflects that. Your offer depends on what we learn about your impact, craft, leadership, and communication during the interview process. We will tell you early where you’re tracking and talk comp with you before offer stage. Team members in the EU, UK, and APAC receive locally competitive benefits aligned with regional norms and regulations.

57126eaab5c0.title: Senior Backend Engineer, Platform (f/m/d)
57126eaab5c0.description: Join Apaleo and shape the future of hospitality tech Apaleo is the world's most open, API-first property management platform, powering the next generation of hospitality operations. Our modular, AI-powered infrastructure lets hoteliers customise their tech stack, automate routine work and deliver seamless, personalised guest experiences, powered by best-in-class apps and autonomous AI agents that adapt to every stay. If you're driven by the idea of making hospitality smarter, more human and powered by cutting-edge technology, we'd love to hear from you. About the role You'll join our Platform team as an individual contributor, working directly with our Platform Lead, who sets Platform's technical direction. Platform owns infrastructure, developer experience and security foundations for the whole engineering organisation. It's a small team, so you'll cover a wide surface area, with no dedicated DevOps or QA function to hand work to. This is a high-ownership seat. You'll take on substantial, ambiguous, cross-cutting initiatives, agree the direction with the Platform Lead, then drive them from first analysis through to completion with real autonomy over how you get there. We don't run a groomed backlog or sprint planning. We assign a significant topic to someone who owns it end to end. If you thrive with structure handed to you, this isn't the role. If you love spotting the problem worth solving and driving it yourself, you'll fit right in. What you'll be up to Designing and building scalable, reliable and maintainable backend systems. Spotting and scoping problems and initiatives yourself, not just picking up assigned tickets: weighing impact, priority and timing. Contributing to architectural decisions and design discussions, and bringing other teams along. Driving substantial, cross-cutting initiatives end to end, coordinating with stakeholders across engineering. Building and maintaining internal tools and infrastructure (AWS, Terraform) that help teams deliver faster and more reliably. Owning observability, logging and operational excellence to keep the platform highly available. Sharing knowledge through code reviews, design reviews and pairing, and helping raise technical standards. Spotting where AI and automation can improve how we build and run software. Some of the challenges waiting for you You'll take ownership of one of these as your first initiative, with no other distractions. Solving horizontal write-scaling for our database. Modernising our CI/CD pipeline for faster, more reliable delivery. Migrating our infrastructure-as-code fully from CloudFormation to Terraform. Extracting and reworking common services to get us ready for our next scale level. What you'll bring to the team 5+ years of backend development experience, with a track record of owning significant technical work from ambiguity through to completion. Substantial hands-on ownership of infrastructure, reliability or performance, ideally on a platform or infrastructure team rather than a pure product team. Strong engineering fundamentals that transfer across languages and cloud platforms. We care more about how you think than which stack you've used. Experience designing and scaling distributed systems in cloud-native environments (AWS preferred; strong Azure fundamentals and genuine enthusiasm for the switch work just as well). Comfort with containerised services and infrastructure-as-code (Docker, Terraform; CloudFormation exposure is relevant given our current stack). Confidence writing your own unit and integration tests, as we don't have a dedicated QA function. A project you can talk about in depth: the problem, what you did and the impact it had. Fluent English. Nice to have Direct experience with C# (.NET), PostgreSQL, AWS and ECS or Kubernetes: a great fit, though not a hard requirement if your fundamentals are strong. Experience setting up infrastructure-as-code from scratch and working with it day to day, ideally with Terraform, including migrating or consolidating from other approaches (like CloudFormation). Experience with Kafka or other event-driven and streaming systems (Azure Service Bus, RabbitMQ or SQS are good transferable equivalents). Experience owning observability and logging for highly available systems. Hands-on use of AI-assisted development tools (GitHub Copilot, Cursor AI, ChatGPT, Amazon CodeWhisperer) and a genuine interest in AI-driven engineering improvement. Experience mentoring other engineers, and introducing new technology, like AI tooling, to other teams. Culture & Growth What We Offer An International Team: Work alongside colleagues from over 20 nationalities. Growth and Development: 360° feedback reviews, an evolving career framework and an annual learning budget of €1,000+. Autonomy and Ownership: Great ideas can come from anywhere. We trust you to make decisions and contribute directly. Real Impact: Join a fast-growing scale-up transforming hospitality. From day one, your work drives real impact. Fair Pay: Competitive salaries guided by benchmarking data, with recognition for performance and contribution. Flexible Work: Work from home, the office or a hybrid mix. We focus on results, not clocking hours. Time Off and Wellbeing: 30 days of vacation and an EGYM Wellpass membership. Free Public Transport: A fully covered Deutschland Ticket for travel across Germany. Team Connection: Regular team dinners, company meetups and offsite events. How you make an impact joining Apaleo: Joining Apaleo is more than taking on a role. It's about driving real change in the hospitality industry. Your contributions will directly shape our innovative platform, influence company-wide decisions and help redefine the future of hospitality tech. At Apaleo, your voice matters, your ideas are valued and your impact is tangible. Be part of a team where your work fuels progress, collaboration sparks innovation and growth is a shared journey. We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity and Affirmative Act

16815bc5b025.title: Senior Systems Software Engineer, GPU Compute
16815bc5b025.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The role

We’re looking for a Senior Software Systems Engineer to join our team and play a key role in the development of our cutting-edge hyperscaler platform. The GPU & InfiniBand team is responsible for enhancing and optimizing the core components of our Cloud platform, with a specific focus on GPU computing, InfiniBand networks, and the KVM/QEMU stack. You’ll work closely with hardware virtualization and device emulation technologies, ensuring high performance and security in multi-GPU, HPC environments. The role involves analyzing, troubleshooting, and improving infrastructure to support new hardware, fine-tuning system performance, and automating fault detection and resolution in a complex system.

In this position, you will be responsible for:

  • Tuning the performance of GPU clusters and InfiniBand networks to ensure optimal operation in HPC and GPU-based environments.
  • Analyzing and troubleshooting the root cause of issues related to GPUs and InfiniBand networks, and proposing corrective actions.
  • Integrating new hardware into the existing infrastructure, including support for new GPU hardware through software stacks like Kubernetes, QEMU, and KVM.
  • Enhancing automation systems for proactive monitoring, detecting, and resolving issues in GPU and InfiniBand environments.
  • Configuring and managing GPU devices and InfiniBand fabrics, ensuring efficient and reliable operation.

We expect you to have:

  • 5+ years of professional experience in system-level software development (focused on performance optimization, low-level programming).
  • 3+ years of hands-on experience with Linux systems (administration, troubleshooting, and performance tuning).
  • In-depth understanding of server architecture, including PCIe devices, NICs, Linux OS/Kernel, and high-performance computing (HPC) systems.
  • Strong proficiency in one or more performance-oriented programming languages (C/C++, Go, Python).

It would be a plus if you have:

  • Experience with GPU end-to-end testing in a cluster environment using InfiniBand networking.
  • Proven track record of analyzing and optimizing the performance of HPC workloads (e.g., simulations, data analysis, AI/ML workloads).
  • Familiarity with RDMA, RoCE, and InfiniBand protocols for high-performance communication.
  • Background in Software-Defined Networking (SDN) and experience with HPC cluster networking.
  • Understanding of QEMU/KVM virtualization and managing virtualized environments.
  • Experience with deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch and TensorFlow, and their integration with HPC systems.
  • Familiarity with collective communication libraries like MPI and NCCL for distributed computing. 

We offer competitive salaries ranging from $170k-$300k + equity based on your experience.

We conduct coding interviews as part of the process.

 

#LI-LH2

  • Competitive compensation
  • Career growth and learning opportunities
  • Flexibility and ownership
  • Collaborative and innovative culture
  • Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects
  • International environment and talented teams

What's it like to work at Nebius:

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI
