de3b49ff8317.title: Full-Stack Software Engineer, Child Safety Tools & Systems
de3b49ff8317.description:
About the Team

The Intelligence & Investigations Engineering team builds systems that detect, analyze, and disrupt abuse across OpenAI’s products. We partner closely with the Child Safety team and cross-functional groups to protect users while advancing OpenAI’s goal of developing AI that benefits everyone.

About the Role

As a Fullstack Engineer focused on child safety, you’ll build data-intensive, AI-powered applications and infrastructure that enable operators and investigators to work effectively and responsibly. You’ll adapt quickly in ambiguous, fast-moving environments to deliver well-crafted, reliable tooling for high-severity safety work.

*Candidates should understand this role involves exposure to sensitive and egregious content.

In this role, you will:

 - 7+ years of experience as a software engineer

 - Prototype, build, and maintain intelligence systems that detect, triage, and enable efficient human review of possible high severity harm

 - Work hand in hand with operators and investigators, designing and delivering systems that enable them to do their work faster, more accurately, and more safely.

 - Develop across the stack: UIs, services, pipelines, and anything else required to solve the problems we face.

 - Interact with partners across Product Policy, Platform Integrity, Safety Systems, and Research

 - Contribute to the team’s technical strategy, especially for child safety related tools and systems

 - Report on impact in a data-driven fashion

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have a strong software engineering foundation and enjoy owning systems end-to-end—from infrastructure and data ingestion to frontend tooling

 - Are energized by working at the frontier of AI capabilities, integrating new models and APIs into practical systems

 - Have experience building and operating large-scale data pipelines or search/retrieval systems

 - Are proficient in Python and/or TypeScript, and familiar with tools like Spark, Kafka, Flink, data warehouses, and SQL

 - Take a product-minded approach, design with user workflows in mind, and iterate quickly based on feedback

 - Favor pragmatic solutions and can ship in hacky, low-support environments when needed

 - Are comfortable navigating ambiguity and open-ended problem spaces with evolving goals

 - Have prior experience working on engineering for high-severity harms

 - Bring intuition for the pain points and workflows of operations and investigative teams, and curiosity about solving complex investigations

 - Bonus: prior knowledge of child-safety-specific challenges such as secure handling of quarantined content and reporting to NCMEC

4b46bf9aed45.title: RTL Design Engineer, Networking / NoC
4b46bf9aed45.description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. The team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform.

About the Role

We’re looking for an RTL Design Engineer to help design and develop next-generation AI accelerator silicon. In this role, you'll work across architecture, microarchitecture, and RTL implementation, translating complex system and performance requirements into efficient, scalable hardware designs.

You'll collaborate closely with silicon architects, hardware and software engineers, verification, and physical design teams to co-design hardware solutions optimized for demanding AI workloads. This is a hands-on engineering role with opportunities to influence architectural decisions, drive microarchitecture development, and own RTL design from early concept through implementation and integration.

We're particularly interested in engineers with experience in Network-on-Chip (NoC), networking, interconnect architectures, or high-performance data movement, though the role encompasses broader RTL design and hardware co-design challenges.

In this role, you will:

 - Design and implement high-performance RTL for next-generation AI accelerator silicon, from microarchitecture definition through implementation and integration.

 - Collaborate with architecture and software teams to translate system-level requirements into efficient hardware microarchitectures.

 - Drive hardware/software co-design efforts to optimize performance, power, area, and scalability for AI workloads.

 - Develop and optimize RTL for complex datapaths, control logic, interconnects, and other critical silicon subsystems.

 - Evaluate architectural and microarchitectural tradeoffs across bandwidth, latency, throughput, and resource utilization.

 - Partner with design verification and formal verification teams to ensure functional correctness, develop verification strategies, and debug complex design issues.

 - Work closely with physical design teams to optimize RTL for synthesis, timing closure, power, and area.

 - Contribute to architecture reviews, design specifications, and cross-functional discussions to influence future silicon designs.

 - Support block-level and SoC-level integration, debugging, and performance optimization.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have strong hands-on experience with ASIC RTL design and microarchitecture development using SystemVerilog or Verilog.

 - Have experience designing and implementing complex digital hardware blocks, from architecture and specification through RTL development and verification.

 - Understand hardware architecture and microarchitecture tradeoffs, including performance, power, area, latency, and throughput.

 - Have experience collaborating across architecture, software, verification, and physical design teams to develop optimized hardware solutions.

 - Can reason about complex hardware systems, identify performance bottlenecks, and translate architectural requirements into efficient RTL implementations.

 - Have experience with synthesis, timing closure, and physical implementation considerations.

 - Enjoy working on ambiguous, technically challenging problems and taking ownership of designs from concept through integration.

 - Bring experience with Network-on-Chip (NoC), networking, interconnect fabrics, packet-based architectures, or high-bandwidth data movement systems.

 - Experience with AI accelerators, high-performance computing, or hardware/software co-design is a plus.

To comply with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidates for this role may need to meet certain legal status requirements as provided in those laws and regulations.

c8da111fec66.description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. Our Scaling Recruiting team helps build the teams behind the data centers that train and run our models. We hire across the full data center lifecycle, from securing land and power to designing electrical and cooling systems, overseeing construction, commissioning facilities, and supporting site operations.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Recruiter to join our Data Center Infrastructure recruiting team. You’ll own searches from intake through offer and start, partnering closely with hiring managers, recruiters, and sourcers across sites and regions. Your portfolio will span specialized technical searches and recurring site-based hiring. You might open an electrical design search, build a local pipeline for construction managers, and close a commissioning lead ahead of a site handover.

In this role, you will:

 - Build relationships with hiring managers before searches open to understand site milestones and anticipate hiring needs.

 - Lead search intake, align on what each hire needs to deliver, and calibrate candidate profiles and interview criteria with the hiring team.

 - Develop and execute sourcing strategies with sourcers and through direct outreach. Map local contractors and project owners for site-based roles and search across regions for specialized talent.

 - Manage multiple searches across sites and reset priorities with hiring managers as build schedules shift. Coordinate interviewer coverage and keep candidates informed.

 - Use pipeline data and candidate feedback to identify bottlenecks, test sourcing assumptions, and keep interviews and debriefs moving.

 - Keep leaders informed about which hires and start dates are on track and where they need to make a decision.

 - Own the candidate relationship from first outreach through start. Set clear expectations about the work and any site, travel, or relocation requirements.

 - Lead closing conversations, bring in the right leaders to answer candidate questions, and coordinate offer approvals and start dates.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - Full-cycle recruiting experience for technical or operational teams, with a track record of supporting multiple hiring managers and balancing specialist searches with recurring hiring across sites.

 - The ability to build trust with hiring managers who work differently, challenge assumptions with market evidence, and bring stakeholders to a decision when priorities compete.

 - Experience building pipelines across multiple geographies and learning unfamiliar technical domains quickly enough to recognize relevant experience beyond job titles.

 - Experience recruiting for data centers or adjacent environments such as energy, construction, advanced manufacturing, or field operations. Data center recruiting experience is a plus, not a requirement.

ed15784cbed1.title: Applied AI Engineering Manager, Startups | Core
ed15784cbed1.description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The Applied AI Engineering team partners closely with customers to help them move from experimentation to production with OpenAI’s technologies. We act as trusted technical advisors, working across customer strategy, architecture, deployment, and adoption to help organizations realize meaningful impact from frontier AI.

The Startups segment serves fast-moving, high-growth companies that are often building new products, workflows, and businesses directly on top of AI. These customers move quickly, operate with high ambiguity, and expect practical, creative, and technically rigorous partnership.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for an Applied AI Engineering Manager, Startups to lead and scale the Startups Applied AI Engineering motion. This team helps high-growth startups move quickly from experimentation to production, unlock meaningful usage, and build durable technical partnerships with OpenAI.

This leader will operate in a high-velocity customer segment where founders, CTOs, and technical teams expect speed, judgment, and hands-on problem-solving. They will balance team leadership, technical depth, customer prioritization, and cross-functional influence across Sales, Product, Engineering, Research, and broader go-to-market teams.

In this role, you will define how OpenAI supports startup customers at scale: identifying where deep technical engagement can unlock outsized impact, building repeatable deployment mechanisms, and ensuring the team can serve a broad and dynamic customer base without losing quality or strategic focus.


IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Craft and continuously refine the strategic vision and operating model for the Startups Applied AI Engineering team, aligning it with OpenAI’s broader company objectives and the evolving needs of high-growth startup customers.

 - Lead, mentor, and grow a team of high-performing technical ICs supporting startup customers across AI-native, developer-led, and product-led companies.

 - Help startups move from early experimentation to production usage by identifying technical blockers, advising on architecture, and driving practical paths to deployment.

 - Partner closely with Sales to determine where technical engagement can accelerate adoption, production usage, and long-term account growth.

 - Represent the technical voice of startup customers by synthesizing high-signal feedback, especially around developer experience, product gaps, deployment blockers, model performance, and emerging use cases.

 - Translate recurring startup needs into repeatable playbooks, starter packs, reference architectures, internal tooling, and customer-facing assets that help the broader team move faster.

 - Serve as a senior technical escalation point for priority startup customers, including founder-, CTO-, and technical executive-level conversations.

 - Balance urgent customer needs with OpenAI’s broader product and platform priorities, especially when startups request niche features, bespoke support, or accelerated roadmap changes.

 - Coach Applied AI Engineers on technical quality, customer judgment, prioritization, executive communication, and cross-functional partnership.

 - Partner across Sales, Product, Engineering, Research, and other GTM teams to improve how OpenAI supports startups from early adoption through scaled production usage.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have proven experience founding, scaling, or operating within early-stage startups, ideally in technical leadership roles where you owned both product or customer outcomes and technical execution.

 - Have a strong track record of building and leading technical, customer-facing teams in high-growth, ambiguous, or startup-heavy environments.

 - Bring strong technical depth across APIs, platform products, AI/ML systems, developer workflows, and production deployment considerations.

 - Have experience creating scalable operating models, not just managing one-off customer escalations.

 - Are comfortable working directly with founders, CTOs, technical executives, and highly technical ICs.

 - Demonstrate strong judgment about when to go deep for a strategic customer versus when to build repeatable mechanisms for the broader segment.

 - Can translate complex technical and product considerations into clear decisions, practical guidance, and customer-facing recommendations.

 - Operate with speed, iteration, and pragmatic customer impact without sacrificing quality, safety, or OpenAI’s long-term platform strategy.

 - Are personally committed to fostering the safe and beneficial development of AI.


SUCCESS WILL BE MEASURED BY:

 - A strong cadence of successful customer sprints and production-oriented technical engagements.

 - Strong Product and Research feedback loops informed by startup customer needs and emerging use cases.

 - Increased startup account usage, including tokens, requests, and production workloads.

 - High-quality customer stories, founder and CTO satisfaction, and referenceable startup wins.

 - Creation of repeatable startup deployment patterns, starter packs, templates, and reference architectures.

 - A healthy, high-performing team with strong prioritization, clear operating mechanisms, and the ability to scale coverage across a high-demand segment.






About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

7232454c8bbd.description: Here at The Exploration Company, we are building spacecraft for humanity. Key Responsibilities In your capacity as a Software Functional System V&V Engineer, your role will be continuously evolving, but day to day your duties will include: Keep a holistic view of the system-level software functional requirements and ensure they are correctly implemented and verified. Decide, per requirement, the right verification level: low-level unit test, SIL scenario, PIL run, HIL run, or vehicle-in-the-loop run. Define, plan, and execute verification campaigns across these levels, and analyse and report the results. Work day to day with the functional chain responsible in each subsystem team to define functional chains, test cases, and required test facilities. Dive into the details when needed: analyse failures in the code and make hands-on adjustments to test scripts, test harnesses, and software, in coordination with the FSW team. Maintain traceability from system requirements to implementation and verification evidence. Review test descriptions, expected inputs and outputs, and verification reports for completeness and correctness. Triage test failures, drive issue resolution with the FSW team, and manage related deviations and waivers. Prepare test readiness and review material, and report verification status to the FSW lead and the Chief Engineer. What we would love to see from you In the role of Software Functional System V&V Engineer, ideally you will have the following: What we would love to see from you Degree in Aerospace, Software, Electrical, or Computer Engineering, or a related field. 5-10 years of experience working on complex space projects, including software verification and validation of embedded, real-time, or safety-critical systems. Hands-on experience with at least two of: SIL, PIL, HIL, or vehicle-level test campaigns. Holistic system thinker who is also ready to go into the code and make adjustments when the details require it. Strong C/C++ reading and debugging skills, plus scripting for test automation (e.g., Python). Solid understanding of spacecraft subsystems and how functional chains span them (e.g., AOCS, power, thermal, propulsion, avionics). Experience with requirements management and traceability tools. Structured, precise, and ownership-driven, with the ability to align multiple subsystem teams. Clear written and verbal communication in English. Nice to have Experience in flight software on spacecraft or launch vehicles. Familiarity with NASA & ECSS standards for space software and verification. Experience operating or setting up SIL, PIL, HIL and/or vehicle-in-the-loop facilities. Why you should join us! What makes us special here at The Exploration Company and why we think you will enjoy working here is: We’re Agile - we make decisions fast whilst keeping our goals and systems in mind We’re Open and Collaborative - we are transparent about risks and obstacles, so that we can cooperate to overcome them We have a lot of Fun - we refuel our energy knowing we are democratising space. 23157f5949c9.description: The AI orchestration of your wildest imagination. n8n is the open workflow orchestration platform built for the new era of AI. Shape review practices, such as PR evidence that shows what changed, what ran, what risks remain and where human judgment is needed. Measure what works Build benchmarks from real historical engineering tasks to evaluate output quality, failure modes, review burden and production risk. Define and track quality and adoption signals, such as reviewer acceptance rate, CI pass rate, rework rate and developer satisfaction. Use data and feedback to change course, retire what doesn't work, and build trust across engineering. Requirements Must-haves 🔥 Frontier obsession: You live at the frontier. You try new models and tools as they land, and you have strong, evidence-backed opinions on what's real and what's hype. 🧭 Staff-scope ownership: You’ve led complex platform, DevEx or engineering productivity initiatives across teams, from defining the problem to sustained adoption and measurable impact, where there was no established approach to follow. 🤖 Agentic depth: You use coding agents daily as a power user, and you've built infrastructure around them, such as repo context and instructions, tool or MCP integrations, sandboxed execution or agent workflows in CI, that other engineers rely on. 🎯 Product mindset for internal platforms: You treat engineers as your customers. 383065119c40.title: Staff Product Engineer
383065119c40.description: About Parloa Parloa's mission is to make every customer conversation feel effortless for both customers and the companies serving them. As agentic AI accelerates, Parloans are shaping the foundation of a new era in customer experience, one where customer support is no longer transactions, but meaningful exchanges. It is not just a vision; Parloa has powered over ONE BILLION interactions between global enterprise brands and their customers, with companies like Booking.com, HealthEquity, Allianz, SAP, BarmeniaGothaer, and TUI already deploying Parloa at scale. About the role: As a Staff Product Engineer , you will work directly inside our most strategic enterprise customers. You will build the software that makes their AI agents work in production, and be measured by the difference it makes for the customer. Our agents are built by business users in Parloa’s platform, AMP. AMP already comes with a broad library of tools and integrations. Your job is the part AMP does not cover yet for a given customer: the last connection into their systems, or a capability the product does not have. Our customers are large enterprises in financial services, telecom, insurance, travel and retail. For them, a working prototype is where an engagement starts, not where it ends. The work comes in two forms. Some engagements run for years. You stay with the account, deepen its integrations and help it grow into new use cases. Others are short experiments. You test a new idea with a real customer and decide quickly whether it is worth building. At Staff level, you take on the hardest cases of both: accounts where a pilot-grade solution would fail in production, and capabilities nobody at Parloa has built before. Staff means harder problems and more ambiguity, not less hands-on work. On many accounts, you work alongside a Deployment Strategist. Think of the two of you as the account’s leadership team. The Deployment Strategist acts as its CPO and defines what success looks like. You act as its CTO and own the architecture and the build. On accounts without a Deployment Strategist, you own the engineering yourself. Areas of ownership: Lead the hardest engagements. Run complex programmes with several workstreams. Make the architecture decisions that span Parloa’s platform and several parts of the customer’s organization. Build what AMP does not cover yet. Systems of record, telephony and contact-center integrations, state management, data readiness, multi-agent orchestration and retrieval. When the answer is unclear, build a prototype quickly and decide whether it is worth pursuing before Parloa invests a full quarter in it. Own production quality and security. Evals, production readiness, observability and incident playbooks for enterprise-scale traffic. Meet the data handling standards a regulated customer expects, including PII, access control and audit trails. Debug live issues, whether they are technical or caused by model behaviour. Grow the account, and share what belongs in the product. Drive the second use case, the second business unit, the renewal. Set the delivery standard for other engineers on complex accounts. When something you build would help every customer, flag it. That is how Parloa decides what goes into the core product. Mentor other Product Engineers , and take part in interviewing and hiring. Use AI well, and set the standard for it. Decide how AI-assisted work is validated before it reaches a customer’s production traffic. Represent Parloa with senior technical stakeholders. Work directly with the customer’s principal engineers, architects and security leaders. Be the engineer commercial teams bring in when a prospect asks how the solution would work for them. What this role is not: Not running the Parloa platform itself. That is a separate engineering role. The platform is your foundation, and you build what a specific customer needs on top of it. Not agent configuration. Business users design and configure agents in AMP. You build the integrations and capabilities those agents need. Not a people-management role. You are an individual contributor and write and review code every week. OUR TECH STACK: Go, TypeScript, Node.js, Python, FastAPI, frontier LLMs, MCP, Azure, Kubernetes, Docker, Terraform, MongoDB, Redis, Kafka/NATS You will not use all of these, and most engagements add something new. Who you are: 8+ years of professional software development , delivering production systems end to end. Fluent in TypeScript or Python, or able to get there quickly. 5+ years leading the design and architecture of large-scale production systems in customer-facing or enterprise environments, with a focus on reliability, scale and failure modes. Experience leading agentic, spec-driven development in production. You know when a coding agent’s output is wrong and what checks it needs before it ships. 167cabeb1836.description: [OUR MISSION AND CUSTOMERS] We are creating the freedom for SMEs to succeed by delivering Europe's leading finance workspace with banking at its core, augmented by financial tools. We are proud to be rated 4.7 on Trustpilot, based on 60,000 reviews. Our culture puts customer satisfaction at the core of what we do (more about our culture here ). [OUR JOURNEY] Founded in 2016 and launched in 2017 by Alexandre and Steve , Qonto has grown to 1,700 Qontoers serving over 750,000 customers across 8 European countries. We have been profitable since 2023, and we are just getting started. [OUR BELIEFS] We hire for skills and potential. With 80+ nationalities, 45% women, and 56% of women in our leadership team, diversity isn't a program; It's who we are. We've built a discrimination-free hiring process because the best teams are built on merit. [AI AT QONTO] AI is deeply embedded in how we work ( here ) - Every Qontoer gets unlimited access to the best AI tools. We want people who experiment without waiting for permission, push AI beyond the obvious, know when to trust it, and when to question it. Location: You can apply to work at Qonto as long as you're living in (or willing to relocate to) Germany, France, Italy, Serbia, Portugal, or Spain. Join us as a Senior Product Engineer (iOS/Swift) to build the mobile app that 750,000 customers across Europe use to run their business finances every day, and to keep it fast and reliable as it grows. Impact: Your work ships to the customers who use Qonto's iOS app for their daily payments and cash management. You will join one of our squads, each owning a clear product scope. You'll work with a team lead, Product, Design, and Frontend and Backend engineers. Squads have 5 to 10 people. ➡️ What you'll do Own features end to end: Take mobile features from technical design to production, on critical architecture and UI work that customers use daily. Solve real-time challenges: Tackle real-time synchronization issues and lead new initiatives in your squad's scope. Raise quality: Keep the codebase healthy through continuous refactoring, unit tests and snapshot tests. Migrate to SwiftUI: Move screens to SwiftUI (MVVM, async/await) as part of the ongoing migration. Collaborate across disciplines: Work with back-end teams, designers and product managers so the whole team shares one vision. ➡️ What we're looking for iOS expertise: You have proven experience as a native mobile engineer, with strong Swift skills and a deep understanding of the iOS SDK and development lifecycle. You'll use it daily on a 100% Swift app. Quality-driven development: You're committed to best practices such as unit testing (XCTest, FBSnapshots), clean code and SOLID principles. This matters in a codebase with 30,000+ unit tests. Pragmatic problem solving: You deliver tangible value in a fast-moving context, and you pick the simplest solution that works. Collaboration: You communicate clearly in English and work well with technical and non-technical colleagues. Curiosity: You enjoy learning new technologies and use AI tools to raise the bar, not only to go faster. ➡️ What we can offer you A mature, modern codebase: 100% Swift, MVP and Clean Architecture, 35+ independent modules and a centralized design system. New screens use SwiftUI, and 80+ are already migrated. Solid engineering practices: Upfront technical design, team code reviews, 450+ snapshot tests, and CI/CD on GitHub Actions, Bitrise, Firebase Test Lab, Sonar, Fastlane and Tuist. Autonomy inside a clear mission: Each project has one team lead and a clear mission, and your squad decides how it works. We use Kaizen and PDCA to improve together, following the Qonto Way . AI in your daily work: Every engineer gets access to Cursor or Copilot, and LLMs are part of our development workflow. A large mobile community: You'll be part of a 140-strong mobile engineering community within a 500-person Product Engineering department. You get mentorship, Tech Weeklies and Monthlies, and conference opportunities. Read about our mobile performance indicators here . ➡️ Your future manager We hire for several squads and domains, so you'll meet your future team lead during the interview process. They run one clear project mission and hand you full ownership of a product scope. You'll talk to them directly before you decide. [DIVERSITY] At Qonto, we understand that true diversity isn’t just about ticking boxes on a hiring checklist. Apply regardless of the boxes you tick - who knows? You may have the missing piece of the puzzle we’ve been searching for all along. [HIRING PROCESS DURATION] On average, our hiring process lasts 20 working days. More information on our candidate journey here [DATA RETENTION] By applying, you agree that Qonto processes your personal data to assess your application. Your data is kept for up to 2 years in our candidate pool. Read our Privacy Notice for full details. Find Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

c8e08a14844a.description: tonies is the world’s leading interactive audio platform for children, with over 12 million Tonieboxes and 173 million Tonies sold globally. Our intuitive, screen-free system empowers children to learn and play independently in a safe and engaging way. With a presence in over 100 countries and a diverse portfolio of ~1,500 Tonies across multiple languages, we continue to redefine how children experience storytelling and learning. Since our IPO in 2021, our global team of 630+ colleagues is united by a shared mission: shaping the future of play, learning, and imagination. Engineering Manager - Device Plattform (all genders) Your Role & Impact At tonies, we are continuously evolving our device and system architecture to strengthen the foundation for future product experiences. As Engineering Manager for the Device Platform team, you define the system architecture (RTOS, Embedded Linux, Android, or alternatives) and deliver a stable, performant firmware platform that ‘Experience teams’ can build against with confidence. In our JDM setup, the manufacturing partner handles electronics hardware, low-level drivers, BSP, and mechanics, while your team steers platform decisions to ensure a reliable, product-grade system. You will scale our existing core team, primarily through external engineering partners, to drive our platform roadmap. Our device architecture is feature-rich, battery-powered, and connected—requiring expertise in connectivity, sensors, tight power budgets, and real-time requirements. What you'll do Team Leadership & Build-up: Take ownership of the existing team and scale it — largely through external partners — while building a cohesive engineering culture across internal staff, external engineers, and JDM partner engineers. Platform Selection & Architecture: Drive the programme's most consequential technical decision: choosing and validating the system platform based on product requirements, resource constraints, time-to-market, and long-term extensibility. JDM Steering: Act as the engineering counterpart to the JDM on electronics and firmware — defining deliverables, setting quality standards, reviewing hardware designs and drivers, and ensuring BSP drops integrate cleanly. Interfaces & Delivery: Experience teams specify the APIs they need; your team delivers them reliably. You turn every boundary — JDM below, experience teams above — into a testable contract rather than a coordination bottleneck. Leading Through Ambiguity: Requirements will shift, trade-offs will be sharp (performance vs. battery, flexibility vs. time-to-market). You keep the team productive and aligned through that uncertainty. Technical Credibility: Stay close enough to the firmware to challenge architectural choices, evaluate JDM deliveries with authority, and step in on critical problems yourself. Delivery Excellence: Own milestones, JDM integration gates, and release cadence to the experience teams — keeping the programme plannable and on track. Your team's responsibilities Evaluating, selecting, and bringing up the system platform (RTOS, embedded Linux, Android, or hybrid) Owning the firmware stack above the BSP: OS configuration, middleware, system services, power management, connectivity, and security Delivering the APIs specified by experience teams, decoupling feature development from platform internals Steering the JDM on electronics and firmware: specifying deliverables, managing BSP integration, holding quality standards Ensuring platform stability through automated testing, integration gates, and systematic validation of JDM deliveries Contributing to the broader tonies® platform strategy where it makes sense What You Bring Leadership: You have led engineering teams and built or significantly grown at least one. You know how to step into a small team, set direction, and scale it — including sourcing, onboarding, and managing a majority of external engineers alongside a smaller internal core. Leading Across Boundaries: You have run a team where external engineers are the planned model, not a temporary supplement. You know how to create shared standards, retain critical knowledge in-house, and keep partner relationships collaborative. JDM/ODM experience is a strong plus. Deep Embedded Platform Expertise: The core of the role. Years of hands-on experience with embedded system platforms — ideally more than one of RTOS, embedded Linux, or Android — and a well-founded opinion on when each is the right choice. Connected-Device Experience: You have worked on resource-constrained, battery-powered, connected devices. Power management, wireless connectivity, sensor integration, and tight hardware budgets are familiar territory. Architectural Vision: Modular, well-layered systems with clean separation between BSP, platform services, and application layer — so experience teams move fast without destabilising the foundation. The Toolbox: C/C++ is your native language. At home in Linux, comfortable with hardware-near debugging (JTAG, logic analysers), Git, GitLab, and CI/CD as daily workflow. Work Style: Pragmatic, technically rigorous, comfortable with ambiguity. You communicate confidently in professional English (German is a plus) and collaborate with your team in a hybrid setup. Last but not least: You are enthusiastic about our product and want to join us on our exciting journey! Why Join Us? Global Teamwork : We collaborate across departmental and country borders. 28f8d17e020c.title: Technical Support Engineer - Healthcare IT/Telematikinfrastruktur (x/f/m)
28f8d17e020c.description: Gemeinsam gestalten wir die Gesundheitsversorgung der Zukunft Du hast ein starkes technisches Wissen und Lust, Dich tief in die deutsche Healthcare-IT einzuarbeiten? Dann bist Du hier richtig. Im Technical Services arbeitest Du an der Schnittstelle zwischen unserer Doctolib-Plattform und der deutschen Healthcare-IT-Landschaft. Du löst komplexe Integrationsprobleme, unterstützt unsere Kund:innen bei technischen Herausforderungen und trägst aktiv dazu bei, dass Doctolib reibungslos in die Infrastruktur unserer Kund:innen integriert ist. Du musst nicht vom ersten Tag an alles wissen. Mit Deinen fundierten Grundlagen und Deiner Motivation, unterstützen wir Dich, Dich in Themen wie die Telematikinfrastruktur und API/Konnektoren, einzuarbeiten. Deine Aufgaben Du bist technische Ansprechperson rund um die Deutsche Telematikinfrastruktur – von der Schnittstellen-Architektur über Kartenverwaltung bis hin zu Gematik-Standards. Kein Tag ist wie der andere. Produkte, die laufen: Du supportest Doctolib-Lösungen rund um die Deutsche Telematikinfrastruktur. und sorgst dafür, dass sie korrekt konfiguriert sind – und wenn doch mal etwas hakt, findest du heraus, warum. Komplexe Probleme, echte Lösungen: Interoperabilitätsprobleme mit Konnektoren und APIs gehören zu deinem Alltag – du arbeitest eng mit IT-Service-Partnern zusammen und bringst auch schwierige Fälle zum Abschluss. Tiefer tauchen, sauber dokumentieren: Du analysierst technische Herausforderungen eigenständig, hältst alles strukturiert in Jira fest und arbeitest direkt mit den Entwicklerteams zusammen, um Fehler nachhaltig zu beheben. KI als Werkzeug, nicht als Buzzword: Du nutzt KI-Tools aktiv, um schneller zu Lösungen zu kommen und Dir fundiertes Wissen aufzubauen – effizient und zielgerichtet. Wissen, das bleibt: Du teilst dein Know-how proaktiv mit internen Teams, damit Probleme gar nicht erst entstehen und unsere Kund:innen das bestmögliche Erlebnis haben. Dein Profil Das solltest du mitbringen: API-Integration und Troubleshooting sind für dich kein Neuland – du hast echte Erfahrung damit, Probleme zu identifizieren und zu lösen. Du kennst dich mit komplexen IT-Infrastrukturen, Netzwerken und sicherheitskritischen Systemen aus – und weißt, worauf es in solchen Umgebungen ankommt. Du kannst technische Sachverhalte so erklären, dass sie ankommen – egal ob du gerade mit einer Entwicklerin oder einer Praxismanagerin sprichst. Deutsch fließend (C1) und Englisch solide (B2) – du bewegst dich in beiden Sprachen sicher. Das ist ein Plus – oder du lernst es bei uns: Kenntnisse rund um die Telematikinfrastruktur, Gematik-Standards oder andere Healthcare-IT-Systeme – wer schon mal mit KIM+, eAU- oder E-Rezept-Workflows gearbeitet hat, ist klar im Vorteil. Erfahrung mit Observability-Tools wie Kibana, Datadog oder Elasticsearch. Ein Abschluss in Informatik, Medizinischer Informatik oder eine vergleichbare Berufserfahrung ist willkommen – aber kein Pflichtfeld. 9a54ff9ebaac.description: Gemeinsam gestalten wir die Gesundheitsversorgung der Zukunft Du hast ein starkes technisches Wissen und Lust, Dich tief in die deutsche Healthcare-IT einzuarbeiten? Dann bist Du hier richtig. Im Technical Services arbeitest Du an der Schnittstelle zwischen unserer Doctolib-Plattform und der deutschen Healthcare-IT-Landschaft. Mit Deinen fundierten Grundlagen und Deiner Motivation, unterstützen wir Dich, Dich in Themen wie die Telematikinfrastruktur und API/Konnektoren, einzuarbeiten. 145076af3564.title: Senior Engineer, Graphics
145076af3564.description:
We are looking for a Senior Graphics Engineer. This role can be based remotely in the UK, Ireland, Portugal, Spain or from our Barcelona hub on a hybrid basis. If you're open to working in any of these locations, there's no need to apply more than once. We'll discuss location preferences during the hiring process. We can support with visa sponsorship from any location.  

We are looking for strong rendering expertise and a passion for delivering high-quality, high-performance visuals. You will work on real-time rendering features and optimizations that help our game look and run its best across a wide range of devices. 

We are in the early stages of development on an ambitious, unannounced, cross-platform Strategy/MMO title, creating a team of talented and passionate game makers to join us on this exciting journey!

At Scopely, we care deeply about what we do and want to inspire play, every day — whether in our work environments alongside our talented colleagues or through our deep connections with our communities of players. We are a global team of game lovers who are developing, publishing, and innovating the mobile games industry, connecting millions of people around the world daily.

What You Will Do

  • Develop and optimize real-time rendering features on mobile platforms using Vulkan (Android) and Metal (iOS).

  • Work with clustered/meshlet-based geometry systems, implementing GPU-driven visibility, culling, and LOD.

  • Integrate and refine modern rendering techniques such as clustered/tiled lighting, temporal anti-aliasing (TAA), and super-resolution (TSR).

  • Assist in the development of real-time global illumination features in collaboration with senior technical staff, ensuring scalability across different device tiers.

  • Write and optimize shaders (HLSL/GLSL/MSL) for power-efficient mobile performance.

  • Profile GPU/CPU performance and analyze rendering bottlenecks using tools like RenderDoc, Perfetto, Xcode GPU Debugger, and Mali/Snapdragon profilers.

  • Contribute to GPU memory layout design, draw submission strategies, and render pass optimizations for tile-based GPUs.

  • Collaborate closely with engine and content teams to ensure visuals meet quality and performance goals across platforms.

  • Stay informed on industry rendering trends and suggest improvements to our pipeline.

What We Are Looking For

  • 5+ years of graphics programming experience, with a focus on mobile platforms.

  • Strong C++ skills with experience working in performance-critical rendering code.

  • Solid knowledge of Vulkan and/or Metal APIs.

  • Experience with Unity’s Scriptable Render Pipeline (SRP), including extending or customizing SRPs.

  • Understanding of mobile GPU architecture (tiling, bandwidth, power constraints).

  • Proficiency in GPU performance profiling and optimization workflows.

  • Familiarity with compute-based rendering techniques, GPU-driven pipelines, and modern culling/visibility approaches.

Bonus Points

  • Experience with UE5’s Nanite/Lumen or equivalent advanced rendering solutions.

  • Background in custom engine development or low-level rendering systems.

  • Contributions to open-source graphics tools or technical publications.

  • Cross-platform rendering experience beyond mobile (PC/console).

 

About Scopely

Scopely is a leading video game and global interactive entertainment company, home to many of the world’s most beloved and enduring experiences, including two of the most successful mobile games of all-time “MONOPOLY GO!” and “Pokémon GO,” along with “Stumble Guys,” “Star Trek™ Fleet Command,” “MARVEL Strike Force,” “WWE Champions,” the Scrabble® franchise, “Yahtzee® With Buddies,” and many others. Across mobile, web, PC, and console, Scopely creates, develops, publishes, and live-operates one of the most diversified and award-winning portfolios in the games industry — bringing hundreds of millions of players together through a shared love of play.

Founded in 2011, Scopely is powered by its exceptional team — including thousands of world-class gamemakers around the globe, a distinctive tenet-driven culture, and its proprietary technology platform, Playgami. Together, these strengths have fueled Scopely’s position as the #1 mobile games company in the U.S. and #2 globally, generating more than $10 billion in lifetime revenue. Whether building global sensations like “MONOPOLY GO!” from the ground up, or expanding through strategic acquisitions, including the FoxNext, GSN, and Scopely Explore games businesses — Scopely consistently delivers experiences players love today and return to for years to come.

Recognized multiple times as one of the "100 Most Influential Companies in the World" by TIME magazine and one of Fast Company's "World's Most Innovative Companies" and “Best Workplaces for Innovators,” Scopely believes that video games can be a force for good — creating meaningful connections, vibrant communities, and making life better through play.

Scopely has global operations and partners across four continents in more than a dozen countries worldwide. For more information, visit: https://www.scopely.com/.

2caab749bc21.description:
CSQ327R39

As a Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) for the Emerging Enterprise & Digital Natives business in EMEA. you will work with customers to build and productionize solutions to their data & AI challenges using the Databricks platform. You will own the architecture, lead design decisions, and implement end-to-end systems spanning data engineering, AI, and application development. We work cross-functionally to shape long-term strategic priorities and initiatives alongside engineering, product, and developer relations. FDEs deliver with customer empathy, integrating with client systems, training, and other technical needs to help customers get most value out of their data. 

 

This is a hands-on, customer-facing role for builders who thrive at the intersection of technology and business impact. The ideal candidate combines engineering expertise with adaptability, curiosity, and a passion for working with customers and teammates to solve complex problems that drive measurable outcomes. FDEs are billable and know how to complete projects according to specification with exceptional customer empathy.

 

The impact you will have:

  • Production Solution Delivery: Lead impactful customer technical projects by delivering production-grade systems, designing and building reference architectures, custom applications and data ingestion and ML/AI model integration
  • Transformational Impact: Guide strategic customers as they implement transformational big data projects including end-to-end design, build and deployment of industry-leading big data and AI applications. Work with engagement managers to scope technical delivery work with input from the customer
  • Empower Customers: Guide customers on architecture and design; bootstrap or implement customer projects which leads to a customers' successful understanding, evaluation and adoption of Databricks.
  • Own the Architecture: Lead architecture and design decisions, ensuring solutions are secure, scalable, and aligned with both customer needs and Databricks best practices.
  • Work with the Databricks technical team, Project Manager, Architect and Customer team to ensure the technical components of the engagement are delivered to meet customer's needs.
  • Work with Engineering and Databricks Customer Support to provide product and implementation feedback and to guide rapid resolution for engagement specific product and support issues.
  • Customer Immersion: Embed with customer teams, engaging with stakeholders from technical ICs to executives to deeply understand challenges and deliver impact.
  • Reusable Assets & Scale: Contribute accelerators, frameworks, and best practices that scale impact across accounts and influence the Databricks product roadmap.

 

What we look for:

  • Extensive experience in data engineering, data platforms & analytics, or software engineering
  • Comfortable writing code in either Python, Scala, JavaScript/TypeScript, and modern frameworks
  • Working knowledge of two or more common Cloud ecosystems (AWS, Azure, GCP) with expertise in at least one
  • Deep experience with distributed computing with Apache Spark™ and knowledge of Spark runtime internals
  • Familiarity with CI/CD for production deployments
  • Working knowledge of MLOps, ML/AI models and AI APIs
  • Design and deployment of performant production end-to-end data architectures and applications that combine data pipelines, ML/AI models, and user-facing interfaces.
  • Experience with technical project delivery - managing scope, timelines and measurable outcomes, translating complex concepts into actionable solutions.
  • Documentation and white-boarding skills.
  • Experience working with Emerging Enterprise & Digital Natives businesses, and managing conflicts across a broad stakeholder range
  • Build skills in technical areas, and demonstrate curiosity, adaptability, and eagerness to explore new technologies which support the deployment and integration of Databricks-based solutions to complete customer projects.
  • Travel to customers 20% of the time
  • Databricks Certification

About Databricks

Databricks is the Data and AI company. More than 20,000 organizations worldwide — including adidas, AT&T, Bayer, Block, Mastercard, Rivian, Unilever, and 70% of the Fortune 500 — rely on the Databricks Data + AI Platform to build and scale data and AI apps, analytics and agents. Headquartered in San Francisco with 30+ offices around the globe, Databricks offers a unified platform that includes Genie, Lakebase, Agent Bricks, Lakeflow, Lakehouse, and Unity Catalog. To learn more, follow Databricks on LinkedIn, X, YouTube, and Instagram.

29cb5a60211b.title: Forward Deployed AI Engineer
29cb5a60211b.description:
Forward Deployed AI Engineer

DEPT® is a Growth Invention company built to help the world’s most ambitious brands grow faster. Operating at the intersection of technology and marketing, our 4,000+ specialists deliver growth invention services across Brand & Media, Experience, Commerce, CRM, and Technology & Data. We’re 50|50 tech and marketing, partner-led, and first to move. Clients include Google, Lufthansa, Meta, eBay, and OpenAI. We have been certified B Corp and Climate Neutral since 2021.

About the job

Global AI Strategy & Solutions defines how DEPT®’s clients respond as AI agents become the primary layer between customers and brands. The Future of the Customer Journey (FCJ) is the team’s flagship offer: it maps how AI systems intermediate customer journeys, diagnoses where a brand’s product reality diverges from what AI systems say about it, and directs investment accordingly. Growth and strategy teams across markets are selling and delivering it now.

As a Forward Deployed AI Engineer, you are an embedded builder inside that motion. You will sit with growth and strategy teams, understand the problem in front of them, and answer with working software rather than documentation. You will convert FCJ methodology into agentic components, prototypes, and internal tools, and integrate with infrastructure that lets new prototypes appear in days. When needed, you will work across global client projects on a partially billable basis, making sure the firm-wide strategy is captured and implemented properly rather than reinvented market by market. As components mature, you will collaborate with product and craft teams to keep everything compatible with the long-term platform and hand over cleanly. 

You will be given broad problem statements to help collaborate and solve, not specific product ideas and features to create. We are not looking for someone to lead on devops or CI/CD, this is about having great ideas that are sensitive to our clients’ real challenges, and shipping prototypes and strategic tools rapidly. 

Your most important collaboration is with the FCJ core team on the global growth strategy: deciding what gets built next, for which market, to unlock which engagement. The toolchain will keep changing underneath you, new models, new vendor products, new technology-partner platforms, and that is the point. This role suits an engineer who learns by shipping and treats every new AI product as something to master in the field.

Responsibilities

  • Work with the FCJ core team on the global growth strategy, converting methodology into working agentic components, prototypes, and internal tools.
  • Collaborate closely with growth and strategy teams to understand their problems and provide working solutions at prototype pace.
  • Work across global client projects on a partially billable basis, ensuring the firm-wide FCJ strategy is captured and implemented consistently across markets.
  • Collaborate with product and craft teams where necessary to document integration paths, maintain platform compatibility, and hand over validated components.
  • Work with technology partners to evaluate, adopt, and integrate new AI products; maintain an AI-native toolchain and share what works across markets.

Minimum qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience prototyping and shipping software in any modern backend language (Python, TypeScript, Go, or similar), with the ability to leverage AI tooling to spin up prototype frontends and APIs quickly.
  • Experience building applications across the mainstream LLM model families (Gemini, GPT, Claude), connecting models to enterprise data and tools using patterns such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and skills-based agent systems.
  • Proficiency in working with APIs to connect different services, authentication, data exchange, and integration across platforms.
  • Experience developing agentic systems with orchestration frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph, or equivalent.
  • AI-native way of working: AI tooling is the default across coding, research, and delivery, with comfort spanning the tools in use across different markets.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience in a forward-deployed, customer engineering, solutions engineering, or applied AI role within an agency, consultancy, or AI company.
  • Experience presenting working software to non-technical stakeholders, including strategists and clients, and iterating live on their feedback.
  • Knowledge of emerging integration standards such as OpenAPI and Model Context Protocol (MCP) for connecting agents to business systems.
  • Knowledge of any of the following: paid media, social platforms, user behaviour, agentic commerce, or generative engine optimisation (GEO).
  • Experience with evaluation, tracing, and observability for LLM applications.
  • Demonstrated learning mindset: a record of adopting new AI products from technology partners quickly, learning by doing rather than waiting for training.

We Offer

  • A flexible, hybrid working policy (2 days from the office in London).
  • An excellent salary based on experience and equal pay policies
  • Pension, free private healthcare, mental health support, and company sick pay scheme.
  • 26 days paid holiday (plus UK Bank Holidays).
  • Help getting you to work with a season ticket loan and cycle to work scheme.
  • Enhanced family friendly policies to support new parents.
  • Social and Cultural Events, plenty of opportunities to connect with colleagues through organised activities and celebrations.
  • Inspirational Talks, bringing the outside in with regular guest speakers and eve

de9971dcd10b.description: Our team shared’s mission is deploy AI agents to transform how patients and doctors connect We believe healthcare shouldn’t be defined by missed calls, endless waiting lines, and overwhelmed staff. Patients and professionals deserve better. Vocca builds AI voice agents that answer every call instantly, schedule and reschedule appointments, and free up staff to focus on what matters most: care. Already trusted by 15 000+ providers, we’re transforming the patient–provider relationship, one call at a time. Want to shape the future of healthcare? Join us ! Discover our company culture and values Here is a product teaser Eliott's interview for Welcome to the jungle Eliott's quick interview for Speedinvest Articles on our A round ( techfundingnews , Maddyness , les echos , our blog ) Vocca in a few words Vocca is an AI voice agent that answers 100% of the calls of medical centres. The patient calls, the AI books the appointment or answers the question, and the medical secretaries keep their time for the cases where a human is really needed. $20M raised, with the founders of Alan and Datadog as investors Close to 1 million calls a month going through the platform Opening the US market The problem Every medical practice runs on software that holds its calendar and its patients. There are dozens of different ones. Most were built twenty years ago and some have no API at all. To book an appointment during a call, our AI agent has to read and write in that software in real time, while the patient waits on the line. On several of these systems, Vocca is the only integrator in the world. This is the work with the most direct impact on the business. A clinic whose software is connected to our agent does not switch. Retention, pricing power, our lead over competitors: it all depends on these integrations. Every software we cannot connect is a clinic we cannot sign. The next step is writing back. Today the agent reads and books. Tomorrow it updates records in EHR, PMS and RIS systems, which raises the reliability bar a lot. In the US, we are opening the dental software ecosystem, with the compliance work that comes with it (HIPAA, SOC2). There is no product manager on this scope. You would be the one deciding. What you will own The architecture of our booking layer. Today it is code written provider by provider, under pressure, partly in Python. It is becoming one unified layer in TypeScript that handles the rules of each medical centre, where adding a new software takes days, not weeks. Speed and reliability at close to 1M calls a month. A call to a clinic software can take several seconds, and the patient cannot wait. You decide how we detect a booking failure in a clinic within 24 hours and what a healthy integration looks like. The roadmap of your scope. You decide which software we connect first, with the sales, ops and support teams and the clinics themselves, and you prove it worked with a number: bookings that go through, failures caught, clinics signed. The relationship with the software vendors, in France and in the US. The hard integrations are the ones nobody else wants to do. They are what makes Vocca hard to replace. The team. You define how this scope works (reviews, documentation, technical decisions), you take part in hiring the next engineers and you help them ship in their first week. How we build Experimental, not R&D. You test, you prove with data, you ship. Challenging a decision means coming back with a result, not a debate. Ship, then fix the last 1%. We ship the version that works, then fix the last 1% when it shows up. With AI, this trade off is much cheaper than before. The judgment about what not to touch is yours. AI, seriously. Agents in every workflow, Claude Max provided. A migration estimated at 3 months was done in 2 weeks. Close to the field. You talk every day with the ops team that deploys clinics, the support team that hears when something breaks and, when it matters, the clinics and the software vendors themselves. Stack TypeScript everywhere (Node, monorepo), PostgreSQL, REST and SOAP APIs from software vendors. We are migrating our last Python services to TypeScript over the coming months. Who does well here 6 to 10 years building products in production, mostly in startups that were growing fast, with at least one place where you stayed long enough to see your system live in the long run. You have built something that mattered: an early engineer at a startup that took off, a system you launched that real users depended on. You can tell us who it was for, what problem it solved and which number moved. You have integrated systems you did not control and you know the difference between a clean API and the real world. Strong in TypeScript and Node, comfortable across the stack. You think about the product and the business as much as the code. You can say no, reduce the scope and explain a technical decision to a founder in two minutes. You are at ease with clients and partners, in French and in English. Probably not for you if you want to manage without coding, or if you need a stable, fully specified environment before you move. What we expect from you First week. Onboarded on the stack, your first fix on a live integration is in production. First month. You own one integration end to end, from the software vendor to production, and show what it changed. You write down how our booking layer should evolve. First 3 months. The unified booking layer in TypeScript is the standard. Adding a new software takes days, not weeks. We detect a booking failure in any clinic within 24 hours. 6 to 12 months. Our first US integrations run in production. You have hired at least one engineer and they ship on their own. 1d1459e037b4.title: Principal Design Engineer - Mechanical Equipment (80-100%)
1d1459e037b4.description: Lead technically by doing. Join our Design Engineering team as a highly experienced individual contributor. You will take on challenging mechanical design problems yourself, from concepts and CAD models to manufacturing drawings, prototypes and tested hardware, while helping the wider team make strong technical decisions. As a Principal Design Engineer, you are a hands-on member of our Design Engineering team, designing Climeworks’ CO2 collectors, the heart of our direct air capture plant. Improving how they perform, are manufactured and scale is central to the future success of DAC. Mechanical concept & product design: You personally turn new concepts into robust physical products: developing mechanical concepts, creating CAD models, designing components and complete collector assemblies, producing manufacturing drawings, and supporting hardware through fabrication, assembly and testing. Engineering problem-solving & risk reduction: Your experience helps you find the right solutions faster, anticipate problems early and reduce risk before issues reach manufacturing or testing. CO2 collector design: You take mechanical systems from requirements and concepts through to detailed, manufacturable designs. You develop solutions, perform engineering calculations and make the decisions needed to create robust industrial hardware. First-principles engineering: You use experience and first-principles reasoning to identify risks early, evaluate alternatives quickly and converge on simple, robust solutions. You apply calculations, tolerance analysis, design reviews and testing to reduce uncertainty. Own design from concept to commercialisation: You work directly in SolidWorks to create and modify parts, assemblies and system layouts. You manage complex interfaces, packaging constraints and design changes so the complete system works together. You produce and maintain high-quality 2D manufacturing drawings, including appropriate GD&T, tolerances, materials, finishes and manufacturing requirements. Prototype fabrication, assembly & testing: You stay closely involved after the CAD work is complete. You support prototype fabrication, assembly and testing, investigate issues and incorporate the learning back into the design. Technical leadership & design reviews: You act as a senior technical reference for the team, supporting the Design Engineering line manager with design reviews, engineering standards and approval of critical designs. You support the extended team with technical judgement on complex mechanical design decisions, help maintain strong engineering practices and share your experience through everyday collaboration, mentoring and constructive challenge. Cross-functional engineering collaboration: You work with manufacturing, testing, process engineering, procurement, suppliers and other engineering disciplines to ensure mechanical designs work as part of the complete product. You integrate external design resources where needed. What makes you stand out Your experience makes your engineering more effective: you spot promising solutions early, expose weak points before they become expensive, and deliver designs that are clear, manufacturable and ready to perform in the real world. Mechanical Design Experience : You bring 15+ years of hands-on mechanical design experience, ideally developing complex industrial equipment from concept through manufacture, assembly and testing. Sheet Metal Design & Manufacturing : You have deep practical experience designing sheet-metal parts, structures and assemblies for manufacture at scale. You understand bending, welding and joining methods, forming, tolerances, material and thickness selection, and how design choices affect tooling, cost, assembly and quality. CAD & Drawings : You are an expert SolidWorks user and remain hands-on with CAD. You personally create high-quality manufacturing drawings and are confident with GD&T and tolerance chains. System Design & Engineering Judgement: You have experience designing from components and mechanisms through subsystems, interfaces and complex assemblies. You understand how decisions at one level affect the complete collector and can balance structures, airflow, movement, sealing, process interfaces, manufacturability, reliability and cost to arrive at robust solutions. Manufacturing & DFMA : You have strong knowledge of machined parts, welded structures, materials and manufacturing processes, and apply DFMA to create robust, cost-effective designs. Collaboration & Technical Leadership : You work effectively with engineers, technicians, manufacturers and suppliers. You share your experience, challenge constructively and help others make better technical decisions. Education: You have a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or similar. This job is not for you, if… you mainly want to manage people or projects. you mainly do simulation, concept work or system-level engineering without your own CAD work. you have no experience with sheet metal, welded structures or manufacturing at scale. Our promise: At Climeworks, you are accepted for who you are, and we are committed to building an inclusive environment where everyone feels valued. We encourage all qualified applicants to apply – regardless of background, identity, or experience. Studies show that women and individuals from minority backgrounds often only apply for jobs when they meet 100% of the listed criteria. If this sounds like you, don’t hold back. If you think you’d make a great fit for this role, we’d love to hear from you, even if you don’t check every single box. Let’s tackle one of humankind’s greatest challenges together. What we offer: Time Off: Enjoy 25 paid vacation days every year, plus public holidays. Flexibility: Work how it suits you best. We offer a hybrid work setup and up to 4 weeks of remote work annually within any EU country. Ownership: Fair base pay paired with an equity package – because your contributions matter. Fami

a195de3f6bc0.title: Product Frontend Engineer
a195de3f6bc0.description: quinn is becoming the way people employ, across the globe, through one app. quinn is an app-based, managed payroll and employment-administration service. We run it for private households employing a cleaner, nanny, or caretaker, and for businesses that manage employment relationships at scale. The customer stays the legal employer: quinn registers the employment, runs payroll, and handles social insurance, taxes, and filings on their behalf, automated end to end. Where everyone else sells software, quinn sells the outcome. We don't sell payroll software. We run payroll. The purpose behind it is simple: Fair employment. For all. Correct and fair employment, made simple and accessible for any employer and any employee, in any market quinn enters. Where this is going Think about what Revolut did to banking. All of the complexity (the regulation, the clearing, the compliance) handled invisibly in the background, and one simple experience at the front. Nobody using Revolut thinks about what happens behind the screen when they open a new account, swap currencies or send money abroad. It just works, in a couple of taps. Nobody should have to think about it in order to employ someone either. That is what quinn is building, and it is further along than most people assume: a profitable core business, running today in Switzerland, Germany and the UK, expanding into new markets both by launching and by acquiring. By 2030 quinn intends to be the destination brand for fair employment across six countries and more, on one platform, with one experience. One platform means one frontend. One experience means it looks and behaves like quinn whether you are in Zurich or in London, a household or a company. In this strategy that is not a nice-to-have. It is the strategy. Which is why the surface matters more than anything else. Everything quinn does is designed to disappear. The interface is the only part the customer ever sees, and it is the whole proof that the complexity behind it is really handled. Why this role exists Today , quinn runs on several separate web apps: one per product and market, each with its own frontend, grown over the years as the company grew. Our backend engineers built them alongside everything else, plus an internal admin tool that grew the same way. They all work: thousands of employers run payroll through them every month. But nobody was ever tasked with owning the frontend development, so each one got built the way frontend is built by Backend Developers, seen as a hassle rather than the main aspect users interactive with. What comes next is one frontend that replaces all of them, built from scratch: one quinn app for employers, employees and our own support team, in the browser first, then in the App Store and Google Play from the same work. Alongside it, the frontend of Maestro, the internal tool that replaces the old admin for batch processes. The phone app is the surface that matters most, so everything is built for it from the first screen rather than adapted to it afterwards. That is the opening. How we work We are AI-native, and we mean it operationally rather than as a slogan. AI is how the work gets done here. It is why a small team ships like a large one, and it is a large part of how one person will be able to hold the standard we are describing. We expect you to be at the front of that. Not to have heard of the tools, to live in them, and to build your own leverage with them: scaffolding, visual regression checks, design-token pipelines, whatever takes manual work out of the way. And we expect the judgement that has to come with it. AI writes code that looks right and is subtly wrong: structure that doesn't scale, patterns that fall apart three screens later, components that work once and never again. You take the speed and throw away the rest. AI never lowers the bar here. It is the reason the bar can be this high. Tasks What you will own Everything on the screen: The frontend of the quinn app and the web app. App first. One app for everyone who uses quinn: the employer, the employee, and our own support team working inside the customer's account. The frontend of Maestro, our internal batch tool. Desktop and dense: queues, runs, tables, filters, multi-select, keyboard shortcuts. A different discipline from the app, built on the same components. The component library across quinn Home and quinn Business: one frontend, one experience, every market and every device. Whether the app feels native: response, scrolling, gestures, transitions, biometric login, push. Nothing that gives away it isn't native. The quality of what you ship. Nothing leaves your hands half-finished. Where design ends, engineering begins. We have a design team, and they own how quinn looks and behaves: the flows, the visual design, the tokens, the component specs. You don't design. You own everything from there: how it is built, and everything a design file cannot reasonably specify, such as gestures, keyboard, safe areas, what happens between the drawn breakpoints, the loading, offline, pending and failed states, what a three-line German label does to a layout that was designed for English. You are in the room before design starts, saying what already exists in the library and what a new pattern costs. Not at the end, receiving a handover. When you and design disagree, they decide how it looks and behaves and you decide how it is built. Nothing enters the component library without both of you. Requirements Who we are looking for You care about interfaces more than anyone else in the room. You see the two-pixel misalignment without being told, and it bothers you until it is fixed. You build and maintain UI components and design systems, not one-off screens. You can build a mobile app that feels like one. And you can also build a desktop tool full of tables, filters and keyboard shortcuts, because Maestro is one. You understand UX and how people actually behave, not only how a screen looks. And you

c4a54336d027.description:
Who We Are

WPP Enterprise Solutions designs, builds, and operates the growth systems that competitive businesses rely on. In a world where Al is reshaping how companies drive growth, we lead clients in business transformation and marketing modernization, connecting strategy directly to execution. Our 12,000 experts in engineering and platforms, commerce, consulting, content transformation, CRM, and CX work within a unified global operating unit across 40+ markets. VML, part of WPP, supports WPP Enterprise Solutions by helping brands activate transformation through creativity and experience.

Working in technology & innovation with WPP Enterprise Solutions

At WPP Enterprise Solutions Netherlands, we create connected brands to drive growth. Our expertise spans the full customer journey, with deep capabilities in commerce, consultancy, CRM, CX, data, production, technology, content, media and more. We deliver end-to-end solutions for ambitious B2B and B2C brands, supported by the wider WPP network.

Our work combines strategy, product thinking, experience design, data, engineering and AI to solve real business problems, from enterprise commerce modernisation and digital shelf excellence to AI-enabled content operations, marketing automation, GEO, workflow orchestration and custom AI agents.

About the team

You’ll join the Product Management & AI Solutions team: the group that bridges business strategy, customer experience and technology to deliver scalable commerce and enterprise solutions. We work closely with UX/CX, Data & AI, SEO/GEO, Content, CRM, Paid and Retail Media, Engineering and Delivery teams.

Our ambition is to move beyond isolated skills and build repeatable, outcome-led propositions around commerce growth topics such as Search & Discovery, Personalisation, CRO & Experience Optimisation, Product Data/PIM & Digital Shelf, Content Supply Chain & AI Content Operations, CRM & Lifecycle Growth, Performance & Retail Media, SEO/GEO and Composable Commerce Modernisation. Alongside this, we are growing our applied AI work: shaping and delivering custom AI agents and AI-enabled workflows for clients, from discovery and pilot through to production and continuous improvement.

Why this role exists

Clients are increasingly asking for integrated solutions rather than isolated delivery capacity. They need people who can understand the business problem, shape the product direction, define the right solution, translate it into clear specifications and guide teams through delivery. At the same time, AI is changing how commerce, content, marketing and operations work, creating a need for analysts who can combine structured requirements thinking with product ownership, enterprise technology understanding and the design of AI-enabled workflows and agents.

This role is designed for someone who can operate as a strong Business Analyst, step into Product Owner responsibilities when needed, advocate for product thinking inside the organisation and help turn our AI and commerce capabilities into scalable client value. You will work across both our commerce and enterprise product work and our applied AI work. The mix depends on client demand, and we expect the AI share to grow over time.

The role

As Business Analyst, Enterprise & AI Solutions, you bridge business needs, product direction and technical delivery across enterprise digital commerce and martech ecosystems. You analyse business processes, clarify user and stakeholder needs, define requirements and support solutioning across the commerce stack: CMS, Search, PIM/PXM, DAM, ERP, OMS, CDP, CRM, analytics, marketing automation, paid/media platforms and integration layers.

You will also work on AI initiatives such as custom AI agents (for example for pricing, search or customer service), content and marketing automation, product/content enrichment, GEO and organic discoverability, AI orchestration and workflow automation. You do not need to be a machine learning engineer or a domain expert, but you must be technically curious and comfortable working with APIs, data flows, automation tools, LLM-based workflows, AI quality evaluation, governance requirements and human-in-the-loop processes.

Depending on your experience and the project context, you may act as a hands-on BA, a product-minded discovery partner, a proxy Product Owner or a work stream lead. In all cases, your job is to make ambiguity manageable, decisions explicit and delivery focused on measurable value.

What you will do

  • Collaborate with Solution Architects and Product Owners and translate business goals into clear requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, process flows, tech architecture, data flows and integration specifications that delivery teams can act on.

You will lead the entire customer delivery lifecycle, from identifying high-value business opportunities and designing multi-agent architectures to deploying production-ready systems. Your responsibilities will also include establishing best practices for agent development, evaluation, monitoring, and governance while mentoring other technical professionals. Accountabilities: Own the technical success of enterprise customers' agentic AI initiatives, managing the complete delivery lifecycle from initial discovery and solution design through development, production deployment, ongoing operations, and advisory services. Lead customer workshops to identify, assess, and prioritize high-value agentic AI use cases, translating business objectives into measurable and technically achievable workflows. Develop, review, and troubleshoot production-quality software using Go or Python, building agents, plugins, tools, and integrations that meet enterprise requirements. Deploy and operate agentic AI applications using Docker, Kubernetes, and major cloud platforms, ensuring scalability, reliability, and maintainability. Integrate AI agents with enterprise applications, data sources, and legacy systems through MCP servers, A2A protocols, REST APIs, and event-driven messaging architectures. Implement retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), vector databases, knowledge bases, embeddings, and real-time event context strategies to improve agent accuracy and access to relevant information. Apply the Agent Development Lifecycle (ADLC) throughout solution delivery, covering requirements gathering, architecture design, evaluation pipelines, testing, version control, release management, monitoring, and operational documentation. Establish robust observability, security controls, governance frameworks, and responsible AI practices for agentic systems, including tracing, quality evaluation, cost and latency monitoring, access control, and auditability.
