7bc6d1d5fdf4.title: Model-Based Systems Engineer
7bc6d1d5fdf4.description: About Us QuantWare is building the world’s most powerful quantum processors to solve humanity's greatest challenges. We do this with our unique VIO™ technology, the only QPU architecture that breaks the hardware barriers that have held quantum computing back, unlocking the path to MegaQubit quantum processors. With VIO, we are paving the way for the hyper-scale quantum computers that will change the world. And delivering on that vision demands people who don’t shy away from tackling the hardest challenges of our time. That’s where you come in! Our Systems Integration Team is seeking a Model-Based Systems Engineer to build the tools and framework we use to design the systems that operate our VIO and QPU technology. This role is focused on establishing QuantWare’s MBSE methodology and turning knowledge from cryogenics, wiring, control electronics and software into a single, executable system model. You will define how we model our systems and build the libraries, analyses and integrations that make the model useful day to day. Working closely with processor, hardware and software teams, you will play an important role in enabling the design of the large-scale quantum computers built around VIO-powered QPUs. What are you going to do? Define and own QuantWare’s MBSE methodology, modelling conventions and architecture framework for quantum computing systems, covering the quantum processor, cryostat, signal chain, control and readout electronics, and software stack. Select, set up and maintain the MBSE toolchain (e.g. SysML v2, Capella or Cameo), including version control, model reviews and integration with existing engineering tools. Build reusable model libraries for key subsystems, including QPU interfaces, cryogenic wiring and attenuation, microwave signal paths, and control electronics. Develop automated analyses on top of the model, such as heat-load, signal-integrity and noise budgets, channel counts, scalability, and full-system metrics such as power consumption as qubit counts grow. Establish requirements traceability from customer and system-level requirements down to component specifications and verification tests. Connect the system model to simulation and measurement data, creating a digital thread between design and test. Support system architecture and trade studies for new VIO and QPU generations and customer system integrations. Drive adoption across the company, training and supporting engineers in using the models and tools in their day-to-day work. Qualifications Core Requirements: BSc. or MSc. in systems engineering, electrical engineering, physics, mechanical engineering or a related field. 3+ years of hands-on MBSE experience, including building or extending a modelling framework rather than only using existing ones. Hands on experience with hardware system models that encompass multiple subsystems with differing requirements and interfaces. Strong working knowledge of SysML (v1 and/or v2) and at least one MBSE tool, such as Cameo, Capella or equivalent. Proficiency in Python for model automation, analysis and tool integration via APIs. A solid track record in requirements engineering and verification of complex, multidisciplinary hardware systems. Strong organisational and communication skills. You thrive in a cross-disciplinary environment and are comfortable taking ownership from day one. Bonus Points Experience with cryogenic, RF/microwave or precision instrumentation systems, or direct experience with superconducting quantum hardware. Background in high-tech, semiconductor, aerospace or scientific instrumentation industries. Experience introducing MBSE into an organisation and driving its adoption. Familiarity with SysML v2 APIs, digital thread concepts or co-simulation (e.g. FMI), as well as systems engineering standards such as ISO/IEC 15288. Don't tick every box? Apply anyway! Research shows women often self-select out if they don't meet every requirement. Here's our take: nobody ticks every box. This is a description of our ideal candidate, not a filter. If most resonates and you're keen to learn the gaps, apply. We hire for trajectory, not perfection. What We Offer: At QuantWare, you’ll be part of a high-performing team of world-class experts in an ambitious, fast-moving environment. From day one, you’ll have the trust, tools, and support to do your best work. Here’s what you can expect: Competitive salary - A salary that reflects the impact and importance of the role (and of course 8% holiday allowance) Pension that’s built to last - A generous and future-proof pension plan that includes partner and dependent coverage. Flexibility built on trust - We focus on outcomes. Work flexibly, in a hybrid setup, with an open vacation policy that lets you manage your time Personal growth - We invest in your L&D, with a budget available to each team member, dependent on their individual ambitions, development needs, and performance A connected team - We make space to celebrate wins together, with team events, offsites, and spontaneous moments that bring us closer Diversity & Inclusion at QuantWare We’re an ambitious company, not only for our goals but also to become an even more diverse and inclusive team. We know great candidates don't always follow a straight path, and we value diverse experience, perspectives, and ways of thinking. We know this helps us make better decisions, drives more innovation, and strengthens our culture. As part of our recruitment process, candidates may be required to undergo pre-employment screening. 8767b912b739.title: Senior Integration Software Engineer

Optics11 is a deep-tech company developing advanced fiber-optic sensing technologies for challenging environments and applications in energy and underwater security. Our systems enable high-performance sensing and monitoring through advanced photonics, signal processing, and data-driven intelligence. We are expanding our R&D team with an Integration Software Engineer who enjoys building clean, reliable interfaces between components and working where software meets hardware, and who takes ownership of making complex systems work together end to end. As a Senior Integration Software Engineer, you will support their integration into operational systems: connecting algorithms to the backend through robust APIs, building data connectors, health reporting and control software, and defining and verifying integrations with Command and Control (C2) systems. You will work closely with domain experts in acoustics, signal processing and machine learning, and with the software engineering team, and hands-on with our monitoring systems at our headquarters and production facility. You will also take technical ownership of work delivered by internal and external engineers and set the standard for good engineering practices. Key Responsibilities Lead software integration engineering for our underwater acoustic sensing systems, ensuring frontend and backend components, algorithms, and hardware systems work together reliably. Integrate the algorithmic toolbox with our system backends, turning research code into maintainable, versioned and deployable software components. Implement data interfaces for our real-time sonar processing pipeline, to ingest multiple sensors (acoustic, heading, temperature, pressure, etc.) from internal and external data acquisition systems. Implement health reporting, logging and monitoring, so that the status and performance of software and system components is visible and actionable. Address performance, latency and scalability of the integrated pipeline, together with algorithm and backend developers. Review the work of junior engineers and external development partners in depth, promote good practices for packaging, versioning and release, and share integration knowledge across the team. Why Join Us? Join one of Europe’s most promising deep-tech scale-ups. Shape the future of a rapidly growing multidisciplinary R&D organization. Competitive salary and benefits package. Enjoy regular team activities and company events. Fresh team lunches provided 5 times/week. Qualifications: BSc or MSc in Computer Science, Software Engineering or a related field. Proven experience designing and implementing APIs and messaging interfaces (e.g. MQTT, WebSocket) and data serialization (e.g. protobuf). Experience reviewing code and designs, mentoring junior engineers, and setting engineering standards. An outcome-focused mindset, with the ability to own a problem end to end or break it down for others. Ability to work with algorithm developers and translate research code into robust, maintainable software. Experience developing software interfaces for controlling instruments or devices. Experience with other messaging or streaming frameworks (e.g. Kafka, ZeroMQ, DDS). 0c75a6b7cc9c.description: Who we are Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. Although you will be focused on security incident response, you will also have the opportunity to create and maintain runbooks, and automated workflows, and assist in process refinement and implementation. 587bb4aee4a0.title: Engineering Manager - Developer Ecosystem
587bb4aee4a0.description: RDQ427R369 At Databricks, we are passionate about enabling data teams to solve the world's toughest problems — from making the next mode of transportation a reality to accelerating the development of medical breakthroughs. We do this by building and running the world's best data and AI infrastructure platform so our customers can use deep data insights to improve their business. Our Developer Ecosystem organisation shapes how developers and the AI agents working for them build on the Databricks Data and AI Platform, from within the product to the tools they already use. We are hiring an Engineering Manager to lead our declarative deployment framework, which turns data and AI projects into versioned, reviewable, repeatable software. It is one product with two entry points. Third-party developers use our open-source CLI from their IDEs, terminals, and CI/CD systems. First-party, they author, deploy and inspect the same projects inside the Databricks workspace. In both, AI agents increasingly do the work: coding agents drive the CLI, and our in-product AI assistant authors and deploys projects alongside the developer. Thousands of organisations run their CI/CD on it, and it is one of the fastest-growing parts of the platform. The team owns the deployment engine and CLI, the in-workspace authoring and deployment experience, and the metadata service and deployment history that record every deployment. The hard problems are real infrastructure-as-code problems: reconciling declared and live state, making plans safe for humans and agents to approve, keeping visual authoring and code in sync, and shipping weekly releases that remain backwards-compatible for our largest customers. The impact you will have: Lead and grow the team: Manage a team of senior engineers across three closely connected areas (the deployment engine and open-source CLI, the in-workspace authoring and deployment experience, and deployment history and metadata), working with strong tech leads. Hire, coach and promote, and grow engineers into tech leads. Make agentic development the default path: Shape how developers and AI agents author, validate and deploy projects, both inside the workspace and from the developer's own coding agent. Design the tools, skills and guardrails so agents get the same safety and auditability as humans. Own the strategy and roadmap: Partner with Product and Design to set a multi-quarter roadmap for declarative deployment: agentic development, governed deployments and deployment history, enterprise CI/CD, and new resource coverage. Make the trade-offs explicit when the demand is larger than the team. Raise the bar on execution and operational excellence: Run a predictable delivery process for a fast-moving, open-source product with frequent releases. Own reliability, on-call health, incident response and the quality bar for a tool customers depend on to ship to production. Treat backward compatibility as a product feature: Lead engine and configuration migrations without forcing customers through a flag day, and communicate change clearly to customers, the community and field teams. Lead across the platform: Drive alignment with the many platform teams whose resources and services the framework deploys, and with our sibling teams in Developer Ecosystem (SDKs, CLI, IaC provider, IDE). Make the whole toolchain feel like one product. What we look for: 3+ years managing software engineering teams, and 8+ years of software engineering experience overall. A track record of building and shipping developer tools or platforms used by many external developers or internal teams, such as infrastructure-as-code, deployment or CI/CD systems, CLIs, SDKs, or internal developer platforms. A deep understanding of declarative systems and deployment workflows: plan/apply, state management, drift and reconciliation, environment promotion, GitOps. Enough technical depth to engage on architecture and trade-offs with senior and staff engineers, and to hold a high-quality bar for public, versioned interfaces. Experience leading teams through ambiguity, with competing priorities from customers, partners and platform dependencies, and making clear calls. Strong product sense and a customer-first mindset. You enjoy talking to developers, reading their issues, and turning feedback into roadmap. Excellent written and verbal communication, including with executives, partner teams and an external developer community. Stand-out experience: Built or led teams on infrastructure-as-code or deployment platforms, e.g. Terraform, Pulumi, AWS CDK / CloudFormation, Kubernetes controllers, Argo CD / Flux / Helm, or Vercel / Netlify-style deploy platforms. Managed an open-source developer tool with an active community and a frequent release cadence. Shipped developer workflows for AI coding agents (CLI-first tooling, agent skills, MCP), or AI-assisted authoring. About Databricks Databricks is the Data and AI company. More than 20,000 organizations worldwide — including adidas, AT&T, Bayer, Block, Mastercard, Rivian, Unilever, and 70% of the Fortune 500 — rely on the Databricks Data + AI Platform to build and scale data and AI apps, analytics and agents. Headquartered in San Francisco with 30+ offices around the globe, Databricks offers a unified platform that includes Genie, Lakebase, Agent Bricks, Lakeflow, Lakehouse, and Unity Catalog. To learn more, follow Databricks on LinkedIn , X , YouTube , and Instagram . Benefits At Databricks, we strive to provide comprehensive benefits and perks that meet the needs of all of our employees. For specific details on the benefits offered in your region click here . Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion At Databricks, we are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture where everyone can excel. We take great care to ensure that our hiring practices are inclusive and meet equal employment opportunity standards. Individuals looking for employment at Databricks are considered without regard

f5ca816dad46.description: Sr. Research Scientist - Agent Flywheel P-1213 Company Description At Databricks, we are obsessed with enabling data teams to solve the world's toughest problems, from security threat detection to cancer drug development. We do this by building and running the world's best data and AI platform so our customers can focus on the high-value challenges that are central to their own missions. The Databricks AI Research organization is pushing the frontier of next-generation enterprise AI. We believe a company's data is its greatest competitive advantage, and we're building the models and agents that unlock it. Our work spans the full stack, from model training to advanced multi-agent systems. Job Description As a Research Scientist on the Agent Flywheel team, you will build the context layer for recursive self-improvement and autofix loops for agents: turning raw production session traces from Databricks’ data agents into online signals agents can optimize against. You will research how to convert messy, real customer interactions into deterministic metrics, calibrated LLM judges, and failure clusters, and close the loop so those signals drive training and agent improvement. You will join a collaborative team of researchers with diverse backgrounds and encode your findings into products our customers rely on. The impact you will have Turn raw production session traces from Genie Code and Genie One into online signals agents can optimize against. Train and calibrate LLM judges so model feedback becomes reliable, repeatable signal, including calibration against expert human ratings. Convert multi-turn agent trajectories into datasets and reward signals for post-training, closing the loop between production signals, evaluation, and agent improvement. Design benchmarks and RL environments from real customer workloads that probe long-horizon, tool-using agent behavior. Advance evaluation research: online evals on live traffic, automated raters, verifiable rewards, and measurement that keeps pace with agents that act. Keep up with the latest developments in deep learning and create new techniques that go beyond the state of the art. What we look for Expertise in debugging and diagnosing failures in complex, stochastic, multi-component systems Deep instinct for designing metrics and evals that track what actually matters, and questioning noisy, sparse, or biased signals Experimental rigor and causal thinking, from offline ablations to online experiments A drive to turn measurement into improvement: closing the loop from signals to changes that move the numbers Solid AI research and software engineering skills Strong communication skills and excitement to work on a small, fast-paced team A drive to get your work into the hands of real users Nice to have Experience with agent systems, such as coding agents, long-horizon tool-using agents, or building evaluation environments A track record of novel research on learning from feedback, such as post-training, RLHF, or reward modeling Pay Range Transparency Databricks is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. 91986773ba73.title: Integration Reliability Engineer, Technical Operations
91986773ba73.description: Who we are About Stripe Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies, from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups, use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career. About the team Stripe's Money Management products (Financial Accounts, Treasury, Global Payouts, Issuing, and Capital) let businesses and platforms hold, move, spend, and earn on their money using the same infrastructure they already use for payments. APAC Money as a Service (MaaS) is a newly formed team, based in Singapore, responsible for bringing this product suite to Asia-Pacific markets, enabling global businesses and platforms to use these capabilities directly or offer them to their APAC users, and building the local rails, compliance, and partner integrations that make it all work. None of this works without financial partners: the banks, card networks, and licensed institutions whose systems our products run on in each market. Technical Operations in APAC MaaS owns the day-to-day health of those partner integrations, existing and new, and the working technical relationship with the partners behind them. We sit between product and platform engineering, Stripe's partnerships and compliance teams, and our partners' technical teams, which gives us an unusually complete view of how money moves in the region: the code and the real-world mechanics behind it. What you'll do This role sits where Stripe's engineering meets the financial institutions we build on, and it is broader than most technical operations seats. You'll own the health of the partner integrations that power APAC MaaS, and you'll be the technical face of Stripe to the banks, networks, and institutions behind them. One week that means working through a partner specification and reconciling settlement files; the next, shipping tooling or running an operational review with a partner's engineering team. Because every APAC launch depends on partner readiness, you'll have direct line of sight into what the team ships and a real say in how. It's a role that builds technical depth and partner judgment at the same time, in a region where we're still writing the playbook. Responsibilities Own the operational health of APAC MaaS's financial partner integrations across accounts, payouts, and card issuing: monitor them, catch problems early, and drive issues to root cause and durable fixes. Act as the primary technical point of contact for our partners in the region. Run recurring operational reviews, manage escalations end to end, align on product usage and specifications, and keep both Stripe and the partner on track against their commitments. Lead partner-facing technical change: onboarding and certifying new integrations, specification changes, migrations and cutovers, and incident reviews, coordinating Stripe engineering, partnerships, compliance, and the partner's teams. Investigate and resolve issues across the stack. Read and write code, query data, work through logs and partner reports and files, and make scoped changes in Stripe's codebase when that is the right fix. Build reconciliation and anomaly detection so that money moving through our partner integrations is correct, traceable, and accounted for, in collaboration with engineering, accounting, and partnerships. Remove manual work through code, tooling, or changes to how we operate with partners. Become the team's domain expert on how money actually moves in each APAC market: rails, cutoffs, settlement cycles, file formats, return codes, and partner-specific behavior. Document it and make it usable by the rest of the team. Bring partner realities into product and engineering decisions, and define what "partner-ready" means for each market launch. Who you are You're equally at home in a partner's steering call and in a debugger, and you enjoy moving between the two. You are precise: you read the specification to the end, you notice when a reconciliation is off by one record, and you follow up until the loose end is closed. You build trust with external counterparts by being prepared, direct, and reliable, and you can hold a partner (or Stripe) to a commitment while keeping the relationship strong. We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement. Minimum requirements 6+ years in a technical role (for example Technical Operations, Software Engineering, Integration Engineering, or Solutions Architecture), including meaningful time working directly with external technical counterparts Experience owning working relationships with external partners such as banks, card networks, processors, or similar institutions: running operational reviews, managing escalations, and driving technical changes to completion across organizations Ability to write high-quality, maintainable code and SQL, read and navigate an unfamiliar codebase, and make scoped changes safely; familiarity with developer tools such as Git Knowledge of payments or money movement technologies and ecosystems, such as bank transfers, payouts, card issuing, settlement, or reconciliation Exceptional attention to detail, with a track record of working from specifications, file formats, and financial data where small errors have real consequences Great communication skills, both oral and written, with the ability to frame messages for technical and non-technical audiences inside and outside Stripe Great problem-solving skills, with an ability to develop a working understanding of a technical system using a variety of methods: reading and writing

5189ce9cf637.title: Staff Software Engineer, Code Forge
5189ce9cf637.description: Who we are About Stripe Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career. About the team In this role, you’d be joining the Code Forge team in Developer Productivity. Our team is responsible for the systems that store Stripe’s code and its history, and serve it to every engineer, AI agent, and CI job. Our team helps Stripe increase the GDP of the internet by helping Stripe engineers ship faster and more safely. Stripe has a massive monorepo, and it keeps growing. AI is changing how software is built, and the demand on our systems grows with it. Our goal is source control that scales to meet any demand and serves each of its users in the way that best fits their work: engineers who write and review code, AI agents that work in parallel, and CI jobs that build and test every change. Change management is a critical function at Stripe. We work closely with the Code Review team so that engineers and agents can move changes through review and approval quickly and safely. We put users first. We spend time with the engineers who use our systems, we measure their experience, and we let what we learn guide our decisions. AI tools change quickly, and our plans change with them. We like this pace, and we adapt quickly. What you’ll do In this role, you’ll lead how Stripe stores and serves its code as demand grows. You’ll work with engineers across Stripe to understand what slows them down, turn that into a technical direction, and bring teams and leaders along with you. You’ll lead large projects that involve several engineers and teams, and you’ll also write a large part of the code, and shepherd your projects from beginning to end. You’ll make sure that our systems stay correct, available, and fast. This is a highly collaborative, high-visibility role. You’ll partner with engineering to define and drive the long-term vision. You’ll work closely with the Developer AI teams, the Developer Environments organization, and the Code Review team, as well as CI/Build infrastructure, reliability, security, and compliance teams. You’ll mentor engineers on our team and beyond, and you’ll use AI coding agents every day to build systems and to understand them. Responsibilities Work with engineers across Stripe to understand how they, their agents, and their CI jobs use source control, and use their feedback and data to decide what to build next Set technical direction for how Stripe stores and serves code, build alignment across teams and leaders, and lead large, multi-engineer projects from design through delivery and adoption Design and build storage systems for code and its history that scale with our monorepo and with the growing load from engineers, agents, and CI, making decisions about data models, indexing, and caching Make sure that engineers never lose work and are not blocked by outages, through high availability, redundancy, and disaster recovery across regions Partner with the Developer AI and Developer Environments teams to remove latency in the paths that engineers, agents, and CI/Builds use most, such as starting work, resuming it on another machine, saving changes, and merging Work closely with the Code Review team so that humans and agents can move changes through Stripe’s change management process quickly and safely Mentor engineers, and help the team use AI to build and understand systems faster while keeping quality and reliability high Who you are We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement. Minimum requirements BS or MS in Computer Science or a related field 10+ years of professional software engineering experience, including designing, building, and operating distributed systems, databases, or storage infrastructure in production Experience building critical, latency-sensitive systems that require strong consistency, durability, high availability, and disaster recovery Experience leading large, complex projects with multiple engineers across teams and organizations, explaining technical tradeoffs, building alignment with partners and leaders, and mentoring engineers in an environment where technologies and priorities change quickly Experience using AI coding agents in your daily work to write, test, and understand software Preferred qualifications Experience building developer tools that help engineers move faster, scaling large monorepos, or working with source control systems such as Sapling/Mononoke, Jujutsu (JJ), Mercurial, or Git Experience using user feedback and data to understand user needs and guide engineering decisions Experience building storage engines or databases, including on-disk formats, indexing, compression, and replication Experience with consensus, replication protocols, or strongly consistent distributed databases Experience with algorithms and data structures for large graphs or content-addressed data Proficiency with profiling, tracing, and debugging tools (for example, perf or eBPF) to find performance problems in distributed systems Proficiency in Go for high-performance distributed services

f20bfa81b415.title: Senior Response Engineer (Application & network security)
f20bfa81b415.description: About Us At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company. At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in. Available Location: Singapore About the Department Cloudforce One is Cloudflare's threat operations and research team, responsible for identifying and disrupting cyber threats ranging from sophisticated cyber criminal activity to nation-state sponsored advanced persistent threats (APTs). Cloudforce One works in close partnership with external organizations and internal Cloudflare teams, continuously developing operational tradecraft and expanding ever-growing sources of threat intelligence to enable expedited threat hunting and remediation. Members of Cloudforce One are at the helm of leveraging an incredibly vast and varied set of data points that only one of the world's largest global networks can provide. The team analyzes these unique data points at massive scale and efficiency, synthesizing findings into actionable threat intelligence to better protect our customers. About INTERDICT I.N.T.E.R.D.I.C.T. (Identify, Neutralize, Triage, Engage, Respond, Disrupt, Integrate, Contain, Threat Hunting) is Cloudforce One's unified operational security organization responsible for identifying, analyzing, and responding to threats targeting Cloudflare and its customers. INTERDICT encompasses three main sub-functions: Cloudflare Managed Defense (CMD): Network and application security monitoring for 'Under Attack' mitigation support. PhishGuard: Managed email threat detection and response service. Detection Engineering: ML model development and detection optimization. Together, INTERDICT provides comprehensive 24×7×365 protection across email, application, and network threat surfaces. Role Summary As a Senior Response Engineer within the Cloudflare Managed Defense Center (CMDC), you will serve as a subject-matter expert and technical escalation point for threat mitigation across Cloudflare’s strategic enterprise customer base. In this role, you will lead the response to sophisticated, multi-vector cyberattacks spanning OSI Layers 3, 4, and 7, operating beyond standard playbooks to diagnose anomalies, engineer custom mitigations, and stabilize mission-critical infrastructure under fire. Beyond active incident command, you will act as a force multiplier: architecting customer-specific defense strategies, authoring and refining automated detection logic, mentoring Tier 1 and Tier 2 engineers, and collaborating directly with Cloudflare Product and Engineering teams. We are looking for an experienced, high-ownership technical leader who excels during high-stakes incidents and is passionate about mentoring others while advancing threat mitigation at scale. CMDC operates 24×7×365. This role participates in a regional shift rotation and on-call escalation rota including periodic weekend and public-holiday coverage as part of a follow-the-sun model across AMER, EMEA, and APAC. Role Responsibilities Act as the technical lead and incident commander during high-impact, multi-vector security events, designing and deploying bespoke mitigation strategies when standard runbooks do not suffice. Perform deep-dive forensic analysis into complex Layer 3/4 and Layer 7 traffic anomalies, identifying zero-day attack patterns, sophisticated bot networks, and novel evasion techniques. Apply advanced mitigation strategies and filter malicious traffic using Cloudflare’s core security suite, including Magic Transit, Web Application Firewall (WAF), and Advanced Rate Limiting. Lead technical communications and incident bridge calls with enterprise C-level executives, principal network engineers, and security teams during critical events, clearly articulating root causes, impact assessments, and remediation paths. Monitor and investigate proactive security alerts across internal telemetry systems to rapidly triage incoming events, assess blast radius, and validate threat severity. Adhere to and champion strict customer SLAs for alert response times, event analysis, and clear executive reporting. Mentor and elevate Tier 1 and Tier 2 engineers through structured shadowing, technical post-mortems, and internal training. Partner with internal Engineering and Product teams to translate operational attack trends into prioritized platform enhancements, tool feedback, and automated detection logic. 8c85a8c61a16.description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops silicon and system-level solutions designed for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. The team is responsible for building the next generation of AI-native silicon while working closely with software and research partners to co-design hardware tightly integrated with AI models. In addition to delivering production-grade silicon for OpenAI’s supercomputing infrastructure, the team also creates custom design tools and methodologies that accelerate innovation and enable hardware optimized specifically for AI.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for an experienced Thermal Engineer with 7+ years of experience in thermal management of IT hardware from chip/package to system levels. You’ll work alongside experts in thermal, mechanical, electrical, software, and systems engineering to support the design, analysis, and validation of thermal solutions that ensure the reliability, efficiency, and longevity of mission-critical hardware. This position requires strong analytical skills, hands-on testing experience, and the ability to work in a fast-paced, cross-disciplinary environment.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Design and optimize thermal solutions for data center hardware, including chips, power modules, and system-level cooling architectures

 - Evaluate thermal performance at the chip, package, and board levels, addressing challenges related to power density, heat dissipation, and thermal interface materials

 - Perform thermal modeling and simulation to predict temperature profiles and identify thermal bottlenecks

 - Collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate thermal management strategies into hardware design, from concept to mass production

 - Support lab testing and validation, including the setup of thermal experiments, data acquisition, and troubleshooting of thermal performance issues

 - Design and select thermal components, such as cold plates, heat sinks, fans, vapor chambers, and thermal interface materials (TIMs)

 - Work with firmware and electrical engineers to define and implement thermal control algorithms for dynamic power and cooling management.

 - Conduct feasibility studies and trade-off analyses to evaluate cooling technologies and improve system thermal efficiency

 - Partner with suppliers and manufacturers to support the development of custom thermal components and ensure quality in production


QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Thermal Engineering, or a related field (Master’s preferred).

 - 7+ years of industry experience in thermal design, simulation, and validation for IT hardware

 - Proficiency in thermal simulation software and CAD tools

 - Strong understanding of heat transfer principles, thermodynamics, and fluid mechanics, with an emphasis on electronics cooling

 - Hands-on experience with thermal testing equipment, including thermocouples, infrared cameras, wind tunnels, and P-Q characterization setups

 - Experience in chip/package-level thermal analysis, including die-level heat spreading, and package thermal modeling

 - Ability to analyze experimental data, identify root causes of thermal issues, and implement corrective actions

 - Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to perform first-principles calculations to support design decisions.

 - Self-driven, detail-oriented, and able to work independently or collaboratively in cross-functional engineering environments


PREFERRED SKILLS

 - 10+ years of industry experience in thermal design, simulation, and validation for IT hardware

 - Extensive experience with data center hardware or high-performance computing systems at scale

 - Practical experience in developing advanced cooling technologies

 - Familiarity with thermal control algorithms and dynamic thermal management techniques

 - Understanding of reliability testing, failure analysis, and thermal stress testing for electronic components

 - Experience working with suppliers and manufacturing partners to support thermal solution development and production ramp-up

5c5d57187730.title: AI Deployment Manager (Korean Speaking)
5c5d57187730.description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The AI Deployment Manager (ADM) team enables organizations to turn OpenAI products into real, sustained impact through world-class enablement and training execution.

Our mission is to advance customer skills, confidence and capabilities to turn AI into lasting, measurable value. We partner with enterprises to translate the potential of OpenAI’s technology into durable capability—through structured training, technical enablement, and scalable deployment programs.

By helping customers move from experimentation to production, the ADM team accelerates time-to-value, deepens meaningful adoption, and helps make OpenAI indispensable to how organizations work.


ABOUT THE ROLE

The AI Deployment Manager role is a specialist post-sales technical enablement role focused on delivering high-impact enablement and adoption services across OpenAI’s product suite. You help customer teams use OpenAI products independently in their day-to-day work. You work with business teams and developers, diagnose what’s getting in their way, and build and test practical examples they can learn from.

This role blends deep technical fluency, instructional design, and customer advisory. You will lead live trainings, workshops, and adoption interventions for audiences ranging from hands-on builders to executive leaders, helping customers understand not just what OpenAI’s products can do, but how to use them effectively in real-world contexts.

Success in this role means accelerating customer confidence and value, increasing product adoption, helping customers progress toward production use, and turning lessons from individual engagements into resources and practices that benefit many customers.

We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.


IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Own the technical enablement of OpenAI products, including ChatGPT Work, OpenAI APIs, Codex, Daybreak and other platform capabilities, helping define effective enablement patterns that support adoption across customer segments

 - Lead customer training and enablement across the full customer lifecycle, from initial onboarding through expansion, optimization, and long-term adoption.

 - Design and deliver high-impact training engagements, including onboarding sessions, advanced capability trainings, executive briefings, hackathons, and hands-on workshops for audiences ranging from senior leaders to working teams.

 - Drive customer activation, sustained usage, and measurable business value through structured enablement and deployment programs designed for durable adoption at scale

 - Partner closely with Sales, Applied AI Architects, Delivery Leads to drive adoption across our core product suite.

 - Develop and refine reusable training assets, playbooks, and best practices based on patterns observed across customers and regions.

 - Gather customer feedback from training and enablement engagements, synthesize themes across accounts, and relay insights to internal stakeholders to inform product and program improvements.

 - Serve as a Subject Matter Expert (SME) for designated product areas, building deep expertise, supporting internal enablement, identifying emerging customer use cases for new product surfaces, and aggregating customer feedback to inform product development.


YOU’LL THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Speak fluent business-level Korean, as you will be engaging with Korean-speaking customers

 - Have 6+ years of experience owning an enterprise enablement or adoption initiative from discovery through results, aligning executive sponsors, business users, and technical teams around a measurable customer outcome.

 - Possess exceptional presentation and communication skills, particularly when conveying the value of technical concepts clearly to senior and executive-level audiences.

 - Can build, test, and troubleshoot a working example using APIs or developer tools such as Codex. You can walk developers through how it works, explain how to evaluate the results, and help them adapt it to their own use case.

 - Can design and lead sessions for developers, knowledge workers, and executives. You can guide developers through a hands-on lab, help a business team apply AI to a recurring task, and lead an executive discussion about where AI can deliver value and how to measure it.

 - Strong ability to connect technical features and capabilities to concrete business outcomes such as productivity, efficiency, cost reduction, risk mitigation, or revenue impact.

 - Have a humble attitude, an eagerness to help others, and a desire to pick up whatever knowledge you're missing to make both your team and our customers succeed.

 - Comfortable thinking on their feet in live customer settings, adapting quickly to new information, shifting priorities, and real-time questions while maintaining clarity, ownership, and momentum.

 - Are personally committed to fostering the safe and ethical evolution of AI.

About the Team

Enterprise Platform Engineering builds products and capabilities that improve enterprise workflows, partnering closely with engineering, functional teams, and system owners.

About the Role

As a Business Platform Engineer, you will translate business problems into reliable software and workflows. You will move between requirements, architecture, implementation, testing, rollout, and operational ownership, using functional expertise to deliver measurable outcomes.

Workplace & Location

San Francisco

In this role, you will:

 - Translate business workflows into requirements, process and data definitions, exception handling, and acceptance criteria.

 - Build services, APIs, integrations, data flows, and automation with maintainable code and meaningful tests.

 - Own delivery from design and implementation through validation, deployment, support, and continuous improvement.

 - Design permissions, approvals, auditability, retries, idempotency, reconciliation, and recovery appropriate to the workflow.

 - Partner with business and system owners on prioritization, operational readiness, and adoption.

 - Measure reliability, quality, cycle time, and user outcomes; turn successful solutions into reusable capabilities.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have demonstrated experience building and operating software that solves business problems.

 - Bring functional understanding of finance, procurement, accounting, or adjacent enterprise workflows, and can learn an unfamiliar domain.

 - Can write and debug code and reason about APIs, integrations, data models, and system boundaries.

 - Understand controls, failure modes, testing, and reliable production operation.

 - Can structure ambiguous problems and turn them into practical increments with clear tradeoffs.

 - Communicate clearly across engineering and business teams and follow through on delivery and adoption.

Preferred signals

 - Experience turning specialist knowledge into reusable tools, data products, or workflow capabilities.

 - Practical AI-assisted workflow experience with evaluation, human review, monitoring, and controlled actions.

 - Evidence of enabling others to adopt a capability and measuring the resulting improvement.

We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

28e454bdfa37.title: Growth GTM Engineer, Revenue Operations
28e454bdfa37.description:
In 2026, we launched Computer, the defining product for the new era of agentic AI. Millions of people and teams adopt Perplexity and Computer on their own, and our marketing programs bring in thousands more leads. To turn that demand into pipeline, every lead has to be enriched, scored, and routed to the right next step within minutes.

We're hiring a Growth GTM Engineer on the Revenue Operations team to own the lead-to-engagement engine: the enrichment platform that completes every marketing and product lead, the routing that sends each lead to nurture or to BDRs and Sales, and the syncs that move data from our warehouse into Salesforce and our GTM tools. You'll also put lead and account scores to work with Data Science, who own the scoring models, and help deliver our BDRs' prospecting tools.

You'll report to the Head of Pipeline Operations, who sets the priorities for this work and owns our marketing automation platform, campaign operations and attribution.

You'll build mostly with AI, so we care more about your instinct for go-to-market systems than your depth in any one programming language. You'll measure everything you build against meetings, pipeline and revenue.

Tech stack: Salesforce | Clay | Reverse ETL (Hightouch or similar) | Routing and scheduling (Default, Chili Piper or similar) | Snowflake | SQL | Python | Computer | LLM APIs




WHY PERPLEXITY IS DIFFERENT

 - Craftsmanship. We build high quality, tasteful products targeting both the AI native and AI curious.

 - Ownership. You identify the problem, design the solution and ship it.

 - Entrepreneurship. We think like founders, act with urgency, and hustle to deliver for each other and our users.

 - Scholarship. Work among highly talented peers, pursuing knowledge and truth, upleveling ourselves, our teams, and our products.

 - Partnership. We amplify each others' strengths, break down silos, and give selflessly to help our colleagues deliver excellence.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the enrichment platform. Design and run waterfall enrichment across third-party providers, AI research agents and first-party data for every marketing and product lead. Handle lead-to-account matching, deduplication, field governance, data freshness and provider cost. Publish enriched data to the warehouse for Data Science and other teams to use.

 - Own lead routing. Design the decision logic that sends each lead, from marketing programs or product usage, to Marketing for nurture or to a BDR, AE or Account Manager for engagement, based on score, segment, territory, account ownership, capacity and existing opportunities. Co-define lifecycle stages, handoff SLAs, recycle rules and speed-to-lead triggers with the Head of Pipeline Operations, and enforce them in Salesforce and our routing tools, with MQLs and PQLs on the same lifecycle and SLAs. Deliver the enrichment, signals, routing and alerts behind our account-based plays.

 - Own the syncs between our warehouse and our GTM tools. Build and maintain the reverse ETL syncs, APIs and webhooks that move data from Snowflake into Salesforce, marketing automation, routing and engagement tools. Build on the models the Data team publishes, and make sure every synced field has one owner and every sync is monitored. Support the rollout of our first marketing automation platform by building its Salesforce sync and warehouse feeds, along with the nurture enrollment rules and campaign tracking the Head of Pipeline Operations designs.

 - Put lead and account scores to work. Data Science owns our scoring models, including product-qualified lead scoring. Partner with them on marketing-qualified lead scoring by bringing in enrichment data, marketing engagement and Sales feedback, and help set the thresholds that trigger action. Make sure scores and their reasons reach Salesforce on time and that Sales understands them.

 - Close the feedback loop. Track the funnel from lead creation to closed-won. Find where leads stall, which sources and signals predict pipeline, and whether our qualification criteria still hold, then feed that back into routing, Marketing programs and Data Science's scoring work. Capture the campaign and touchpoint data behind attribution, which the Head of Pipeline Operations owns.

 - Help deliver the BDR prospecting toolset. It combines vendor solutions and internal applications. The Head of Pipeline Operations owns these systems, and BDR leadership decides the sequences and plays that run on them. Implement the vendor tools and integrate them with Salesforce and our data. Build the workflows and agents around them, such as signal-triggered alerts, prioritized outreach queues and pre-call research briefs. Resolve the system and data issues that slow reps down. Supply our GTM Platform team, which builds our rep-facing applications, with the data, signals and requirements they need. Talk to users, track adoption and retire what doesn't get used.

 - Partner across the business. Work with Marketing, Growth, BDR and Sales leadership, Data Science, Data Engineering, GTM Platform and Sales Systems to turn messy processes into durable systems, and use the scores and product usage signals Data Science and Growth publish to drive routing.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

In your first 30 days:

 - Audit enrichment coverage, routing rules, warehouse-to-Salesforce syncs and lead SLAs, and document the gaps that cost us pipeline.

In your first 60 days:

 - Take ownership of the syncs that write scores and lead fields to Salesforce, with monitoring and one owner per field.

 - Work with Data Science to bring enrichment and marketing engagement data into MQL scoring.

9a29f33aa95b.title: Member of Technical Staff (Web Access Engineer, Search Crawler)
9a29f33aa95b.description:
Perplexity is hiring a Web Access Engineer for the Crawler team to build reliable fetching and rendering systems for AI-powered search. You'll work on freely available public web content, within site permissions and approved access policies, and develop the infrastructure that supplies content to downstream indexing and retrieval systems.

Your focus will be diagnosing network errors, page-loading issues, and incomplete rendering. You'll trace problems from network protocols through client-side execution, distinguish technical failures from intentional access restrictions, and turn findings into production fixes that improve content quality and efficiency at scale.



Responsibilities

 - Own fetching and rendering improvements end to end, from investigation through implementation and production rollout, partnering with crawler engineers and SREs.

 - Investigate fetch and rendering failures across DNS, TLS, HTTP, caching, redirects, and client-side rendering, and classify root causes.

 - Improve page loading, completion detection, and content capture to preserve relevant content and handle dynamic pages reliably.

 - Ensure the crawler respects site-imposed access restrictions and rate limits, identifies itself clearly, and retries only transient technical errors.

 - Build tools to reproduce failures, compare crawler output against expected page content, and turn findings into regression tests.

 - Define metrics for fetching reliability, content completeness, and error classification, and use them to prioritize improvements.
   
   

Qualifications

 - 5+ years of software engineering experience in web infrastructure, browsers, CDNs, or crawling, with strong programming skills in at least one of Go, Python, Rust, or C++.

 - Deep understanding of HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and HTTP/3, including status semantics, caching, conditional requests, content encoding, and redirects; strong knowledge of TLS, DNS, cookies, and sessions.

 - Understanding of CDN caching and content delivery, HTTP error handling, retry backoff, and server-defined rate limits.

 - Knowledge of page lifecycle, network idle, service workers, client-side rendering, and shadow DOM; experience debugging JavaScript and fluency with Chrome DevTools, CDP, HAR files, curl, and packet captures.

 - Comfort working independently when the path forward is not fully defined.

Nice to have

 - Experience developing CDN, caching, or web performance systems.

 - Experience operating crawlers, headless browsers, or distributed content-acquisition systems at scale.

 - Contributions to a browser engine or JavaScript runtime.

60111103d128.title: Member of Technical Staff (Site Reliability Engineer, Search Crawler)
60111103d128.description:
Keeping a crawler running is not the same as keeping it productive. Queues can grow while servers look healthy, and a small change can become a fleet-wide bottleneck. On Perplexity's Crawler team, you'll improve throughput, plan capacity, and build operational reliability through safer deployments, better observability, and durable fixes.



Responsibilities

 - Operate and optimize Kubernetes workloads and supporting infrastructure for crawler services, including fetching and rendering fleets.

 - Build and maintain infrastructure as code and CI/CD pipelines, with safe rollouts, validation, and fast rollback.

 - Define SLOs and build monitoring, alerting, and observability for availability, latency, throughput, and resource saturation.

 - Own capacity planning and resource efficiency; diagnose queue backlogs, network failures, and resource bottlenecks with service owners.

 - Participate in the team's on-call rotation, lead incident response, and turn blameless postmortems into durable reliability improvements.

 - Write production software to automate diagnosis and routine remediation, with validation and approval gates for high-impact actions.



Qualifications

 - 5+ years of experience in SRE, production engineering, or infrastructure-heavy backend roles, with strong programming skills in Python, C++, Rust, or Go.

 - Hands-on experience with cloud infrastructure, production Kubernetes, infrastructure as code such as Terraform, and automated deployment workflows.

 - Strong Linux and networking fundamentals, including TCP/IP, DNS, TLS, HTTP, and load balancing.

 - Experience building observability with tools such as Datadog, Prometheus, or Grafana, and using SLOs to guide reliability improvements.

 - Proven experience diagnosing distributed-system failures, leading production incidents, and improving system performance or resource efficiency.



Nice to have

 - Experience operating web crawlers, search infrastructure, or browser fleets at scale.

 - Experience with distributed queues, backpressure, workload isolation, or multi-region recovery.

2c1e6e6cc2a4.title: Information Security Engineer - Infrastructure Security
2c1e6e6cc2a4.description:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


The Role
We're looking for an Information Security Engineer who can think broadly about how infrastructure is built, attacked, defended, and improved. You may have deep experience in one area—such as endpoint security, Active Directory, Data Loss Prevention, cloud security, identity, or detection and response—but you’re motivated by solving security problems across the environment.

As an Information Security Engineer focused on infrastructure security, you'll help protect Palantir's global endpoints, servers, identity systems, applications, networks, and data flows. You'll work across teams to reduce attack surface, improve defensive controls, investigate security events, and turn security findings into durable architectural and operational improvements.

This is not just a corporate security role; the adversaries we face are sophisticated. We need someone who understands both the details and the broader system: how a weakness in one part of the environment can create risk somewhere else, how controls interact, and how to build security improvements that hold up in practice.

Core Responsibilities
Design, implement, and improve security controls across endpoints, servers, identity systems, cloud services, SaaS applications, networks, and data flows. Drive security posture improvements through hardening standards, configuration management, vulnerability remediation, access controls, monitoring, and ongoing validation. Assess security risks in new platforms, products, architectures, vendors, and services, and turn findings into practical recommendations and engineering work. Build and maintain automation for security operations, including configuration validation, drift monitoring, patching, access reviews, policy enforcement, alert triage, and security hygiene. Partner with Identity, Infrastructure, Engineering, Legal, and other Information Security teams to strengthen security architecture and address recurring risks. Turn insights from assessments, red team exercises, incident investigations, and operational reviews into durable fixes, such as configuration changes, architectural improvements, policy updates, and automation. Build expertise in one or more security domains while contributing across the broader infrastructure security lifecycle.
What We're Looking For
Experience securing one or more major infrastructure domains, such as Windows, macOS, Linux, Active Directory, cloud platforms, SaaS applications, networking, identity systems, or enterprise endpoints. A broad infrastructure security mindset and curiosity about systems beyond your primary area of expertise. Familiarity with common infrastructure attack paths, adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures, and the controls used to prevent, detect, and contain them. The ability to assess complex environments and recognize how weaknesses across identity, endpoints, applications, networks, cloud services, or data flows can combine to create risk. Experience evaluating security tools and validating that controls are deployed effectively and continue to work as intended. Familiarity with infrastructure-as-code, configuration management, CI/CD, or other approaches to making security controls repeatable and scalable.
What We Value
The ability to own projects, make progress through ambiguity, and balance competing priorities while working well with colleagues. Experience in complex, high-assurance, regulated, or rapidly changing environments. Comfort moving between strategic problem-solving and hands-on technical work. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical risks and work with partner teams to drive remediation. Contributions to security programs, tooling, automation, incident investigations, or technical research—whether public or internal.
What We Require
5+ years of hands-on experience in information security, infrastructure security, security engineering, security operations, or a closely related field. Demonstrated experience securing at least one major infrastructure or security domain, with the ability and interest to work across multiple domains. Active TS/SCI security clearance, or eligibility and willingness to obtain one. A strong sense of ownership, sound judgment, and integrity.
Life at Palantir
 
We want every Palantirian to achieve their best outcomes, that’s why we celebrate individuals’ strengths, skills, and interests, from your first interview to your longterm growth, rather than rely on traditional career ladders. Paying attention to the needs of our community enables us to optimize our opportunities to grow and helps ensure many pathways to success at Palantir. Promoting health and well-being across all areas of Palantirians’ lives is just one of the ways we’re investing in our community. Learn more at Life at Palantir and note that our offerings may vary by region.
 
In keeping consistent with Palantir’s values and culture, we believe employees are “better together” and in-person work affords the opportunity for more creative outcomes. Therefore, we encourage employees to work from our offices to foster connectivity and innovation. Many teams do offer hybrid options (WFH a day or two a week), allowing our employees to strike the right trade-off for their personal productivity. Based on business need, there are a few roles that allow for “Remote” work on an exceptional basis. If you are applying for one of these roles, you must work from the city and or country in which you are employed. If the posting is specified as Onsite, you are required to work from an office.
 
If you want to empower the world's most important institutions, you belong here. Palantir values

Our vision is to create a culture of continuous excellence in managing vulnerabilities. What you’ll do You’ll build the systems that identify and prioritize vulnerabilities across Stripe’s codebases, production infrastructure, and employee laptops. Alongside this engineering work, you’ll help teams across Stripe understand their exposure, prioritize fixes, and drive remediation. The role combines building data pipelines and security automation with hands-on vulnerability analysis and security guidance for partner teams. The typical balance of hands-on work is about 70% coding and 30% reasoning about security issues or providing guidance to partner teams. ABOUT THE TEAM

The ChatGPT Finances team builds experiences that help people connect their financial accounts, understand their financial picture, and ask useful questions about their finances through ChatGPT.

Our work spans account connectivity, data ingestion, dashboards, personalized insights, and conversational experiences. We collaborate across product, design, research, infrastructure, security, and data integrations to make complex financial information understandable and actionable.

This is an early and ambitious product area with a substantial roadmap. We are looking for engineers who want to shape both the first user experiences and the durable systems required to earn and keep users’ trust.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for full-stack product engineers to build and scale ChatGPT Finances. You will own features across the stack—from polished frontend experiences to the APIs, services, and data models that power them.

This role is well suited to engineers who combine strong product judgment with broad technical depth. You should care about how quickly users can understand their financial lives, how reliably data moves through the system, and how AI can answer financial questions in a grounded, transparent, and useful way.

You will work closely with product, design, research, infrastructure, security, and data integration teams to take ideas from early prototypes to reliable production experiences.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL

 - Own full-stack product features from user experience and frontend implementation through backend services, data models, deployment, and observability.

 - Build polished, accessible, and performant interfaces for account connection, dashboards, insights, and conversational workflows.

 - Design APIs and backend systems that safely ingest, normalize, and serve financial data.

 - Build resilient integrations that handle synchronization, data freshness, partial failures, permissions, and user consent.

 - Bring new AI capabilities into production while prioritizing grounding, accuracy, transparency, and user control.

 - Establish architecture, performance standards, testing practices, and operational safeguards for a fast-growing product area.

 - Debug and improve complex behavior across client, server, infrastructure, and external integrations.

 - Use qualitative feedback, product metrics, and experiments to improve user outcomes without compromising clarity or trust.

 - Collaborate across disciplines to turn ambiguous product opportunities into simple, reliable experiences.




YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU

 - Have experience building and shipping full-stack consumer products in production.

 - Are comfortable working in a modern frontend stack and building the APIs and services behind it.

 - Care deeply about product craftsmanship, performance, accessibility, and details that affect the user experience.

 - Understand API design, data modeling, system reliability, and the tradeoffs involved in evolving production systems.

 - Can move effectively between frontend, backend, and product decisions rather than remaining in a narrow implementation area.

 - Have strong product judgment and can take a feature from a rough idea to a shipped, measurable outcome.

 - Work well in ambiguous, high-impact areas where the product and technical architecture are still taking shape.

 - Think carefully about privacy, security, reliability, and user trust when working with sensitive data.

 - Enjoy diagnosing problems across system boundaries and improving the underlying engineering foundations.

 - Are interested in AI-native interfaces and new ways to make complex personal information easier to understand.

 - Experience operating consumer products or distributed systems at scale.

 - Experience with fintech, personal finance, banking, payments, investing, or sensitive-data domain.

 - Familiarity with authentication, identity, permissions, privacy, and secure data flows.

 - Experience building dashboards, data visualizations, or insight-oriented products.

We're looking for a hands-on Software Engineer to build these products end to end, from the security logic and agent workflows to the integrations and product surfaces customers use. You'll ship to design partners and enterprise customers quickly, and you'll work directly with the security engineers who do this work internally, so what we build is grounded in real codebases, real environments, and real attackers.



RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Build security products from zero to one across domains such as application security, penetration testing and offensive security, cloud security, and detection and response.

 - Build agents that do real security work: review code and find vulnerabilities, test applications and infrastructure like an attacker, assess cloud configurations, and investigate threats, then validate findings and recommend or apply fixes.

 - Build the systems underneath: multi-tenant services, data pipelines, and secure execution environments that run against customer code, cloud accounts, and telemetry.

 - Build integrations with the tools customers already use: source control and CI/CD, cloud providers, identity providers, security tools, ticketing, and chat.

 - Ship the product surfaces customers use: APIs, dashboards, onboarding, and workflows that fit how security and engineering teams actually work.

 - Hold the product to the same standard we hold ourselves: strong tenant isolation, least privilege, safe handling of customer secrets and data, and tight controls on any agent that acts in a customer environment.

 - Define how we measure quality (finding accuracy, false positive rate, exploitability, time to fix, cost) and use it to drive improvements.

 - Work directly with design partners and customers, and help decide which security problems we should build products for next.
   
   

QUALIFICATIONS

 - 4+ years of experience as a software engineer building production systems, with meaningful time spent on security products, security data platforms, or security engineering with heavy software development.

 - Proficiency in at least one major programming language (such as Python, Go, TypeScript, or Rust) and experience owning production services end to end.

 - Hands-on depth in at least one security domain, such as application security, penetration testing or offensive security, cloud security, or detection and response, and curiosity to work across the others.

 - Experience integrating with security- or developer-relevant systems such as source control, CI/CD, cloud provider APIs, identity providers, scanners, or SIEMs.

 - Familiarity with cloud infrastructure (AWS preferred) and building secure, multi-tenant SaaS.

 - Comfortable working directly with customers and shipping pragmatic improvements quickly in an ambiguous, early-stage product area.

 - Bonus: experience building LLM-powered agents, evaluation frameworks, or tool-using automation for security or other high-stakes domains.

 - Bonus: experience at a security product company (AppSec, pentesting, cloud security, detection and response) or on an internal security platform at scale.

f771fe365fd2.title: Forward Deployed Software Engineer - AUS Government
f771fe365fd2.description:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


The Role
 
Forward Deployed Software Engineers (FDSEs) work directly with customers to quickly understand their greatest problems and design and implement solutions to use data against them. Our customers rely on Palantir’s platforms for some of their most critical operations, and projects often start with an open ended question like “Why are we delaying so many flights?” or “How can we better identify instances of money laundering?” As an FDSE, you’ll apply your problem solving ability, creativity, and technical skills to help organizations use their data to drive a real impact in the world. You’ll have the opportunity to gain rare insight into and contribute to some of the world’s most important industries and institutions.
 
As an FDSE your responsibilities look similar to those of a startup CTO: you’ll work in small teams with minimal supervision and own end-to-end execution of high stakes projects. Your day might span discussing architecture with fellow engineers, wrangling massive-scale data, coding a custom web app, speaking with customer executives, or establishing strategy for your team.
 
Whether you aspire to be an entrepreneur or an engineering leader, we believe Palantir is the best place — with the best colleagues — to learn how. You’ll learn how to unpack a problem and understand the costs and consequences of its solution. You’ll learn new technologies and languages, and even develop them yourself. You’ll work autonomously and make decisions independently, within a community that will support and challenge you as you grow and develop.

Our Principles
Impact: We take on meaningful and challenging projects that change the world for the better. Ownership: We see projects through from beginning to end, working through any obstacles we may encounter. Collaboration: We work internally with people from a variety of backgrounds — such as other FDSEs, product teams, and Deployment Strategists. We also work externally with our customers, often on-site, to understand and solve their problems. Trust: We trust each other to effectively manage time and priorities and give people the space to think for themselves. Growth: We encourage ourselves and our peers to seek new challenges and opportunities for growth, as well as find new ways to innovate and share knowledge. Learning: We often face entirely novel problems where we need to pick up a lot of new knowledge and learn how to use it to make progress. We believe experiential learning is one of the best teachers.
What We Value
Strong engineering background, preferred in fields such as Computer Science, Mathematics, Software Engineering, Physics, and Data Science. A highly analytical mindset and eagerness to solve technical problems with data structures, storage systems, cloud infrastructure, front-end frameworks, and other technical tools. Experience or interest in working with and using large scale data to solve valuable business problems. Strong coder with demonstrated proficiency in programming languages such as Python, Java, C++, TypeScript/JavaScript, or similar. Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively in teams of technical and non-technical individuals, and comfortable working in a rapidly changing environment with dynamic objectives and iteration with users. Ability to continuously learn, work independently, and make decisions with minimal supervision. Willingness and interest to travel as needed to client sites. Ability to travel 25-50% preferred, but requirements vary by team and location. Veterans encouraged to apply.
What We Require
1+ years of relevant, post-college work experience. Strong engineering background, preferred in fields such as Computer Science, Mathematics, Software Engineering, Physics, and Data Science. Strong coder with shown proficiency in programming languages such as Python, Java, C++, TypeScript/JavaScript, or similar. Ability and interest to travel up to 25%, as needed to client sites, but flexible based on personal preferences. Active Security Clearance
Life at Palantir
 
We want every Palantirian to achieve their best outcomes, that’s why we celebrate individuals’ strengths, skills, and interests, from your first interview to your longterm growth, rather than rely on traditional career ladders. Paying attention to the needs of our community enables us to optimize our opportunities to grow and helps ensure many pathways to success at Palantir. Promoting health and well-being across all areas of Palantirians’ lives is just one of the ways we’re investing in our community. Learn more at Life at Palantir and note that our offerings may vary by region.
 
In keeping consistent with Palantir’s values and culture, we believe employees are “better together” and in-person work affords the opportunity for more creative outcomes. Therefore, we encourage employees to work from our offices to foster connectivity and innovation. Many teams do offer hybrid options (WFH a day or two a week), allowing our employees to strike the right trade-off for their personal productivity. Based on business need, there are a few roles that allow for “Remote” work on an exceptional basis. If you are applying for one of these roles, you must work from the city and or country in which you are employed. If the posting is specified as Onsite, you are required to work from an office.
 
If you want to empower the world's most important institutions, you belong here. Palantir values excellence regardless of background. We are committed to making the application and hiring process accessible to everyone and will provide a reasonable accommodation for those living with a disability. If you need an accommodation for the application or hi

You will be part of the Provisioning & Licensing team, the vital "glue team" between our business functions and the core platform.

  • The team owns the latency-sensitive internal APIs for automatically creating new tenants based on customer data, as well as our internal Feature & Configuration system (like a car configurator, just for microservices!).

Our stack is modern, cloud-native, and focused on portability to support our strategic on-premise deployments.

  • Core Technologies: Java 25, Spring Boot, Postgres as the main datastore.
  • Containerization: We are all in on containerization and orchestration, running our applications on Kubernetes (K8s).
  • Architecture: We develop within a new & modern modular monolithic application with strongly enforced boundaries between the modules.
  • DevOps: Writing deployment files with the help of Kustomize and deploying our applications with Github CI and Kargo. We use Datadog for metrics, logs, and as our APM tool.
