b610d3809f0f.title: Partner Applied AI Engineer, AWS
b610d3809f0f.description:
About the team

The Applied AI Engineering team ensures the safe and effective deployment of Generative AI applications for developers and enterprises. We serve as trusted technical advisors, helping customers and partners move from early experimentation to production-scale AI systems.

As a Partner Applied AI Engineer focused on AWS, you will operate at the center of one of our most strategic partnerships, driving joint customer success and enabling AWS and partner ecosystems to scale adoption of OpenAI-powered solutions.

 

About the role

We are looking for a highly experienced technical leader to serve as the primary technical counterpart to AWS field leadership (Solutions Architects, Specialists, and Partner teams).

This role goes beyond individual deal support—you will shape strategy, define engagement models, and build repeatable systems that scale across AWS globally. You will work across pre- and post-sales, guiding complex enterprise customers from ideation to production while enabling AWS and partners to independently drive deployments.

You will combine deep technical expertise, strong judgment, and ecosystem leadership to maximize impact across a portfolio of high-priority opportunities.

 

This preference is that this person is based in our New York, NY office but open to remote (US-East). We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

 

In this role, you will:


STRATEGIC AWS ENGAGEMENT & INFLUENCE

 - Serve as the senior technical counterpart to AWS field leadership, building trust and credibility across regions and teams.

 - Influence joint account strategy and technical direction for high-priority opportunities.

 - Shape how OpenAI engages with AWS by defining engagement models, prioritization frameworks, and best practices.

 - Proactively identify and drive net-new opportunities and high-impact use cases across the AWS ecosystem.


COMPLEX DEAL LEADERSHIP & EXECUTION

 - Lead technical strategy for large, ambiguous, and high-stakes enterprise engagements.

 - Guide customers from early ideation through architecture design, prototyping, and production deployment.

 - Act as a technical decision-maker and escalation point, de-risking complex implementations.

 - Apply strong judgment to prioritize opportunities and allocate limited technical resources for maximum impact.


SOLUTION ARCHITECTURE & HANDS-ON BUILDING

 - Design and communicate end-to-end AI architectures leveraging OpenAI and AWS services.

 - Build and guide development of prototypes, POCs, and reference implementations to accelerate adoption.

 - Establish best practices for scalable, secure, and production-ready GenAI systems.

 - Ensure solutions are designed for repeatability, extensibility, and partner-led delivery.


ECOSYSTEM ENABLEMENT & SCALE

 - Enable AWS and partners through scalable technical motions (workshops, playbooks, reference architectures, demos).

 - Develop reusable solution patterns and assets that can be deployed independently by AWS teams and SIs.

 - Mentor and uplift partner technical teams, accelerating their path to self-sufficiency.

020f62fa3f55.title: Staff Software Engineer, Data Infrastructure
020f62fa3f55.description:
WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!


WHY THIS ROLE?

The Data Infrastructure team at Cohere is responsible for the storage and data movement layer underlying every model training run. We're building the unified storage layer that feeds our training workloads at petabyte scale. In this role, you would have the opportunity to architect and lead the design of this system from the ground up, serving petabytes of training data and model checkpoints fast enough to keep thousands of GPUs busy across several training clusters. You'd be a key contributor, leading the effort to solve a problem few teams have tackled at this scale.


IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Design, architect, and operate the distributed storage system that feeds model training and evaluation, driving the technical vision from concept through production.

 - Lead and own the deployment of this system across multiple Kubernetes clusters at petabyte scale, setting standards and best practices for the organization.

 - Collaborate with researchers and training-infra teams to define how jobs read and write data, translating those patterns into throughput, latency, and durability requirements that shape the platform's roadmap.

 - Navigate the networking, I/O, and consistency challenges of moving large datasets and checkpoints across regions and backends, with GPU idle time and time-to-insight as the key metrics of success — and drive the solutions that improve them.


YOU MAY BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU HAVE:

 - Strong storage fundamentals, including replication, consistency, caching, and data lifecycle management, with demonstrated architecture and design experience.

 - Strong coding ability in Python and Go, with the ability to lead implementations and mentor others in either language, and the willingness to contribute to the other.

 - Proven experience running stateful systems on Kubernetes, including Persistent Volumes, CSI drivers, and StatefulSets, with the capacity to design and execute operational strategies.

 - Hands-on experience with cloud object storage such as S3 as well as POSIX-style filesystems.


IT’S A BONUS IF YOU HAVE:

 - Experience with parallel or HPC filesystems such as Weka, VAST, or Lustre, and a track record of applying them at scale.

 - Familiarity with the data-loading and checkpointing patterns used in large-scale model training, with the ability to innovate on them.

 - An interest in how large models are trained and evaluated, including the trajectory and eval data those runs generate, and a desire to understand the workloads the platform is serving — with the capacity to guide others in that understanding.




FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS:

 - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

 - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.

 - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

 - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.

 - Annual enrichment benefits:
   
   Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.
   
   Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

 - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)

 - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.




HOW AND WHERE WE WORK:

 - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.

 - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.

 - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.

 - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.
   
   

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. 


We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12a6IrLdF3kI2nonKSr4tiFuz18rLQbaeYV-JM9L4o9Q/edit, and we will work together to meet your needs.



We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider.



Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers https://cohere.com/careers page.

8334b06357c5.title: Member of Technical Staff (Enterprise Security Engineer)
8334b06357c5.description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

Perplexity is growing fast, and every new employee, laptop, SaaS app and integration expands what we have to protect. We want enterprise security that's strong by default, mostly automated, and invisible to people doing their jobs.



We're looking for an Enterprise Security Engineer to own the security of how Perplexity works internally: our identities, devices, SaaS applications and corporate access. You'll sit on the Security Engineering team and work closely with IT, building controls and automation together so the secure path is also the easy one.



RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own identity security: SSO and MFA policy, conditional access and device trust, privileged and admin access, service accounts, and break-glass procedures.

 - Harden our SaaS stack. Manage OAuth app and integration risk, admin roles, sharing and retention settings, and audit logging across our core collaboration and productivity tools.

 - Define and enforce endpoint security baselines with IT, across EDR, device management, disk encryption, OS and browser policy, and software allowlisting.

 - Build access governance that scales: just-in-time and request-based access, regular access reviews, and joiner/mover/leaver automation that removes access promptly and reliably.

 - Write detections for corporate threats such as account takeover, OAuth abuse, data exfiltration, insider risk and malicious extensions, and respond when they fire.

 - Automate everything you can. Write code and infrastructure-as-code to configure systems, remediate drift, and replace manual tickets with self-service workflows.

 - Secure corporate network access and email, including zero-trust remote access, phishing protection and domain security.

 - Partner with IT, People, Legal and GRC on new tools and vendors, security reviews, and evidence for compliance programs.



QUALIFICATIONS

 - 4+ years in security engineering, with significant time on corporate or enterprise security, identity, or endpoint security.

 - Hands-on depth with at least one major identity provider (such as Okta or Entra ID), including SSO, SCIM, MFA and conditional access policy.

 - Experience securing SaaS environments such as Google Workspace or Microsoft 365, Slack, and developer tools, including OAuth and third-party app risk.

 - Experience with endpoint security and device management across macOS (and ideally Windows and Linux), including EDR, MDM and configuration baselines.

 - Proficiency in at least one programming language (such as Python or Go) and comfort building automation against vendor APIs. Experience with infrastructure-as-code is a plus.

 - Experience writing detections and investigating incidents with a SIEM or log platform.

 - Good judgment about trade-offs between security and productivity, and the ability to roll out controls without slowing the company down.

 - Bonus: experience at a fast-growing company where you built enterprise security from an early stage.

 - Bonus: experience securing AI tools and agents in the workplace, such as agent access to SaaS data, browser agents, and AI app governance.

d7fb09b7c19b.description: Platform Associate (m/f/d): Talent, Growth, Content & AI Workflows Remote, with offices in Munich and Karlsruhe · Start January or February 2027 About us First Momentum invests in deep tech and industrial tech founders across Europe at pre-seed when there's more lab than traction. We've made 40+ investments into industries like energy, space, industrial, and semicon, and our companies went on to raise from Khosla Ventures, Sequoia, or Insight Partners. We're a team of engineers, scientists, and operators on a mission to build a different kind of VC fund. Our goal isn't the biggest fund or the loudest headlines, but to be the VC deeply technical teams need and deserve at inception. Someone who truly understands their tech, is humble and candid, and connects them with the relevant people they need at a given stage, be it a designer or a pilot customer. You won't find us at the after-party; instead, we're obsessing over good reads, fast bikes, and the latest moonshots we want to bring to life. Your tasks For us, platform is like a product with multiple customer groups: founders, LPs, Scouts, and the investment team. While we get inspired by playbooks and what other funds are doing, we treat them as what they are: past successes. For us, platform is much more similar to what our portfolio teams are doing: building products and driving growth, whether for our fund or our portcos. We come up with new ideas, identify the most impactful ones, test them, measure, iterate, or drop them and rerun the entire sprint. Your north star: helping our portfolio founders succeed through intros, hires, and any other random request. We measure ourselves on support per euro invested. Much of that support runs through the Platform team. Call it Founder's Associate , Chief of Staff , Venture Ops , GTM , or Growth . Here, it means you take on some of the most pressing problems of our portfolio companies and the fund operations. You'll work with several super-technical, highly humble founders and the investment team at once. Hiring for the portfolio: The first 10 people shape a startup more than anything else. You run multiple outbound campaigns in parallel, from sourcing and outreach to the final intro, and learn each field well enough to find the best talent. Sometimes that means building teams from zero for our incubation projects; previous ones: Telura (deep geothermal) and Starforge (fusion energy). Content and website: You turn the technical and industry expertise from First Momentum's investment team and portfolio news (funding rounds, launches, technical results) into content for LinkedIn, our blog, and our newsletter. You also own our Webflow site and how AI search finds us. European deep tech community: You grow our community of 100+ technical Venture Scouts and bring them into hiring and deals. You support in-person events like our annual meeting and help co-organize the European Spinoff Summit in Munich. Tooling and workflows: If you've done something by hand twice, you build a Claude skill or automation for it the third time. Your profile 1–2 years of hands-on work at a startup, VC, recruiting firm, or similar Sourcing or outbound experience, whether in recruiting or in sales/GTM You write well in German and English (full working proficiency in both) You can run 10+ workstreams at once without daily steering and know where the 80/20 is You're fast, friendly, and specific with founders, partners, and candidates You like building generally, also with AI tools, BUT know when not to use them and when your own judgment beats the model's You're curious about many fields and fine switching from a Head of Biology search to a blog post to a website fix in one afternoon A good eye for design What we offer Work with people building fusion reactors and foundation models You work with the teams behind 40+ deep tech companies and with our partners from day one. See Technology 5–10 years earlier You see what comes straight out of research labs long before most people meet it in a product. Your next job is already in the portfolio You'll get to know dozens of startups from the inside. If at some time you feel like moving on, you’ll have a great network to rely on, but we will also actively help. If you want, you can stay part of First Momentum after your time with us through our Venture Scout program. Some Scouts have since joined Y Combinator, built $20M-funded robotics spinouts, or moved to Anthropic's design team. More here: https://www.firstmomentum.vc/venture-scouts Room to build New tools, workflows, and formats. If it works, it stays. You'll have few meetings, coordinate mostly async, and plan your own week. Five fields in one job Recruiting, content, design, web, and AI tooling. Most people with 1–2 years of experience get to work in one of them. Remote Culture Our team is spread across Germany, Austria, the UK, and Spain. We don't hire local optimum but hire the best people wherever they are in Europe. To work together and have some fun, we meet every two months for our team days. 1818846a5322.title: Founder's Associate Intern
1818846a5322.description: Als Founders Associate Intern arbeitest du direkt an der Seite des Founding Teams und bist in die wichtigsten strategischen und operativen Themen eingebunden. Du entwickelst neue Ideen und Geschäftsansätze mit und bringst sie hands-on in die Umsetzung. Dabei übernimmst du von Anfang an Verantwortung, treibst eigene Projekte voran und sorgst dafür, dass aus Ideen konkrete Ergebnisse werden. Neben Business Development und Business Operations bist du auch im Daily Business eng eingebunden und koordinierst wichtige Schnittstellen zu Investoren, Banken und weiteren Stakeholdern. Wir suchen bewusst keine klassische Praktikantin bzw. keinen klassischen Praktikanten, sondern jemanden mit Entrepreneurial Mindset und echtem Drive, der Lust hat, ein Unternehmen von Anfang an mit aufzubauen. Die Rolle ist dabei mehr als ein Praktikum: Unser Ziel ist es, die Person im Anschluss idealerweise als ersten Full-Time Hire langfristig ins Team zu holen. Worum es geht Die Energiewende braucht Kapital. Gleichzeitig wächst in Deutschland der Markt für Erneuerbare-Energie-Projekte – doch die passende Finanzierung kommt noch viel zu selten effizient zustande. Was bislang fehlt, ist ein Tech-Layer, der Investoren, Projektentwickler und Banken intelligent miteinander verbindet. Wir glauben, dass darin enormes Potenzial steckt. Deshalb arbeiten wir aktuell im Stealth Mode an einer neuen Lösung, die genau hier ansetzt. Dafür suchen wir Menschen, die Lust haben, von Anfang an Verantwortung zu übernehmen, eigene Ideen einzubringen und die Entwicklung aktiv mitzugestalten. Mehr über unsere Vision und das, woran wir arbeiten, erzählen wir dir gerne im persönlichen Gespräch. Was du in den 6 Monaten machst Ein großer Teil deiner Arbeit besteht darin, das Tagesgeschäft am Laufen zu halten, Themen eigenständig voranzutreiben und dafür zu sorgen, dass wir als Unternehmen immer schneller werden. Gleichzeitig arbeitest du eng mit dem Founding Team an strategischen Fragestellungen und entwickelst die Hypothesen mit, die unsere Richtung und unser Wachstum bestimmen. Operations: Du steuerst den Prozess mit Investoren von der ersten Anfrage bis zum Finanzierungsabschluss. Dabei koordinierst du die dazugehörigen Prozesse und entwickelst unsere operativen Abläufe weiter. Strategie: Gemeinsam mit dem Founding Team entwickelst du unsere Unternehmensstrategie weiter und baust das Finanzmodell auf, mit dem wir unser Wachstum planen und steuern. AI und Automatisierung: Du baust mit AI und No-Code-Tools, automatisierst Prozesse und bringst unsere Plattform auf das nächste Level. Go-to-Market: Du arbeitest aktiv an unserem Markteintritt mit, identifizierst potenzielle Partner und baust Beziehungen zu Banken und anderen Finanzierern auf. Was du mitbringst Idealerweise hast du deinen Bachelor oder Master abgeschlossen oder bist kurz vor dem Abschluss. Das ist aber keine zwingende Voraussetzung. Erste Praktika in Start-ups, Beratung oder Venture Capital. Erfahrung in Finance oder im Bereich erneuerbare Energien ist ein Plus. Du denkst unternehmerisch, erkennst Probleme und wartest nicht darauf, dass dir jemand die Lösung vorgibt. Du arbeitest täglich mit AI-Tools und setzt neue Tools direkt in deiner Arbeit ein. Du triffst Entscheidungen auch dann, wenn nicht alle Informationen vorliegen, und stehst für das Ergebnis ein. Die Energiewende interessiert dich. Fließendes Deutsch und Englisch Eher nicht passend, wenn ... du suchst ein klassisches Praktikum mit klar abgegrenzten Aufgaben und festen Routinen. du fühlst dich wohler mit klaren Vorgaben, statt eigene Lösungen zu entwickeln. du lieber auf Freigaben wartest, als selbst anzufangen. dich Rückschläge schnell aus der Bahn werfen. In einem frühen Unternehmen läuft vieles nicht beim ersten Mal, und Probleme landen oft ungefiltert auf dem Tisch. du den ganzen Tag nur an der großen Strategie feilen willst. Der Alltag in der Early Stage besteht zum Großteil aus Umsetzung, auch bei den Gründern. 3d8f44f22c3c.description: Help us use technology to make a big green dent in the universe! Kraken powers some of the most innovative global developments in energy. We create the technology that redefines utilities and unlocks a new energy system of the future. By optimising renewable generation, building a more intelligent grid, and empowering utilities to deliver an exceptional customer experience, our operating system is transforming the industry worldwide. It’s an incredibly exciting time to work in energy. Join us on our mission to improve the lives of ONE BILLION humans within the decade and shape a cleaner, better future for everyone. You'll be assessed by/ join an English speaking team- please submit your application in English 🐙 Kraken Generation Flex The energy industry is undergoing the largest transformation since industrialisation, at an unprecedented rate of change and we are positioning ourselves at the heart of it. In Germany, home to the largest electricity market in Europe and a roadmap toward Net Zero by 2045, we are scaling rapidly to integrate Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) into the grid. Kraken is recognised as a thought leader and innovator. We are building a SaaS business that digitally connects hundreds of thousands of DERs with energy markets. As we expand our footprint in Germany and the wider European market, we are looking for a Senior Electrical Engineer to lead our regional technical market-access and integration efforts. 🏠 Where you’ll fit in and role summary As we enter a stage of rapid commercialisation and customer growth in Germany, we are looking for a Senior Electrical Engineer to work with stakeholders to develop our DSR (Demand Side Response) and flexibility pipeline. You will be bringing your regional technical expertise to aid the development of our asset integration technologies. The role is highly cross-functional: you'll bridge our software and hardware capabilities with the rigorous requirements of the four German Transmission System Operators (TSOs) and 900+ Distribution System Operators (DSOs). The detailed Gateway (Kraken’s IoT Edge Hardware&Software) configuration and protocol engineering is owned by our UK-based team, whom you will feed with regional knowledge and design input, and who will support you on the technical aspects of how Kraken integrations work. You will own the regional relationship, the integration approach, and the design that the UK team then implements. The role may require you to attend customer calls, as well as calls with the TSO and DSOs to technically explain/defend our strategy. You will join a team, based in Manchester, that is innovative and engineering-focused, with a culture that fosters collaboration and fresh thinking to create a new energy system. 🚀 What you'll own Market Access & Prequalification: Drive the technical approach for connecting assets — mainly BESS (grid-scale and C&I) and RES (Wind and Solar) into German ancillary-service markets (FCR, aFRR, mFRR) and Redispatch 3.0. (Grid-code and plant-compliance obligations such as VDE-AR-N 4110/4120 remain with the plant/PPC; your focus is enabling market access, telemetry, and dispatch.) Integration Technology (your core deliverable): Carry out research, engage technical stakeholders and engineers to design our established integration approaches for various asset types such as BESS, Wind, Solar, CHP and more. This can cover both new projects and retrofits. Regional Technical Expertise: Be the regional authority who feeds and supports the UK team with knowledge of German hardware requirements, industrial protocols, connectivity, cyber-security expectations, and TSO/DSO and ancillary-service requirements. Help evaluate hardware and connectivity solutions for regional fit. Stakeholder Liaison: Act as the technical point of contact for TSOs, DSOs, customers, and internal commercial teams to resolve connection, onboarding, or operational issues. Hardware & On-site Support (occasional): Hardware is deployed remotely in most cases via O&Ms and third parties. However, occasional regional support and hands-on intervention may be required before or after a deployment, including some hardware handling and on-site engineering. You’ll ideally be based close to Kraken’s Berlin office and the role requires the ability to travel when needed, though this is kept to a minimum. 🧠 What you'll bring to the party Language: Native or professional fluency in German and English , essential for technical documentation and TSO/regulator communication. Engineering background: Bachelor's in Electrical Engineering, Automation/Control, or a related field ( or equivalent practical experience in industrial/energy integration). Integration & connectivity: Proven experience establishing industrial communication and connectivity between field equipment and external systems (telemetry and/or control). Power-plant systems: Working understanding of power-plant control systems and instrumentation, including metering. German market knowledge: TSO/DSO hierarchy and the connection/integration process. Ancillary services (FCR, aFRR, mFRR) prequalification and technical requirements. Redispatch 3.0 regulatory framework. Customer-facing delivery: Ability to produce technical integration approaches and communicate them to customers, regulators, and internal teams. Travel: Occasional travel may be required. A drive to get things done in a collaborative, agile environment , comfortable navigating the complexity of a multi-TSO, decentralised grid, and comfortable being the regional face of a technical function whose deep build sits with a partner team in the UK. ⭐️ Bonus points Knowledge of industrial communication protocols: IEC 60870-5-104, IEC 61400-25 (wind), OPC-UA, Modbus , or similar IEC protocols. da02efd299ab.title: QA Engineer - Payments
da02efd299ab.description: SumUp is already live in 38 markets and still growing. Our Global Expansion Team takes SumUp's payment products into new countries, with Mexico and Canada among our most recent launches and more markets like New Zealand and Argentina on the way. As a QA Engineer in our Berlin payments team, you'll build the automated and manual tests that decide when a new card reader can go live in a market, across frontend, backend and mobile flows, and you'll also help complete L3 certification (the final round of testing that acquiring banks and card networks require). It's hands-on engineering work with real launch impact, because your tests help new markets go live and recently launched ones stay stable, so small businesses there can take card payments with confidence. What you'll do Build and maintain frontend and backend test automation, with mobile where relevant, and add targeted regression tests to continuous integration (CI) workflows so market specific checks run consistently after code changes Test SumUp products across markets, with a mix of automated and manual testing, functional, integration and regression checks, plus edge cases and recovery scenarios. Spot ways to improve how we test, explain why they matter and make a convincing case for the changes with the biggest payoff Trace failures through complex payment flows using logs and transaction traces, then raise clear, prioritised defects and work with engineers and external partners until they're fixed Own the testing of end-to-end communication between a payment terminal, software applications, and an acquiring network. with acquiring banks and card networks, and keep the team informed on certification status, quality risks and release readiness so launch decisions rest on evidence Work closely in collaboration with engineers, product and market-launch teams, as well as acquirers, card schemes and certification labs. What you'll bring Programming or scripting skill to build and maintain automated tests for frontend web and backend APIs, and comfort reading code in languages such as Golang, Kotlin, Java or others on our Tech Radar. Experience testing software both manually and with automation, including turning requirements into test scenarios and deciding what to automate first based on customer, launch and technical risk. Ability to analyse logs, transaction traces and test results, and to write defect reports that include reproduction steps, expected versus actual behaviour, impact and evidence. Comfort working with Git and Jira (or similar tools) Experience with SQL and test-data setup, contract testing, mocking or service virtualisation. An engineering mindset: the ability to spot what can be improved, explain the reasoning and persuade others with clear evidence A curious, ownership minded approach: seeking out context when things are unclear and using AI tools where they help. Nice to have Experience with Card payments, payment terminals, acquirers, card schemes or certification labs. Market launches, device integrations, external technical partners or business-to-business communication. Payments experience is helpful but not required. We'll support you in learning card payments, devices and the certification process. Why you should join SumUp 🌎 Opportunity to work with SumUppers globally on large-scale fintech products used by millions of businesses worldwide, from our Berlin office. This involves an office-first set up 🌈 Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion: be part of a workplace that values and promotes diversity, fostering an inclusive environment where everyone's perspectives are respected and embraced 🚀 Enrolment onto our Virtual Stock Option programme: you will own a stake in SumUp's future success 📚 A dedicated annual L&D budget of €2000 for your individual development, which can be used to attend conferences and/or advance your career through further education 💶 A corporate pension scheme where we match up to 20% of your contributions 🏖️ Generous time off: enjoy 28 days of paid leave plus public holidays and special leave days 🚵🏾‍♂️ Numerous other benefits such as Urban Sports Club subsidy, Kita placement assistance, subsidised office lunches 🌴 Break4me: 1-month sabbatical after 3 years of service 🔗 Referral Bonus: earn additional rewards by referring talented individuals to join the SumUp team Job Application Tip We recognise that candidates feel they need to meet 100% of the job criteria in order to apply for a job. Please note that this is only a guide. If you don't tick every box, it's ok too because it means you have room to learn and develop your career at SumUp. Find Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

Your software runs on real hardware in the field, often within weeks of the first idea, and you work next to the hardware and embedded engineers who build the system around it. Junior engineers take ownership of well-defined components and grow quickly through work on real systems. c0af288c014e.title: Rust Product Engineer – MLS (m/f/d)
c0af288c014e.description: Do you want to bring modern end-to-end encryption to people who rely on it every day? Then we're looking for you as a Rust Product Engineer - MLS (m/f/d) on our MLS team! We're bringing Messaging Layer Security (MLS, RFC 9420) to secure messaging for the German public sector. MLS defines the cryptographic core of group messaging and leaves delivery, ordering, identity and federation to whoever integrates it. That's the part we build: a Rust SDK, the server that orders and delivers MLS messages, and its integration with Matrix. Much of it has no off-the-shelf answer yet. We're also following the IETF's MIMI effort, which aims to let different messengers interoperate over MLS, and expect it to shape how our system federates. How we work: Small team, close collaboration. At Famedly the MLS team will be four to five engineers. We build the system together with a larger group of engineers at partner companies. Ownership in small groups. Day to day you work with two or three others on a project or a part of the system, and you own it from spec to operations. AI where it helps, people where it counts. We use coding agents a lot, for implementation, tests and exploring options. Protocol design, security-relevant decisions and the final review stay with people, and we keep adjusting where that line runs. Think first, then build. Architecture decision records, specs and written invariants keep both humans and agents on track, and we check our code against them. Your responsibilities: Turn requirements from our customer, the MLS standard and Matrix into specs and architecture decisions. Decide with your team and our partners where a change belongs: the SDK, the server, or a spec proposal. Build and run server-side MLS components in Rust, including message delivery, the Matrix integration and federation between servers. Ship your work to production yourself, including in our customer's environments. Contribute to spec proposals where they affect what we build. Improve our agent workflows and share what you learn. What you should bring: At least three years of experience with Rust in production, including async Rust (Tokio or similar). You already work with coding agents every day and have your own workflows for them. Sharp judgment in code review: you notice when generated code looks plausible but is wrong, for example a race in message ordering or an error path that silently loses state. Experience with distributed systems or network protocols: ordering, consistency, failure modes. You can read an RFC and turn it into code and tests. You enjoy writing: specs, decision records, review comments. Fluent German and English. Nice to have: MLS, MIMI, Matrix, applied cryptography, experience in regulated markets (public sector, healthcare, critical infrastructure), or rigorous testing approaches such as property-based testing. Please note: For this position, we are currently only able to consider applications from candidates based in EU/EEA. Why you should work at Famedly: Work at a fast-growing startup in an exciting phase. Since 2019 we have grown rapidly and we have big plans ahead! Famedly brought the first gematik-certified TI-Messenger to market, and with your help we're now bringing MLS-secured messaging to the public sector. Meaningful ownership. Take responsibility for software people rely on every day in critical environments. Deep technical work. Help build one of the first MLS deployments in the German public sector, on a protocol whose ecosystem is still taking shape. Small, close-knit teams. Work in a small team with short decision paths. Modern AI tooling. Use up-to-date coding agents and models without having to count tokens. Your perfect work-life balance. With remote work and flexible hours, you decide when and where you are most productive. You also have the option to work from our office in Berlin. Your choice: set up your home office or use a co-working space! Attractive conditions. A permanent contract with competitive compensation, a training budget, work equipment of your choice, and 28 vacation days per year. Flexible Benefits with Probonio. You receive a monthly wellbeing budget that you can use for vouchers from a wide range of food, mobility, retail, and lifestyle partners or for a discounted membership with Urban Sports Club. A diverse and international team. We value an open mindset and a diverse, inclusive culture where everyone feels welcome. Regular team events. Workshops, team-building activities, virtual game nights, and company events such as our Summer and Winter Summit. We are a proud equal-opportunities employer and place great value on mutual tolerance and acceptance in a diverse environment. Everyone receives the same opportunities in our application process. We look forward to hearing from you! Sounds good? What are you waiting for? Apply now! We are excited to get to know you! Instead of a cover letter, send us a link to something you've built (Rust preferred) and two or three sentences about how you work with coding agents. We’re home to the UK’s largest choice of properties and are the go-to destination for millions of people planning their next move, reading the latest industry news, or just browsing what’s on the market. 

 

The role

As a Senior Platform Engineer in our Cloud Foundations team, you'll play a crucial role in designing, implementing and maintaining our cloud infrastructure on Google Cloud Platform (GCP). You'll be responsible for ensuring the scalability, security and reliability of our cloud environment, enabling Rightmove to deliver innovative solutions efficiently and cost-effectively.

What you'll be doing

  • Designing and implementing scalable, secure cloud infrastructure solutions using GCP services
  • Operating, hardening and improving critical Rightmove infrastructure
  • Architecting, implementing and maintaining infrastructure provisioning and automation through Terraform-based Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tooling
  • Implementing and managing container orchestration using Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) and Helm
  • Designing and configuring key components of our cloud network infrastructure, including CDNs, load balancers, API gateways and service mesh
  • Optimising cloud resource utilisation and implementing cost management strategies
  • Defining cloud and network security policies and ensuring compliance
  • Implementing and maintaining monitoring, logging and observability solutions for our cloud infrastructure
  • Troubleshooting and resolving complex infrastructure issues
  • Mentoring junior engineers and contributing to the team's technical growth

What you'll bring to the role

  • 4-5+ years of experience in cloud infrastructure engineering, with a strong focus on GCP
  • Extensive experience with Infrastructure as Code, particularly Terraform
  • Proficiency in containerisation technologies, including Docker and Kubernetes (GKE)
  • Experience implementing and managing service mesh solutions
  • Strong knowledge of networking concepts and how to implement them in cloud environments
  • Experience with GitLab CI/CD pipelines for infrastructure deployment and management
  • Proficiency in at least one programming language commonly used for infrastructure work
  • Experience implementing and managing secrets management, telemetry and observability tools
  • The ability to drive DevOps/SRE processes and culture, keeping site reliability and delivery velocity in balance
  • A strong understanding of cloud security best practices and compliance requirements
  • Experience with cost optimisation techniques in cloud environments

Bonus points for

  • Knowledge of Google Pub/Sub, Kafka and microservices architectures
  • Performance optimisation of search databases (e.g. Elasticsearch)
  • Familiarity with serverless computing concepts and implementations
  • Experience with infrastructure performance tuning and optimisation
  • Knowledge of AI/ML infrastructure requirements and implementations on GCP

Soft skills and personal qualities

  • Excellent problem-solving and analytical thinking skills
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • The ability to collaborate effectively in cross-functional teams
  • Adaptability and an eagerness to learn new technologies
  • Leadership skills, with the ability to mentor junior team members
  • Strong time management and prioritisation skills
  • Attention to detail and a commitment to delivering high-quality work

Life at Rightmove

Despite our growth, we’ve remained a friendly, supportive place to work, with employee #1 still working here!  We’ve done this by placing the Rightmove Hows at the heart of everything we do. These are the essential values that reflect our culture, and include:

  • We create value…by delivering results and building trust with partners and consumers.
  • We think bigger…by acting with curiosity and setting bold aspirations.
  • We care deeply…by being real, having fun, and valuing diversity.
  • We move together…by being one team - internally collaborative, externally competitive.
  • We make a difference…by focusing on delivering measurable impact.

 

 

We believe in careers that open doors and help our team develop by providing an open and inclusive work environment, offering ongoing   training opportunities, and supporting charity fundraising events. And with 89% of Rightmovers saying we’re a great place to work, we’re clearly doing something right!

b0a63a22fd55.title: Junior Software Developer
b0a63a22fd55.description: The Software Developer I, Connector role supports Trial Interactive’s proprietary platform, Connector - the cloud-based integrations that move life science data between clients’ clinical systems (for example EDC/eCRF and IRT systems) and Trial Interactive’s life science products. Working under the guidance of senior engineers, the role helps build and maintain connectors, keeps client data flowing accurately, and resolves issues when it does not. This is a blended role, covering development and maintenance up until handling client requests. This role works closely with the Solutions, DevOps and Engineering teams. DESCRIPTION As part of the Development and maintenance responsibility, the resource handles: • Develop, test and maintain connector components in C# on .NET (AWS Lambda), including the parsers and mappers that convert source-system data (API payloads, files) into the formats required by the Trial Interactive CTMS and eTMF. • Configure and extend mappings for new studies, sites and visit/status definitions on existing connectors, reusing existing modules wherever possible. • Assist in the technical onboarding of new clients and studies: connector configuration, test runs in non-production environments, and verification before go-live. • Work with the AWS services connectors are built on (Lambda, SQS, S3, EventBridge/Step Functions, Secrets Manager, CloudWatch) and make small, reviewed infrastructure changes using Terraform under supervision. • Consume, test and troubleshoot REST APIs (client/vendor APIs and Trial Interactive import APIs) using code and tools such as Postman, and help extend APIs that improve connector stability and connectivity. • Write unit and functional tests; use Git (feature branches, merge requests, environment branches) and follow the team’s code review and release process. • Keep code, configuration and change records documented so that others can maintain them. • Work on special projects, such as local test environments using LocalStack. As part of handling Client communication, support and ticket resolution, the resource does: • Own assigned support tickets from triage to closure: reproduce the issue, investigate, fix or escalate, and record the outcome in the ticketing system (for example Jira, ServiceDesk Plus). • Investigate data issues end to end – trace a record from the source payload through the archive, parser, connector database and logs to its CTMS/eTMF import result – and establish the root cause (RCA) with evidence. • Reconcile source-system data against the CTMS/eTMF when a client reports missing or mismatched subjects, visits or statuses, and explain any differences. • Communicate with clients and Solutions Engineers by email, tickets and calls: acknowledge requests promptly, ask clear clarifying questions, give regular status updates, and explain findings and next steps in plain language. • Monitor connector health (CloudWatch logs, failed imports, notifications) and respond to failures within agreed response times. • Escalate appropriately to senior engineers, DevOps or the vendor, with a concise summary of what happened, when, in which environment and for which records. • Write up RCAs, fixes and known issues so that repeat problems are resolved faster, and help keep support documentation current. • Handle client and clinical data with care: use the minimum data needed, never share one client’s information with another, and follow Trial Interactive data-protection and change-control procedures. General • Keep learning the connector platform, the clinical-trial data domain and cloud and software development best practices. • Complete all other tasks that are deemed appropriate for this role and assigned by the manager/supervisor. About the job

Deliver the power, cooling and capacity that enable Graphcore’s engineers to bring up and test AI systems.

Based in Bristol, you’ll lead regional lab and data centre infrastructure delivery and own operational readiness. As Graphcore’s client-side representative, you’ll turn agreed engineering requirements into practical delivery plans and improvements.

Your work will keep existing environments effective while creating capacity for testing and experimentation. You’ll identify constraints before they affect engineering work and improve reliability for high-density AI workloads.

You’ll guide builds, expansions and upgrades from site assessment through design, installation, commissioning and handover. You’ll manage approved budgets, supplier commitments, schedules and delivery risks.

As an individual contributor, you’ll use independent technical judgement to balance regional projects with day-to-day operations. Experience with liquid cooling and pressurised infrastructure is particularly relevant to this work.

The team and culture

You’ll agree regional priorities with Systems Engineering, hardware engineering, IT, facilities, health and safety, and finance. You’ll coordinate internal teams and suppliers, making readiness, capacity constraints, costs and risks clear.

You’ll resolve competing priorities and escalate changes that need additional investment or wider decisions. Working with counterparts in other regions, you’ll share improvements and apply consistent infrastructure standards.

What we’re looking for

  • Experience leading client-side infrastructure projects in data centres, labs or mission-critical environments, including hyperscale or high-performance computing.
  • Strong understanding of data centre power distribution, cooling, rack infrastructure, connectivity and building requirements.
  • Experience guiding projects through design, procurement, construction, commissioning and operational handover.
  • Ability to interpret engineering drawings and technical specifications, and assess supplier proposals against agreed requirements.
  • Project management skills covering budgets, schedules, dependencies and risks, alongside infrastructure capacity planning and operational readiness.
  • Clear communication across technical and non-technical teams, with experience coordinating suppliers and resolving competing priorities.

While we have outlined a set of requirements, we value transferable skills and diverse experiences. We also welcome engineers returning to the profession after a career break, including through returnship routes.

Benefits

  • Flexible working: Balance your work and personal life with greater flexibility
  • Generous leave: Take time to rest, recharge and enjoy life outside of work
  • Retirement planning support: Up to 5% matched pension
  • Phantom equity: Share in Graphcore’s success
  • Workplace experience: Enjoy thoughtfully designed office spaces for collaboration, with free food and an on-site barista to support your day
  • Peace of mind protection: Income protection and life assurance to provide financial security for you and your loved ones

bceef231c3b3.title: Marketing Automation Engineer
bceef231c3b3.description:
Growth at CFO Insights

The world’s most demanding investors are busy managing trillions, and ignore anything average. Are you excited by the challenge of making them act?

Are you looking to work in an exceptional entrepreneurial team with ambitious, motivated and extremely driven people? And do you want real ownership from your first week? If so, now is the time to apply for the Growth role at Private Equity Insights.

The mission: build the world's largest network for private equity investors.

You will work in sprints and get fast execution under your skin. AI has completely changed the game: You will learn to deploy it to outperform a marketing team of 20+ people, while also learning the fundamentals of copywriting that makes elite investors act, get it to the right investor at a meaningful frequency and deploy what works across every marketing channel.

If you want an ambitious mission, real ownership and the fastest learning curve of your career: apply.

Why CFO Insights

CFO Insights is Northern Europe’s largest CFO forum and aims to connect and develop CFOs, finance leaders, and tomorrow's innovators by addressing the issues of the future CFO. We are connecting more than 11,000 professionals from more than 15 countries.

CFO Insights is part of United Media which focuses on building large scale industry media and conferences products in sectors such as insurance, HR, private equity, retail, etc. As of today, we have organically launched 8 media companies and acquired one.

What we offer you

  • Master the highest bar in the world. Our audience is the world's most demanding investors. They ignore anything average. If your work can make them act, you can make anyone act.
  • Unlimited growth potential. You will get responsibility before you feel ready. That is how you grow fast. We strongly believe in and have a track record of promoting internally. You can expect coaching and development from leaders, peers and experts.
  • Skills that compound for life. Fast execution, copywriting, pricing, conversion optimisation, structured problem solving, and the ability to create impact anywhere in the business at scale.
  • Ownership from the very start. You own outcomes, not tasks. We agree the goal, and you find the way.
  • Travel opportunity. You will be joining our 10+ conferences.

What you will do

Responsibilities in this job will vary, however, feed into the mission: build the world's largest network for private equity investors. They will be mostly centered around the following:

  • Build the audience. Identify, target, and convert every fund into our community, and make sure each one receives the right message, at the right time, and never one too many.
  • Own marketing channels that drive revenue. Through existing and new marketing channels, you execute activities that ultimately will drive revenue
  • Write copy that persuades. Every email, landing page and post. Become the best copywriter and leverage it at scale with AI.
  • Sprint, test, implement. Measure the impact of all experiments you run, test offers, copy, prices and pages until the numbers move.
  • Build systems, not one-offs. Anything you do twice becomes a playbook or an AI workflow, so the next win takes less effort than the last.
  • Do whatever it takes to win. Some days that means designing an AI workflow. Some days it means checking investors in at the registration desk at 7am. Nobody here is too good for the work that deliver value for investors and fund managers.

What we expect from you

  • 1 to 3 years of experience
  • Min. a bachelor or master degree with great results
  • A UK work permit. We do not sponsor visas.
  • Strong work ethic with a sense of urgency
  • Exceptional drive and desire to be the best at what you do
  • Proactive approach and sense of ownership/responsibility of everything you do
  • A humble approach and share our passion for building companies and developing people
  • Interested in continuous learning and proactively searching for ways to optimise

Practical details

Full-time, in person from our London office (WeWork), 5 days a week. Expect to travel for work about 20 days a year. The start date is flexible.

0053ad2b8408.title: Electrical Engineer II (Integrations)
0053ad2b8408.description: Help us use technology to make a big green dent in the universe! Kraken powers some of the most innovative global developments in energy. We create the technology that redefines utilities and unlocks a new energy system of the future. By optimising renewable generation, building a more intelligent grid, and empowering utilities to deliver an exceptional customer experience, our operating system is transforming the industry worldwide. It’s an incredibly exciting time to work in energy. Join us on our mission to improve the lives of ONE BILLION humans within the decade and shape a cleaner, better future for everyone. 🐙 Kraken Generation Flex The energy industry is undergoing the largest transformation since industrialisation, at an unprecedented rate of change and we are positioning ourselves at the heart of it. In the UK, with a legally binding Net Zero target for 2050 and a clean-power ambition for 2030, we are scaling rapidly to integrate Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) into the grid. Kraken is recognised as a thought leader and innovator. With complete independence from Octopus Energy, we are building a SaaS business that digitally connects hundreds of thousands of DERs with energy markets. As our UK fleet grows and we support our expansion across Europe, we are looking for an Integrations Engineer to help turn customer sites into market-connected, controllable assets. 🏠 Where you’ll fit in and role summary As we scale our fleet of integrated assets, we are looking for an Electrical Engineer to support the delivery of our site integrations and grow into owning them, learning the full lifecycle from the early information stage through design, deployment and testing. You’ll be part of an engineering delivery team, based in Manchester, who take an integration project from the very early information stage, design how it will be integrated into Kraken’s platform and then turn that design into a live, controllable, market-participating asset. Engineering delivery is an innovative and engineering-focused team with a culture that fosters collaboration and fresh thinking to create a new energy system. Alongside design, deployment and testing; they constantly look into ways to improve efficiency through tooling and the automation of repetitive tasks. They collaborate daily with delivery managers and customer success to onboard new sites as well as support the existing. 🚀 What you'll own Integration design contribution: With guidance, analyse provided information and contribute to hardware and software integration approaches. When necessary, exchange information with customer technical representatives through meetings and emails, and take part in design discussions with other team members. Technical judgement: Develop your technical judgement, making well-reasoned decisions and trade-offs with support from senior engineers, and contributing technical input to discussions within the team. Developing domain knowledge: Build up your knowledge in one or more technical areas. This could include grid regulations (G99, G100, Grid Code etc.), energy markets, multi BMUs, industrial communication protocols, industrial networking, internet of things, cyber security and so on. Gateway application & configuration: Learn how the Gateway software (developed by an internal software team) works and how it is configured. Understand the requirements for an integration and judge if the gateway software is able to support it or will need new development work. The team will help you get gateway configuration literate and you will carry out deployments and changes independently over time. Hardware and Software Deployments: Learn the process of our hardware and software deployments. Over time, take ownership of the configuration, deployment and testing with guidance from the senior engineers. Networking and cyber security: Contribute to hardware and network connectivity designs, keeping our own cyber security posture in mind as well as addressing the concerns from customers, with the support of the internal security team. Site testing & commissioning: Carry out site testing and commissioning initially with the support of the team and building toward doing this independently as onboarding demand grows. Incidents & compliance: Help address engineering help requests from other teams and support incident response in the case of issues at existing sites. 🧠 What you'll bring to the party Understanding of the Regulations: Working knowledge of the UK Grid Code, G99 and the other obligations of a grid-connected asset before it can participate in the energy markets. Understanding of the UK Energy Markets: Working understanding of the NESO ancillary services (Dynamic Containment / Moderation / Regulation, Firm Frequency Response), the Balancing Mechanism, and the DNO connection/integration process. Technical judgement: Sound technical judgement and a structured approach to problems, working with the team to agree and implement a solution. Power plant systems: Ability to read and analyse single line diagrams for a given power plant to understand the site architecture for the points of metering and control instrumentation. Asset integration: Exposure to, or a keen interest in, integrating BESS (grid-scale and/or C&I) and/or RES (Wind and Solar) for telemetry and control. Integration design: Ability to contribute to clear integration designs and design documentation. Hardware and Networking: Familiarity with control systems deployments and their connectivity including the local networking and cyber security aspects, and an ability to help debug site connectivity and networking issues (including 4G routers and firewalls) with support. Industrial Communication Protocols: Practical experience or a good working knowledge of Modbus (TCP/RTU); awareness of one or more of IEC 60870-5-104, IEC 61400-25, OPC-UA or DNP3 is a plus. CAD, Diagrams and Tools: Experience or familiarity with CAD tools such as AutoCAD or BricsCAD, Miro and Notion

19224c7c7489.title: Supplier Quality Engineer (Orly)
19224c7c7489.description: About Us Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected. About the Role We are looking for a Supplier Quality Engineer to ensure that our suppliers are delivering at the right level of quality, in particular through audits and supplier development. Responsibilities Conduct supplier qualification and approval (new sources, special processes). Conduct supplier / process audits (AS9100, special-process, APQP). Ensure FAI (AS9102) and PPAP review; receiving-inspection strategy and defect containment. Implement supplier 8D / corrective actions, scorecards, and be the owner of the supplier development; NDAA / AQAP flow-down. Collaboration and Communication Work with cross-functional teams, including R&D, Engineering, and Supply Chain, using platforms such as Jira or Confluence to document and track quality topics related to design projects. Communicate effectively with internal and external stakeholders, including customers and regulatory bodies, on project quality status and resolutions. Continuous Improvement Participate in initiatives to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of the design and development processes, focusing on reducing design-related risks and ensuring first-time-right product realization. Collect and analyze quality data from the design phase to support performance monitoring and reporting for project milestones. Candidate Requirements Engineering degree in quality, industrial, aeronautical, or mechanical engineering. 3 to 5 years of relevant experience in supplier / procurement quality, preferably in the aerospace, defense, or automotive sectors. Strong experience in Supplier audit & qualification, PPAP / FAI run, Supplier corrective action (8D) Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to work effectively across teams and departments in an international environment. 482b6094cf41.description: About Us Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces. Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected. Overview Harmattan AI is developing new hardware products within the Launcher module: field-deployable drone launchers designed to be deployed and operated autonomously in demanding field environments. These products require dedicated electronics design with complex architecture in a constrained environment – PCBs integrating power conversion, energy management, control and communication interfaces – optimised for cost at volume. The Launcher team is seeking a dedicated hardware engineer to own electronics design end-to-end and accelerate the path to production milestones. Ideal candidate A senior hardware engineer who has designed and shipped complex PCBs, ideally mixing digital and significant power (hundreds of watts), into production. They are rigorous on schematics, layout, and bring-up, and have a strong instinct for cost and manufacturability. They design with real-world operating conditions in mind - temperature, moisture, surges - and an interest in battery thermal management; direct experience of outdoor-deployed equipment is a plus rather than a prerequisite. They are comfortable working autonomously in a small team and can bridge hardware and firmware. Skills required PCB schematic and layout design (Altium Designer preferred) Power electronics design: ~300 W DC/DC conversion, protection, derating, efficiency and thermal budgets Thermal regulation: temperature sensing and control loops, battery storage temperature management, heatsinking Power over Ethernet (IEEE 802.3af/at/bt): combined power and data delivery, isolation, cable budgets Mixed-signal design: power management, MCU interfaces, communication buses (SPI, I2C, UART, USB, CAN, Ethernet) Hardware bring-up and debug: bench equipment proficiency DFM/DFA for PCB manufacturing and assembly Component selection and BOM management Experience in lightning and surge protection is a plus Responsibilities: Schematic Design - Design complete schematics for mixed-signal and power boards, from power stages to digital and communication sections. PCB Layout & Routing - Perform or lead board placement and routing with attention to signal integrity, EMC, and power-path constraints. Power & Thermal Architecture - Define and validate the power architecture of the product and the thermal strategy, including battery temperature management. Environmental Robustness - Ensure the electronics withstand outdoor deployment conditions and define the associated qualification plan. Component Selection & BOM Optimization - Select components with cost, availability, and reliability in mind; drive BOM cost reduction for mass production volumes. Hardware Bring-up & Debug - Lead board bring-up, debug issues with oscilloscopes, power bench equipment, and other bench equipment; write bring-up scripts when needed. EMC & Safety Compliance - Address EMC challenges; ensure signal integrity across the board and electrical safety of the power and battery sections. Collaboration with Embedded SW - Work closely with the embedded software engineer to define hardware/software interfaces; support firmware bring-up. Collaboration with Mechanical - Ensure seamless PCB integration into mechanical enclosures (connectors, mounting, thermal, sealing, shielding). Supplier & Manufacturing Ramp-up - Qualify PCB manufacturers and assembly houses; support DFM/DFA review for production; manage NPI transitions. Documentation - Maintain schematics, layout files, test procedures, and hardware specifications. 729d5b9ab94d.title: Product ML Engineer
729d5b9ab94d.description: About us Founded in 2019 and part of Y Combinator’s Summer 2020 cohort, Photoroom is the leading AI photo and video solution for e-commerce, helping businesses sell at first sight. Backed by Series B funding, we’ve reached 300M+ downloads and now process around 7 billion images a year for businesses of every size, from solo sellers to global brands and marketplaces like Amazon, Decathlon, and Depop. We serve them through our mobile app, web platform, and API, with tailored solutions for enterprise catalogs. We’re an international team of 130+, with offices in Paris and New York. We take ownership of what we build, move quickly to learn what works, and speak candidly, united by our ambition to create exceptional impact for e-commerce businesses worldwide. Role Summary We're looking for a Product ML Engineer to join one of our product experience teams — SMB, Scaler or Enterprise — and own the ML side of short, high-impact projects. You'll work on focused ML problems with a clear product outcome, sometimes fine-tuning one of our models, sometimes integrating the best externally available model, but always choosing the fastest and most effective path to customer value. You'll bring the technical depth of an Applied Scientist while operating with the pace and pragmatism of a product engineer. You'll own the journey from framing the problem through to shipping, measuring and iterating on the feature in production. Your time horizon is weeks rather than quarters, and success is measured by what reaches users and the impact it creates. About the role Embed directly within a product team. Work closely with the SMB, Scaler or Enterprise team on focused ML problems tied to clear customer and business outcomes. Own ML projects end to end. Frame the problem, choose the approach, execute the plan, ship the feature and monitor its performance in production. Make the build vs. buy decision. Determine when to fine-tune or build a model yourself versus integrating an external model, API or existing library. Move from idea to production quickly. Work on projects scoped in weeks rather than quarters, prioritising rapid iteration and customer impact. Work closely with the ML team. Leverage shared infrastructure, evaluation tooling and expertise while remaining embedded in the product team's priorities and cadence. Stay close to users. Get rapid feedback from customers, monitor how people use what you've shipped and use those insights to drive the next iteration. Balance technical depth with pragmatism. Know when deeper modelling work is necessary and when an existing solution is already good enough to ship. Write production code. Work directly in the product team's codebase rather than operating primarily through research notebooks and experiments. Own quality in production. Build sound evaluations, monitor performance and investigate failures once the feature is live. About You You've shipped ML into production. You have 2+ years of hands-on experience building and shipping ML-powered products, with strong experience in PyTorch or equivalent frameworks such as TensorFlow or JAX. You have applied-science depth. You can fine-tune vision or diffusion models, design meaningful evaluations and debug training runs when necessary. You're a pragmatic builder. You care about solving the customer's problem rather than proving that your own model is the best approach. You'll happily use an external model, API or existing library when that's the fastest route to value. You're product-minded. You measure success through shipped features, user behaviour and business outcomes rather than papers or benchmarks alone. You're comfortable in production codebases. You can move between experimentation and production engineering, writing maintainable code that lives inside a real product. You have strong ownership. You're comfortable taking an ambiguous ML problem, deciding what matters, choosing an approach and driving it through to production. You iterate quickly. You enjoy short feedback loops and would rather ship something useful, learn from users and improve it than spend months optimising something that hasn't reached production. You're curious and collaborative. You can both explain your expertise and learn from the deep technical expertise around you. You value knowledge sharing and humility. You're fluent in English. French isn't required. Nice to have: experience shipping generative image models or diffusion models into production; experience evaluating third-party AI APIs against internal alternatives; experience working in a fast-growing startup or directly within a product team. Benefits Competitive salary + meaningful equity Hybrid working from our Paris headquarters Visa sponsorship and relocation support up to €10,000 MacBook Pro Private healthcare Regular company off-sites and team retreats International English-speaking team Language lessons in English and French Hiring Process Screening with an ML Researcher / Engineer Home technical assignment and review with the team Culture fit interview and meet the team Reference check and offer Support: We value diversity and aim to create an inclusive experience for all applicants. Please let us know if there's anything we can do to make the process more accessible for you. Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging We're committed to enabling everyone to feel included and valued at work. We believe our company and culture are strongest when composed of diverse experiences and backgrounds. That's also why we have flexible working hours, trust people to work in a hybrid environment, and extended parental leave. All qualified applicants receive consideration for employment without regard to age, color, family, gender identity, marital status, national origin, physical or mental disability, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws. 8da0afa6a8e9.title: Senior Data Collection Operator (FR)
8da0afa6a8e9.description: About Genesis We are a full-stack general-purpose robot company, born across San Francisco, London and Paris and bound by a single mission: to make general-purpose robots a reality, unlocking infinite physical labor for the world and freeing people for creativity, exploration and the pursuits they love for their own sake. We're building the engine that will teach robots to do real work in the real world. We recently unveiled Eno, our wheeled, dexterous robot powered by our GENE foundation model and we are starting to put it to work with real customers. The role General-purpose robots learn from real, dexterous human work, the kind of data that does not exist on the internet. We capture it with our own collection hardware: a person wears it, does the work, and the robot learns to do it too. You will be a senior member of the team scaling our data collection operation in Paris, working closely with our Paris research and engineering teams and with the operation in the Bay Area. You will help lead the day-to-day execution and quality bar on the Paris floor while remaining deeply hands-on with data collection, teleoperation, task setup, and real-robot testing. You will wear our gloves and cameras, teleoperate our hardware, and take ownership of complex collection requests from setup through execution and quality review. You will work shoulder to shoulder with our model engineering and research teams, turning their requests into physical demonstrations and feeding what you learn on the floor back to them. You will be expected to operate autonomously, help guide and train other operators and contribute to how the Paris operation evolves as the team grows. This is a hands-on leadership role. You will not just run existing tasks: you will help shape how they are executed, how quality is measured, and how other operators are trained to deliver consistently. What you will do Help lead the Paris data collection floor. Set the execution and quality bar for day-to-day collection work and help the team scale effectively. Own complex collection setups. Take a loosely defined request and turn it into a working, repeatable collection task, including the setup, fixtures, props, environment, and procedure, with minimal support from engineering. Create high-quality training data. Wear our gloves and cameras, teleoperate our hardware, and produce precise demonstrations that can be used to train our models. Own the full collection workflow. Go beyond collecting the data itself: review and quality-check your work, identify unusable episodes, support annotation, and help ensure that what reaches research is trainable data. Build repeatable tasks. Turn new collection requests into clear, repeatable processes that can be executed consistently by other operators. Partner with research and model engineering. Translate their requests into physical collection tasks, share observations from the floor, and iterate with them on setups and collection strategy. Improve the operation. Identify when a fixture, station layout, procedure, or collection method can be improved and proactively help implement those improvements. Write and improve the playbook. Own SOPs, quality checks, and training materials that allow the Paris operation to scale while maintaining a consistent quality bar. Guide other operators. Help onboard, train, and mentor operators and reinforce consistent execution across the team. Run real-robot testing. Partner with reliability and engineering teams to test robots on the floor, document what you observe, and help surface issues. Own quality. Review your own work and the team's, take direct feedback, and keep raising the bar. What we are looking for You have done precise, repetitive physical work to a high quality bar and can explain what made your work good and how you measured it. This could include data collection, teleoperation, motion capture, robotics lab work, assembly, fine craft, or another hands-on technical environment. Hands-on robot or glove-based data collection experience is a strong plus, but not a requirement. This kind of data collection is new, and we will teach you our specific tools and approach. You build, not just run. Give you a vague request and a scrappy setup, and you can turn it into a clean, repeatable task with the right fixtures, environment, process, and written procedure. You can operate autonomously. You are comfortable taking ownership of complex collection tasks with limited day-to-day support from engineering. You understand quality beyond collection. You can review your work, recognize when collected data is unusable or below the quality bar, and understand why. You are ready to lead. This is a technical and product-oriented data role. You'll collaborate closely with product, engineering, and data teams to find what we can learn from our data and turn those learnings into production systems. Use statistical methods, heuristics, experimentation, or machine learning depending on what is most appropriate for the problem. Iterate on features and models based on real-world data and continuously improve their accuracy and reliability. Help bridge the gap between exploratory data work and robust systems running in production. Continuous Improvement Improve the performance, reliability, and maintainability of our data infrastructure. Monitor data quality and proactively investigate unexpected changes or anomalies. Stay up to date with developments in data engineering, analytics, and machine learning, and bring relevant ideas and technologies into our stack.
