c46b72f65b45.title: Senior Backend Engineer, Backend Platform (PHP and Python)
c46b72f65b45.description: WHO WE ARE 🌍 Creating content that resonates is great — turning that attention into growth is even better. That's what Manychat does. Our AI-powered automations help creators and brands engage with audiences across Instagram, Messenger, WhatsApp, and TikTok — at the right moment, with the right message, minus the manual work. We're 400+ people across three continents behind the leading platform for conversational growth, with AI skills shaping how we build, how we work, and how we grow. WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR 🌟 Want to own how the backend works for everyone, not just one corner of it? We’re looking for a Senior Backend Engineer who works across PHP and Python and wants a say in the bigger picture. You’ll lead company-level projects like our Auth Service: one authorization layer for PHP and Python, so Python products can handle their traffic directly instead of going through PHP. When things are unclear, you’ll research first, weigh the trade-offs and write them down. Then you’ll ship in small, safe steps. You’ll also decide where code should live based on what’s best for the system, not on which language you know best. Product teams will come to you for advice, reviews, and a way through when they're stuck. The team is still taking shape, so you'll also help define ownership, standards, and how we work. If that mix of deep technical work and influence across teams sounds like you, keep reading. YOUR FUTURE TEAMMATES 👋 Meet the Backend Platform team: We're a small team of engineers from core PHP, Infra, and AI backgrounds. We lead technical initiatives across the whole backend and own its health. Product teams build and run their own components, and we give them the tools, standards, and expertise to do it well. Each of us leads our own project, from planning to agreeing with other teams to production. We work in weekly cycles and write our decisions down. Right now we're bringing PHP and Python platform work together into one common backend platform. WHAT YOU'LL DO 🚀 Lead company-level technical projects end to end, from design and planning to rollout and support, such as completing our Auth Service development and shaping authorization as a separate layer for PHP and Python. Shape the shared PHP and Python platform, and decide where each module should live based on the needs of the whole system. Build the foundations that let new Python products launch and scale without being wired through PHP each time. Define clear ownership of technical components across the backend, including who owns monitoring and knowledge for each. Improve how we spot and handle problems: bug and incident management, less noise in alerts and error tracking, and Grafana Cloud dashboards for how services interact. Find root causes across PHP and Python services using metrics, logs, and distributed tracing. Make performance part of everyday work, not something we fix after incidents: clear performance metrics, tools that show where things slow down, and analysis of unusual user behavior that causes degradation. Make architecture decisions with high load in mind, working with databases, servers, proxies, and DNS alongside the Infra team. Work with the Security team to fix vulnerabilities, build in security practices, and keep libraries and dependencies up to date. Improve developer experience: dev environment, CI/CD, routine automation, one documentation approach for PHP and Python, and tools for AI coding assistants. Turn product teams' requests into solutions: find what really hurts, propose the best fix, and support them with architecture advice and reviews in shared components. TO SHINE IN THIS ROLE 💥 You'll need: Production backend experience in PHP or Python, and the ability to read and work with the other. You'll write production code in both. Experience with high-load production systems and improving their performance. Experience designing multi-component systems with clear boundaries, planning for failures, rollout, and rollback, with security in mind. Experience comparing technical options, naming the trade-offs, and explaining your choice in writing (ADRs, Design Docs). Hands-on observability experience: metrics, dashboards, alerts, logs, and distributed tracing, and using them to find root causes. Experience leading a project that spans several teams: breaking it into small, testable steps, getting other teams on board, and taking it to production. A track record of improving engineering quality beyond your own tasks, for example setting up error monitoring, or a new process when things kept breaking. Enough infrastructure knowledge (databases, servers, proxies, DNS) to work well with Infra and see how your changes affect them. Clear communication: you explain your point of view, find the real problem behind a request, and flag risks early. Experience leading work independently while supporting your team: taking feedback, helping colleagues grow, and changing your mind when the arguments are good. It would be great if you have: Experience on a Platform or Core team. Strong production experience in both PHP and Python. Experience with authentication and authorization systems (for example, JWT or Ory Oathkeeper). Experience defining SLOs and building symptom-based alerts. Experience running incidents and blameless post-mortems. Experience with Grafana Cloud, Rollbar, or similar tools. Experience building developer tooling, CI/CD, or tools for AI coding assistants. Experience mentoring engineers or leading knowledge sharing across teams. WHAT WE OFFER 🤗 We care deeply about your growth, well-being, and comfort: 🌍 Hybrid onboarding to start work remotely and relocation support for you and your family. 💙 Comprehensive health insurance for both you and your family. 📚 Professional development budget for conference tickets, online courses, and other relevant resources to help you grow. 🫶 Flexible benefits package: no one-size-fits-all perks here. 1c81b16053d2.title: Principal Software Engineer (f/m/d)
1c81b16053d2.description:
The role

Reporting directly to the VP Technology, you'll build new capability for Awin with AI at the core, free from the constraints of our established delivery model. You'll take ideas from concept to production quickly, prove what works, and turn the best of it into patterns the wider engineering organisation can adopt.

You'll work closely with product and commercial leaders to find where AI changes the economics of our affiliate marketing platform: what we can build, how fast, and at what cost. You'll be hands-on most of the time, writing code, shipping and measuring results, rather than coordinating others.

You'll know enough of our existing platform to connect new things to it safely, but you won't be absorbed into running it. Your job is to show what modern, AI-native engineering looks like at Awin, and make it real.

This is a step-up opportunity. We're looking for a bright, self-starting engineer who is ready for more scope than their current role allows. You might not have held a principal title yet. What matters is that you're already building this way, you learn fast, and you want the room to prove it. You'll have direct access to senior leadership, real problems with commercial weight, and the freedom to choose how you solve them.

Key tasks and accountabilities

Build and ship

  • Design, build and run AI-powered products, tools and services from prototype to production
  • Own outcomes end to end: problem framing, architecture, implementation, evaluation, release and operation
  • Run fast, time-boxed experiments; scale what works and stop what doesn't, with the evidence to back either call
  • Set up and evolve the AI infrastructure these builds rely on: model access, evaluation tooling, observability and guardrails

Shape direction

  • Work with the VP Technology to set Awin's engineering-specific AI direction, grounded in what has actually been built and measured
  • Scope strategic opportunities early with product and commercial leaders, with effort, cost and value made explicit
  • Make clear recommendations on build vs buy, model and vendor choice, and where AI should not be used

Architecture and design

  • Design new capability so it connects safely to the existing platform: APIs, events, data and identity
  • Select tools and technologies, and define the patterns and practices for AI-native development at Awin
  • Weigh long-term maintainability, economic viability and reuse against speed, and document the trade-offs

Spread what works

  • Turn proven builds into reusable patterns, templates and internal tools, and share them so other teams can adopt them without hand-holding

Ways of working

  • Works autonomously, guided by the VP Technology's priorities rather than team-level delivery processes
  • Engages directly with engineering, product, data, security and commercial stakeholders as each build requires

Skills & Expertise

AI-native engineering

  • Builds with coding agents (e.g. Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) as the default way of working. Can show how they decompose work, manage context and review agent output to get production-quality code at pace
  • Has shipped LLM-powered features to production: prompt and context engineering, tool use and function calling, structured outputs, retrieval (RAG) and multi-step agent workflows
  • Builds evaluations first: test sets, automated evals and regression checks for non-deterministic behaviour, with quality measured before and after release
  • Connects models to enterprise systems and data safely, e.g. MCP servers, internal APIs and event streams, with clear permissions and audit trails
  • Understands model selection, token economics, latency, caching and fallback strategies, and can explain cost and benefit trade-offs to commercial stakeholders
  • Designs for AI-specific security and privacy risks: prompt injection, data leakage, PII handling under GDPR, and guardrails on what models can do

Engineering foundations

  • Expert in at least one modern language (Python or TypeScript ideal), and able to work in our existing Java, PHP and JavaScript estate when integrating
  • Strong cloud-native and serverless architecture on AWS, with infrastructure as code (Terraform)
  • Experience with event-driven and distributed systems (Kafka/MSK, SQS/SNS) and with relational and non-relational data stores
  • Builds observability into everything: tracing, logging and monitoring, including LLM-specific telemetry
  • Treats automated testing, CI/CD and secure-by-default design as standard, and automates as much of the delivery loop as possible

Ways of building

  • Takes an idea to a working prototype in days, then hardens it for production, and knows when to stop
  • Leaves behind reusable patterns, templates and internal tools, not one-off solutions

Soft skills

  • Bias to action: ships, measures and iterates rather than waiting for perfect requirements
  • Comfortable with ambiguity: frames vague opportunities into concrete, testable bets
  • Commercially minded: connects technical choices to revenue, cost and customer outcomes, and balances effort against value
  • Intellectually honest: kills their own ideas when the evidence says so, and says plainly where AI is not the answer
  • Clear communicator: explains technical trade-offs to executives, engineers and commercial teams in la

b3d57d923745.title: Senior/Staff Site Reliability Engineer (Server Infrastructure)
b3d57d923745.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The Role

Server Infrastructure is a Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) team responsible for the full lifecycle of Nebius Cloud hardware: from newly delivered bare metal through provisioning, operation, maintenance, and decommissioning. Almost every Nebius service runs on servers within our domain. Our mission is to make the hardware layer fast, reliable, and invisible.

We apply software engineering to infrastructure operations. We build services and automation that bring servers into the cloud, keep them healthy, recover them from failures, and retire them safely. Our work spans CPU and GPU platforms, the base GNU/Linux system, and the infrastructure supporting our hardware fleet.

As a Senior / Staff Engineer, you’ll take ownership of complex infrastructure challenges and help shape the team’s technical direction. You’ll combine hands-on engineering with architecture, mentoring, and coordination across teams, turning operational needs into reliable services and automation.
You’ll work closely with data center engineers, capacity managers, cloud compute developers, networking teams, and hardware suppliers. Your work will directly affect the reliability and capacity of the entire cloud platform.

Your responsibilities will include:
  • Design, build, and operate services for netboot, provisioning, maintenance, automated recovery, and decommissioning.
  • Lead technical initiatives from problem definition and design through implementation and production operation.
  • Help shape the technical roadmap, balancing reliability improvements, new hardware integration, and long-term engineering work.
  • Define meaningful reliability indicators and service level objectives, using them to guide engineering priorities.
  • Reduce operational toil by turning recurring failures and manual procedures into reliable automation.
  • Improve on-call practices, incident response, and learning through blameless incident reviews.
  • Strengthen fleet observability, alerting, testing, deployment safety, and operational readiness.
  • Drive support for new CPU and GPU platforms and improvements to the base GNU/Linux system.
  • Mentor engineers, provide thoughtful design and code reviews, and help the team develop sound engineering practices.
  • Coordinate delivery across teams, communicate technical tradeoffs, and resolve dependencies.
We expect you to have:
  • Strong software engineering experience in Go and a solid understanding of Linux systems.
  • Experience designing, building, and operating infrastructure services, including distributed systems and failure handling.
  • A track record of owning complex technical initiatives and bringing them into production.
  • Practical knowledge of SRE principles: service level objectives, observability, incident management, capacity planning, and toil reduction.
  • Sound technical judgment and the ability to guide architecture and investigate difficult production problems.
  • Experience mentoring engineers and improving engineering practices through collaboration and technical example.
  • Clear communication and the ability to work effectively across engineering and operational teams.

We welcome candidates at senior and staff levels. The scope of ownership and technical influence will reflect your experience.
Experience with hardware provisioning, bare metal infrastructure, GPU platforms, or large server fleets would be valuable.
Familiarity with Kubernetes, infrastructure as code, GitOps, SaltStack, and Terraform is also useful.
We conduct coding interviews as part of the process.

Benefits & Perks:

  • Competitive compensation
  • Career growth and learning opportunities
  • Flexibility and ownership
  • Collaborative and innovative culture
  • Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects
  • International environment and talented teams

What's it like to work at Nebius:

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI 

Equal Opportunity Statement:

Nebius is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse workplace and to providing equal employment opportunities in all aspects of employment. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, ancestry, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Applicants must be authorized to work in the country in which they apply and will be required to provide proof of employment eligibility as a condition of hire.

07637afc291c.title: Senior Site Reliability Engineer (Data Platform)
07637afc291c.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The Role

We’re looking for a Senior Site Reliability Engineer to join the team building and operating Nebius Data Platform — a distributed storage and a processing platform that acts as the company’s “source of truth” and the backbone of many internal (and some external) products.
Nebius Data Platform is a single multi-tenant ecosystem based on YTsaurus — instead of running separate HDFS/Kafka/HBase-style systems, we provide storage, compute, and analytics capabilities inside one platform.

We operate across data centers worldwide, running YTsaurus in dedicated Kubernetes clusters with Kubernetes operators and supporting services written primarily in Go. We maintain our own Nebius distribution, develop functionality across the core and platform services, and contribute upstream where it makes sense. This gives us the ability to take improvements from design through implementation to production.

At scale today, this includes ~500 servers, ~20k CPU cores and ~10 PB of compressed data in our largest production cluster, supporting workloads ranging from business-critical pipelines and financial transactions to large-scale ML/LLM training datasets and compute.
As an SRE, you’ll combine software engineering with production ownership: understand how the platform behaves, identify what limits its reliability and growth, and build lasting improvements alongside the developers and teams who use it.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Own and improve the reliability, performance, and capacity of our YTsaurus clusters, with particular attention to data durability and predictable behavior under load.

  • Develop services, Kubernetes automation, and operational tooling in Go to simplify cluster provisioning, upgrades, and maintenance.

  • Improve monitoring, alerting, and diagnostic tools so we can detect problems early and understand their impact on users.

  • Investigate failures across Linux, networking, Kubernetes, and distributed storage and compute. Participate in on-call, lead incident investigations, and turn findings into lasting fixes.

  • Improve resource utilization and workload isolation as the platform grows and serves more teams.

  • Work with platform developers and users to make architectural decisions, deliver changes safely, and reduce repetitive operational work.

We expect you to have:

  • Experience operating distributed, stateful systems in production and taking responsibility for their reliability.

  • Strong Linux and networking fundamentals, including the ability to investigate resource bottlenecks and failures beyond the application layer.

  • Practical Kubernetes experience: deploying, operating, and troubleshooting production workloads.

  • Strong programming skills and experience building maintainable software. We primarily use Go; experience in another language and a willingness to learn Go are welcome.

  • A systematic approach to troubleshooting, using evidence from logs, metrics, traces, and system behavior.

  • The ability to drive improvements from problem identification through delivery, communicate trade-offs clearly, and collaborate with developers and platform users.

It will be an added bonus if you have:

  • Experience with Big Data systems (YTsaurus/Hadoop/Spark/ClickHouse/Kafka-like ecosystems).

  • Experience developing Kubernetes operators or controllers.

  • Experience with performance analysis, capacity planning, or resource management in multi-tenant systems.

We conduct coding interviews as part of the process.

Benefits & Perks:

  • Competitive compensation

effeb3e0aed3.title: Principal Engineer Capacity/Compute
effeb3e0aed3.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the Role Anthropic manages one of the largest and fastest-growing infrastructure fleets in the industry — spanning multiple accelerator families, cpu families and clouds. The Capacity Engineering team is responsible for making sure all our infrastructure resources are accounted for, well-utilized, and efficiently allocated. We own the data, tooling, and operational systems that let Anthropic plan, measure, and maximize utilization across first-party and third-party compute. As an engineer on Capacity Engineering, you will build the production systems that power this work: data pipelines that ingest and normalize telemetry from heterogeneous cloud environments, observability tooling that gives the org real-time visibility into fleet health, and performance instrumentation that measures how efficiently every major workload uses the hardware it’s running on. You will be expected to write production-quality code every day, operate alongside Kubernetes-native infrastructure at meaningful scale, and directly influence decisions around one of Anthropic’s largest areas of spend. You’ll collaborate closely with research engineering, infrastructure, inference, and finance teams. The work requires someone who can move between data engineering, systems engineering, and observability with comfort — and who thrives in a high-autonomy, high-ambiguity environment. This is a pipeline role feeding four areas. Depending on your background and business priority, you’ll focus primarily in one, but the boundaries are fluid and the problems overlap: Data platform Pipelines that ingest occupancy and utilization telemetry from Kubernetes clusters, normalize billing and usage across cloud providers, and serve the BigQuery tables the rest of the org queries against. Correctness, completeness, and latency are the job, not a footnote. Consumers range from research engineers to finance to leadership, so it's product work as much as engineering: defining schema contracts, making data discoverable, and figuring out what people actually need. Planning Knowing what the fleet has, where it's going, and what's in the way. Making the state of the fleet legible and actionable in real time: cluster health tooling, capacity planning platforms, alerting on occupancy drops and allocation problems, and systemic fixes to scheduling and fragmentation. Kubernetes operations on one side, cross-team coordination on the other. Efficiency Measuring and improving how effectively every major workload uses the hardware it runs on. Instrumenting utilization across training, inference, and eval systems, building benchmarking infrastructure, establishing per-config baselines, and working directly with system-owning teams to close the gaps. The metric has to be good enough that the team on the hook for it agrees with the number. Attribution and forecasting Connecting what the fleet costs to what the business is doing with it. Reconciling CSP billing exports against vendor telemetry and internal systems with mismatched schemas, attributing spend to the workloads and teams that generate it, and turning inference demand signals and research roadmaps into a defensible compute plan. Efficiency metrics have to survive contact with finance: stripped of pure demand and unit-price effects, reproducible month over month, and legible to a CFO. Key responsibilities Build the planning and allocation stack — the tools leadership uses to allocate capacity, teams use to plan against their allocations, and the scheduler enforces. Cross-region and cross-provider placement, guardrails, queueing, occupancy KPIs. Drive the efficiency programs: stranding and rightsizing, unused capacity recovery, and job-level utilization across training, inference, and eval. Establish per-config baselines and work with system-owning teams to close the gaps. Utilization improvements are worth enormous sums at our scale. Own attribution and forecasting — reconcile billing across ten-plus providers against telemetry and internal systems, attribute spend to the workloads that generate it, and turn demand signals and research roadmaps into a defensible compute plan and supply pipeline. Build the data platform underneath all of it: pipelines ingesting occupancy, utilization, and cost from a rapidly diversifying fleet into BigQuery, with real ownership of completeness, latency SLOs, and gap detection. Every new provider is a net-new integration. Operate Kubernetes-native systems at scale — collection agents, workload labeling, and the taint/reservation/scheduling behavior that determines what capacity is actually usable. Treat the output as a product, not a pipeline. Gather your own requirements, define schema contracts, and design for consumers ranging from research engineers to a CFO — including on-call and SLOs, because these surfaces are load-bearing for the company. What you bring A strong track record building and operating production systems. This is a hands-on engineering role with a devops flavor. Python and SQL at production quality. Most pipeline code is Python; the presentation layer is BigQuery SQL, including table-valued functions and views. Both need to be idiomatic, well-tested, and maintainable. Deep experience with at least one major cloud provider (Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, or Microsoft Azure) and its operations Experience with observability tooling stack, including Prometheus, PromQL, and Grafana, including writing recording rules and building monitoring that engineering teams rely on. Ability to gather your own requirements and work across organizational boundaries in an ambiguous environment with limited direction. Pref

e41c273d913f.title: Research Engineer, Beneficial Deployments
e41c273d913f.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Beneficial Deployments ensures AI reaches and benefits the communities that need it most. We partner with nonprofits, foundations, and mission-driven organizations to deploy Claude in education, global health, economic mobility, and life sciences — focusing on raising the floor for those who need it most. We're looking for a Research Engineer to make Claude better at the real-world work that matters most to Beneficial Deployments. You'll identify where our models fall short, build the environments and reward signals used to train them, run experiments, and measure whether new capabilities generalize beyond the training data. You'll also work closely with the Beneficial Deployments team, using your knowledge of the capability frontier to advise on how they can achieve their goals over the coming years. Key responsibilities Identify capability gaps in our models and turn them into a research agenda Own the end-to-end process of creating RL environments, from task sourcing and reward design through training, using both real-world and synthetic data Collaborate with domain experts to design data pipelines Develop and improve QA frameworks to catch reward hacking and ensure env quality Run generalization experiments to measure how data strategy changes improve model capabilities Partner with other RL research teams and product teams to align on capability goals Minimum qualifications Have experience with fine-tuning large language models for specific domains or real-world use cases Have experience with reinforcement learning, reward design, or training data curation for LLMs Have a track record of setting your own direction and delivering on ambiguous, high-stakes work with little oversight, such as by running your own team, research program, or company Can turn deep technical understanding into clear strategic recommendations that influence senior, non-technical leaders Think rigorously about how quickly AI capabilities are advancing and are ready to plan around the possibility that transformative AI arrives soon Find value in reading through datasets to understand them and spot issues Are excited about a role that combines hands-on applied research with strategy and influence Preferred qualifications Have experience training production ML systems Have experience designing evals or benchmarks for LLMs Have domain expertise in healthcare, global health, or philanthropy Have experience with multilingual models or low-resource languages Have worked with NGOs, ministries of health, funders, or other partners in low- and middle-income countries The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $500,000 — $850,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goal

f7b3235cacb3.title: Research Operations, External Artifacts
f7b3235cacb3.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Every time Anthropic releases a model, we publish a system card: a long-form technical document that describes the model's capabilities, safety properties, evaluation results, and the reasoning behind our deployment decisions. System cards are some of the most consequential and widely read documents we produce, and they are one way we hold ourselves publicly accountable for the safety claims we make. We're hiring a Research Operations Specialist to help own system card production. You'll work embedded with research and safety teams through each launch, coordinating contributions from dozens of researchers, holding the schedule and the open-threads list, and making sure the document ships on time as a single, accurate, internally consistent whole. Along the way you'll do real editorial work: turning results and researcher notes into clear, honest prose and pushing back when an explanation doesn't hold together. System cards sit within a wider family of external safety artifacts, including risk reports and Responsible Scaling Policy (RSP) updates. Part of this role is keeping the system card consistent with those documents so that Anthropic's public safety story reads as one coherent account rather than several. This role sits in Research Operations and works closely with Alignment, Safeguards, Frontier Red Team, and capabilities research. The core of the job is part project management, part translation: keeping a complex, many-author, hard-deadline document on track while making frontier safety research legible to researchers, policymakers, journalists, and the public — without sacrificing precision. Key responsibilities Drive system card production end to end — own the timeline, the contributor list, the open-threads tracker, and the definition of done for each launch Coordinate dozens of contributors across Alignment, Safeguards, Frontier Red Team, Interpretability, and capabilities research; chase drafts, resolve differences of perspective, seek ground truth, and run final formatting and polish Edit, and sometimes write, content; work directly with researchers to turn their results, notes, and plots into clear, scientific, non-marketing prose and maintain Anthropic's voice across sections drafted by many different people Guard accuracy and consistency; catch terminology drift, claims that subtly contradict each other, and discrepancies between internal communications and system card drafts Keep the system card aligned with related artifacts; track what's being said in risk reports, RSP disclosures, and other safety documentation so the system card stays consistent with them, and flag conflicts early Improve the process between launches; build and maintain templates, style guidance, contributor guides, checklists, and reusable section scaffolds so each cycle starts from a stronger baseline Pick up other research-adjacent operations and writing, such as internal research summaries, release notes, and documentation that helps research leadership communicate clearly Minimum qualifications Strong project management and execution skills; able to track dozens of open threads to closure during compressed launch periods with many moving parts and many owners Demonstrated ability to coordinate and influence without direct authority, building trust while chasing drafts and giving constructive editorial feedback Excellent technical writing skills; able to take dense, jargon-heavy source material and produce prose that is precise, honest, and readable by a non-specialist Comfort working closely with researchers; able to read an evaluation results table, ask the right clarifying questions, and push back when an explanation doesn't hold together Working knowledge of large language models (LLMs) at a conceptual level, including fluency with vocabulary such as pretraining, reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), context windows, evals, and red-teaming Data communication literacy; able to identify how a chart or table could be made clearer and more accurate High integrity and a genuine sense of accountability around producing documents that hold Anthropic publicly responsible for its safety claims Preferred qualifications Familiarity with AI safety, AI policy, alignment research, evaluation methodology, or the RSP landscape beyond baseline LLM knowledge Background in science communication, research publishing, or technical journalism A track record of shipping long-form technical documents, such as research reports, whitepapers, technical standards, regulatory filings, or science journalism Experience with safety, risk, or compliance documentation, such as regulatory submissions, safety cases, security disclosures, or clinical or scientific reporting Skill in visual communication and experience shipping polished, on-brand documents Light scripting or tooling ability (enough to automate a formatting check or wrangle a spreadsheet) The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. Kubernetes operations on one side, cross-team coordination on the other. Efficiency Measuring and improving how effectively every major workload uses the hardware it runs on. Instrumenting utilization across training, inference, and eval systems, building benchmarking infrastructure, establishing per-config baselines, and working directly with system-owning teams to close the gaps. The metric has to be good enough that the team on the hook for it agrees with the number. Attribution and forecasting Connecting what the fleet costs to what the business is doing with it. Reconciling CSP billing exports against vendor telemetry and internal systems with mismatched schemas, attributing spend to the workloads and teams that generate it, and turning inference demand signals and research roadmaps into a defensible compute plan. Efficiency metrics have to survive contact with finance: stripped of pure demand and unit-price effects, reproducible month over month, and legible to a CFO. Key responsibilities Build the planning and allocation stack — the tools leadership uses to allocate capacity, teams use to plan against their allocations, and the scheduler enforces. Cross-region and cross-provider placement, guardrails, queueing, occupancy KPIs. Drive the efficiency programs: stranding and rightsizing, unused capacity recovery, and job-level utilization across training, inference, and eval. Establish per-config baselines and work with system-owning teams to close the gaps. Directly influence decisions around a significant area of company investment. Own attribution and forecasting — reconcile billing across ten-plus providers against telemetry and internal systems, attribute spend to the workloads that generate it, and turn demand signals and research roadmaps into a defensible compute plan and supply pipeline. Build the data platform underneath all of it: pipelines ingesting occupancy, utilization, and cost from a rapidly diversifying fleet into BigQuery, with real ownership of completeness, latency SLOs, and gap detection. Every new provider is a net-new integration. Operate Kubernetes-native systems at scale — collection agents, workload labeling, and the taint/reservation/scheduling behavior that determines what capacity is actually usable. Treat the output as a product, not a pipeline. Gather your own requirements, define schema contracts, and design for consumers ranging from research engineers to a CFO — including on-call and SLOs, because these surfaces are load-bearing for the company. What you bring A strong track record building and operating production systems. This is a hands-on engineering role with a devops flavor. Python and SQL at production quality. Most pipeline code is Python; the presentation layer is BigQuery SQL, including table-valued functions and views. Both need to be idiomatic, well-tested, and maintainable. Deep experience with at least one major cloud provider (Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, or Microsoft Azure) and its operations Experience with observability tooling stack, including Prometheus, PromQL, and Grafana, including writing recording rules and building monitoring that engineering teams rely on. Ability to gather your own requirements and work across organizational boundaries in an ambiguous environment with limited direction. Preferred qualifications Experience with capacity planning,

77c73fdb6f2c.description: CSQ128R208 PLEASE NOTE: Due to federal contract requirements and client site access obligations, U.S. citizenship and eligibility for a U.S. government secret clearance are required to access classified information. Candidates with an active Secret or higher clearance are strongly encouraged to apply. About Databricks: At Databricks, we are passionate about enabling data teams to solve the world's toughest problems, from making the next mode of transportation a reality to accelerating the development of medical breakthroughs. We do this by building and running the world's best data and AI infrastructure platform so our customers can use deep data insights to improve their business. Ensure applications are secure, highly available, scalable, and set the standard for modern software engineering and Databricks best practices globally. Deliver Technical Excellence: Orchestrate multi-team, multi-quarter technical engagements. Product Engineering Influence: Partner heavily with Databricks Core Engineering and Product leadership. Translate complex, edge-case developer challenges from the field into actionable product roadmap initiatives, APIs, and platform enhancements. Pioneer and open-source massive-scale code accelerators, global development frameworks, and engineering best practices that scale impact across all federal accounts and elevate the entire FDE organization. What We're Looking For: Minimum Qualifications: 10+ years of experience in software engineering, backend development, or distributed systems engineering, with a proven track record of architectural leadership. Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Information Systems, Applied Science, Mathematics, Engineering, or equivalent relevant years of experience in an Engineering function. Expert-level proficiency writing scalable production code in Python, Scala, Java, Go, or JavaScript/TypeScript, and architecting solutions using modern application frameworks. Deep, authoritative multi-cloud architectural expertise (AWS, Azure, GCP) with the ability to design cross-cloud or hybrid distributed systems. Advanced experience with distributed computing with Apache Spark™ and deep internal knowledge of the Spark runtime engine, optimization, and scaling. Mastery of CI/CD pipelines, containerization (Docker, Kubernetes), and infrastructure as code (Terraform) for complex, high-security production deployments. Proven ability to design and deploy performant, end-to-end software architectures that combine backend services, ML/AI models, and user-facing interfaces with zero-downtime requirements. Extensive experience steering complex technical project delivery—managing massive scope, driving agile engineering teams, and translating ambiguous business requirements into actionable, enterprise-grade software solutions. 3188271fe9eb.title: AI Transformation Lead, Marketing
3188271fe9eb.location: San Francisco, New York, Seattle, Chicago, Atlanta, Remote in the US
3188271fe9eb.description: Who we are About Stripe Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies — from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups — use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career. About the team The Stripe Marketing organization is undergoing a fundamental transformation in how it works. We're building a team of Forward Deployed AI Accelerators (FDAs) embedded directly with marketing cohorts to make AI the default mode for all work — not an occasional tool, but the foundation of how every marketer at Stripe executes. Today, marketers are already achieving remarkable results — building their own data dashboards, creating agents that compress multi-day processes, and authoring tools that accelerate workflows. The FDA team exists to take what's working and systematically scale it across the entire marketing organization. What you'll do As a Forward Deployed AI Accelerator, you'll be embedded with a cohort of 25–45 marketers organized by functional team, shared workflow, or location. You'll build alongside them, and you'll help them fundamentally change how they operate. Your measure of success is the number of workflows you've permanently transformed and the extent to which those in your cohort start any task with an AI tool. Responsibilities Identify and document the highest-leverage workflow transformations within your cohort's day-to-day work by deeply understanding their processes and outputs Build custom tools, agents, automations, and skills tailored to each marketer's specific responsibilities Coach and partner with each marketer through a progressive journey — from awareness, to first win, to regular AI integration, to full workflow transformation, to self-sufficiency Teach marketers to build and iterate on their own tools over time, creating independence Recognize patterns across your cohort and systematically scale what works — a tool built for one marketer will be reusable for their peers Document every tool, playbook, and transformation pattern you build so the entire FDA team uses each other's work Share wins visibly within your cohort and with leadership to build momentum, inspire, and celebrate success Track individual and cohort progress rigorously against a defined maturity model, moving every marketer toward self-sustaining, AI-first work Prepare marketers for an agentic future — not just prompt writing, but designing, building, and overseeing autonomous, multi-agent workflows Who you are We're looking for people who have already lived the transformation they'll be driving for others. You've used AI to fundamentally change how work gets done, not as a novelty, but as your default operating mode. You are a deep AI practitioner. You build agents, automations, and tools fluently. You don't just know what AI can do in theory. You've built things that changed how real teams operate, and the people you built for actually use what you shipped. You build in real time alongside the people you support. You spot transformation opportunities and execute on them. You look at a team's workflows and see where AI changes the economics: where existing work can be done in a fraction of the time, or where entirely new programs become viable that weren't worth doing before. Then you build the thing, not just the slide. You understand marketing work. You either have direct experience in marketing or quickly learn the workflows, deliverables, tools, and pressures of your assigned cohort. You know that understanding someone's work is a prerequisite to transforming it. You are a pattern recognizer. When you build something that works for one person, you immediately see how it applies to others. You think in systems, not one-off solutions. You are a strong communicator. You explain technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences, adapt your style to different people, and make progress visible to leadership and stakeholders. You are high-caliber, persistent, and versatile. Your skills and experience are valuable across the company. You're the kind of person who succeeds in many roles at Stripe. You bias toward action and speed. You'd rather show someone a working proof-of-concept on their own deliverable today than present a polished deck about what's theoretically possible next quarter. You are comfortable with ambiguity and evolution. This is a new team building a new operating model. The playbook will be rewritten as we learn. You thrive in that environment. Minimum requirements 5+ years of professional experience in a role requiring diagnostic thinking, problem-solving, and cross-functional collaboration Demonstrated, hands-on experience building and deploying AI-powered agents, tools, automations, or workflows that real people use in their actual work, whether that made existing processes meaningfully more efficient or made previously unviable work possible for the first time Proficiency with AI development tools and platforms (e.g., Claude Code, Codex, custom agent frameworks, API integrations, workflow automation tools) Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences and adapt your style to different learners Comfort working across multiple workstreams and relationships simultaneously (you'll be supporting 25–45 marketers at varying stages of their AI journey) Track record of coaching, teaching, or enabling others, with evidence that people you've helped actually changed how they work Preferred qualifications Experience in a formal AI transformation role where the job was substantially about identifying opportunities for workflow transformation and executing on them with hand

This role combines hands-on technical leadership with cross-functional influence, with a particular focus on evaluating agentic approaches to merchant fraud detection and account reviews. You'll define how we measure the quality and impact of these approaches, translate findings into technical priorities, and align partners on where and how to apply them. You'll bring scientific rigor and practical judgment to decisions that balance fraud prevention, operational efficiency, and the experience of legitimate users. Responsibilities Shape the team's technical vision and roadmap across merchant fraud detection, account reviews, and interventions, identifying opportunities where data science can have the greatest impact. Lead cross-functional initiatives with Fraud Engineering, Risk Operations, Product, and other partners, turning ambiguous fraud problems into clear technical plans and measurable outcomes. Define evaluation frameworks for AI agents used in fraud investigations and account reviews, including evaluation datasets, quality metrics, offline testing, and online experiments. Combine model and agent evaluations with reviewer feedback and business outcomes to identify failure modes, guide iteration, and inform deployment decisions. Provide hands-on technical leadership in machine learning, statistical modeling, experimentation, and measurement, helping teams work through complex problems from research to production. Develop approaches to measure the impact of fraud interventions, accounting for tradeoffs among fraud losses, review efficiency, and friction for legitimate users. Translate technical findings into recommendations that influence priorities and investment across teams. Raise standards for evaluation, reproducibility, and production monitoring, and mentor data scientists in their technical and professional development. Lead complex projects from problem definition through modeling, implementation, and evaluation. Stay hands-on with analysis, code, and model development, and partner with engineering teams on production deployment. Establish strong practices for model evaluation, monitoring, reproducibility, and analytical rigor. Mentor data scientists and help peers grow their technical judgment, business understanding, and ability to deliver results. b04fea14d71b.description: About Us At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company. At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in. Locations: Austin TX, Champaign IL, Lisbon Portugal, London England, Atlanta GA, Washington DC, Location (all hybrid): Austin, TX; Champaign, IL; Seattle, WA; Atlanta, GA; Washington, DC; London, UK; Lisbon, PT About the team Cloudflare is redefining the way networks are run at scale, and some of the largest networks in the world now run their traffic through us. Companies connect their data centers, offices, and clouds to Cloudflare, and our network carries, routes, and protects that traffic from hundreds of cities around the world. Our teams build the systems that make those connections work: the APIs customers use to describe their networks, the control planes that turn that into configuration on every server we run, the health checks that move traffic away from failing paths, and the BGP sessions we run with customer networks (the systems behind products like Magic Transit and Cloudflare WAN). We are a team of engineers and product managers who obsess over quickly building products that solve real customer problems, using techniques that take advantage of Cloudflare's unique architecture and global network footprint. About the role We're looking for engineers who like hard distributed systems problems: keeping state consistent across hundreds of data centers, changing configuration safely while traffic is flowing, and deciding what to do when parts of the system fail. You don't need to be a networking expert; we'll help you learn the rest. Some of the things you'd work on: The APIs and control plane services that take a customer's network configuration (tunnels, routes, health checks) and push it to every server in our network, quickly and safely Tunnel health checks that run from every data center, and the logic that reroutes customer traffic when a path degrades An anycast BGP implementation where customer sessions survive being moved between servers and data centers, built partly on Cloudflare's own developer platform Experimental tooling that catch routing flaps and failures before customers do Getting logs and analytics back to customers so they can see what their networks are doing You'll build, deploy, and operate these systems on top of one of the largest edge networks in the world. You'll partner with some of the best engineers and product managers, on our teams and across Cloudflare, to solve big problems that have a meaningful impact in the lives of our customers and users. We're looking for curious, empathetic engineers who are excited to join us in changing the way networking is done! For Champaign IL based hires: Estimated annual salary of $168,000 - $210,000. For Washington, DC based hires: Estimated annual salary of $185,000 - $230,000. For Seattle, WA based hires: Estimated annual salary of $185,000 - $230,000. For Portugal based hires: Estimated annual salary is between €66,000 - 83,000. ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI’s Integrity team protects people and businesses using ChatGPT, Codex, and the API from fraud, abuse, and harmful misuse. Our work spans payment and promotional abuse, compromised accounts and API credentials, business and advertiser integrity, and emerging misuse of frontier AI capabilities. We also help product teams measure authentic usage so that abuse doesn’t distort decisions about how our products are growing.

Integrity Data Science helps teams decide where to intervene and whether those interventions work. A payment control can prevent fraud while blocking legitimate purchases. A product launch can make it easier for customers to get started while creating new opportunities for abuse. We measure both sides of those decisions.



ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Data Scientist on Integrity, you’ll find emerging abuse patterns, size their impact, and lead the analytical work behind decisions about detection, enforcement, and product launches. You’ll work with Product, Engineering, Research, Policy, and Operations to turn findings into improvements and measure what happens after they ship.

 - Investigate anomalous activity across products. Estimate how common a problem is, who is affected, and what it costs users or the business. Use that evidence to recommend where to focus.

 - Define outcome metrics and guardrails, establish baselines, and build monitoring that surfaces changes in abuse, customer friction, and operational performance.

 - Help build and evaluate detection rules, classifiers, and human review workflows. Use labeled samples and review outcomes to understand what the systems miss, where they flag legitimate activity, and how those errors vary across users and products.

 - Design randomized holdouts and use quasi-experimental or observational methods when randomization is impractical. Estimate harm or fraud losses prevented alongside effects on legitimate users, revenue, compute costs, and review workload. Recommend whether to launch, expand, adjust, or retire a control.

 - Trace where signals, review decisions, or enforcement actions break down. Work with partners to close gaps and build reusable datasets, analyses, and investigation tools.



IDEAL CANDIDATE

 - You use AI tools to investigate large, messy datasets, test hypotheses quickly, and automate recurring analyses. You’re fluent in SQL and Python and can verify AI-generated queries, code, and conclusions against the underlying data.

 - You have strong statistical judgment and experience with experimentation, causal inference, or observational analysis. You can reason from incomplete or biased labels and explain how uncertainty affects a decision.

 - You take ownership of open-ended problems, from deciding what to measure through recommending an action and checking whether it worked.

 - You communicate clearly with technical and nontechnical partners and can explain the tradeoffs behind a recommendation.

 - Experience in integrity, trust and safety, fraud or risk analytics, security analytics, or applied ML evaluation is helpful. Experience evaluating detection systems, human review, or LLM-based classifiers is a plus.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Applied organization brings OpenAI’s most advanced technology to people and organizations around the world through products such as ChatGPT and the APIs that power a growing ecosystem of developer and enterprise applications. Data Engineering builds and operates trustworthy, secure, and reliable data systems that support decisions across OpenAI.



The Trust & Safety Data Engineering team builds privacy-safe foundations that help OpenAI understand and mitigate abuse, launch products safely, and operate accountable safety systems at scale.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a Data Engineering Manager to lead the Trust & Safety Data Engineering team. This role is accountable for the team’s health, talent, priorities, and results, as well as the data strategy for abuse detection, investigations, enforcement, safety measurement, launch readiness, and transparency reporting.



You will partner with senior individual contributors and cross-functional leaders to turn sensitive, fast-moving safety needs into durable, governed data products and ML data capabilities.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Build and grow a high-performing, inclusive team; hire well, develop senior engineers, give clear feedback, and manage performance effectively.

 - Define the data strategy and roadmap with senior technical leaders, establishing clear ownership and delegation boundaries so decisions are made at the right level.

 - Lead the delivery of scalable, governed datasets, pipelines, and data products for critical Trust & Safety workflows.

 - Enable ML development with high-quality features, labels, training data, evaluation datasets, and production data pipelines.

 - Set strong standards for metric definitions, data quality, privacy, security, access controls, documentation, reliability, observability, and incident response.

 - Partner across Trust & Safety, Integrity, Investigations, Engineering, Data Science, Policy, Privacy, and Operations to translate ambiguous needs into measurable outcomes.

 - Set clear goals, make explicit capacity and priority tradeoffs, and communicate progress, risks, and commitments across technical and operational stakeholders.




YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have led and scaled data engineering teams, with evidence of strong hiring, senior-talent development, performance management, and sustained delivery through the team.

 - Bring strong technical judgment across large-scale data systems—including SQL, Python or Scala, Spark, orchestration, data modeling, streaming, and lakehouse or warehouse architectures—and can challenge designs and guide senior engineers without owning every implementation detail.

 - Have experience in trust and safety, integrity, abuse prevention, fraud, investigations, risk, privacy, or another domain where data systems inform consequential decisions.

 - Build strong cross-functional partnerships and turn ambiguous needs into clear ownership, durable data contracts, technical roadmaps, and reliable execution.

 - Care deeply about privacy, security, governance, data quality, and the operational health of systems used for sensitive workflows.




WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Trust & Safety teams across OpenAI move faster because they can rely on trustworthy, well-owned data foundations provided by this team.

 - The team operates with clear goals, healthy execution rhythms, explicit capacity tradeoffs, strong technical and operational standards, and a hiring and development plan that matches the domain’s ambition.

65ab84d96e90.title: Protection Scientist Engineer, Integrity
65ab84d96e90.description:
About the Team

The Integrity team is responsible for the scaled systems that help identify and respond to bad actors and harm on OpenAI’s platforms. We protect users and the wider world by developing responses to complex harms and building the harm protections needed for new product and model launches. Integrity’s work spans not only across frontier harms like biological weapons and cybersecurity, but also high severity abuses such as child safety, nation-state misuse, and violence.

About the Role

Protection Scientists within Integrity design, orchestrate, and mature systems of defence against usage harms enabled by OpenAI's products. We are systems thinkers that combine deep harm domain expertise with breadth across investigation, data science, machine learning, policy and operations. Our distinctive strength is understanding how these disciplines fit together and translating between them to design and build effective systems of defence.

In San Francisco, we are hiring for protection work focused on sextortion, trafficking, national security (including nation-state misuse), and jailbreaks. Depending on your domain expertise, your work could include identifying AI-enabled coercion and exploitation, detecting misuse that supports trafficking, uncovering coordinated activity by state-linked actors, or investigating attempts to circumvent model safeguards. You will translate these evolving threats into detection systems and interventions that reduce harm.

Your core hands-on technical responsibility is harm detection. You will design, build, evaluate and maintain production detection systems, drawing on investigative expertise, data and shared engineering platforms. You will develop signals and classifiers that identify abusive behaviour and patterns across accounts and activity, and adapt them as adversaries change tactics.

You will also own the strategy and cross-functional delivery of protection work for a harm area or product launch. Working closely with investigators and other domain experts, you will ground the design in a deep understanding of how the harm occurs and translate that understanding into a system of defence. You will connect detection with policy, review, interventions, enforcement and measurement, continually calibrating the system against real cases and expert judgement as it scales.

You will identify what needs to be built or changed and make it happen. Success requires setting clear priorities, aligning partners, resolving dependencies and communicating evidence, decisions and trade-offs crisply. It also requires a willingness to jump in and work directly on whatever is blocking system effectiveness, using your breadth of skills.

This role is based in our San Francisco office and includes participation in an on-call rotation that may involve resolving urgent escalations outside normal working hours. Some investigations may involve sensitive content, including sexual, violent or otherwise disturbing material.

In this role, you will:

 - Define and drive protection strategy for a harm area or launch. Translate ambiguous risks into goals, priorities and roadmaps, and make trade-offs based on evidence, risk and available capacity.

 - Directly build and maintain harm detection. Develop production signals, classifiers and pipelines using SQL, Python, machine learning and language models, integrating with shared engineering platforms.

 - Lead cross-functional execution. Translate between specialist roles, establish shared understanding and ownership, resolve technical and organisational dependencies, and communicate recommendations and specific asks clearly.

 - Investigate exploitation and national security threats within your area of focus. Work with domain experts to understand actor behaviour, recognise patterns of coercion, exploitation or coordinated misuse, and turn case findings into detection criteria.

 - Connect detection to effective action. Partner with Policy and Operations to develop review and escalation protocols, distinguish abusive activity from legitimate use, and improve interventions as new cases reveal gaps.

 - Evaluate and improve the complete system of defence. Measure remaining harm, detection quality and intervention effectiveness and collaborate with Data Science on more sophisticated metrics. Use expert feedback and operational outcomes to guide improvements.

 - Protect product and model launches. Define data, detection and review requirements; establish monitoring; investigate gaps and critical escalations; and drive improvements informed by post-launch findings.

 - Scale effective approaches with language models, agents and reusable tools. Choose where automation and human judgement are needed, and build documentation and processes that improve reliability and help others extend the work.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Think in systems. You have enough breadth across technical, analytical, investigative and operational disciplines to understand how they fit together, recognise gaps and translate between specialist perspectives.

 - Bring deep expertise in at least one of sextortion, trafficking, national security, jailbreaks or a closely related harm domain. Relevant backgrounds may include trust and safety investigations, counter-exploitation, threat intelligence, investigations of state-linked actors, or adversarial testing of AI safeguards. You do not need expertise across all of these areas.

 - Have experience investigating adversarial behaviour and translating incomplete, evolving evidence into actionable signals. You can connect individual cases to broader patterns while being explicit about uncertainty and the risk of misidentifying legitimate activity.

 - Are proficient in SQL and Python and have experience writing reliable and efficient production code for detection and data processing. Additional ML or SWE experience is a plus.

 - Can apply quantitative analysis and machine-learning methods to measure risk

14aca00e8863.description:
About the Team

The Model Policy team within OpenAI’s Safety Systems organization defines how increasingly capable AI models should behave in real-world settings. We turn research on emerging risks into model behavior policies, evaluations, and safeguards.

About the Role

As AI systems become more capable, the same advances that expand their legitimate uses can also lower barriers to harm. Emerging misuse risks range from AI assistance with conventional weapons development and the misuse of AI-enabled robotics to fraud, impersonation, and other forms of abuse that people can carry out at scale using AI agents. You’ll build threat models for how people could misuse AI in digital and physical settings, assess what access to AI changes in practice, and use that evidence to define how models should respond.

This role is based in San Francisco. We offer relocation support and work from the office three days a week, with optional work from home on Thursdays and Fridays.

In this role, you will: 

 - Build and update threat models as capabilities evolve. Assess what people could plausibly do, what expertise and resources they would need, and how AI changes those barriers.

 - Define when models should help, limit assistance, or refuse in situations where the same capability has legitimate and harmful uses.

 - Turn expert safety judgment into instructions, training examples, and evaluations that teach models when to help, when to limit assistance, and when to refuse.

 - Turn threat models into evaluation scenarios and grading guidance. Analyze model outputs, red-team findings, and deployment data to identify where models enable misuse or block legitimate work.

 - Partner with research, engineering, security, and product teams to apply findings to model training, deployment decisions, and monitoring.

You might thrive in this role if you: 

 - Have hands-on experience building, testing, or assessing dual-use technologies, or a track record of threat modeling grounded in how people use and misuse real systems.

 - Demonstrate deep practical experience in one relevant domain and the judgment to know when to bring in experts from others.

 - Are able to assess whether a capability demonstrated in a test materially changes what someone could do outside it.

 - Can translate technical evidence and uncertainty into clear policy boundaries and measurable evaluation criteria.

 - Have experience analyzing gold sets, evaluation results, and training data to spot inconsistent human labels, assess how annotator disagreement affects measured performance, and decide what to investigate next.

 - Are comfortable working hands-on with model data and evaluation results, including inspecting examples, analyzing failure patterns, assessing data quality, and distinguishing policy failures from grader, model, or system failures.

 - Use empirical evidence to develop and refine safety policies and safeguards.

 - Work well across disciplines and revises their judgment as capabilities and evidence change.

 - Enjoy fast-paced, collaborative research environments where priorities shift as models, evidence, and risks change.

Relevant Publications

About the Team

Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and advancing toward AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world environments. Working across the full model and systems stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the physical constraints of real-world systems to improve people’s lives.

About the Role

As a Mechanical Design Engineer on the Robotics team, you’ll design battery packs for robots and help define how those packs integrate into the rest of the system. In this hands-on individual contributor role, you’ll own mechanical designs from early architecture and packaging through prototyping, validation, and production. You’ll work closely with electrical, thermal, systems, and manufacturing engineers to build packs that are safe, reliable, and practical to assemble and service.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA and requires in-person presence 4 days a week.

e61dc5fad211.description: About Us At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company. At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in. Available Locations: Austin, TX | London, UK (Hybrid) Role Summary Replicate is now part of Cloudflare, and we are bringing its AI inference platform onto Cloudflare's global network and Workers AI. As a Senior Platform Engineer on the Replicate team, you will design, build, and operate the core distributed systems that accept, schedule, execute, and meter customer inference requests across Kubernetes clusters, multiple cloud providers, and heterogeneous GPU infrastructure. You will be a key technical driver in migrating Replicate’s models, workloads, and traffic onto Workers AI while maintaining high availability, low latency, and seamless backwards compatibility for existing customers. You will partner closely with engineers across Workers AI, core infrastructure, and product teams to solve hard problems in container orchestration, cold-start optimization, multi-tenant GPU scheduling, and high-throughput API routing. We are looking for an engineer who thrives in complex production environments, brings pragmatic architectural judgment, and elevates the engineering bar through strong code, thoughtful design reviews, and technical mentorship. Role Responsibilities Architect and Build Core Platform Systems: Design, implement, and maintain the backend services powering Replicate's inference lifecycle—including public APIs, request queueing, workload scheduling, container runtime orchestration, and usage metering/billing. Drive the Workers AI Migration: Architect and execute the technical migration of Replicate models and live inference traffic to Workers AI, building translation layers, dual-routing/shadowing pipelines, API compatibility adapters, and graceful fallback mechanisms with zero customer disruption. Optimize Performance, Scale, and Cost: Profile and improve system throughput, cold-start latency, and GPU utilization across multi-cloud Kubernetes clusters and Cloudflare's edge infrastructure. Ensure Production Reliability: Participate in the team’s on-call rotation, lead triage and mitigation during live production incidents, author thorough post-incident reviews, and build automated remediation and observability tooling. Raise the Technical Bar: Author clear technical design documents (RFCs), conduct thorough code and architecture reviews, and mentor fellow engineers on distributed systems best practices and operational excellence. Cross-Team Technical Collaboration: Partner directly with Workers AI, networking, storage, and security engineering teams across Cloudflare to integrate Replicate’s platform primitives into Cloudflare’s broader AI stack. Role Requirements (Must-Have Skills) Distributed Systems Experience: 5+ years of software engineering experience designing, building, and operating high-throughput, low-latency distributed production systems with strict availability requirements. Strong Programming Proficiency: Deep hands-on proficiency in Go, Python, or TypeScript, with experience writing clean, concurrent, maintainable, and well-tested backend services.
