c3d241907988.title: Graduate Quantitative Researcher 2028 – Expression of Interest
c3d241907988.description:
Register your interest below. This is an expression of interest, not a job application, and it does not start an assessment process.

Looking to start full-time in 2027? Our Graduate Quantitative Researcher (2027 Start) role is currently open. Apply here.

If you enjoy using mathematics and code to investigate difficult questions, you could make a direct contribution to Optiver’s success in global markets. As a Graduate Quantitative Researcher, you’ll work across the full research process, from framing the question and choosing the data to building, testing and deploying models. Machine Learning is central to the work, whether you’re extracting signals, forecasting prices or modelling relationships. Our data, compute and production infrastructure let you test ideas quickly, understand where they fail and decide what to investigate next.

Our researchers believe in academic discourse and invite fellow researchers, traders and engineers to challenge each hypothesis. Different perspectives help improve the question, the model and how it performs in production. Through constant testing, analysis and refinement, you’ll help our quantitative models adapt as markets evolve.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

Your onboarding 

You’ll participate in Global Optiver Academy, a structured onboarding programme for graduates. It gives new joiners a shared foundation in how Optiver trades, builds systems, and manages risk before they move into their teams. As part of your onboarding, you'll gain exposure to the AI tools and technologies that support research and development across the business. 

Your responsibilities 

Depending on the team you join, you'll own the research end to end. That could include:

  • Building models for pricing, forecasting and signal discovery, choosing the statistical, mathematical or Machine Learning methods that best fit the problem.
  • Working across petabytes of market, order-flow and unstructured data to find signals that improve strategies as conditions change.
  • Monitoring models in production and using live behavior to refine your assumptions and decide what to investigate next.
  • Using deep learning and AI-enabled workflows to shorten the loop from hypothesis to evidence.
  • Working directly with researchers, traders and engineers to shape problems and understand how system constraints affect performance.

WHO YOU ARE

We're looking for aspiring Quantitative Researchers who are versatile and creative in innovating and suggesting new solutions. In return, we'll give you the freedom to pursue your ideas and implement them right into our production systems. 

In terms of skills and qualifications, we're looking for:

  • An academic degree in Engineering, Physics, Maths, Econometrics, Computer science or equivalent, with outstanding academic achievements
  • Programming experience in any language (preferably Python, but C, C++, Basic, JAVA, etc. are also a plus)
  • Ability to apply concepts of probability, calculus and linear algebra
  • Competitive attitude and eagerness to constantly improve
  • Ability to learn quickly
  • Excellent verbal and written English language skills

WHAT YOU’LL GET

You’ll join a culture of collaboration and excellence, where you’ll be surrounded by curious thinkers and creative problem solvers. Motivated by a passion for continuous improvement, you’ll thrive in a supportive, high-performing environment alongside talent colleagues, working collaboratively to tackle the toughest problems in the financial markets.

In addition, you’ll receive:

  • A performance-based bonus structure, enabling all of our employees to benefit from our global profit pool
  • The opportunity to work alongside best-in-class professionals from over 50 countries
  • 25 paid vacation days in your first year, increasing to 30 from your second year onwards
  • Training opportunities, discounts on health benefits, and fully paid first-class commuting expenses
  • Extensive office perks, including breakfast, lunch and dinner, world-class barista coffee, bi-weekly chair massages, Friday afternoon drinks, a bicycle to explore Amsterdam and much more
  • Training and continuous learning opportunities, including access to conferences and tech events
  • Competitive relocation packages and visa sponsorship where necessary for expats

HOW TO REGISTER

Are you interested in furthering your career on one of the most dynamic and exciting trading floors in Europe?

Complete the short form below with your details and upload your CV in English. Registering your interest is not a job application, and it does not start an assessment process. We'll contact you when we have opportunities that match your profile.

Kindly note that we do not require any assistance from third-parties including agencies in the recruitment of this role. If you have any questions feel free to contact our Recruitment team via our recruitment inquiry form.

Diversity statement

Optiver is committed to diversity and inclusion.

We encourage applications from candidates from any and all backgrounds, and we welcome requests for reasonable adjustments during the process to ensure that you can best demonstrate your abilities. Please let us know if you would like to request any

1b427dda5c7f.description: This is an Atlantic porfolio company. The opportunity Demand for AI compute is outrunning the infrastructure to deliver it, and the environmental bill is growing with it: more fossil power, more freshwater, more land. New capacity on land also means waiting years for power, sites and permits. We take a different route: we bring compute to the power. Far offshore, the wind blows stronger and steadier than anywhere on land, and no grid will ever reach it. Using it lets AI scale without adding carbon or competing with communities and nature for water and land. We're building fleets of autonomous ships that turn that wind into AI compute at sea. Each ship carries its own wind turbines and computing on board, and navigates on its own across the open ocean, following the strongest and steadiest winds. No mooring, no cables to shore: the fleet goes where the energy is. It's AI infrastructure built from the ground up for the open ocean, from power systems and autonomy to high-density computing, engineered to run in one of the harshest environments on Earth. No grid queue. No freshwater. No land. Zero-carbon compute that scales with the fleet. Firm, low-carbon power at a target cost of ~€50/MWh, one of the biggest costs in running AI compute 70%+ capacity factor: offshore wind that behaves like baseload First demonstrator at sea in late 2027 Founded in 2025 by repeat entrepreneurs and industrial leaders. Backed by major international investors. The mandate You'll work directly with the CEO and the board and own the company's business strategy as we go from first demonstrator to fleet. Our platform opens several paths to value across compute and infrastructure, from capacity to hardware to the services around them. You'll decide which to pursue first, build them into the core of the company, and open new ones as the fleet grows. What you'll own Business model & strategy. Shape the business model and evolve it as we scale: products, markets, pricing and unit economics. Turn a breakthrough technology into a bankable one. Strategic partnerships. Decide which partners and customers we build the company with, from AI labs and cloud providers to chipmakers and sovereign compute programmes, and secure the relationships that shape our first fleet. Capital strategy. Work with the CEO on how the business case underpins project finance and fundraising, and own that story with investors and the board. Product direction. Make sure what we build at sea is shaped by where the market is going, working hand in hand with our marine, power and systems engineers. Ecosystem & alliances. Build the partnerships a new infrastructure class needs: chip and systems vendors, cloud platforms, data center operators, ports and financiers. Category leadership. Be our external voice on summit stages, with policymakers and in the press, and make us the reference for AI infrastructure at sea. The business organisation. Build and lead the team across strategy, partnerships and commercial that takes us from demonstrator to fleet. Who you are You've built businesses in deep tech or infrastructure. You've led strategy, business development or a P&L in AI, cloud, data centers or semiconductors, and shaped large, multi-year partnerships. You've taken frontier technology to market. You've brought new, capital-intensive technology to its first major customers and closed the off-take agreements, capacity reservations or long-term contracts that made it bankable. You build, not just run. You've built something from zero, whether a company, a business line or a market, and you're at your best when the playbook doesn't exist yet. You see the whole board. You move between unit economics, partnerships, financing and long-term strategy in the same afternoon. You know AI infrastructure from the inside. Compute economics, workload constraints, and where the market is heading. Compute and infrastructure are your world. GPUs, data centers, power and the economics that tie them together. You hold your own with engineers and turn technical depth into business strategy. The mission matters to you. A business built on AI infrastructure at sea excites you, and you want your work to help AI grow without costing the planet. You work in English. Fluent English is required; French is a plus. How you operate Ownership. You treat the company's outcomes as your own, well beyond your remit. First principles. You reason from the economics and the physics, not from how the market has always worked. Bold and rigorous. You make big bets and do the work to back them. AI-native. You use modern tools to think, decide and move faster. Why this role A C-level mandate across strategy, product and capital, working directly with the CEO and the board The chance to define how compute infrastructure at sea becomes a business, and to keep redefining it as it scales An uncompromising team of repeat entrepreneurs and industrial leaders, backed by top-tier international capital Based wherever you do your best work, with a global mandate and flexible hours. ed2ea128b192.title: CDI - Senior AI Engineer - Paris
ed2ea128b192.description:
Mission

De nouveaux modèles, ouverts ou fermés, sortent chaque mois : encore faut-il choisir ceux qui sont assez bons pour la production, et le démontrer. Applications et agents s’appuient sur les grands modèles de langage (LLM), et la partie modèle de ces systèmes est entre vos mains. Nos clients s’en servent pour répondre à leurs propres clients, traiter des documents et interroger leurs connaissances.

Ce que le modèle voit, la manière dont il retrouve les connaissances, les outils qu’il peut appeler : ces choix vous appartiennent, de même que la mesure de la qualité des réponses. Le modèle retenu doit tenir l’objectif de coût et de qualité.

Ce poste est fait pour vous si vous voulez savoir si un système d’IA donne des réponses justes, et pas seulement s’il tourne.

Artefact accompagne les plus grandes entreprises du monde dans le déploiement de l’IA : 3 000 AI makers dans plus de 30 pays, plus de 1 000 clients. En France, le département Engineering réunit environ 300 personnes sous la responsabilité du CTO ; vous y rejoignez le chapter AI Applied Engineer, archétype AI Engineer.

 

Activités et responsabilités

Les Product Engineers construisent l’application autour du modèle ; le comportement du modèle à l’intérieur vous revient. Les Context & Analytics Engineers préparent les connaissances que vos agents retrouvent, et les Platform Engineers exploitent le serving, le harness et l’observabilité sur lesquels vous vous appuyez.

Avec l’AI Product Manager et les experts métier du client, une bonne réponse se définit, puis les résultats s’examinent ensemble. La relecture de code entre pairs et l’accompagnement des nouvelles recrues font partie du quotidien.

Vos responsabilités :

  • Construire des applications et des agents LLM : conception du contexte, appel d’outils, workflows multi-étapes.
  • Concevoir la façon dont les agents exploitent les connaissances : requêtes de retrieval, re-ranking, citations.
  • Construire des jeux et des pipelines d’évaluation : réponses de référence, scoring automatisé, relecture par des experts métier.
  • Suivre la qualité des réponses en production et corriger ce qui se dégrade.
  • Choisir les modèles selon la qualité, le coût et la latence ; faire du fine-tuning ou de la distillation sur un modèle plus petit quand le prompting ne suffit pas.
  • Ajouter des garde-fous contre les mauvaises réponses, les fuites de données et le prompt injection.
  • Traiter des documents avec des LLM : extraction, classification, résumés.

 

Profil recherché

Les indispensables :

  1. Vous avez construit une application ou un agent qui appelle un LLM, et vous savez expliquer ce qui a fonctionné et ce qui a échoué.
  2. Votre code est testé et maintenable.
  3. Les coding agents font déjà partie de votre quotidien, et vous vérifiez ce qu’ils produisent.
  4. La qualité des sorties d’IA se mesure chez vous avec des jeux de test et des métriques, et vous savez limiter les hallucinations, le prompt injection et les fuites de données.
  5. Mettre en production une application LLM et la maintenir (déploiement, monitoring, coût, latence) n’a pas de secret pour vous.
  6. Le point de départ, pour vous, est le problème métier plutôt que le modèle ; reconnaître que l’IA n’est pas toujours le bon outil, et l’expliquer à des personnes non techniques, fait partie de votre pratique.

Un plus, pas un prérequis :

  • Du fine-tuning ou de la distillation de modèles de langage.
  • Une formation en machine learning ou en statistiques, par exemple en data science.
  • Des frameworks ou des protocoles d’agents, comme MCP.
  • Des entrées multimodales : documents, images, voix.
  • Des outils d’observabilité LLM : tracing, suivi des coûts.

Pas besoin de cocher toutes les cases pour postuler : si vous avez l’essentiel des indispensables et l’envie d’apprendre le reste, parlons-en.

 

Pourquoi nous rejoindre ?

Dans ce métier, la difficulté est moins de faire parler un modèle que de savoir s’il dit juste. L’AI Engineer répond à cette question par la mesure : jeux de test, évaluations, suivi en production, plutôt que par l’impression d’une démonstration réussie.

Nous sommes des AI makers : l’IA se construit avec nos clients, pas seulement pour eux. Leurs enjeux deviennent les nôtres, et nos choix techniques s’expliquent dans le langage du métier. Les positions que nous prenons sont claires ; elles évoluent face aux faits, jamais sous la pression.

Notre domaine change tous les mois, et ce rythme nous convient : les nouvelles technologies et les nouveaux secteurs s’apprennent vite, et les habitudes qui ne servent plus s’abandonnent sans regret. Devant un problème difficile, le réflexe est de le découper en étapes vérifiables, avec un haut niveau d’exigence sur le code comme sur les livrables.

Quand il manque quelque chose, pour un client ou pour le chapter, nous le construisons. La progression passe par des retours constructifs, par le partage des connaissances, par la demande d’aide sans attendre et par la reconnaissance du travail des autres. Il y a beaucoup à apprendre, et beaucoup à construire.

Un counsellor accompagne vos premiers mois. L’onboarding technique ouvre le parcours, suivi d’un premier projet client ; si aucun n’est prêt, les starter kits internes prennent le relais.

Le reste s’approfondit sur les projets : évaluation, conception d’agents, adaptation de modèles, avec l’appui de la communauté AI Engineer. À partir de 2027, l’archétype AI Engineer disposera de sa propre grille de compétences et de son propre parcours de formation, en plus du socle commun à tous les AI Applied Engineers (responsabilité en produ

Les Context & Analytics Engineers préparent les connaissances que vos agents retrouvent, et les Platform Engineers exploitent le serving, le harness et l’observabilité sur lesquels vous vous appuyez.

Avec l’AI Product Manager et les experts métier du client, une bonne réponse se définit, puis les résultats s’examinent ensemble. La relecture de code entre pairs et l’accompagnement des nouvelles recrues font partie du quotidien.

Vos responsabilités :

  • Construire des applications et des agents LLM : conception du contexte, appel d’outils, workflows multi-étapes.
  • Concevoir la façon dont les agents exploitent les connaissances : requêtes de retrieval, re-ranking, citations.
  • Construire des jeux et des pipelines d’évaluation : réponses de référence, scoring automatisé, relecture par des experts métier.
  • Suivre la qualité des réponses en production et corriger ce qui se dégrade.
  • Choisir les modèles selon la qualité, le coût et la latence ; faire du fine-tuning ou de la distillation sur un modèle plus petit quand le prompting ne suffit pas.
  • Ajouter des garde-fous contre les mauvaises réponses, les fuites de données et le prompt injection.
  • Traiter des documents avec des LLM : extraction, classification, résumés.

 

Profil recherché

Les indispensables :

  1. Vous avez construit une application ou un agent qui appelle un LLM, et vous savez expliquer ce qui a fonctionné et ce qui a échoué.
  2. Votre code est testé et maintenable.
  3. Les coding agents font déjà partie de votre quotidien, et vous vérifiez ce qu’ils produisent.
  4. La qualité des sorties d’IA se mesure chez vous avec des jeux de test et des métriques, et vous savez limiter les hallucinations, le prompt injection et les fuites de données.
  5. Mettre en production une application LLM et la maintenir (déploiement, monitoring, coût, latence) n’a pas de secret pour vous.
  6. Le point de départ, pour vous, est le problème métier plutôt que le modèle ; reconnaître que l’IA n’est pas toujours le bon outil, et l’expliquer à des personnes non techniques, fait partie de votre pratique.

Un plus, pas un prérequis :

  • Du fine-tuning ou de la distillation de modèles de langage.
  • Une formation en machine learning ou en statistiques, par exemple en data science.
  • Des frameworks ou des protocoles d’agents, comme MCP.
  • Des entrées multimodales : documents, images, voix.
  • Des outils d’observabilité LLM : tracing, suivi des coûts.

Pas besoin de cocher toutes les cases pour postuler : si vous avez l’essentiel des indispensables et l’envie d’apprendre le reste, parlons-en.

 

Pourquoi nous rejoindre ?

Dans ce métier, la difficulté est moins de faire parler un modèle que de savoir s’il dit juste. L’AI Engineer répond à cette question par la mesure : jeux de test, évaluations, suivi en production, plutôt que par l’impression d’une démonstration réussie.

Nous sommes des AI makers : l’IA se construit avec nos clients, pas seulement pour eux. Leurs enjeux deviennent les nôtres, et nos choix techniques s’expliquent dans le langage du métier. Les positions que nous prenons sont claires ; elles évoluent face aux faits, jamais sous la pression.

Notre domaine change tous les mois, et ce rythme nous convient : les nouvelles technologies et les nouveaux secteurs s’apprennent vite, et les habitudes qui ne servent plus s’abandonnent sans regret. Devant un problème difficile, le réflexe est de le découper en étapes vérifiables, avec un haut niveau d’exigence sur le code comme sur les livrables.

Quand il manque quelque chose, pour un client ou pour le chapter, nous le construisons. La progression passe par des retours constructifs, par le partage des connaissances, par la demande d’aide sans attendre et par la reconnaissance du travail des autres. Il y a beaucoup à apprendre, et beaucoup à construire.

Un counsellor accompagne vos premiers mois. L’onboarding technique ouvre le parcours, suivi d’un premier projet client ; si aucun n’est prêt, les starter kits internes prennent le relais.

Le reste s’approfondit sur les projets : évaluation, conception d’agents, adaptation de modèles, avec l’appui de la communauté AI Engineer. b6e8de9f8edb.title: Senior Software Engineer - Vector Search - Elasticsearch
b6e8de9f8edb.description:
Elastic, the Search AI Company, enables everyone to find the answers they need in real time, using all their data, at scale — unleashing the potential of businesses and people. The Elastic Search AI Platform, used by more than 50% of the Fortune 500, brings together the precision of search and the intelligence of AI to enable everyone to accelerate the results that matter. By taking advantage of all structured and unstructured data — securing and protecting private information more effectively — Elastic’s complete, cloud-based solutions for search, security, and observability help organizations deliver on the promise of AI.

What is The Role

We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join the Elasticsearch - Search Relevance team. This globally-distributed team of expert engineers focuses on delivering a robust and feature-rich search experience, including contributing to improving the search experience in Lucene. This technical leader is responsible for contributing to the technical direction and vision for our search capabilities, including design and implementation of new search features, enhancements to search functionality, and resolving bugs.
 
Our company is distributed by intention. We hire the best engineers we can find wherever they are, whoever they are. We collaborate across continents every day over email, GitHub, Zoom, and Slack. At our best, we write fast, scalable and intuitive software. We believe that the best way to do that is to empower individual engineers, code review every change, decide big things by consensus, and strive for incremental improvements.

What You Will Be Doing

  • Lead initiatives within Elasticsearch to produce an industry-leading search engine offering, supplying unparalleled speed and relevance in search.
  • Contribute to Elasticsearch full time, building new search features and fixing intriguing bugs, all while making the code easier to understand. Sometimes you'll need to invent a new algorithm or data structure. Or find one and implement it. Sometimes you'll need to get close to the operating system and hardware.
  • Work with a globally distributed team of experienced engineers focused on the vector search capabilities of Elasticsearch.
  • Be an expert on Elasticsearch search relevance. You'll identify and drive improvements this area based on your questions and your instincts.

Backed by deep robotics research and now deployed across multiple countries with leading construction and equipment partners, our team is rapidly growing to bring this technology to a trillion-dollar industry. The Gravis RACK is a machine-agnostic retrofit kit that adds autonomy to excavators and wheel loaders from 10 to 100+ tonnes: LiDAR and camera sensing, GNSS RTK, networking hardware and rugged edge compute that works offline. Paired with the Slate tablet and our Copilot software, it lets an operator run a machine manually, with AI assistance, or fully autonomously. If you enjoy using mathematics and code to investigate difficult questions, you could make a direct contribution to Optiver’s success in global markets. As a Graduate Quantitative Researcher, you’ll work across the full research process, from framing the question and choosing the data to building, testing and deploying models. Machine Learning is central to the work, whether you’re extracting signals, forecasting prices or modelling relationships. Our data, compute and production infrastructure let you test ideas quickly, understand where they fail and decide what to investigate next.

Our researchers believe in academic discourse and invite fellow researchers, traders and engineers to challenge each hypothesis. Different perspectives help improve the question, the model and how it performs in production. Through constant testing, analysis and refinement, you’ll help our quantitative models adapt as markets evolve.

Your onboarding 

You’ll participate in Global Optiver Academy, a structured onboarding programme for graduates. It gives new joiners a shared foundation in how Optiver trades, builds systems, and manages risk before they move into their teams. As part of your onboarding, you'll gain exposure to the AI tools and technologies that support research and development across the business.

  • Building models for pricing, forecasting and signal discovery, choosing the statistical, mathematical or Machine Learning methods that best fit the problem.
  • Working across petabytes of market, order-flow and unstructured data to find signals that improve strategies as conditions change.
  • Monitoring models in production and using live behavior to refine your assumptions and decide what to investigate next.
  • Using deep learning and AI-enabled workflows to shorten the loop from hypothesis to evidence.
  • Working directly with researchers, traders and engineers to shape problems and understand how system constraints affect performance.

WHO YOU ARE

We're looking for aspiring Quantitative Researchers who are versatile and creative in innovating and suggesting new solutions. In return, we'll give you the freedom to pursue your ideas and implement them right into our production systems. 

In terms of skills and qualifications, we're looking for:

  • Programming experience in any language (preferably Python, but C, C++, Basic, JAVA, etc. are also a plus)

  • Competitive attitude and eagerness to constantly improve
  • Ability to learn quickly
  • Excellent verbal and written English language skills

WHAT YOU’LL GET

Motivated by a passion for continuous improvement, you’ll thrive in a supportive, high-performing environment alongside talent colleagues, working collaboratively to tackle the toughest problems in the financial markets.

In addition, you’ll receive:

  • Training opportunities, discounts on health benefits, and fully paid first-class commuting expenses

9016ce0ab2c0.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
9016ce0ab2c0.description:
As a Forward Deployed Engineer at Auterion, you will play a pivotal role in the successful development, integration and deployment of Auterion-powered drone systems. 

In this role, you will collaborate closely with the production, hardware engineering, and firmware/software teams, as well as operations, ensuring that every platform transitions smoothly from an airframe concept into a fully validated flying robot ready for deployment. You will serve as the primary technical interface for partners, work closely with them to understand their technical requirements, configure and adapt existing solutions, contribute to core software development, and ensure successful implementation. 

This role is ideal for an engineer who enjoys combining hands-on technical work with customer collaboration and system-level problem solving, bridging the gap between hardware, firmware, and real-world flight performance. 

Responsibilities and Duties

  • Operate in a highly hands-on environment with evolving system requirements, rapidly iterating across hardware and software integration challenges.
  • Manage software releases and perform firmware flashing and configuration using PX4 or adjacent autopilot ecosystems, including sensor calibration, ESC tuning, and system bring-up.
  • Provide deep avionics and airframe expertise, including autopilot tuning, sensor and payload integration, power systems and airworthiness considerations.

4560caf98dd4.title: Research Engineer / Research Scientist, Post-Training — Collective Alignment (User Signals)
4560caf98dd4.description:
About the Team

The Collective Alignment (User Signals) team is a post-training research team working at the intersection of data science, human feedback, and reinforcement learning. We develop methods for learning from real-world user interactions to build AI systems that deliver lasting value, helping people learn, grow, and accomplish increasingly complex goals with ChatGPT.

Learning from user feedback presents fundamental research challenges: signals are often noisy, biased, and difficult to interpret, and improvements in offline metrics do not always translate into better experiences for users. Our team develops scientific approaches to understanding these signals and translating them into improvements in model behavior through evaluations, reward modeling, and post-training.

About the Role

As a Research Engineer or Research Scientist, you will investigate how AI systems can learn from human feedback and real-world usage to better serve users over time.

You will develop new approaches to extracting meaningful learning signals from complex user interactions and incorporating those signals into model training.

This role requires strong deep learning research skills, scientific rigor, and curiosity about how people interact with AI. You will design controlled experiments and ablations, critically examine the relationship between offline evaluations and online model behavior, and work closely with research, product, and data science teams to understand whether improvements translate into meaningful value for users.

In this role, you will:

 - Develop novel methods for learning from human feedback and user interaction signals.

 - Research approaches to incorporating feedback into reward modeling, reinforcement learning, and post-training.

 - Design rigorous experiments and ablation studies to isolate the effects of new data, objectives, and training methods.

 - Develop offline evaluations and investigate their relationship with online experiments and real-world user outcomes.

 - Analyze unexpected results, investigate discrepancies between evaluation metrics and user behavior, and develop hypotheses to guide further research.

 - Evaluate tradeoffs and regressions to improve targeted model behaviors while preserving broader capabilities.

 - Collaborate with research, alignment, product, and data science teams.

 - Implement and debug experiments across large-scale deep learning research systems.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have a strong background in deep learning research through academic or industry experience.

cd443bd3c4a3.title: Research Engineer / Research Scientist, Human Flourishing
cd443bd3c4a3.description:
About the Team

The Human Flourishing team’s mission is to ensure AI systems understand and advance human flourishing. As AI becomes more capable and plays a larger role in people’s lives, we want its human benefits to grow with its capabilities. The Human Flourishing team is part of the broader Post Training organization.

Our approach has two parts. Firstly, we measure and improve models’ understanding, capability, and propensity to act according to people’s values and to help them achieve their long-term goals. Secondly, we directly scale tangible impact for users in human domains like education and mental health, working across research, product, and partnerships to increase the benefits over a billion people experience weekly when they use ChatGPT.

Our recent work includes Beneficial RL https://alignment.openai.com/beneficial-rl/, which investigates how training for beneficial behavior generalizes across settings, and MentalHealthBench https://openai.com/index/introducing-mentalhealthbench/, a benchmark developed with mental health experts to evaluate realistic conversations.

About the Role

We’re looking for an exceptional, hands-on researcher to turn difficult-to-define signals of long-term flourishing into measurable improvements in model behavior. You’ll help set research direction, build what is needed to test your ideas, and drive successful work into the models and products we ship.

We’re especially interested in researchers with deep experience improving frontier models through pretraining or reinforcement learning (RL) / post-training, especially on less verifiable problems, or researchers who combine strong LLM skills with deep expertise in domains like education or mental health. Prior experience in these domains is not required.

In this role, you will

 - Develop scalable training methods across the training stack that improve how models understand people’s values, support their agency, and help them achieve long-term goals.

 - Lead high-leverage research from an open question to a shipped improvement: choose a hard-to-define problem, iteratively define success, run experiments, and integrate into frontier models.

 - Build RL environments for difficult-to-verify outcomes, and study whether beneficial behavior generalizes across settings.

 - Create evaluations grounded in human expertise and feedback that reveal capability gaps, unintended incentives in RL, and failures that aggregate scores can miss.

 - Test whether measures of model behavior predict better learning, wellbeing, and other long-term outcomes, and use those findings to guide training.

 - Build new 0→1 capabilities in human domains that may have an increasing impact with upcoming increases in model intelligence and test-time compute.

 - Partner with product teams, engineers, partnerships teams, and domain experts to deploy promising methods, measure their effects in real use, and turn what you learn into further improvements.

 - Assess AI’s impacts on human flourishing at the scale of over a billion users.

You might thrive in this role if you

 - Care deeply about helping AI improve people’s lives, and feel this is a responsibility that comes with increasingly capable models.

 - Have an unusually strong research record in pretraining or RL / post-training research, especially in a hard-to-verify area; or combine strong LLM research skills with deep expertise in education, mental health, or a related field of human benefit.

 - Are a hands-on builder who can turn ideas into rigorous experiments, write and debug code, and work directly with data and training infrastructure.

 - Have the taste to choose consequential problems and actionable steps on the path to solving those problems.

 - Take ownership of ambiguous problems and choose methods based on the impact they can deliver, including when the most useful work is unglamorous.

 - Care about whether a capability will scale, generalize, and make it into the real world—not just whether it can be shown in a paper or prototype.

 - Work well across disciplines and can grok the most important bottlenecks to scaling our impact in a multidisciplinary problem.

If you’re excited about ensuring AI systems advance human flourishing, we’d love to hear from you.

1ec27bd93196.description:
About the Team

The Health team, within OpenAI’s broader Post Training organization, has a mission to ensure AGI improves health for all humanity.

Improving human health will be one of the defining impacts of AGI. Hundreds of millions of people already turn to ChatGPT for questions about their health and millions of clinicians use it weekly to support care delivery. Increasingly capable models create an opportunity to make high-quality medical intelligence more accessible across patients and clinicians—raising the floor of human health—and accelerate the new capabilities and scientific advances that raise the ceiling of human health.

Our job is to make those benefits real. We work across the full model stack—pretraining, midtraining, reinforcement learning, post-training, evaluations, harnessing, and deployment—and connect that research to the patients, clinicians, and real-world outcomes we aim to improve.

About the Role

We’re looking for an exceptional, hands-on researcher who wants to build frontier health capabilities and turn them into impact at scale. This is a role for someone who can take an important, underdefined problem from 0→1: identify the right bet, build what’s needed to test it, and drive it all the way to a measurable improvement in the models and products we actually ship.

We’re especially excited about two kinds of people: researchers with the technical depth to move the frontier in pretraining, reinforcement learning (RL) / post-training, or evals; and researchers with real depth in developing frontier biomedical AI capabilities. Prior experience in healthcare is helpful but not required. Research excellence, velocity, ownership, and alignment with the mission are most important to us.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

 - Own a high-leverage research direction end to end—from deciding which problem matters and how to measure it, to designing and running experiments, to integrating successful work into frontier models.

 - Develop scalable methods across pretraining, midtraining, reinforcement learning, and post-training to improve health reasoning, knowledge, reliability, calibration, and behavior.

 - Build and study RL environments grounded in real health problems; understand which data and training setups produce robust, generalizable improvements rather than just higher benchmark scores.

 - Create meaningful, trustworthy, and unsaturated evaluations that tell us whether our models are actually getting better at what matters for patients and clinicians.

 - Advance new 0→1 capabilities in health that may have an increasing impact with upcoming increases in model intelligence and test-time compute.

 - Develop models and agents that can work over longitudinal, multimodal health data to produce useful predictions, surface new scientific insights, and support better individual- and population-level decisions.

 - Work closely with researchers, engineers, clinicians, and product teams to bring health capabilities into the models and products used by hundreds of millions of people.

 - Help establish that AI improves real health outcomes, not just that it can produce impressive answers or demos.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Care deeply about using increasingly capable AI to improve human health, and take seriously the responsibility of deploying it safely.

 - Have an unusually strong track record in machine learning or AI research, with the depth to push at least one important area forward: pretraining, reinforcement learning / post-training, evals (not necessarily specific to health); or substantial depth in a relevant frontier health / biomedical AI problem.

 - Are a hands-on builder: you can design experiments, write and debug code, work directly with data and training infrastructure, and move quickly from an idea to evidence.

 - Have strong research taste and can distinguish an important problem or a promising approach from an interesting one.

 - Own ambiguous problems end to end, and are willing to learn whatever is missing to get the job done.

 - Stay goal-oriented rather than method-oriented, and don’t shy away from unglamorous work if it is the highest-leverage path to impact.

 - Care about whether a capability will scale, generalize, and make it into the real world—not just whether it can be shown in a paper or prototype.

 - Enjoy working with low-ego, ambitious people across research, engineering, medicine, and product.

 - Bonus: Experience with health AI, longitudinal health data, or clinical research.

 

If you want your work to help make medical intelligence widely accessible—and to work on some of the most important frontier problems at the intersection of AI, science, and human health—we’d love to hear from you.

36db04652a93.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role We're looking for engineers to join Model-to-Product Behavior Engineering, the team responsible for getting Claude's behavior right across Anthropic's products. You'll work with product, research, and safeguards teams to make sure Claude behaves in ways that are consistent, safe, and genuinely helpful, whether in a new feature, a new model, or a launch. Evals are one of the sharpest tools we have for getting Claude's behavior right, but not the only one. You'll build evals to see clearly where Claude shines and where it slips, use what you learn to inform how to close the gap, and build the harness improvements that get us there. That takes your own intuition and judgment about model behavior, both to decide what is worth building and to know what to do with what you find. Your work will shape launch decisions and give research and product teams a signal they can trust. You'll also build the infrastructure behind our evals, along with tooling that makes it easy to test and ship prompt fixes. And you'll create self-serve tools that let other teams build their own evals and improve Claude's behavior in their products, so that getting model behavior right scales well beyond any one team. You'll work across many projects and product surfaces at once, holding a high bar for the details while adapting as model capabilities change. Key responsibilities Build evals that measure Claude's quality, behavior, and capabilities across Anthropic's products and model releases, with sound methodology: deciding what to measure, validating datasets and graders, and interpreting noisy results with statistical rigor Apply judgment to model outputs to separate real regressions and capability gaps from noise, and turn findings into clear recommendations Support model launches by catching regressions before they reach users and giving decision-makers a clear read on model readiness Act on what the evals show: build and ship Your focus is GitLab's internal operations, rather than customer implementations or development of the GitLab product. Building fast matters, and we want engineers who ship. You'll partner with senior engineers and stakeholders to understand the real problem first: how work moves across teams, where the real constraint lives, and whether AI is the right intervention. Design, develop, and ship AI-powered solutions quickly, delivering working prototypes in days, not months, with a focus on practical outcomes and measurable business value. Build solutions that reduce bottlenecks, shorten lead times, and increase throughput. Track flow, adoption, and ROI metrics defined for the work. You're as energized by a well-designed API integration as you are by the latest foundation model release. AI is a powerful part of your toolkit, but it sits on top of solid engineering fundamentals, not in place of them. Competent, Confident Coding Skills - You can build working solutions end-to-end, write clean and maintainable code, and debug effectively. Whether your skills were honed in a traditional engineering role, through building automations, or shipping side projects, what matters is that you can deliver production-quality work independently. AI & LLM Technical Depth - Strong proficiency in at least one modern scripting language (Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, or similar) and a solid understanding of REST APIs, GraphQL, and integration patterns. 3fc8fe0514ee.description: About Us At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company. At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in. Job Location - Bengaluru, India Work Mode - Hybrid (3 Days WFO) Internship Duration - 6 Months starting Jan 2027 About the Role : We are looking for ambitious, tech-forward HR interns to join our People Operations team for a 6-month intensive apprenticeship. This is not a typical administrative internship—it is a fast-paced, high-impact, end-to-end People Operations role designed for high-potential talent. During your tenure, you will work directly on critical People Operations functions, HR business partnering initiatives, and high-impact cross-functional projects. If you are extremely data-fluent, comfortable with ambiguity, and eager to leverage modern HR technology and AI to solve business challenges, this role is built for you. Key Responsibilities : As a People Operations/HRBP Intern, you will gain hands-on ownership across the employee lifecycle, including but not limited to: Employee Experience & Engagement: Assist in designing and executing employee engagement programs, pulse surveys, feedback loops, and culture-building initiatives to drive retention and satisfaction. Compliance & Labor Code Audits: Participate in internal HR compliance audits, statutory labor code alignments, and document verification processes to ensure seamless operational governance. Payroll & Benefits Management: Support monthly payroll processing workflows, leave & attendance reconciliations, vendor coordination, and employee benefits administration. Onboarding & Exit Management: Own end-to-end joining logistics, orientation sessions, documentation, exit interviews, and offboarding workflows to deliver a memorable employee journey. Skill Requirements & Qualifications : Academic & Eligibility Background Currently pursuing a full-time MBA (4th Semester) with a focus on HR / General Management. NAPS Eligibility: As per the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS), candidates with prior full-time experience or an active PF/UAN account are in-eligible to apply. Prior internship experience in similar field will be an added advantage Core Soft Skills Interpersonal Excellence: Exceptional emotional intelligence, empathy, and the ability to build trust quickly across cross-functional teams. Communication Skills: Outstanding verbal and written communication skills with strong presentation capabilities. Problem-Solving Ability: High learning agility, critical thinking, and the drive to work independently on open-ended problems. Technical & Functional Skills : AI & HR Tech Literacy: Hands-on usage of AI tools (e.g., Gemini, ChatGPT, AI prompt engineering, automation tools) and familiarity with any HR software/HRIS platforms. Data Fluency: Strong proficiency in MS Excel / Google Sheets, data visualization, basic metrics analysis, and data-driven decision-making. What Makes Cloudflare Special? We’re not just a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company. We’re a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company with a soul. Fundamental to our mission to help build a better Internet is protecting the free and open Internet. Project Galileo : Since 2014, we've equipped more than 2,400 journalism and civil society organizations in 111 countries with powerful tools to defend themselves against attacks that would otherwise censor their work, technology already used by Cloudflare’s enterprise customers--at no cost. Athenian Project : In 2017, we created the Athenian Project to ensure that state and local governments have the highest level of protection and reliability for free, so that their constituents have access to election information and voter registration. Since the project, we've provided services to more than 425 local government election websites in 33 states. 1.1.1.1 : We released 1.1.1.1 to help fix the foundation of the Internet by building a faster, more secure and privacy-centric public DNS resolver. This is available publicly for everyone to use - it is the first consumer-focused service Cloudflare has ever released. Here’s the deal - we don’t store client IP addresses never, ever. We will continue to abide by our privacy commitment and ensure that no user data is sold to advertisers or used to target consumers. Sound like something you’d like to be a part of? We’d love to hear from you! Please note that applicants who progress to the offer stage of the interview process may be asked to attend an in-person interview within one of the Cloudflare Offices or Cloudflare Hubs. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company. At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in. Available Locations Austin, US Miami, US US About the Role Senior Customer Engineer - Brazil (US Based). In business generation and expansion, you’ll be tasked with qualification of prospect and customer use cases, technical requirements discovery, leading demonstrations, solution identification and design, and collaborative work on proofs-of-concept (PoCs). For our existing customers, Solutions Engineers are part of a dedicated account team that advises the customer on technical best practices, implementation of Cloudflare products and features, and strategic guidance on internet security and performance. You appreciate the diversity of challenges in working with customers, and look forward to helping them realize the full promise of Cloudflare. On the Solutions Engineering team, you will find a collaborative environment where everyone brings different strengths and jumps in to help each other. Demonstrated experience with a scripting language (e.g. Python, JavaScript, Bash, Lua, Go) and a desire to expand those skills. Expertise in internet technologies: OSI Model layers 1-7, BGP, GRE, TCP/UDP, DNS (authoritative and recursive), HTTP(S), SSL / TLS. Familiarity with Zero Trust Framework and SASE related concepts. 12 years plus of experience in a customer-facing sales or consulting role. Technical curiosity and passion: Cloudflare is at the cutting edge of internet technology, and our Solutions Engineers are viewed as subject-matter experts. It’s incumbent on us to stay up to date not only with Cloudflare’s specific products, but with industry trends. A focus on learning, teaching, collaboration, mentorship, and growth, not only personally but also within the team and company. Aside from technical and collaborative skills, we place a high value on project management, relationship building, and EQ. You've built web applications before, or contributed to existing web applications in a meaningful way. You understand the role of a firewall, the difference between L3, L4, and L7 firewalls, and that ‘ACL’ doesn't always mean Anterior Cruciate Ligament. You're not afraid of command-line interfaces, RESTful APIs, or analyzing HTTP request and response in a browser’s web inspector. You can describe the differences between CSRF, XSS, and SQLi in detail, and Cloudflare's role in defending against them. Understanding of, or experience with, regulatory requirements such a PCI DSS, HIPAA, and SOC-2. An undergraduate degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related field. Reminder: this is not a strict requirement at all. Candidates from all walks of life are welcome. Available Locations: United States: Austin, TX; San Francisco, CA; New York City; Washington D.C. United Kingdom: London About the Role Cloudforce One is Cloudflare’s threat operations and research team, responsible for identifying and disrupting cyber threats ranging from sophisticated cyber criminal activity to nation-state sponsored advanced persistent threats (APTs). Cloudforce One works in close partnership with external organizations and internal Cloudflare teams, continuously developing operational tradecraft and expanding ever-growing sources of threat intelligence to enable expedited threat hunting and remediation. Members of Cloudforce One are at the helm of leveraging an incredibly vast and varied set of data points that only one of the world’s largest global networks can provide. The team is able to analyze these unique data points, at massive scale and efficiency, synthesizing findings into actionable threat intelligence to better protect our customers. As a Software Engineer on this team, you will own the entire software development lifecycle—from design and architecture to deployment and monitoring—for systems that serve both threat disruption and legal response efforts. You will be responsible for translating complex legal and security requirements into robust, scalable, and high-performance applications that have a direct impact on making the internet better, safer, and more powerful every day. Responsibilities While the majority of our services are now written in Golang and TypeScript, you will also work with technologies such as Rust, Kafka, Redis, Kubernetes, Terraform, Temporal and PostgresSQL. We also pride ourselves in dogfooding our own products and services so you will be extensively working with Cloudflare’s developer platform as well. We are looking for great engineers regardless of experience with any of these specific technologies. This role may require flexibility to be on-call outside of standard working hours to address technical issues as needed. Design, build, run, and scale distributed tools and services that support both cyber threat disruption and platform abuse efforts. Develop critical data pipelines and services to collect, analyze, and expose threat intelligence data for Cloudforce One analysts and Cloudflare customers, helping to identify Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures (TTPs) and Indicators of Compromise (IOCs). Collaborate closely with Threat Intelligence, Trust & Safety, Legal, and Product teams to understand goals and translate complex technical requirements into elegant, scalable solutions. Improve system design and architecture to ensure stability, performance, and maintainability of both internal and customer-facing compliance and security services. Analyze, communicate, and help prioritize complex technical concepts across teams. Ongoing monitoring and maintenance of production services, including participation in on-call rotations. Mentor and guide other developers in the team, helping to build collective technical expertise and promote best practices for writing well-tested, modular, and reusable code. 3f04417f2172.description:
About the team

OpenAI’s Forward Deployed Engineering team partners with customers to turn research breakthroughs into production systems. We operate at the intersection of customer delivery and core platform development.



About the role

Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) lead complex end-to-end deployments of frontier models in production alongside our most strategic customers. You will own discovery, technical scoping, system design, build, and production rollout, partnering directly with customer engineering and domain teams.



You will measure success through production adoption, measurable workflow impact, and eval-driven feedback that changes product and model roadmaps. You’ll work closely with our Product, Research, Partnerships, GRC, Security, and GTM teams.



This role is based in Dublin. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week. We offer relocation assistance. Travel up to 50% is required.



In this role you will

 - Own technical delivery across multiple deployments from first prototype to stable production

 - Build full-stack systems that deliver customer value and sharpen how we learn

 - Embed closely with customer teams, understand their needs, and guide adoption of what you build

 - Scope work, sequence delivery, and remove blockers early

 - Make trade-offs between scope, speed, and quality; adjust plans to protect delivery

 - Contribute directly in the code when progress or clarity depends on it

 - Codify working patterns into tools, playbooks, or building blocks that others can use

 - Share field feedback that helps Research and Product understand where the models succeed and where they can improve

 - Keep teams moving through clarity and follow-through



You might thrive in this role if you

 - Bring 5+ years of engineering or technical deployment experience that includes customer-facing work

 - Have scoped and delivered complex systems in fast-moving or ambiguous environments

 - Write and review production-grade code across frontend and backend using Python, JavaScript, or comparable stacks

 - Have built or deployed systems powered by LLMs or generative models and understand how model behaviour affects product experience

 - Simplify complexity and make fast, sound decisions under pressure

 - Communicate clearly with engineers, product teams, and customer stakeholders

 - Spot risks early and adjust without slowing down

 - Model calm and judgment when the stakes are high

About the Team

OpenAI’s Technology Strategic Sourcing team helps Engineering, Research, and other technology teams secure the supplier capabilities they need to scale. We work with technical, finance, legal, security, and business leaders to shape commercial strategy, negotiate critical agreements, and build resilient supplier relationships.



About the Role

Own sourcing strategy for infrastructure software and the Engineering and Research stack. You’ll manage billion-dollar-scale spend, personally lead the most complex commercial negotiations, and deliver measurable savings while protecting the capabilities Engineering and Research rely on.

This is a principal-level individual contributor role with no direct reports at launch. You’ll lead cross-functional deal teams and coach sourcing peers. People management experience is a plus; the role may expand to include management as the team and spend grow.

Build multi-year category strategies across data platforms, observability, developer tools, and software for machine learning research, training, and inference. Use technical roadmaps, demand, and market intelligence to decide where to build, buy, consolidate, compete, or transition. Develop credible alternatives before they’re needed.

Build lasting relationships with senior Engineering and Research leaders and supplier executives, including suppliers that are also OpenAI customers. Work with Sales, Finance, and Legal to align buying and selling strategies while evaluating each decision on its own merits.



This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.



In this role, you will:

 - Deliver significant savings and better unit economics, and validate results with Finance against comparable baselines.

You might thrive in this role if you:

06b159bb5475.title: Cyber Partner Applied AI Architect
06b159bb5475.description:
About the Team

Frontier AI is changing how organizations discover vulnerabilities, remediate risk and defend their environments. Realizing that potential at scale will take an ecosystem of partners who can put the technology to work. The Cyber Partnerships Team works to bring together providers of cybersecurity products, systems integrators, and our hyperscaler partners to accelerate deployment of this technology to enterprises around the world.

Within the team, Partner Applied AI Architects work with strategic partners—including global and regional system integrators, consulting and advisory firms, and technology partners—to extend OpenAI’s technical reach and help partners deliver high-quality AI solutions for our joint customers. We bring together technical strategy, partner enablement, architecture expertise, and practical deployment experience, working closely with Partnerships, Sales, Product, Engineering, Research, Security, and specialist cybersecurity teams.

About the Role

As a Cyber Partner Applied AI Architect, you will be a senior technical advisor to a portfolio of strategic cybersecurity partners and the primary technical counterpart to their leadership and delivery organizations. You will shape how partners build practices around OpenAI, develop solutions using our products, and take joint customers from unmet cybersecurity needs and technical evaluation through production adoption and measurable business impact.

You will own the technical strategy and architecture across partner engagements involving our Daybreak access programs, specialized cybersecurity products, existing non-cybersecurity product portfolio, and other agentic AI solutions. In close partnership with the broader partnerships team, you will translate joint business priorities into technical strategies, solution patterns, enablement plans, and a focused portfolio of high-value customer opportunities.

You will work directly with partners on strategic customer engagements—leading discovery, shaping architectures, navigating complex technical decisions, and helping secure technical wins—while building the partner capabilities required to deliver successfully and independently at scale.

You will remain accountable for the technical quality and outcomes of the partnership while bringing in the right specialists across deployment, implementation, security, product, enablement, and other teams when deeper expertise is needed. The role calls for strong architectural judgment, executive presence, partner leadership, and the ability to move confidently between business strategy and hands-on technical conversations.

In this role, you will:

 - Serve as the primary technical advisor and long-term technical relationship owner for cybersecurity practices across a portfolio of strategic partners, building trusted relationships with their executives, AI leaders, architects, engineering teams, and delivery organizations.

 - Partner closely with the broader partnerships team as one virtual team, aligning partner strategy, technical priorities, joint customer opportunities, and measures of success.

 - Develop the technical strategy and plan for each partner, identifying priority solutions, use cases, technical capabilities, enablement needs, delivery risks, and opportunities to drive customer adoption.

 - Assess prospective and existing partners’ cybersecurity capabilities and delivery readiness, identifying strengths, gaps, and the investments required to successfully deliver OpenAI-powered solutions.

 - Lead technical discovery with partners and joint customers to identify, qualify, and prioritize cybersecurity use-cases.

 - Develop clear Applied AI architectures spanning models, applications, enterprise data, integrations, identity, security, privacy, governance, evaluation, reliability, and deployment.

 - Guide partners through their initial and most strategic cybersecurity deployments, helping them navigate technical tradeoffs and production dependencies while ensuring solutions meet a high bar for quality, security, reliability, and responsible deployment.

 - Build partner capability and technical self-sufficiency through tailored enablement, architectural guidance, reusable solution patterns, technical workshops, and mentorship.

 - Establish clear standards and mechanisms for partner-delivered solution quality, identifying risks early and intervening when architecture, implementation, security, evaluation, or adoption issues threaten customer outcomes.

 - Orchestrate the right OpenAI specialists across Deployment Engineering, Product, Security, implementation, enablement, and domain teams while maintaining clear ownership and handoffs between OpenAI and partner delivery teams.

 - Track partner capability, joint pipeline technical progress, production adoption, usage, solution quality, and measurable customer impact to identify where additional investment or intervention is needed.

OpenAI’s Applied AI Engineering team helps organizations turn frontier AI capabilities into safe, reliable, and high-impact production systems. Enterprise deployments are defined by complexity rather than any one industry: existing architectures, diverse data environments, security and governance requirements, multiple stakeholder groups, and organization-wide change. We turn lessons from these deployments into better products and reusable patterns for customers everywhere.

You will combine deep technical judgment, hands-on engineering, and customer leadership to take ambitious ideas from use-case selection and architecture through prototyping, evaluation, production launch, and scale. Success is measured by production systems, sustained adoption, and meaningful customer impact—not simply activity or successful demonstrations. 

This is a rare opportunity to work as one of the early hires for a new segment within Applied AI Engineering, contributing real-world deployments at the frontier of AI while directly influencing how OpenAI’s products evolve.

This role is based in our SF or NYC office. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

 - Partner directly with enterprise customers to identify high-value opportunities and translate them into technical architectures, implementation plans, evaluation strategies, and measurable success criteria.

a267879cdf8a.description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform.

About the Role

We’re looking for an Optical Mechanical Engineer to design, prototype, and validate high-density fiber interconnects for our AI infrastructure. You’ll work across MT ferrule–based connectors and adapters, optical transceiver mechanical designs, tray-level optical assemblies, and fiber shuffle solutions, translating optical and system requirements into reliable, manufacturable hardware.

This is a hands-on role spanning detailed mechanical design, lab testing, and integration. You’ll partner with optical, mechanical, networking, manufacturing, and data center teams to make fiber connections practical to assemble, route, test, and service—from within a tray or rack to the cabling infrastructure connecting racks.

In this role, you will:

 - Design and test MT ferrule–based fiber connectors and adapters, addressing alignment, tolerances, retention, mating repeatability, and serviceability.

 - Develop mechanical designs for optical transceivers and tray-level optical solutions, balancing packaging density, thermal interfaces, assembly access, and fiber management.

 - Design and validate high-density fiber shuffle assemblies, including shuffle cassettes, with clear connectivity maps, controlled routing, and accessible test interfaces.

 - Define and execute optical-mechanical validation plans, including optical loss measurements, connector inspection, mating cycles, and relevant environmental and mechanical testing.

 - Develop fiber routing within and between racks, accounting for bend radius, strain relief, cable management, labeling, installation, and maintenance access.

 - Partner with data center and network teams to translate fiber layouts and cabling infrastructure requirements into hardware interfaces and integration plans.

 - Work with suppliers and manufacturing partners to build prototypes, resolve failures, improve assembly consistency, and transition validated designs into production.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - You have hands-on experience designing and testing MT ferrule–based fiber connectors and adapters.

 - You have developed and tested fiber interconnects, including high-density fiber solutions, and can connect mechanical design decisions to optical performance.

 - You have experience with the mechanical design and integration of optical transceivers and tray-level optical assemblies.

 - You have designed and validated fiber shuffle solutions, such as shuffle cassettes, including connectivity, routing, assembly, and test considerations.

 - You understand fiber routing within and between racks, including bend-radius constraints, strain relief, connector access, and serviceability.

 - You are familiar with data center fiber layouts and the cabling infrastructure that supports installation, expansion, and operation.

 - You can move between detailed design and hands-on debugging, use measurements to identify root causes, and work with engineering and manufacturing partners to implement practical improvements.
