4edcc8e46815.title: Senior Systems Engineer
4edcc8e46815.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Maneuver Dominance team in London builds the Mission System and Autonomy for Anduril's autonomous air platforms. Aircraft built to operate alongside crewed aviation and deliver effects in contested environments.

A mission system is only useful if it does what the mission needs. Our payloads and subsystems are being developed in parallel, across teams and across companies, and every release has to earn its place against the customer's mission. The mission threads, the analysis, and the evidence that each feature makes a difference are what hold that together. That is the problem you would own.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a Senior Systems Engineer to join us in London and lead mission engineering across our systems. You will bring pragmatic mission engineering thinking to complement and enhance the overall mission system capability, ensuring end-user needs are met in challenging operational environments. You will be part of a lean, high-ownership culture where you directly shape the product and operate at a velocity to fly new designs within months, not years.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Execute a right-sized, Agile Mission Engineering approach as per the Mission Engineering Analysis Plan for development of the Mission System and Payloads at the speed of relevance
  • Support design teams in the evolution and progress of Technical Performance Measures (TPMs) and Measures of Effectiveness (MoEs) throughout the design process
  • Contribute to System Design Reviews (SDR) and engineering governance structures such as Preliminary Design Reviews (PDR), Critical Design Reviews (CDR), Test Readiness Reviews (TRR), Safety Review Boards (SRB) representing the Mission Engineering discipline
  • Own and maintain Mission Threads, operational scenarios and the mission-level decomposition that drives system requirements
  • Develop key Mission Engineering artefacts including the Mission Engineering Analysis Plan, Investigation and Analysis Results, and Assurance Recommendations
  • Run operational analysis of mission scenarios, using simulation, wargaming and analysis of alternatives where they best answer the question
  • Recommend and prioritise development features for each release, justified against customer priorities and the minimum deployable capability, and present the rationale to the customer
  • Champion the use of the Test and Evaluation Master Plan (TEMP) so that test events are designed around mission threads and measures of success
  • Shape the design of simulation and Software In The Loop (SIL) environments used for mission analysis, and input into surrogate testing
  • Create issue board workflows and coordinate ticket triage, action assignment, artefact capture and closure
  • Support wholistic Systems Safety and Airworthiness efforts, including identifying hazardous scenarios for the autonomy assurance process
  • Support ground and flight test of prototype and production representative Mission Systems, analysing results against mission threads and measures of success

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • BEng/BSc/MEng in Aerospace, Mechanical, Electrical, Computer Science, Robotics, Mechatronics, Operational Research, Mathematics, or a similar engineering field, or equivalent experience
  • 7+ years industry Systems Engineering or Operational Analysis experience in the Defence or Aerospace industries, specifically crewed aircraft, rotorcraft, EVTOL, UAS or weapon systems with a focus on Payload Integration, Mission Systems, GNC or Autonomy.
  • Demonstrable Mission Engineering or Operational Analysis proficiency, including solicitation of requirements with the customer/end-user, collaboration with design teams
  • Experience developing Mission Engineering artefacts, including mission threads, concepts of operation and pragmatic analysis plans
  • Experience running scenario-based analysis, simulation or wargaming that has informed design or capability decisions
  • Deep understanding of the test and evaluation process as applicable to developmental, acceptance and operational testing
  • Experience with crewed or uncrewed developmental autonomous aircraft (Group 5 UAS or larger)
  • Outstanding written and verbal communication skills to include presentation of developed artefacts
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active UKSV Security Clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Military operational experience, for example in aviation, ISTAR or fires
  • Experience with open mission system architectures, for example PYRAMID, OMS/UCI, or STANAG 4586, and with modular open systems approaches more generally
  • Experience with mission engineering methods, for example the US DoD Mission Engineering Guide, and with constructive simulation tools
  • Working knowledge of UK export control and security regimes, including the UK Military List, SPIRE and OGELs, F680, and the handling of classified and OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE material
  • Exposure to guidelines, standards and processes such as ARP-4754, ARP-4761, JSP 936 and Def Stan

d17aff48b43b.title: Senior RF Systems Engineer
d17aff48b43b.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Maneuver Dominance team in London builds the Mission System and Autonomy for Anduril's autonomous air platforms. Aircraft built to operate alongside crewed aviation and deliver effects in contested environments.

Autonomy is only as good as the link that carries it. Our platforms are compact airframes with sensors, payloads and radios competing for the same antenna real estate, flying low and in formation, in a spectrum that is actively contested. That is the problem you would own.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a Senior RF Systems Engineer to get hands on with the communications and navigation RF architecture across our systems. You will help drive the RF architecture and then go and prove it: selecting and placing antennas, developing link budgets and co-site analysis, running modelling and simulation, managing the radio, antenna and cabling vendor base, integrating hardware onto the aircraft, and troubleshooting it on the bench and in the field. You will be an authoritative voice for RF in vehicle-level trade studies, which means making calls that other disciplines will build around and being able to defend them.

We are looking for someone with low-ego and high-ownership, mission focused, meticulous about detail and as comfortable arguing a position as revising it when the measurements disagree. If you enjoy being the person a cross-functional team turns to when the RF problem is genuinely hard, this is that job.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Architect, design, integrate, test and optimise communications and navigation RF hardware across the Mission System and its subsystems.
  • Perform antenna selection and placement studies, using installed-performance modelling to trade coverage, blockage and antenna-to-antenna isolation on a dense airframe.
  • Develop RF link budgets, co-site analysis and desense reports, and translate them into design decisions the wider team can act on.
  • Own the platform frequency plan and E3/EMC (electromagnetic compatibility) approach, from the control plan through to qualification testing and airworthiness evidence.
  • Configure, simulate, evaluate and test RF systems and datalinks, in the lab and in the field.
  • Create and maintain RF system interconnect diagrams and supporting design documentation.
  • Select and manage radio, RF component, cable and antenna vendors.
  • Represent RF in vehicle-level, cross-disciplinary trade studies that define and optimise our platforms.
  • Support other engineering teams by bringing an understanding of RF system impacts and trades to their design decisions.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 7+ years of hands-on industry experience in RF systems design, build, test and troubleshooting.
  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Depth in RF link budgets, co-site analysis and desense, and a working understanding of EMI and the system-level integration issues that come with dense platforms.
  • Experience with antenna selection, placement and installed performance on vehicles or aircraft.
  • Working knowledge of MIL-STD-461 and MIL-STD-464, or equivalent military E3 standards.
  • Fluency with RF test equipment: spectrum analysers, network analysers, power meters, signal and function generators, and the judgement to know when a measurement is telling you something real.
  • Experience with RF system modelling and simulation.
  • Experience with the electrical integration of avionics and payloads into air vehicles, UAVs, ground vehicles or weapons systems.
  • Working knowledge of aviation and tactical communications systems, plus the fundamentals of Ethernet and IP networking.
  • Python for test automation and data analysis, and a habit of automating any measurement you take more than twice.
  • The ability to work across disciplines: defining product requirements, running trade analyses, developing specifications, and conducting system-level tests with people who are not RF engineers.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active UKSV Security Clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience integrating tactical datalinks, beyond-line-of-sight communications and resilient (anti-jam) navigation systems on air platforms.
  • Rotorcraft or small-airframe antenna integration experience.
  • Computational electromagnetic tools for installed antenna performance (for example FEKO, CST, HFSS or EMIT).
  • Experience writing or owning an E3 Control Plan; DO-160 or MIL-STD-810 environmental qualification.
  • Familiarity with Ofcom, FCC and UK MOD spectrum and frequency clearance processes.
  • Experience with MANET and mesh waveforms.
  • Experience designing or testing for GNSS-denied and EW-contested environments.
  • Experience with crypto-bearing equipment and red/black separation.
  • Anechoic chamber and antenna pattern measurement experience.

The salary range for this role is an estimate

e9b0d617364f.description:

Boards that work first time, and that are easy to build, test and fix, are what keep the whole system moving. That is the problem you would own.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a Senior Electrical Engineer to join us in London and own electronic hardware across our mission system and payloads. This is a full-cycle role. You will take customer needs and mission parameters, turn them into measurable requirements, and carry the design through schematic, layout, bring-up, qualification and integration on the aircraft. That includes boards that form part of the Stores Management System, where the interface to the weapon has to be right first time. You will be the voice for electrical design in vehicle-level trade studies, and you will be in the lab and at the test range when the hardware needs debugging.

We are looking for someone who sees the whole system, not just the board: low-ego and high-ownership, mission focused, and able to justify a design decision to engineers and to leadership alike. This is a full-time, on-site role, because the work is hands-on and the team learns from each other at the bench.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Own the development of electronic hardware for payloads and subsystems across the Mission System, including sensor interfaces, power management, compute and networking
  • Turn customer asks and mission parameters into quantifiable hardware requirements, and create architectures and designs that meet them
  • Deliver full-cycle PCB design: requirements capture, schematic design, component selection, layout (completing it or supervising it), bring-up, test, debug, qualification and system integration
  • Design mixed-signal boards that combine high-speed digital, precision analogue, RF and high-power circuits, including microcontroller and processor based designs
  • Perform power design and electrical loading analysis, and develop power management and distribution for payloads and subsystems
  • Design, test and qualify boards for the Stores Management System, including MIL-STD-1553 data bus and MIL-STD-1760 aircraft-to-store interfaces, and safety-critical circuits such as release consent, arming and interlocks
  • Develop system interconnect diagrams and define the wire harnesses that connect equipment within a subsystem and onto the air vehicle
  • Design for manufacture, test and the operating environment from the start, applying IPC standards and accounting for temperature, vibration and EMI
  • Troubleshoot issues that span the electrical and software boundaries, using lab equipment and basic software debugging tools
  • Conduct peer-level and cross-discipline design reviews, and represent electrical design at Preliminary Design Reviews (PDR), Critical Design Reviews (CDR) and Test Readiness Reviews (TRR)
  • Collaborate closely with mechanical, RF, software, firmware, systems and test engineers to deliver fully functional, mission-critical products
  • Establish and refine team processes for PCB design, design for manufacturing (DFM), part creation and library standards
  • Support integration, ground and flight test of prototype and production representative hardware, across multiple concurrent projects and customers

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 7+ years of hands-on industry experience designing, testing and troubleshooting complex board-level electronic hardware
  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical or Electronic Engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience
  • Full-cycle PCB design experience, from requirements capture through schematic, layout, bring-up, qualification and sustainment
  • Experience designing mixed-signal, multi-layer PCBs, including stack-up, impedance control, grounding, protection and filtering for power and sensor applications
  • Experience with power design, power management and electrical loading analysis, and with designing and integrating high-power electronics
  • Hands-on experience with microcontrollers and processors, including bring-up, and familiarity with common MCU, CPU and FPGA devices
  • Familiarity with common interfaces such as Ethernet, CAN, I2C, SPI, PCIe, USB, RS-232, RS-422 and RS-485
  • Fluency with lab test equipment: oscilloscopes, DMMs, logic and spectrum analysers, bench power supplies, electronic loads and current probes, plus experience automating tests
  • Experience using Altium Designer (other ECAD tools considered), including component library development and management

Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we’re unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

Senior Software Engineer, Full Stack - EMEA Pricing and Affordability

You’ll join EMEA Pricing & Affordability, the team that owns how an order is priced for consumers across EMEA: service and delivery fees, distance-based pricing and surcharges, fee discounts and the benefits that subscribers get. Our work sits right at the cart and checkout, on the new Pedregal platform shared across Deliveroo and Wolt.

Price is the most visible part of every order. Getting it right means customers can see what they’ll pay and trust it, and can afford to order again. That drives conversion, order frequency and retention, and it is one of the biggest levers on both consumer growth and marketplace economics. Our roadmap covers subscriber pricing, service fee optimisation, distance-based pricing, long distance surcharges and priority delivery, so the work reaches millions of orders in many markets.

As a full stack engineer on this team you’ll take pricing features from idea to production: designing fee and discount logic on the backend, building the checkout and basket experience that shows it, and measuring the result through experiments. About Baringa 

Baringa is a global consulting firm that partners with leaders to drive change and create value. With deep industry expertise, and enabled by advanced technology, the firm helps clients to deliver with greater confidence and certainty. With over 2,000 people across the UK, Europe, North America, Asia and Australia, the firm combines global insight with local understanding.

The firm works across energy and resources, financial services, government and public sector, consumer products and retail, pharmaceuticals and life sciences, manufacturing, and technology, media and telecoms, with capabilities spanning strategy, transformation and operational excellence – all powered by advanced technology, data, AI and digital innovation.

Clients value Baringa’s collaborative approach and the way its teams integrate seamlessly – all working with a shared understanding of what matters most. The firm is known for its kind, curious experts who listen closely and care deeply about client success as they help clients transform energy markets, modernise financial platforms, expand telecoms and digital networks through advanced data analytics, enable digital services in government, and unlock growth in consumer sectors.

Certified as a Great Place to Work around the world, Baringa has been recognised by the Financial Times in 22 categories of its UK Leading Management Consultants rankings, and by Forbes for four consecutive years as one of the World’s Best Management Consulting Firms.

Our Data, AI, Solutions and Engineering practice are looking for experienced Consultants and Senior Consultants to join the team. 

Our Data, AI, Solutions & Engineering team really likes helping our clients solve their complex problems with data, by implementing controls and governance of data, creating actionable insights, embedding machine learning solutions or building data platforms. We bring the right team and skills on the table and can offer deep expertise across Data Strategy, Data Science & Engineering, Data Visualisation, Data Management, Data Architecture and Software Development. 

What you will be doing

You will be using your experience to help our clients solve their most important data challenges. Data and AI strategy and governance call on very similar skills, and you will bring both: understanding what the business is trying to achieve, shaping a clear data vision and business case, and putting in place the right data foundations.  

You will also support the growth of our team, helping them to build the skills they need to solve our clients’ challenges. Depending on your level, you will have the opportunity to help shape the direction of the practice, grow the business and lead our people. 

Most of our engagements span both strategy and governance. Typical engagements look like: 

  • Defining the data strategy for clients, including a UK energy company, to identify the team, capability, technology and governance required to meet growing data needs, and a European energy trader, to set out a vision and establish a well-governed data platform that better supports trading analytics 
  • Supporting a non-profit government-owned organisation in defining their data strategy and implementing a new data management and governance capability

Backed by top-tier investors (Benchmark, Blossom, Index Ventures, and Kima Ventures) and born out of Y Combinator (S18), we’re simplifying complex systems to build the future of travel. Customer Success at Duffel Customer Success owns Duffel's relationship with our customers once the contract is signed. We help them integrate, launch and grow on Duffel across Flights, Stays and more. The team brings together Customer Success Managers, Customer Success Engineers and Technical Support Engineers across London and New York, led by our VP, Customer Success. We're growing the team and building the processes that help customers go live faster and get more from Duffel. The Role We're hiring a Solutions Engineer: the technical expert who helps customers design the right Duffel solution during the sales process, then guides them through building it until they go live. In pre-sales, you'll join our Account Executives on discovery calls and pitches, bringing the technical depth to understand how a customer's product works and design how Duffel fits into it. Once the deal is signed, you'll take that design into implementation as the customer's technical point of contact, making sure they go live smoothly with the best setup for their use case. This is a senior individual contributor role reporting to the VP, Customer Success. You'll be our first Solutions Engineer, so the way you do this job will become how the team works as it grows. That could lead to managing a team of solutions engineers, or to a principal-level technical role shaping how our largest customers build on Duffel. Most of our transaction volume is in the US, so you'll work closely with US-based customer teams from London. What You’ll be doing: Join Account Executives on discovery calls, pitches and technical deep-dives, running technical discovery on the customer's product, architecture, user journeys and travel use case. Design the solution, build demos and proofs of concept, and write solution designs and implementation scopes so customers know what they're building before they sign. Answer technical questions in RFPs and security reviews. Take what you designed into implementation as the customer's technical point of contact: answer their engineers' questions, review integrations, define test plans and run go-live readiness checks. Debug integration issues hands-on with Postman or curl and our API logs, working alongside the Senior Implementation Project Manager, who owns the project plan and dates. Feed integration friction back to Product and Engineering, build reusable assets such as solution templates, sample code and demo apps, and define how pre-sales and implementation run at Duffel. What we're looking for: 5+ years in a customer-facing technical role, such as solutions engineer, sales engineer, implementation engineer or technical account manager, at an API-first company. Experience on both sides of the contract: supporting sales with discovery, demos and solution design, then implementing what was sold and taking enterprise customers live on complex integrations. Hands-on API skills (REST, JSON, webhooks, authentication, sandbox vs production) and enough coding in a language such as JavaScript, Python, PHP, Ruby or Java to build a demo and spot what's wrong in a customer's integration. The ability to explain a solution clearly to engineers and commercial decision-makers in the same meeting, and sound judgement on when to push back on a custom request or bring in Product. Willingness to work regular US-overlap hours. Experience in payments, fintech or travel tech, writing statements of work, SQL or AI-assisted development tools is a bonus. What you'll be working on In your first 30 days: demoing Duffel's core flows end to end, building a test integration yourself, joining live sales calls and taking technical ownership of implementations already in flight. By 90 days: leading technical discovery on new opportunities, with a written solution design before signature on every deal you work on. Shaping how new Duffel products, such as Trains and our AI travel agent, are scoped and implemented for customers. In your first year: customers designed in pre-sales going live faster with fewer surprises, a library of reusable solution templates and demo assets, and an evidence-based view of how the function should scale. Why You’ll Love Working at Duffel We believe in true ownership. That’s why every permanent employee gets equity in the business. Perks That Actually Matter: ✈️ Travel Allowance: We literally pay you to get out of town and explore the world. 🏝️ Work From Anywhere: Flexibility is built in. Work remotely, or take advantage of our Sabbatical Policy . ⚡ Electric Car Scheme: Roll up in a brand-new EV with eco-friendly tax savings. ⚖️ Work-Life Harmony: Flexible bank holidays, generous family leave, and a dedicated volunteering day. 📚 Growth Tools: Paid study days to level up your skills, plus a solid pension and cycle-to-work scheme. 🏥 Health & Wellbeing: Private healthcare, eye test cover, and season ticket loans. 🏡 Family Leave (maternity, paternity and adoption) The Details 📍 Location: Shoreditch, London (Hybrid: In-office Tuesdays & Thursdays). 🧠 Interview Process: Simple & transparent: Talent Partner Screen Hiring Manager Interview Technical Interview Final Stage Interview We are an equal opportunities employer. We believe that the key to our success is employing a diverse team, that's why recruitment decisions are only based on your experience and skills. We value your ability to problem solve and build amazing things so we welcome applications for everyone - regardless of age, sex, disability

d09fc379d7da.description: Why loveholidays? We’re on a mission to open the world to everyone, giving our customers unlimited choice, unmatched ease and unmissable value for their next getaway. Our trailblaze together culture is what drives our success, powered by our people and the way they work. Using progressive technology, we drive cutting-edge innovation and improve how our customers discover, book and experience their holidays. You’ll have the opportunity to accelerate your growth through meaningful challenges, new experiences and the freedom to shape your own path. You’ll create impact for our future by taking ownership, contributing to shared goals and helping shape what comes next, all as part of our enhanced international community of talented, collaborative and passionate teams. The difference you’ll make You’ll sit in the Data Science team, reporting to the Head of Data Science. You’ll work closely with Product and Engineering teams to develop predictive models for pricing, recommendations, and other business domains. Together, the team will leverage data to build statistical models that improve commercial decisions. Data Science sits within our Platform function, which builds the technology and shared capabilities that power the loveholidays experience. By creating scalable products, systems and tools, Platform helps the wider organisation move faster, work more independently and deliver better outcomes for customers. Your day-to-day: Build and improve data science products across pricing, recommendations and other business domains to improve customer experiences and commercial outcomes. Turn ambiguous business problems into practical data science solutions, from exploration and modelling through to experimentation and evaluation. Partner with engineers, analysts and product teams to deploy reliable models and embed recommendations into everyday decision-making. Monitor model performance, investigate changes and continuously improve solutions as customer behaviour and business needs evolve. Communicate findings clearly, challenge assumptions and help teams make confident, evidence-based decisions. Your skillset: Strong experience developing and delivering practical machine learning solutions, balancing model performance, business value and long-term maintainability. Proficiency in Python and SQL, with experience working with large, complex datasets. A solid grounding in statistics, experimentation and machine learning, including model evaluation and causal thinking. Experience collaborating with engineers to deploy, monitor and improve models in production. Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts and influence product and commercial decisions. The interview journey: Intro with a member of our Talent Acquisition team - 30 minutes 1st Stage: Virtual Interview with Hiring Manager - 45 minutes 2nd Stage: Two on-site interviews 50 minutes for a project discussion deepdive with member(s) of the Data Science team 1 hour technical discussion around a case study with member(s) of the Data Science team Final-stage: Virtual interview with key stakeholders - 45 minutes Perks of joining us: Company pension contributions at 5% Individualised training budget for you to learn on the job and level yourself up Discounted holidays for you, your family and friends 25 days of holidays per annum (plus 8 public holidays) increases by 1 day for every second year of service, up to a maximum 30 days per annum Ability to buy and sell annual leave Access to our electric vehicle salary sacrifice scheme Cycle to work scheme, season ticket loan and eye care vouchers Our commitment to inclusion At loveholidays, we focus on creating an inclusive environment where everyone can contribute, grow and succeed. We value the different perspectives, experiences and ideas each person brings, because they help us work better together, challenge our thinking and make stronger decisions. As we continue to grow and evolve, we want everyone to feel supported and able to do their best work. We’re also committed to making our hiring process accessible, so please let our Talent Acquisition team know if you need any adjustments at any stage. Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

f69885a38824.title: GTM Engineer
f69885a38824.description: Can you help us fix the world's most broken supply chain? The fashion industry produces over 100 billion garments a year. 60% end up in landfill, not because people don't want these clothes, but because the supply chain that moves them from donation to resale is offline, manual and broken. Fleek is fixing this. Our mission is to make secondhand the first choice. We run a B2B marketplace where resellers and stores buy clothing in bulk, and we build the AI systems that digitise the supply chain behind it. Our buyers sell on eBay, Vinted, Depop, Whatnot, eBay Live and TikTok Shop, or run vintage stores from Brick Lane to Paris to New York. They source graded stock from wholesalers and rag houses across many countries. Our key enabler is FleekSort, an AI model fine-tuned on secondhand fashion that can grade, price and categorise an item from a single photo. We are now going well beyond vintage. Live sellers can sell almost anything, and there is an opportunity for Fleek to be the backend for B2B resale. We've now started onboarding customers alongside supply from Japan, South Korea, the Philippines and Thailand. Since 2022, we've saved 9 million items from landfill and tripled in size year on year. We've raised ~$50M from a16z, Y Combinator, HV Capital and others, and recently closed our Series B. Our advisors and private investors include operators behind Depop, Shopify and Postmates. We're looking for people who want to build something that matters, and move fast doing it. About the role You'll join the GTM team as our GTM Engineer, reporting to our GTM lead and working day to day with the new business team. You'll own the system we use to find and win customers, on both sides of the marketplace. On the demand side, that means online resellers, live sellers and physical stores in the UK, Europe and the US, buying vintage, deadstock, new with tags and luxury. On the supply side, it means the brands, brokers, wholesalers and rag houses who sell to them. As we add new categories and markets, the system has to find those customers too. We already have pipelines that scrape marketplaces and load leads into our CRM. The next step is everything after that: putting the right leads first, reaching them well, and learning from every outcome. You'll own the engine end to end, from the first scrape to the revenue each new customer brings in. This is not a typical B2B SaaS GTM engineering role. You won't spend your days wiring a CRM to a LinkedIn sequencer or building dashboards. Everyone on our commercial team builds their own tools with AI. You'll take on the problems they can't: systems that improve themselves, infrastructure that scales, and outreach that works within limits set by platforms like Meta. The role is part engineer, part product manager and part commercial. You won't carry a closes target, but you'll own every metric that moves it. The problem you'll solve We want a system that finds the right customers, puts them in order, reaches out, and gets better every week. It runs as a loop: Find. Source leads across marketplaces and social platforms, for every segment and market we sell into. Prioritise. Score each lead on the signals that predict a good customer, not just a likely reply. Reach out. Contact them on Instagram, WhatsApp, email, phone or LinkedIn, personalised by AI and handed to a rep at the right moment. Learn. Feed every outcome back into scoring. If a store replied but wasn't a fit, similar leads drop down the list, so we stop spending tokens and rep time on them. Then back to step 1. To make that loop work, you'll build a second brain for GTM: one layer that holds everything we know about a customer, with models and agents running on top. That includes the messages we sent and how they replied, how fast they replied and closed, what they sell and where, what they click and search for in our app, what they told our reps on calls, and how much they spend and how well they retain. The same data powers our account management team, who look after customers once they've placed their first orders. Matching each buyer with the right supply is one of their next big problems, and you'll help solve it. What you'll do Own the acquisition engine. Learn how our current pipelines work and improve them. If a rebuild is the right call, make the case for it, and keep leads flowing to the reps while you build. Source at scale in new segments. Find vintage stores, live sellers, deadstock and luxury buyers, and new suppliers, in every market we enter. Build the scoring and feedback loop. Define what a good lead looks like for each segment, then keep refining it on what actually closes and what actually spends. Engineer multi-channel outreach. Instagram, WhatsApp, email, calls and LinkedIn, personalised by AI and built around real limits like Instagram DM caps and Meta restrictions. Own the funnel numbers. Leads sourced per day on each platform, reply rate, conversion rate and GMV per close by source. Use them to decide what to fix next. Sit with the reps and talk to customers. Learn why a lead is good and how each segment wants to be sold to. Then automate the repetitive parts of the rep's day. Turn repeat work into agents. Qualification, first messages, reply handling, dedupe and CRM hygiene should run without a person. Keep it efficient. Every system you build should make sense on cost per lead and unit economics. Connect acquisition to retention. Make sure new customers land cleanly with account management, and help build the buyer-to-supply matching they rely on. What you bring A strong technical background. You've built and run real systems, such as data pipelines, scrapers, models or production infrastructure. You've done more than configure tools. An AI-first mindset, a step ahead. You build with Claude and other models every day and know where agents work and where they break. Our commercial team is very AI-literate, and you'll push them further. Curiosity about the customer. It runs in the browser tab, the desktop app, the agent your engineers kicked off, and the copilot embedded in the tools you already pay for. Harmonic Security governs all of it. Our AI Governance and Control (AIGC) platform sits on the device, inside the interaction, at the moment of action, reading what AI is actually doing (not just the traffic around it) and acting in real time. Security teams get full visibility and control across every AI surface, including the agentic and MCP layer that traditional tools can't see. Their people get to innovate without guardrails slowing them down. We're gaining serious traction at the intersection of AI and cybersecurity, and backed by investors who know the space: N47, Ten Eleven Ventures, and In-Q-Tel. As AI adoption inside the enterprise accelerates, the ability to safely observe, control, and enforce policy in real time isn't a nice-to-have. It's mission-critical infrastructure. We expect every new hire to bring a genuine curiosity for AI and a commitment to using it to work smarter, faster, and with greater creativity. 8c30fbadfa52.title: AI Solutions Engineer - R&D
8c30fbadfa52.description: AI Solutions Engineer - R&D ➡️ Do you understand how R&D and engineering teams work, from technical research and technology evaluation through to product development and innovation? ➡️ Have you gone beyond using AI to actually building solutions, integrating APIs, developing agents or automating complex workflows? ➡️ Can you combine hands-on technical capability with the confidence to engage enterprise customers, understand their challenges and design solutions that deliver real value? If this sounds like your next move, we’d love to hear from you. Role Summary: We have an exciting new role as an AI Solutions Engineer to support our R&D customers. You’ll work alongside Account Executives and Account Managers throughout the sales process, speaking directly with prospective customers to understand their R&D and data workflows, uncover what they’re trying to achieve, and design AI-powered solutions around those needs. This isn’t a role where you simply demo an existing product. You’ll be expected to build and tailor the solution for the customer — using Patsnap’s data, APIs, MCP capabilities and AI tools to create agents, workflows, prototypes and proof-of-concepts that bring their use case to life. The brief is simple: Understand the customer. Build the solution. Prove the value. We’re looking for people who can bring together: Domain knowledge + customer-facing experience + real AI build capability A typical day could involve joining several customer calls, running technical discovery, building a prototype between meetings, demonstrating it live to a prospect, refining it based on feedback and, where needed, supporting deployment after signature. We're looking for someone who brings together three core strengths: R&D & Engineering Workflow Understanding: You understand how R&D, engineering and innovation teams operate, the challenges they face and where AI can deliver value. Customer-Facing & Commercial Capability: You're confident engaging enterprise customers, leading technical discovery and translating requirements into compelling solutions. Hands-On AI Development: You can independently build AI agents, integrations, automated workflows and technical prototypes, rather than simply demonstrating existing software. You'll use Patsnap's proprietary R&D and innovation intelligence, APIs, Model Context Protocol (MCP) capabilities and AI technologies to design, build and demonstrate solutions tailored to customer needs. That could involve developing an AI agent to accelerate technical research, integrating Patsnap's intelligence into existing enterprise systems, automating technology scouting processes or creating intelligent workflows to support engineering and product development decisions. You'll take customer challenges from initial discovery through to working prototypes and proof-of-concepts, demonstrating how AI can deliver meaningful improvements to their R&D processes. This is not a traditional software engineering role. You won’t be expected to build production software from scratch, but you will need to be technically confident, comfortable building independently and credible in front of enterprise customers. Want to see the platform you'd be representing? Check out this short overview: This is a hybrid position in our London, UK office, working 1–2 days in the office and the rest from home. Who are we? Patsnap is a global, pre-IPO company that transforms the way organizations harness their Intellectual Property and Research and Development productivity. Our platform revolutionizes how IP and R&D teams collaborate across the entire innovation lifecycle, using domain-specific AI to accelerate the creation of market-ready products. With over 12,000 customers worldwide, including some of the biggest names in innovation, Patsnap is at the forefront of technological advancement. Our $300M Series E funding round brings our valuation to a $1 billion unicorn status, and we still have a remarkable amount of growth ahead. e605b31d20ef.title: Meridial – Senior Research Software Engineer – Image Processing
e605b31d20ef.description: About Meridial Meridial is a Focused Research Organisation (FRO) with a mission to bring connectomics into the living brain. We are building a platform for longitudinal, synapse-resolution mapping of functional neural circuitry in preclinical models. Our aim is to deploy this platform for translational projects and improve drug development outcomes for disorders of the central nervous system. Meridial is a new not-for-profit FRO in the Convergent Research Ecosystem and funded by the Advanced Research and Invention Agency ( ARIA ). The technical challenge Our imaging platform records the activity of neurons and synapses in the living brain. The scientific value of these recordings depends on converting raw images into reliable, quantitative data. This is a demanding image processing problem. Fluorescence signals are faint, noisy and spatially overlapping; residual tissue motion and other imaging artefacts must be corrected; in addition to conventional planar frames, data may be acquired from arbitrarily shaped 3D regions or several depths at once; properties vary between signal types and experimental configurations; and the same cells and synapses must be reliably matched across imaging sessions spanning weeks. You will build a software package that addresses these challenges in two modes: real-time processing and visualisation, with latencies of tens to hundreds of milliseconds, that inform experimental decisions at the microscope, and offline pipelines that deliver maximum accuracy for scientific analysis and serve as the benchmark for the real-time methods. The impact of this work is direct and visible: your software will be used at the microscope as experiments unfold, and your pipelines will generate the data underpinning new insights into how neural circuits function and how they change in disease. Key responsibilities You will own Meridial’s image processing software end to end, starting from the interface with microscope control and acquisition all the way to processed results prepared for biological analysis. This is a role with a high degree of autonomy: you will make the main design and technology decisions, set priorities with the people who use the software, and work out what to build as requirements emerge. Who you will work with Experimental team. The neuroscientists running experiments are the main users of the real-time tools. You will work with them at the microscope, understand their problems and turn joint solutions into reliable tools. Senior Software Engineer. Develops the microscope control and image acquisition software, mostly in Rust. Your real-time code exchanges data with that software but need not be part of it. Together, you will decide how the two systems connect. Neuroscience Data Scientist. Owns Meridial’s database and the downstream scientific analysis. You will ensure processed results reach the database with a full record of how they were produced. Reporting line. You will join the Computational Team and report to its Head once appointed, and to the Director of Experimental Research until then. What you will do Build robust pipelines for motion and artefact correction, segmentation of cells and synapses, separation of overlapping signals and extraction of activity over time, adapted to different signal types. Register data from flexible 3D imaging modes to reference volumes, and build tools that find the same field of view and match cells and synapses across sessions, both live at the microscope and offline at high resolution. Develop real-time versions of these methods that keep up with streaming data, including fast identification of cells as stimulation targets. Build live visualisations and summary measures, such as rolling averages, response histograms and noise metrics, that help scientists steer experiments. Define, with the Senior Software Engineer, the interface between acquisition and processing, with a focus on throughput and low latency. Evaluate and adapt existing open-source tools, develop new methods where needed, and validate them against ground truth, using offline results as the benchmark for the real-time processing. Optimise for speed and scale, using multi-threading, GPUs or compiled languages where needed, so that processing keeps up with large and growing datasets. Write clean, tested and documented code, and set up version control, continuous integration and documentation practices for the codebase. Use AI coding assistants to work efficiently, while keeping code correct and maintainable. Plan and track work in Jira or another project management system, in short iterations with the experimental team. Turn prototypes into reproducible tools that scientists can use and that can be released as open source. The person we are looking for You are an experienced software engineer with a background in image analysis or computer vision. You enjoy hard technical problems and set high standards for correctness, performance and code quality. You like working directly with the people who use your software: understanding their problems, trying out ideas with them and turning the best into reliable tools. You enjoy building from scratch and are comfortable with the ambiguity of an early-stage organisation. As the main developer of our image processing software, you will work independently and shape how it evolves. Experience in any of these areas would help you hit the ground running, but none is required: real-time or streaming data processing, microscopy or scientific image analysis, statistics, or machine learning for image analysis. A background in biology, biophysics or neuroscience would also help. Essential experience Experience with image analysis or computer vision, such as segmentation, motion correction, registration or denoising, including image quality measures like signal-to-noise ratio. 5+ years of software development experience, in industry or research (for example, PhD or postdoctoral work where software was a main output). About Mirakl:

Founded in 2012, Mirakl has been at the forefront of marketplace innovation, empowering every business to compete in the platform economy.

Today, Mirakl’s operating system combines an enterprise marketplace solution (Mirakl Platform) that enables retailers and B2B organizations to launch, scale, and operate marketplaces and dropship, AI-powered multichannel selling (Mirakl Connect), retail media (Mirakl Ads) and an agentic commerce infrastructure (Mirakl Nexus).

With dual headquarters in Boston and Paris, Mirakl helps a global ecosystem of 450+ marketplaces (B2C and B2B) and a network of over 100k third-party marketplace sellers. Brands like Macy’s, Decathlon, Carrefour, Asos, and Airbus Helicopters use Mirakl to grow their businesses in new and remarkable ways.

For more information: www.mirakl.com.

Mirakl in Numbers:

  • 🗓️ Founded in 2012 | Member of French Tech Next40
  • 👥 750+ employees in 9 offices worldwide: Paris, Barcelona, Bordeaux, Boston, London, Munich, New York, Sydney, Tokyo
  • 🇫🇷 350+ Mirakl Tech teams members mainly based in France
  • ⚙️ 5 Saas Solutions

Our Values:

Working at Mirakl means accelerating your career alongside ambitious, passionate, and supportive colleagues. We're proud of the diversity of backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences that make our teams unique.

Our 5 values guide how we collaborate:

  • 💡 Work Hard Together: Teamwork and collaboration are the foundation of our success
  • 🏆 Get Things Done:  We prioritize action and efficiency for impactful results
  • 🚀 Go Above & Beyond:  We tackle challenges proactively and always aim for excellence
  • 🎓 Succeed Through Expertise: Knowledge sharing and continuous learning are core to our culture
  • 🤝 Satisfy & Empower Clients: We're committed to our clients' success

Your role :

As a Software Engineer Java Freelance in the Mirakl Labs product teams, your main mission is to design, develop and deploy new business features proposed by the Product Manager. On a daily basis, you will be implementing these new features across all layers of our applications, from interfaces (UI or REST API) through the business layer to the creation of database schemas and scripts. As part of a team with total ownership over the products it develops, you are a key player in ensuring both the business consistency of the product and its technical stability.

The position is a freelance contract, based in Bordeaux, with up to 1 day of remote work per week. 

95% of our tech teams are based in France and 99% speak French.

Day-to-day activities:

  • Build, test, and ship to production through continuous delivery
  • Harness AI-powered tools like Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor to move faster
  • Join design sessions alongside a team of 5 developers, the Product Manager, and UX/UI designers
  • Shape technical decisions that drive the product forward
  • Sharpen code quality through reviews and pair programming
  • Own what you build — monitor and debug production issues end to end
  • Take part in Stand-ups, Sprint Reviews, and retrospectives
  • Help define the next quarter's labs roadmap
  • Drive continuous improvement in how the team develops software
  • Track the real-world impact of your features: business cycles, adoption, usage

Our tech stack:
Java 21 (with planned migration to 25), Spring Boot, Kafka, React/Redux, PostgreSQL, Elasticsearch, Go, Docker, Kubernetes, AWS, Google Cloud

You'll love this job if : 

  • You have at least 3 years of experience with Java and Spring
  • You are genuinely curious (and pragmatic) about AI, and you believe it's already reshaping how developers work
  • You are eager to work on web-scale challenges and distributed architectures
  • You care deeply about clean, well-crafted code
  • You want a real voice in technical decisions, not just a seat at the table
  • You thrive in fast-paced, demanding environments where you grow every week
  • You're hungry to learn and sharpen your craft
  • You're fluent in French and comfortable working in professional English

7a87b79416ac.title: STAGE - Junior Fullstack Engineer - Jobexit
7a87b79416ac.description: Notre mission ⚖️ Chez Doctrine, nous construisons le leader de l’IA juridique en Europe. Notre conviction ? Le droit ne doit pas être ralenti par des tâches répétitives. Il doit être augmenté par une IA spécialisée, conçue pour comprendre, analyser et produire du raisonnement juridique avec un haut niveau d’exigence. Notre ambition ? Permettre aux professionnels du droit de gagner en fiabilité, en efficacité et en sérénité, grâce à une plateforme unique, exhaustive et sécurisée. Aujourd’hui, 27 000 professionnels du droit, répartis dans cinq pays (France, Italie, Allemagne, Espagne, Luxembourg), nous font confiance. Notre développement est guidé par une approche claire : une vision globale, ancrée dans une compréhension fine des spécificités locales. Derrière cette ambition, une équipe d’environ 250 personnes, réunies autour d’un même objectif : accompagner les juristes et avocats à toutes les étapes de leur travail, de l’analyse à la rédaction. Et nous n’en sommes qu’au début. Sujet de stage Doctrine développe des workflows dédiés aux professionnels du droit pour accélérer et améliorer la gestion de leurs dossiers. Parmi eux, Jobexit accompagne les avocats et juristes en droit social dans la simulation de ruptures du contrat de travail, notamment en calculant les indemnités de départ, les indemnités en cas de contentieux, le calendrier de sortie et les allocations chômage. Dans un litige, un salarié peut demander plusieurs choses à la fois : des salaires impayés, une indemnité de licenciement, des dommages et intérêts, etc. L'objectif du stage est de permettre à l'utilisateur de saisir et d'organiser toutes ces demandes dans l'application, pour mieux estimer les montants en jeu, préparer la négociation avec la partie adverse et générer automatiquement le récapitulatif final destiné au juge. Ceci peut inclure : Concevoir une interface pour ajouter, modifier et réordonner les demandes d'un dossier, chacune avec son montant, son unité de calcul et son ordre Modéliser les dépendances entre demandes (une demande qui ne s'applique que si une autre est refusée par exemple) Calculer et afficher les montants (du coût pour l’employeur au net empoché par le salarié), pour aider l'utilisateur à évaluer les risques Générer automatiquement un document de synthèse clair et structuré, prêt à être intégré dans les conclusions écrites de l'avocat Et d'autres fonctionnalités ! Le ou la stagiaire participera à la compréhension du besoin utilisateur autour de ces outils (en collaboration avec les équipes produit et les juristes) et à la définition des solutions techniques (en collaboration avec les équipes techniques). Il ou elle rejoindra l’équipe Jobexit et participera également au chapter web (regroupement de tous les développeurs fullstack de l’entreprise). Les à-côtés du poste 👁️ Le ou la stagiaire participera comme tous les ingénieurs à son chapter (réuni 2 fois par mois) dont le but est de : Partager des connaissances entre ses membres (amélioration continue, bonnes pratiques) Proposer des améliorations (nouveaux outils et processus) Aider ses membres en fonction de leurs besoins Ce qui t'attend si tu rejoins Doctrine 🤝 Contribuer à un projet ambitieux, avec un impact réel et positif sur la société : rendre le droit plus accessible et plus ouvert. Un onboarding très complet permettant une intégration et une montée en compétence rapides. Une aventure dans laquelle la formation et le partage des connaissances font partis du quotidien. Rejoindre une entreprise avec une vie d’équipe riche et dynamique : conférences, team-buildings, déjeuner, offsite, afterwork, etc. Nos valeurs 🤝 Chez Doctrine, nos 4 valeurs nous accompagnent au quotidien et dans notre ambition de faire bouger les choses. Challenge the status quo : n ous défendons les idées audacieuses qui contribuent à l’évolution de tout un secteur. Liberty and responsibility : n ous encourageons l’autonomie, l’impact de chacun·e et l’ownership. Aujourd’hui, 27 000 professionnels du droit, répartis dans cinq pays (France, Italie, Allemagne, Espagne, Luxembourg), nous font confiance. 9d9b82fb66b8.title: Software Engineer - Dynamics
9d9b82fb66b8.description: Wanna join the adventure? Loft Orbital is looking for a Software Engineer to join the Dynamics team within Ground Platform. Dynamics computes the timeline of what every spacecraft in our fleet can do and when (contacts with ground stations, links, accesses, unavailability windows) and turns it into schedules: which satellite talks to which ground station, when, and in which order of priority. As our fleet grows, these services need to handle more data, more queries, and harder allocation problems. You’ll bring strong backend engineering to that challenge: making our APIs fast, our databases scale, and our contact allocation and scheduling smarter. No astrodynamics background is needed; you’ll work alongside flight dynamics engineers who bring that expertise. If you enjoy hard performance problems and optimization with real-world constraints, we’d love to hear from you. About this role: Build and optimize our scheduling capabilities: model constraints and objectives, design algorithms and solver-based approaches that produce feasible, high-quality schedules across a growing fleet, and replan quickly when things change Evolve contact allocation (Contact Allocation Framework) to share ground station capacity across satellites and missions Improve the performance of our backend services and APIs: profile, find bottlenecks and cut latency for the timeline and scheduling services that operators and other teams rely on Design and evolve our data layer for large, fast-growing time-based datasets: data modeling, partitioning, indexing, query optimization and retention Shape the architecture of Dynamics services for low latency and scale, in step with the rest of Ground Platform Collaborate with flight dynamics engineers, Mission Platform (Execution & Insights) and satellite operators to turn their needs into reliable, performant software Have the opportunity to take part in spacecraft operations through SatDevOps rotations, occasionally helping investigate anomalies Must Haves: Solid backend software development experience, in Python Strong algorithmic foundations for scheduling and optimization problems: modeling constraints and objectives, heuristics, and knowing when to reach for a solver Proven track record improving the performance of APIs or backend services (profiling, caching, concurrency, load testing) Strong relational database skills, ideally PostgreSQL: data modeling, indexing, partitioning, reading query plans Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal Nice to Haves: Experience with constraint programming or operations research (e.g. OR-Tools / CP-SAT , MILP solvers), or with scheduling and allocation problems Django and GraphQL (Graphene) Time-series or geospatial data at scale (e.g. TimescaleDB, PostGIS) Kubernetes and observability tooling (OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Grafana) Interest in space (astrodynamics knowledge not required) Some of Our Awesome Benefits: Equity, we want you to have an active role in our success Up to 35 days of Paid Time Off (vacations & RTT ) and flexible working hours, we want you to be at your best Health and life insurance, we care about your health Lunch Vouchers, because let’s be honest, we love food! (we even have a slack channel about it #loft-gourmand ) Cross-office travel opportunities between San Francisco, Colorado, and Toulouse to learn from our differences Company and team off-sites and many other events to work & celebrate together Relocation assistance to Toulouse when applicable * Research shows that while men apply to jobs where they meet an average of 60% of the criteria, women and other underrepresented people tend to only apply when they meet 100% of the qualifications. At Loft, we value respectful debate and people who aren’t afraid to challenge assumptions. We strongly encourage you to apply, even if you don’t check all the boxes. Who We Are Loft: Space Made Simple. Founded in 2017, Loft provides governments, companies, and research institutions with a fast, reliable, and simple way to deploy missions in orbit. We integrate, launch, and operate spacecraft, offering end-to-end missions as a service across Earth observation, IoT connectivity, on-orbit AI, national security missions, and more. Leveraging our existing space infrastructure and an extensive inventory of satellite buses, Loft is reducing years-long integration and launch timelines to months. With more than 30 missions flown, Loft’s flight heritage and proven technologies enable customers to focus on their mission objectives. With a growing fleet on track to reach 30 satellites by 2027, we are scaling up quickly across our offices in San Francisco, CA | Golden, CO | and Toulouse, France to meet accelerating demand for space infrastructure. As an international company your resume will be reviewed by people across our offices so please attach a copy in English. Find more English Speaking Jobs in France on Arbeitnow

c6dcdcddc1d5.description: Meet Arago and the Aragonians Arago is an AI and computer hardware company whose mission is to drive the course of history forward. We do so by accelerating breakthroughs at the intersection of AI and semiconductors. Founded in 2024 by AI researchers and physicists with deep expertise in photonics, electronics, software, mathematics, and machine learning, Arago brings together a lean team of engineers and scientists from the world’s top companies and research labs. Composed of nine nationalities and operating from hubs in France, North America, and Israel, we believe in great science and fast achievements. Our work is guided by these core principles: Do great things: we deliver work we’re proud to sign our name to. High velocity: speed matters. We move quickly, one step at a time. One unit: we’re all in this together, with relationships grounded in trust, respect, and camaraderie. Arago is backed by executives from Apple, Arm, Nvidia, Microsoft, and Hugging Face, as well as prominent US and European deeptech venture firms and exited founders. What you’ll do As a Drivers & Virtualization Engineer, you will own the host-facing software boundary of Arago’s accelerator. Your mission is to ensure our hardware is accessible, secure, and performant across diverse environments—ranging from bare-metal deployments to complex virtualized and multi-device cloud infrastructures. You will focus on building robust kernel-level interfaces where correctness, isolation, and long-term operational safety are paramount. Required Skills and Experience Master’s or PhD degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field. Deep knowledge of OS internals, particularly kernel memory management and I/O paths. Strong understanding of memory safety requirements in kernel space. Proven hands-on experience in Linux kernel driver development and kernel modules. Solid understanding of virtualization fundamentals (KVM, hypervisors). Practical experience with emulation frameworks, specifically QEMU internals or custom device models. Familiarity with hardware-level protocols: PCIe, DMA, MMIO, and IOMMU. Language: English at a proficient level. French is a plus. Responsibilities Develop and maintain high-performance Linux kernel drivers for Arago’s proprietary accelerator. Implement communication protocols and virtual device interfaces to bridge hardware and software. Manage low-level hardware interactions including PCIe, DMA, MMIO, and interrupt handling. Enable seamless virtualized access to accelerators using QEMU and KVM. Design and implement robust device sharing, passthrough, and isolation mechanisms. Ensure the security of accelerator operations through strict memory protection and resource isolation. Debug complex failures that span the entire stack: from hardware and kernel to hypervisor and guest OS. Support the scaling of our architecture from single-device setups to large-scale multi-device deployments. Pay and benefits Competitive cash compensation, with final package based on location, experience, and the pay of team members in similar positions. Meaningful stock option plan offered at the earliest stage of the company (included in the majority of full time offers). Relocation bonus and coverage of moving expenses for relocation within 20 minutes of the company’s location. Healthcare coverage (including family-friendly options), pension contributions, professional development support, and 25 days of PTO, in addition to public holidays. Ownership of a key technical domain, with significant vertical and/or horizontal growth opportunities, based on performance and individual drive. Reimbursement of 50% of the public transport subscription fee. A high-paced, multicultural (with 10 nationalities), and engineering-led environment. 120a0a15872e.title: Senior Research Scientist 3D Reconstruction & Spatial AI
120a0a15872e.description:
Intrinsic is an AI robotics group at Google aiming to reimagine the potential of industrial robotics. Our team believes that advances in AI, perception and simulation will redefine what’s possible for industrial robotics in the near future – with software and data at the core.

Our mission is to make industrial robotics intelligent, accessible, and usable for millions more businesses, entrepreneurs, and developers. We are a dynamic team of engineers, roboticists, designers, and technologists who are passionate about unlocking the creative and economic potential of industrial robotics.

Role

As a Senior 3D Reconstruction & Spatial AI Engineer, you will own the development of the geometric and semantic perception stacks that power our physical AI framework. You will design real-time systems that enable our robots to translate unstructured, dynamic 3D environments into structured, queryable world models - seamlessly linking high-level task planners (such as VLM/VLA models) directly to robust, low-level manipulation and grasp policies in Flowstate. 

How your work moves the mission forward

  • Design and deploy real-time spatial perception and state estimation pipelines using both in-house models like Gemini/Gemma and open source models
  • Build multi-sensor fusion pipelines integrating RGB-D, stereo cameras, and IMU data into dense spatial representations (ex: point clouds, neural occupancy grids, or implicit signed distance function fields)
  • Ground high-level semantic concepts into 3D geometric structures. This means building queryable, object-centric 3D scene graphs that map not just where an object is, but what it is, and its relationship to the other objects, and its functional properties
  • Integrate open-vocabulary vision language models (ex: CLiP based visual descriptors, DINOv2) into 3D metric space to allow the robot to reason about natural language instructions (ex: ‘pick up the half-eaten apple and put it in the trash bin’)
  • Develop learning-based spatial models (such as 3D Diffusion Policies) that utilize 3D point clouds to predict continuous grasp poses and trajectories
  • Translate abstract semantic logic into functional affordances (ex: identifying the ‘graspable’ part of a mug versus the ‘containment’ part)
  • Collaborate with eng teams to ensure that stochastic, learned semantic models cleanly map to deterministic safe boundaries on physical hardware
  • Drive data strategies for collecting, labeling, and generating 3D synthetic data 

Skills you will need to be successful

  • Education: PhD (preferred) or Master’s in Robotics, Computer Vision, Machine Learning, or a related quantitative field—with a focus on Spatial AI, SLAM, or Embodied AI .
  • 3D Vision: Deep mathematical foundations in multi-view geometry, camera calibration, visual-inertial odometry (VIO), and probabilistic state estimation .
  • Modern Deep Learning: Proven experience training and deploying multimodal architectures (VLMs/VLAs), contrastive learning frameworks, or 3D neural scene representations (NeRFs, Gaussian Splatting)
  • Programming & Systems: Expert level command of Python (PyTorch)

Skills that will differentiate your candidacy

  • Experience with robotics middleware (ROS2) and real time execution constraints would be a plus
  • Hands-on "battle scars" from deploying onto physical robotic manipulators or mobile platforms

Join Proton and build a better internet where privacy is the default

Founded in 2014 by scientists who met at CERN, Proton was built on the belief that privacy is a fundamental human right. What started as an encrypted email service has grown into an ecosystem of privacy-first products, including Proton Mail, VPN, Drive, Pass, and Calendar, used by millions of people worldwide.

We're profitable, independent, and building for the long term. Free from venture capital control and advertising-driven business models, we focus on what matters most: our users. Our work helps protect digital freedom, from everyday privacy to supporting journalists and activists in challenging environments.

Today, we're an international team of 700+ people, with offices across 9 countries. We have high standards for the people we hire and the work we do. You'll work alongside talented, driven colleagues who challenge each other, take ownership, and care about getting things right.

Explore our open-source projects.

Your impact:

We’re hiring Product Engineers across different levels of experience, from junior to staff engineers. Whether you’re looking to take the next step in your career or already have experience leading complex technical projects, we’d love to hear from you. Your scope and level will reflect your experience and the impact you can bring.

As a Product Engineer, you’ll help shape what we build and own work from understanding the problem through to release and improvement. You’ll speak directly with customers, collaborate with Product and Design, and work across the parts of the stack needed to deliver a complete solution.

What you will do:

  • Understand and shape the problem: Work with Product, Design and customers to understand user needs, question assumptions and decide what is worth building.
  • Own complete features: Turn problems into practical solutions across clients, services and data. Take work through testing, release and improvement, paying attention to usability, performance and behaviour in production.
  • Build effectively with agents: Define clear tasks, provide context and evaluate generated code. Investigate failures, challenge suggestions and make changes yourself when needed.
  • Improve how software gets built: Turn recurring problems into better agent instructions, tests, tools and automated safeguards. Share improvements that help the whole team.
  • Build for trust: Make privacy, security, reliability and maintainability part of your decisions. Verify important failure cases, communicate what remains uncertain and make sound trade-offs about release readiness.

What you will bring:

  • Experience delivering production software: You can explain the problems you solved, the decisions you made and what you learned from maintaining your work after release.
  • Technical depth and adaptability: You have strong expertise and can contribute beyond it. You don’t need equal expertise in every layer, but you understand how your work interacts with the wider system.
  • Practical capability with coding agents: You’ve used agents to deliver working software and can explain how you guide them, improve unsuccessful approaches and verify their output.
  • Code fluency and engineering judgement: You can navigate unfamiliar code, trace behaviour, diagnose problems and make precise changes. You can assess an implementation regardless of who — or what — wrote it.
  • Product judgement: You connect technical choices to user needs, care about the quality of the experience and distinguish a useful reduction in scope from a shortcut that puts users at risk.
  • Ownership and collaboration: You move work forward through uncertainty, explain trade-offs clearly, seek out expertise and take responsibility for the outcome.
  • Technical leadership: You’ve led complex projects through ambiguous requirements, made decisions with lasting consequences and helped other engineers develop their judgement while remaining hands-on.

What we offer:

  • Work that Matters: Millions of people trust Proton with their privacy. We answer only to our users — not advertisers, not investors with conflicting agendas, not governments.
  • A Great Team: Diverse, collaborative, and tight-knit, with people from MIT, Harvard, Stanford, Caltech, Cambridge, ETH, and more.
  • Technology: The right hardware and software to do your best work.
  • Learning & Development: We invest in your growth. Proton is one of the fastest ways to accelerate your career — real challenges, real ownership, from day one.
  • Employee Benefits: Strong health coverage, solid retirement options, generous leave, and wellness support.
  • Stock Options: From day one, you have a real stake in what we're building. When Proton wins, you win.
  • In-Person Collaboration: Offices across Geneva, Zürich, Barcelona, London, and more. You'll spend most of your time collaborating face-to-face.
  • Food: Lunch and snacks on us every day in the office.
  • Transport: We cover public transport, bike allowances, or parking — whichever works for you.
  • Flexible Working: You own your schedule. Outcomes matter more than clock-in times.

f00452fced10.title: Product Frontend Engineer
f00452fced10.description: quinn is becoming the way people employ, across the globe, through one app. quinn is an app-based, managed payroll and employment-administration service. We run it for private households employing a cleaner, nanny, or caretaker, and for businesses that manage employment relationships at scale. The customer stays the legal employer: quinn registers the employment, runs payroll, and handles social insurance, taxes, and filings on their behalf, automated end to end. Where everyone else sells software, quinn sells the outcome. We don't sell payroll software. We run payroll. The purpose behind it is simple: Fair employment. For all. Correct and fair employment, made simple and accessible for any employer and any employee, in any market quinn enters. Where this is going Think about what Revolut did to banking. All of the complexity (the regulation, the clearing, the compliance) handled invisibly in the background, and one simple experience at the front. Nobody using Revolut thinks about what happens behind the screen when they open a new account, swap currencies or send money abroad. It just works, in a couple of taps. Nobody should have to think about it in order to employ someone either. That is what quinn is building, and it is further along than most people assume: a profitable core business, running today in Switzerland, Germany and the UK, expanding into new markets both by launching and by acquiring. By 2030 quinn intends to be the destination brand for fair employment across six countries and more, on one platform, with one experience. One platform means one frontend. One experience means it looks and behaves like quinn whether you are in Zurich or in London, a household or a company. In this strategy that is not a nice-to-have. It is the strategy. Which is why the surface matters more than anything else. Everything quinn does is designed to disappear. The interface is the only part the customer ever sees, and it is the whole proof that the complexity behind it is really handled. Why this role exists Today , quinn runs on several separate web apps: one per product and market, each with its own frontend, grown over the years as the company grew. Our backend engineers built them alongside everything else, plus an internal admin tool that grew the same way. They all work: thousands of employers run payroll through them every month. But nobody was ever tasked with owning the frontend development, so each one got built the way frontend is built by Backend Developers, seen as a hassle rather than the main aspect users interactive with. What comes next is one frontend that replaces all of them, built from scratch: one quinn app for employers, employees and our own support team, in the browser first, then in the App Store and Google Play from the same work. Alongside it, the frontend of Maestro, the internal tool that replaces the old admin for batch processes. The phone app is the surface that matters most, so everything is built for it from the first screen rather than adapted to it afterwards. That is the opening. How we work We are AI-native, and we mean it operationally rather than as a slogan. AI is how the work gets done here. It is why a small team ships like a large one, and it is a large part of how one person will be able to hold the standard we are describing. We expect you to be at the front of that. Not to have heard of the tools, to live in them, and to build your own leverage with them: scaffolding, visual regression checks, design-token pipelines, whatever takes manual work out of the way. And we expect the judgement that has to come with it. AI writes code that looks right and is subtly wrong: structure that doesn't scale, patterns that fall apart three screens later, components that work once and never again. You take the speed and throw away the rest. AI never lowers the bar here. It is the reason the bar can be this high. Tasks What you will own Everything on the screen: The frontend of the quinn app and the web app. App first. One app for everyone who uses quinn: the employer, the employee, and our own support team working inside the customer's account. The frontend of Maestro, our internal batch tool. Desktop and dense: queues, runs, tables, filters, multi-select, keyboard shortcuts. A different discipline from the app, built on the same components. The component library across quinn Home and quinn Business: one frontend, one experience, every market and every device. Whether the app feels native: response, scrolling, gestures, transitions, biometric login, push. Nothing that gives away it isn't native. The quality of what you ship. Nothing leaves your hands half-finished. Where design ends, engineering begins. We have a design team, and they own how quinn looks and behaves: the flows, the visual design, the tokens, the component specs. You don't design. You own everything from there: how it is built, and everything a design file cannot reasonably specify, such as gestures, keyboard, safe areas, what happens between the drawn breakpoints, the loading, offline, pending and failed states, what a three-line German label does to a layout that was designed for English. You are in the room before design starts, saying what already exists in the library and what a new pattern costs. Not at the end, receiving a handover. When you and design disagree, they decide how it looks and behaves and you decide how it is built. Nothing enters the component library without both of you. Requirements Who we are looking for You care about interfaces more than anyone else in the room. You see the two-pixel misalignment without being told, and it bothers you until it is fixed. You build and maintain UI components and design systems, not one-off screens. You can build a mobile app that feels like one. And you can also build a desktop tool full of tables, filters and keyboard shortcuts, because Maestro is one. You understand UX and how people actually behave, not only how a screen looks. And you
